title: Production of 135I and 135Xe through proton induced fission of 238U
abstract: Yields of fission fragments [Formula: see text]I and [Formula: see text]Xe populated by proton induced fission of [Formula: see text]U have been measured using stacked foil activation technique. In the yield of [Formula: see text]I and [Formula: see text]Xe, in addition to the direct formation, there are contributions from the decay of the precursors viz., [Formula: see text]I, [Formula: see text]Te and [Formula: see text]Sb, with a time-dependent behavior. These decay contributions are accounted while calculating the yield. [Formula: see text]Xe, having large neutron capture cross-section, acts as a strong reactor poison and affects the criticality of the reactor. The results obtained are analyzed with the theoretical model calculations using TALYS 1.96.
source: International Journal of Modern Physics E

title: Molecular alloying of titanium–oxo clusters for linker-free S-scheme interfaces
abstract: Abstract Heterojunction engineering is one of the most effective strategies for enhancing charge separation and improving the performance of photo-functional materials. However, such heterojunction functionality has been almost exclusively realized in extended solids, and how to translate this concept into atomically precise molecular systems remains an open question. Here, we employ two isostructural yet electronically distinct titanium-oxo clusters, Ti 12 Mn 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 and Ti 12 Cr 6 O 18 (Bz) 30 (denoted as TiMn and TiCr, respectively; Bz denotes C 6 H 5 CO 2 ), as modular nanosized building blocks to construct molecular alloys that form eutectic molecular alloys across the entire compositional range. Free from covalent or ionic linkages, TiMn and TiCr achieve spontaneous Fermi-level equilibration solely through intimate intermolecular packing, thereby establishing an S-scheme junction at the molecular scale. This markedly enhances charge-carrier separation, carrier lifetime, and interfacial charge-transport kinetics, leading to substantially increased photocurrents, accelerated reactive oxygen species generation, and significantly improved elimination of representative waterborne micropollutants. The emergent functionality originates from local electronic complementarity and low-resistance intermolecular charge-transport channels facilitated by ligand π–π interactions, whereas long-range crystalline order is not essential. Our findings suggest a convenient approach for developing nanocluster-level functional donor–acceptor systems without relying on extended frameworks or on covalent fusion between the building units.

title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of C 14 Confronts Ab Initio Theory
abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure N = 8 , the long-lived radioactive isotope C 14 plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of C 14 has remained less precisely known than that of its stable counterpart C 12 . Here, we report a high-precision determination of the C 14 charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor of 5 and revealing a 1.9 σ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With C 12 and C 14 now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

versions.title: Accurate Charge Radius Measurement of $^{14}$C Confronts Ab Initio Theory
versions.abstract: Located at the neutron shell closure $N = 8$, the long-lived radioactive isotope $^{14}$C plays a critical role in geochronology and nuclear structure studies. Despite its widespread use, the nuclear charge radius of $^{14}$C has remained less precisely known compared to its stable counterpart $^{12}$C. Here, we report a high-precision determination of the $^{14}$C charge radius using collinear laser spectroscopy at the COALA setup at TU Darmstadt, improving upon the precision of previous muonic measurements by a factor $5$ and revealing a $1.9\sigma$ discrepancy of combined uncertainty, indicating a likely underestimated uncertainty in the muonic determination. This measurement challenges state-of-the-art ab initio nuclear theory calculations, including auxiliary field diffusion Monte Carlo, the valence-space in-medium similarity renormalization group, and the no-core shell model, augmented by neural-network techniques. With $^{12}$C and $^{14}$C now forming one of the most precisely characterized even-even isotope pairs, these results also enable improved QED tests.

title: Neutrinoless double-beta decay of the Δ − resonance
abstract: The subprocess n n → p p e − e − is a key ingredient in the interpretation of nuclear neutrinoless double- β decay. Intermediate Δ resonances may provide additional enhancements to this transition. We take a first step toward a Δ -full description of n n → p p e − e − by investigating the neutrinoless double- β decay Δ − → p e − e − in the framework of chiral effective field theory. We systematically derive the long-range contribution from light-Majorana-neutrino exchange through loop diagrams and incorporate the short-range part through counterterms required by renormalization. We predict the pion-mass dependence of the decay amplitude in the kinematic configuration with collinear electrons. Furthermore, to facilitate lattice-QCD matching, we calculate the decay amplitude in the degenerate Δ -nucleon mass limit and provide the corresponding long-range prediction.

title: Prompt neutron emission in the spontaneous fission of Sg 258 , 260
abstract: An experimental study of Sg 258 , 260 produced in the complete fusion reactions Cr 52 , 54 + Pb 207 was performed using the SHELS velocity filter. The prompt neutron multiplicities in the spontaneous fission of Sg 258 , 260 were measured for the first time, yielding average values of ν ¯ ( 258 Sg ) = 4.9 ± 0.4 and ν ¯ ( 260 Sg ) = 5.03 ± 0.14 . The α -decay branching ratio of Sg 260 was determined to be b α = 0.29 ± 0.03 . In addition, the half-lives were measured as T 1 / 2 ( 258 Sg ) = 2 . 2 − 1.0 + 2.4 ms [95% C.L. (confidence limit)] and T 1 / 2 ( 260 Sg ) = 7 . 0 − 1.7 + 2.6 ms (95% C.L.).

title: Role of Shell-Closures and Deformations in Fission Mass Distribution of Actinides
abstract: Abstract The present work identifies the fission fragments operating in even-even actinides within the framework of Quantum Mechanical Fragmentation Theory (QMFT). The fragmentation potential is worked out through the incorporation of spherical, quadrupole, and octupole deformed elongated configurations of the probable binary fragments. The shell-closures, binding energies, and deformations emphasize the potential energy minima, and subsequently the preformed cluster probabilities illustrate the fragment distributions in the spontaneous fission channel. The mass-yield distributions, calculated either using the collective clusterization method, or the BSM approach, or where the available experimental data for actinides with \(98\leq Z\leq102\) and \(150\leq N\leq164\), exhibit the single- and double-hump structures, as they are mutually associated with the fragmentation near \ 132 Sn (spherical shape) and \<sup>144\<sup>Ba (pear-shaped), respectively. Therefore, based on this, we have examined about 150 cases of even-even actinides, belonging to \(90\leq Z \leq102\) and \(108\leq N \leq166\) regions. The study reveals a systematic evolution in fission mass distributions: beginning with near-symmetric splits driven by partial shell closures in quadrupole-deformed fragments, progressing to pronounced asymmetry governed by large shell gaps at the deformed magic numbers (\(Z_{\mathrm{HF}}\approx56\) and \(N_{\mathrm{HF}}\approx88\)) of heavy-mass fragments, and ultimately returning to symmetric patterns stabilized by the double magic configuration (\(Z_i\approx50\) and \(N_i\approx82\)) for binary fragments.

title: Exploring anomaly-free dark photon models through solar neutrino-electron scattering in ton-scale dark matter detectors
abstract: We study the phenomenological implications of anomaly-free dark photon models using low-energy solar neutrino-electron elastic scattering data from the ton-scale PandaX-4T and XENONnT experiments. Focusing on U ( 1 ) X gauge extensions that incorporate both kinetic and mass mixing, we derive novel exclusion limits across the parameter spaces of six benchmark models. Our analysis demonstrates that the stringency of these limits is directly correlated with the theoretical leptonic charge assignments of the respective models. Additionally, we provide model-independent limits by isolating the pure kinetic and pure mass mixing scenarios. In the sub-MeV mediator mass regime, our results meaningfully improve upon existing limits from previous neutrino-electron scattering experiments, such as CHARM-II, TEXONO, and GEMMA. Ultimately, these findings yield improved limits on low-mass dark photon models, demonstrating their complementarity with other ventures in the global search for dark portals.

title: Orientation effects of deformed nuclei in intermediate-energy nuclear scattering
abstract: We investigate the effects of nuclear deformation on intermediate-energy nuclear scattering within the Glauber theory. A formalism that explicitly incorporates the orientation dependence of deformed intrinsic states is derived, in which reaction observables are first computed with a fixed orientation and then the angle average of the reaction observables is taken afterwards. This formalism is applied to elastic scattering and total reaction cross sections. In addition, a new expansion scheme of the optical-limit approximation is proposed and shown to include contributions from a class of nuclear excitations, allowing a simple estimate of part of the total inelastic scattering cross section. The orientation dependence is generally weak for both proton- and carbon-target scattering and supports the validity of conventional treatments with an angle averaged density for light and medium-heavy nuclei. However, noticeable deviations emerge for strongly deformed heavy nuclei. The present analysis further demonstrates that the summed inelastic scattering cross section to rotationally excited states can be interpreted as a manifestation of fluctuations of the nuclear surface density associated with deformation. The present study provides a quantum-mechanical interpretation of deformation effects in intermediate-energy nuclear reactions and suggests a pathway toward a more reliable theoretical description of interaction cross section measurements. Brief comments on the role of nuclear deformation in low-energy heavy-ion reactions and ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions are also made.

title: "ISINN-32" Empirical predictions of $\alpha$-decay and spontaneous fission half-lives in the decay chains of elements 119 and 120
abstract: Abstract The competition between $\alpha$~decay and spontaneous fission in the decay chains of isotopes with $Z = 119$ and $120$ is investigated using empirical formulas. The $\alpha$-decay half-lives are calculated using the Viola--Seaborg semi-empirical formula, while the spontaneous fission half-lives are evaluated using an empirical formula based on the neutron excess $N-Z$ and the $\alpha$-decay energy $Q_\alpha$. The reliability of the approach is validated against experimental data for known nuclei with $Z \ge 103$. A number of $\alpha$-decay chains are identified as promising for experimental observation, with six or more consecutive $\alpha$~decays expected before termination by spontaneous fission. The present results may be of interest for future experimental searches for superheavy nuclei.

title: Deposition of $\alpha$ clusters on the surface of $^{28}$Si
abstract: The possibility of the appearance of the clustering structure in the surface is one of the key features determining the nuclear structural properties. In this work, we study the ground-state structure of $^{28}\text{Si}$ using the antisymmetrized quasicluster model (AQCM), focusing on the deposition of the $\alpha$ cluster structure on the surface. Three candidate structural configurations constrained to reproduce the experimental charge radius are investigated based on the $\text{SU}(3)$ shell model, the $j$-$j$ coupling shell model, and a localized $7\alpha$ cluster model. Using Glauber-model calculations for intermediate-energy proton elastic scattering, we demonstrate that the angular distribution at and beyond the first diffraction peak is highly sensitive to surface diffuseness, and that the $7\alpha$ cluster model configuration best reproduces the experimental data due to its sharper surface profile. Also, the elastic charge form factors from electron scattering support the existence of the cluster-induced oblately deformed structure.

title: Systematic Study of Proton, Two-Proton, Alpha, and Cluster Radioactivity Half-Lives based on the Deformed Gamow-like Model and Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$)
abstract: A hybrid framework combining the deformed Gamow-like model ($\mathrm{DGLM}$) with the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network ($\mathrm{TabPFN}$) is developed to improve half-life predictions for two-proton emission, proton emission, $\alpha$ decay, and cluster radioactivity. A total of 583 radioactive nuclei are investigated, including 17 two-proton emitters, 42 proton emitters, 498 $\alpha$ emitters, and 26 cluster emitters. Among the four considered models, $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}+\mathrm{TabPFN}$ achieves the best overall performance, with $\sigma_{\mathrm{RMS}}=0.423$, corresponding to an improvement of approximately $82.2\%$ over $\mathrm{DGLM}^{b}$. The model parameters are optimized for each decay mode using the least-squares method. After introducing $\mathrm{TabPFN}$, the prediction errors for proton emission and $\alpha$ decay are reduced by approximately $80.6\%$ and $87.6\%$, respectively. For $\alpha$ decay, the training, test, and overall RMSEs are 0.208, 0.305, and 0.240, indicating good generalization capability without evident overfitting. The model also reproduces the systematic evolution of $\alpha$-decay half-lives and the shell-closure effect around $N=126$. These results demonstrate that combining $\mathrm{DGLM}$ with $\mathrm{TabPFN}$ significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of radioactive-decay half-life predictions while retaining the physical interpretability of the original model.

title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding for Nuclear Deformation Landscapes
abstract: Locating the minimum of a nuclear collective landscape can require many interacting many-body calculations. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) searches a parameterized Hamiltonian family with a coherent collective-coordinate register and an on-demand ground-energy threshold oracle. The oracle supplies the predicate required for quantum minimum-finding without first constructing the energy landscape point by point. We implement it for a schematic pairing-plus-multipole model using circuit-generated energy estimates during the search. In a four-point calculation, one Grover round raises the probability of the true minimum from 0.25 to 0.921. A $4\times4$ quadrupole--octupole-field calculation extends the complete circuit to two coordinates, although its minimum is first sampled in a round with zero Grover iterations. Its worst-case branch-preparation fidelity of 0.744 falls below the declared target, identifying coherent ground-state access as the current bottleneck. QDMin inherits expected $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ candidate-query scaling in the unstructured model; total advantage depends on the many-body oracle cost and remains unestablished.

title: Progress in reactor-core fusion technologies presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference 2025
abstract: Abstract This paper provides an overview of the recent progress in reactor-core fusion technologies within the vacuum vessel presented at the 30th International atomic energy agency fusion energy conference held in October 2025 in Chengdu, China, including plasma control, neutronics and nuclear data, tritium technologies, design and development of in-vessel components, related materials and intense neutron sources for material irradiation. Plasma control focusing on achievements for International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) and major fusion research devices are covered and the application of digital twin and Artificial Intelligence are highlighted. Research and Development results from the ITER and current devices to future demonstration fusion power plant reactors are summarized, particularly new findings, data validation, design and analysis tool improvement, properties assessment and technical solutions for critical issues.

title: Nuclei on the Light Front and Electron Scattering
abstract: This paper develops relativistic nuclear structure, motivated by past, current and future experi- ments at Jefferson Lab and the Electron-Ion Collider. Building on existing tools from conventional nuclear physics, we reformulate them in a relativistic, light-front-quantized framework. Our light- front nuclear structure calculations reproduce nuclear binding energies and shell structure well, and incorporate the physics of nucleon-nucleon short-ranged-correlations (SRCs) through similarity renormalization group techniques. Our results are that a purely nucleonic description is insufficient to capture inclusive electron-nucleus scattering data. It does not fully reproduce the plateaus seen at high Bjorken-xB, pointing to the importance of non-nucleonic dynamics responsible for the EMC effect

title: Enhanced structure-dependent alpha decay tunneling in deformed odd-odd nuclei via intense two-color laser pulses
abstract: In the present work, we investigate the effect of ultra-intense laser fields on the $\alpha$ decay tunneling of deformed odd-odd nuclei. Calculations performed within the deformed density-dependent cluster model show that, for deformed odd-odd $\alpha$ emitters, the laser-induced variation in the penetration probability separates into distinct branches associated with different valence particle-hole configurations relative to the $Z=82$ and $N=126$ shell closures. In contrast to the even-even and odd-$A$ cases, the odd-odd parent nucleus most sensitive to the laser field is not the one with the lowest $\alpha$ decay energy. This indicates that the laser response is governed not only by $Q_{\alpha}$ but also by structural correlations associated with the simultaneously unpaired proton and neutron. We further examine the pulse-averaged response under a two-color laser field. The results show that an optimized two-color field enhances the pulse-averaged laser response for most of the studied nuclei, while highly sensitive nuclei exhibit an effective gain equivalent to increasing the laser intensity by more than one order of magnitude. These findings identify structural determinants of laser-assisted $\alpha$ decay in odd-odd nuclei and provide guidance for selecting candidate nuclei and optimizing laser parameters in future experiments.

title: Effects of the $a_0(980)$ Meson on Finite Nuclei in a Parity Doublet Model
abstract: We investigate nuclear structure within the parity doublet model (PDM), with particular emphasis on the role of the isovector-scalar $a_0(980)$ meson. We adopt the models with and without the $a_0$ meson and fit their parameters to nuclear matter saturation and ground state properties of selected nuclei, subject to constraints from the vacuum. The resulting parameter sets reproduce the nuclear matter saturation properties and provide a good description of binding energies and charge radii of selected nuclei. Our fits show that a large value of the chiral invariant mass of nucleon is preferred by the fitting: the best fitted value is $m_0 = 689 \pm 71 $ MeV with $a_0$ and $m_0 = 689 \pm 69 $ MeV without $a_0$. We find that the effects of the $a_0$ meson on the binding energies and charge radii are negligibly small. It is difficult to clarify the effect of $a_0$ meson to neutron skin thickness of Sn, Pb, and Ca isotopes, due to the large uncertainty of the predictions. We note that our prediction of $^{208} \text{Pb}$ is consistent with the measurement by PREX-II collaboration, while that of $^{48} \text{Ca}$ cannot explain the CREX result.

title: Cold Hypersonic Gas Jets for Precision Laser Spectroscopy of Radioactive Molecules
abstract: The sensitivity to possible beyond standard model physics via a study of the nuclear Schiff moment (NSM) has since recently been driving laser spectroscopy of short-lived radioactive molecules. These experiments have in part been hindered by inefficient cooling of the molecular degrees of freedom, resulting in complex, difficult to interpret molecular spectra. Hypersonic (de Laval) nozzles have been shown to provide ideal environments to study cold short-lived actinides by means of in-gas-jet laser ionization spectroscopy. We present here the first application of this technique on molecules using $^{229,230,232}$ThO laser ablation targets. Translational and rotational temperatures were characterized via laser spectroscopy and found to be $12.5(25)\,\mathrm{K}$ and $7.2(6)\,\mathrm{K}$, respectively, along the nozzle-collimated $60\,\mathrm{mm}$-long, $5\,\mathrm{mm}$-diameter gas jet. An upper bound of the vibrational temperature was estimated as no transitions from $v''=1$ were observed. Molecular King-plot analysis shows a large field shift of $-4.0(13)\,\mathrm{cm}^{-1}/\mathrm{fm}^2$, indicating enhanced sensitivity to the differential nuclear charge radii. Relativistic FSCCSD calculations reproduce the measured molecular field-shift factor, providing a benchmark between state-of-the-art molecular and atomic calculations.

title: Short-range correlated pair formation and nuclear shell structure
abstract: Short-range correlated (SRC) nucleon pairs, caused by brief, high-momentum interactions between two nucleons, are dominated by neutron-proton pairs with large relative and smaller center-of-mass momenta. However, which nucleons form pairs is not fully understood. Measurements of 40,48Ca and 54Fe showed that intra-shell pairing was much stronger than inter-shell pairing. We measured high- missing-momentum protons knocked out in electron scattering from selected nuclei with a range of shell configurations, A, and N/Z, including 9Be, 10,11B, 12C, 40,48Ca, 54Fe, and 197Au, focusing on the four light nuclei. Unexpectedly, we found that adding one proton to 9Be (to make 10B) increased the number of correlated protons far more than adding one neutron to 10B or adding one proton to 11B, perhaps due to the large spin (J = 3) of 10B or the unusual structure of 9Be. In addition, the increase in pairing probability from 9Be to 12C and from 40Ca to 54Fe was much steeper than the increase from 9Be to 197Au. This shows the importance of low-momentum nuclear structure on the probability of high-momentum nucleon pairing.

title: Nuclear mass table in deformed relativistic Hartree-Fock Bogoliubov model with localized exchange terms
abstract: Abstract The nuclear landscape is investigated within the localized axially deformed relativistic Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (DRHFB) theory using the density-dependent point-coupling functional PCF-PK1, where the exchange terms are incorporated through the Fierz transformation. The ground-state properties, including deformations, binding energies, drip lines, charge radii, and $\alpha$-decay energies, are analyzed and compared with experiment and other functionals. In the deformed calculations for nuclei with $8 \le Z \le 120$, 7550 nuclei are predicted to be bound, with the root-mean-square (rms) deviation of binding energies 2.882 MeV, which is reduced to 1.721 MeV when the rotational corrections are included. The predicted drip line positions are in better agreement with experiment than the spherical case, and the charge radii are reproduced with an rms deviation of 0.0298 fm for 1010 experimental data. Including deformation reduces the rms deviation of $Q_{\alpha}$ from 1.6263 MeV to 0.7215 MeV, and it becomes 0.7511 MeV when rotational corrections are further included. The removal of the spurious shell closures at $Z=58$ and 92 is examined through the shell gaps. In the superheavy region, the neutron magic numbers $N=162$, 184, and 308 are predicted, while no obvious proton magic number is pronounced. To further improve the mass accuracy, a neural-network approach based on the gated recurrent unit is adopted to correct the mass residuals along isotopic and isotonic chains, reducing the rms deviation of the binding energies to 0.089 MeV.

title: Elastic Scattering Cross Section of 10 B Projectile on Light, Medium and Heavy Targets Using Different Effective Interactions
abstract: The present work is a comprehensive and systematic investigation of the elastic scattering of the weakly bound projectile 10 B from a broad range of light, medium, and heavy target nuclei over several incident energies within the double-folding framework. The real and imaginary components of the nuclear optical potential are constructed using the M3Y, R3Y, and B3Y-Fetal effective nucleon-nucleon interactions combined with nuclear density distributions obtained from the two-parameter Fermi (2pF) and relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. The calculated elastic-scattering angular distributions are compared with available experimental data to assess the predictive capabilities of the different interactions and density parametrizations. The calculated angular distributions generally reproduce the main features of the measured elastic-scattering cross sections, although the quality of agreement varies among the investigated systems and incident energies. Among the interactions considered, the B3Y-Fetal interaction generally provides the best overall agreement with the experimental data with calculations employing RMF densities using the NL2 parameter set, while the phenomenological 2pF densities show comparatively weaker performance in several cases. Based on these findings, empirical relations are proposed to predict suitable N R and N I values for elastic-scattering analyses involving 10 B projectiles. Beyond the description of individual systems, the present study establishes global trends in the optical-model parameters and their dependence on target mass and incident energy, thereby providing a unified framework for understanding the reaction dynamics of the weakly bound nucleus 10 B.
source: International Journal of Modern Physics E
publisher: World Scientific Pub Co Pte Ltd

title: Ab Initio Calculations of $^6$He + $p$ Reactions
abstract: The no-core shell model with continuum (NCSMC) is an ab initio framework for description of nuclear structure and reactions. Recent developments of the NCSMC allow for calculations of charge-exchange and nucleon-transfer reactions. We have applied the NCSMC to calculate cross sections of the ($p,p$), ($p,n$), and ($p,t$) reactions on radioactive $^6$He, using chiral nuclear forces as input.

title: A short-range effective theory for single-neutron halo nuclei with a deformed core
abstract: We establish a short-range effective theory for deformed s-wave halos. The theory applies to a system in which neutrons are weakly bound to a core nucleus, and that core nucleus also exhibits a low-lying rotational band with a $0^+$ ground state and a first $2_1^+$ excited state. The effective theory then must have both halo degrees of freedom and degrees of freedom associated with rotation of the core. This leads to the particle plus rotor model of Bohr and Mottelson at leading order. We identify the relevant leading-order operators in the Hamiltonian that respect the symmetries of the system and the small parameters which define the effective theory's power counting. We carry out calculations for the $^{11}$Be and $^{17}$C systems in which we compute the low-lying positive-parity states of the core $+$ neutron systems up to the core$(2_1^+)$-neutron threshold. We do this for several different regulator parameters and establish that these energies can be renormalized using the leading-order set of operators. The spectrum is accurately described at leading order in both cases. Decay widths to d-wave core-neutron states have sizable cutoff dependence, but the Asymptotic Normalization Coefficients (ANCs) in $s$-wave channels exhibit regulator dependence of a size consistent with next-to-leading-order effects. We also compute Coulomb breakup observables and compare with experimental data, finding leading-order results in reasonable agreement with data for both ${}^{11}$Be and ${}^{17}$C. The addition of one next-to-leading-order operator renders the ANCs of all s-wave states stable with respect to the regulator. It consequently also removes most of the 30\% variation of the leading-order Coulomb dissociation cross section with the regulator.

title: $P$--wave quarkonia in jets at the LHC
abstract: We present the first systematic theoretical study of the production of $P$-wave charmonium states $\chi_{cJ}$ and bottomonium states $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ within jets at the LHC using the fragmenting jet function framework at next-to-leading order in $\alpha_s$. Our calculation resums both collinear DGLAP logarithms and threshold double logarithms in the fragmentation functions and accounts for feeddown contributions from higher quarkonium states. We observe a notable contrast between the charmonium and bottomonium sectors. For $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$, the normalized momentum-fraction distributions exhibit a nearly universal shape, with remarkably weak dependence on the choice of long-distance matrix element sets, the radial excitation ($n=1,2,3$), and the total angular momentum ($J=0,1,2$). We attribute this universality to the overwhelming dominance of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ fragmentation channel, while feeddown contributions from higher bottomonium states remain small. In contrast, the shape of $\chi_{cJ}$ distributions exhibits a stronger dependence on the matrix-element set, reflecting the different relative contributions of the ${}^3S_1^{[8]}$ and ${}^3P_J^{[1]}$ channels. We provide predictions for the $\chi_{cJ}$ and $\chi_{bJ}(nP)$ distributions for the CMS and LHCb kinematic selections across a range of jet transverse momenta. We also compare our predictions with \textsc{Pythia}~8 simulations for selected $P$-wave quarkonium states.

title: Mirror and triplet energy differences in sd -shell nuclei using microscopic interactions with isospin-symmetry breaking effects
abstract: Abstract Starting from an isospin-symmetric microscopic interaction of Shin et al. [Phys. Rev. C 110, 034306 (2024)], we developed two isospin symmetry breaking (ISB) shell-model interactions by adding Coulomb interaction, as well as charge-symmetry breaking (CSB) and charge-independence breaking (CIB) components from the Argonne v18 (Av18) interaction at two different radial cutoffs, rc = 0.55 and 0.70 fm. With additional modifications to the proton single-particle energies, we then employed these interactions to calculate the Coulomb displacement energies (CDEs) and triplet displacement energies (TDEs) of the isobaric multiplet masses for nuclei with |Tz| = 1/2 and T = 1 across the sd-shell to test their validity and applicability, and compared with the USDCm interaction. We found that both ISB interactions show important roles of the CSB and CIB components in the CDEs and TDEs. In addition, we investigated mirror energy differences (MEDs) in the low-energy spectra of nuclei around A = 20, and triplet energy differences (TEDs) in the A = 18 and 22 systems. They are generally well described by the ISB interactions, although some discrepancies remain. Furthermore, the calculated E2 transition strengths obtained with the ISB interactions are shown to be in good agreement with experimental data, indicating small ISB effects in these transitions. Overall, both the ISB interactions provide a consistent and physically motivated framework for describing ISB effects, while the phenomenological USDCm interaction achieves closer agreement with experiment due to a larger number of adjustable parameters.
source: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics

With additional modifications to the proton single-particle energies, we then employed these interactions to calculate the Coulomb displacement energies (CDEs) and triplet displacement energies (TDEs) of the isobaric multiplet masses for nuclei with |Tz| = 1/2 and T = 1 across the sd-shell to test their validity and applicability, and compared with the USDCm interaction. We found that both ISB interactions show important roles of the CSB and CIB components in the CDEs and TDEs. In addition, we investigated mirror energy differences (MEDs) in the low-energy spectra of nuclei around A = 20, and triplet energy differences (TEDs) in the A = 18 and 22 systems. They are generally well described by the ISB interactions, although some discrepancies remain. Furthermore, the calculated E2 transition strengths obtained with the ISB interactions are shown to be in good agreement with experimental data, indicating small ISB effects in these transitions. Overall, both the ISB interactions provide a consistent and physically motivated framework for describing ISB effects, while the phenomenological USDCm interaction achieves closer agreement with experiment due to a larger number of adjustable parameters.
versions.source: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics

title: Collinear Factorization and Evolution
abstract: The method of collinear factorization for high-energy inclusive cross sections has found wide use in the analysis of hadronic collisions. We introduce the form of factorized cross sections, and discuss the roles and definitions of parton distributions, hadronic fragmentation functions, and their evolution, starting with parton model concepts. The Drell-Yan process is used to illustrate the calculation of QCD corrections at next-to-leading order. The special role of deep-inelastic scattering structure functions and their relation to hadronic structure are also briefly discussed. We provide an introduction to all-order arguments for factorization and infrared safety, and close with a brief review of related factorization formalisms.

title: $B(E2)$ Anomaly in Asymmetric Two-Fluid Coupling Systems
abstract: Abstract A theoretical investigation into the potential correlation between the $B(E2)$ anomaly and intrinsic two-fluid characters in nuclear systems has been carried out within the proton-neutron interacting boson model. Our analysis demonstrates that the hallmark signature of this anomaly, the reduced $E2$ transitional ratio $B_{4/2}\equiv B(E2;4_1^+\rightarrow2_1^+)/B(E2;2_1^+\rightarrow0_1^+)<1.0$, can be naturally produced in a weakly coupled two-fluid boson system, wherein the proton and neutron boson subsystems occupy distinct collective configurations. We provide a symmetry-based analytical elucidation of the underlying $B(E2)$ anomaly mechanism and apply this framework to describe the structural evolution across the Os isotopes near $A=170$, thereby offering new insights into the observed $B(E2)$ anomaly phenomena.

title: Glashow-Weinberg relation in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter
abstract: The conservation of the axial-vector currents in nuclear matter with finite isospin asymmetry $\rho_n/\rho_p$ is explored in this paper. In explicit calculations in the in-medium chiral perturbation theory, a charged pion becomes massive in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter. In the presence of the massive charged pion, two components of the axial-vector current are not conserved from the two-loop order when applying the massive in-medium pion state. As a result, the in-medium Glashow-Weinberg relation for the charged pions cannot be derived in isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter from operator relations in quantum chromodynamics.

title: Constraining the resolution length of quark-gluon plasma with new jet substructure measurements
abstract: We show that recent measurements of substructure-dependent jet suppression constrain the value of the resolution length of the droplets of quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed in heavy ion collisions. This resolution length, L res , is defined such that the medium can only resolve partons within a jet shower that are separated by more than L res . We first use calculations done in the hybrid strong/weak coupling model for jet quenching (Hybrid Model) to reproduce ALICE measurements of the scaled soft-drop angle θ g for anti- k t R = 0.2 jets reconstructed from charged-particle tracks. We find that the narrowing of the θ g -distribution in PbPb collisions compared to pp collisions that is seen in the ALICE data rules out a picture of fully coherent energy loss ( L res = ∞ ) where each entire parton shower loses energy to the plasma as if it were a single unresolved colored object. We then use Hybrid Model calculations to reproduce ATLAS measurements of d R 12 , the soft-drop angle obtained by applying the Soft Drop grooming procedure to all charged-particle tracks in R = 1 jets reconstructed from R = 0.2 skinny subjets. Our analysis demonstrates that the ATLAS measurements of R AA for such R = 1 jets as a function of d R 12 are inconsistent with a picture of fully incoherent energy loss ( L res = 0 ) in which every splitting in a parton shower is immediately resolved by the plasma. We find that our Hybrid Model calculations agree best with the ATLAS measurements if QGP has a finite, nonzero, resolution length L res ∼ ( 1 – 2 ) / ( π T ) . For the first time, jet substructure measurements are constraining the resolution length of QGP from below, as well as from above.

title: Systematic Investigation of Fission timescale and Fission Time Distributions Using a Langevin dynamical model
abstract: Fission time scale and associated Fission time distributions (FTDs) provide important information on the dynamical evolution of nuclear fission and the competition between particle evaporation and fission. In the present work, a one-dimensional Langevin dynamical model is employed to investigate the fission time scale and corresponding FTDs of the representative compound nuclei 172 Yb, 213 Fr, and 244 Cm. The resulting FTDs exhibit distinct characteristics in the shapes and widths of the distributions, characterized by extended long-time components that significantly impact the average fission time. Further, to understand the transitional behaviour, 213 Fr is studied in detail over a wide range of excitation energies. The excitation-energy dependence of the FTD and the relationship between the average fission time and the last-neutron evaporation time are analyzed to investigate the competition between neutron evaporation and fission. The results provide insight into the excitation-energy dependence of fission-time distributions and the competition between neutron evaporation and fission within the one-dimensional Langevin framework.
source: International Journal of Modern Physics E
publisher: World Scientific Pub Co Pte Ltd

title: Asymptotic Normalization Coefficient of the 14 O → 13 O + n Configuration from the Peripheral 14 O( d,t ) 13 O Reaction
abstract: The neutron transfer reaction 14 O(d,t) 13 O at a deuteron energy of 34.6 MeV has been analyzed within the Modified Distorted Wave Born Approximation (MDWBA) framework. The angular distribution of the reaction was calculated and compared with the available experimental data to investigate the reaction mechanism and determine the degree of peripheral character at the main angular-distribution maxima. The analysis demonstrates that the reaction is predominantly peripheral in the angular region corresponding to the principal maxima, indicating that the measured cross section is sensitive to the asymptotic part of the 14 O→ 13 O+n overlap function. Exploiting this peripheral behavior, an experimental asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) for the 14 O→ 13 O+n configuration was extracted for the first time. The resulting ANC value is [Formula: see text] =610.91±52.54 fm -1 . This result provides an important experimental constraint on the asymptotic properties of the 14 O ground state overlap and demonstrates the applicability of the MDWBA method for extracting reliable ANC value from peripheral neutron transfer reaction.
source: International Journal of Modern Physics E
publisher: World Scientific Pub Co Pte Ltd

title: Why Stellar Sequences Turn Over: Fixed Points, Instability, and Equation-of-State Universality
abstract: We reformulate the stellar structure equations in the language of dynamical systems and show that the maximum mass of stellar sequences arises from the existence of a fixed point in the relativistic regime. In an appropriate representation of the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, this fixed point becomes manifest and is directly associated with the turnover of the mass-radius curve. The existence of a fixed point implies an effective reduction in dimensionality near the onset of instability, which provides a simple explanation for several equation-of-state-insensitive relations and predicts new ones. In the weakly relativistic limit, we identify a complementary universal structure shared by stellar sequences at their maximum mass, which we term the "compressible limit," and derive distinct universal relations governing the maximum mass in the Newtonian and post-Newtonian regimes. Combining these theoretical results with current astrophysical constraints, we show that the J0740+6620 pulsar is unlikely to lie near the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff maximum mass unless the equation of state exhibits a strong first-order phase transition at densities just above its central density.

title: Theoretical Investigation of Neutron Shell Gap at N = 100
abstract: Experimental pairing gap values deduced from binding energy and energy of the first 2 + state show certain discontinuities in rare-earth nuclei around N = 100. The neutron single-particle levels in even-even Z = 60 – 68 nuclei around N = 100 have been studied using Skyrme Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov method with the Skyrme energy density functional SLy6 as well as with Gogny interaction D1N. We find that both interactions show a deformed shell gap at N = 100. This gap plays an important role in determining r-process abundances.
source: International Journal of Modern Physics E
publisher: World Scientific Pub Co Pte Ltd

title: Structure of QC$_2$D ground state fields at nonzero matter densities
abstract: A quantitative investigation into the modification of ground-state field structures in two-color QCD (QC$_2$D) is presented at finite chemical potential. Using lattice simulations with Wilson gauge and fermion actions, we explore the chromo-electromagnetic field strengths under varying matter densities. To ensure accurate measurements, we develop and calibrate two highly improved topological charge operators and evaluate four gradient flow actions. Our results reveal a finite-volume crossover in the regime of the anticipated phase boundary at $\mu = m_\pi/2$, with both chromoelectric and chromomagnetic field strengths suppressed before recovering and exceeding vacuum values at higher chemical potentials. We find the difference between the squared chromoelectric and chromomagnetic field strengths, $E^2-B^2$, to increase in magnitude monotonically with increasing chemical potential. At $a\mu=0.7$, we find an $11\%$ suppression of $E^2$, a relatively small effect. A systematic analysis using sigmoid fits of lattice simulations in the crossover regime is performed to confirm the critical chemical potential obtained from the field structure is in agreement with the phase boundary at $m_\pi / 2$. These findings provide new insight into non-Abelian ground-state vacuum field structures and offer a foundation for future studies in real QCD.

title: Learning nuclear mass systematics with hybrid quantum-classical mixtures of experts
abstract: We introduce a mixture-of-experts framework combining sixteen hybrid quantum-classical neural networks with nucleus-dependent classical gating to learn residual corrections to the WS4 nuclear mass model. On a fixed AME2020 test set, the framework reduces the root-mean-square error from 456.22 to 179.83 keV and outperforms a parameter-matched classical counterpart. The learned corrections improve shell-gap systematics near the Sn and Pb shell closures, while analysis of the gating networks identifies shell-related descriptors as the leading inputs. For 66Ca, the model predicts Sn = 0.577 MeV and S2n = -0.252 MeV, allowing two-neutron emission while the one-neutron channel remains closed.

title: Configuration-Interaction Studies of Alpha Clustering in Atomic Nuclei
abstract: Clustering in atomic nuclei, and $\alpha$ clustering in particular, is a striking form of self-organization in quantum many-body systems, emerging from nucleon--nucleon interactions through the interplay of correlations, symmetry constraints, and continuum coupling. We summarize a configuration-interaction approach in which cluster degrees of freedom are built from center-of-mass boosted fragment wave functions and treated with resonating-group techniques. The norm kernel plays an important role: Pauli blocking suppresses cluster channels at small separations, restructures the relative-motion wave functions, and governs the normalization of clustering strength. As the central development we present a Green's function (GF) method that aids in resolving a long-standing difficulty of harmonic-oscillator based configuration interaction calculations that stems from wave functions with Gaussian asymptotics. The method restores the correct asymptotic behavior and extracts the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) with high accuracy even in very modest harmonic-oscillator spaces. The value of the ANC is very sensitive to the exact position of the state relative to threshold, and yet the GF method establishes the ANC as a structural observable that can be determined precisely from the interior wave function using the experimentally or otherwise known exact energy. A self-consistent iteration, formulated as an integral-operator eigenvalue problem, is also shown to recover both the energy and the ANC in cases when the energy of the state is to be determined. The method is illustrated for near-threshold states, such as the weakly bound $1^-$ state of $^{16}$O, as well as for the ground states of $^{16}$O and $^{20}$Ne.

title: An Eigenvector-Continued Green's Function Method
abstract: Emulating the Green's function using reduced-order equations is challenging because of the amount of information it contains. This information includes the one-particle spectroscopy over the entire energy spectrum, the one-body density matrix, and the ground-state energy. Nevertheless, the computational speedup offered by emulators is essential for applications requiring repeated model evaluations, which are ubiquitous in many-body physics. These include parameter calibration, uncertainty quantification, phase-diagram mapping, and geometry optimization. In this Letter, we introduce a systematically improvable emulator based on eigenvector continuation and moment-matching. The resulting approximation, which we refer to as an ``eigenvector-continued Green's function,'' can be obtained by solving linear equations, enabling an efficient separation of the computational workload into offline and online stages.

title: Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $\Delta(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.

title: Presynaptic filopodia form kinapses and promote convective membrane flow to sustain synchronous neurotransmitter release
abstract: Synaptic plasticity is the principal mechanism by which neural circuits compute and adapt. Presynaptic plasticity is traditionally regarded as a transient adaptation of the synaptic vesicle fusion and recycling machinery, whereas the role of structural remodeling of synaptic boutons remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate a mechanical coupling between presynaptic structural remodeling and synaptic efficacy. We find that dynamic presynaptic filopodia emerge during active synaptic transmission and deform synaptic boutons while forming transient contacts with postsynaptic structures, which we term neuronal kinapses. Filopodia formation is activity dependent and occurs in intact circuits and human brain. Mechanistically, filopodial growth induces convective in-plane membrane flow toward the filopodium, accelerating release site clearance, a process associated with sustained release probability during repeated synaptic vesicle fusion. As a result, filopodia formation favors an increase in synchronous over asynchronous neurotransmitter release. These results indicate that presynaptic structural remodeling can alter the spatial organization of neurotransmission and, through the membrane flow it generates, modulate its temporal precision.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Particle-Soliton Degeneracy in 2D Quantum Chromodynamics
abstract: Quantum chromodynamics in two spacetime dimensions admits a finite noninvertible symmetry described mathematically by a fusion category. This symmetry is spontaneously broken at long distances, leading to distinct vacua. When the theory has a mass gap, the spectrum is therefore characterized by particle excitations above a single vacuum and soliton sectors interpolating between vacua. We use anyon condensation and the representation theory of fusion categories to obtain exact results about this spectrum, exhibiting the allowed multiplets. Often, particles and solitons are in the same representation and therefore must have equal masses. Furthermore, the fusion category symmetry frequently implies the existence of certain stable states in the spectrum. The resulting degeneracies are encoded in quiver diagrams where nodes are vacua and arrows are excited states.
