title: Erratum: “Hyperons in Neutron Stars across the Observed Mass Range: Insights from Λ N and ΛΛ Interactions within a Microscopic Framework” (2026, ApJ, 997, 26)
abstract: Erratum: “Hyperons in Neutron Stars across the Observed Mass Range: Insights from ΛN and ΛΛ Interactions within a Microscopic Framework” (2026, ApJ, 997, 26), Mohammad Ali Looee, A., Shahrbaf, M., Moshfegh, H. R.

title: Depressed chemical weathering inhibited climate stabilization after the end-Permian biocrisis
abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth’s history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO 2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth’s habitability.
authors: Philip A. E. Pogge von Strandmann
citation_authors: Pogge von Strandmann, Philip A. E.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Typed Transverse Momentum Parton distribution function computations
abstract: A transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution enters an extraction through a specified observation map and a parameter- dependent numerical calculation. Equal units and matching array dimensions do not establish that two implementations represent the same inference problem. We present typed-TMD, a computational framework that makes observation semantics, parameter dependencies, and admissible evaluation plans explicit.

title: Precision Studies of Boosted Polarized Vector Bosons with Energy Correlators
abstract: Boosted, hadronically decaying $W$ and $Z$ bosons are among the most abundant heavy objects at colliders, and their vector nature makes their substructure qualitatively richer than that of a scalar. We initiate precision studies of the hadronic decays of boosted polarized vector bosons with energy correlators. In the narrow-width limit, the laboratory-frame two-point energy correlator is a sum of longitudinal and transverse decay spectra, each weighted by its polarized production rate and obtained by a closed-form boost kernel acting on rest-frame correlators. Combining polarized production density matrices, computed at NNLO in QCD for $pp\to V+X$ and at leading order for $e^+e^-\to W^+W^-$, with decay correlators that combine NNLO fixed order with NNLL collinear and N$^4$LL back-to-back resummation, we find for high-$p_T$ $W/Z$ production that polarization shifts the spectrum by $\mathcal{O}(10\%)$ relative to a naive unpolarized treatment. Even without any reconstruction, hadronic $W/Z$ decays stand out over the realistic QCD background of untagged jet samples as a localized angular bump. Our results open the door to using energy correlators for polarimetry of electroweak bosons through their hadronic decays, for standard-candle measurements of electroweak bosons inside jets, and in sharper searches for new resonances.

title: Nonlinear response and retarded three-point correlators of charge transport
abstract: We study nonlinear response of charge transport in relativistic kinetic theory within the relaxation time approximation. For a classical gas of massless charged particles coupled to an external $U(1)$ gauge field, we organize the Boltzmann equation perturbatively in the source and derive a recursive solution for the distribution function to arbitrary response order. At second order we analytically obtain fully retarded three-point correlators at generic frequencies and momenta, verify the Ward identities implied by charge conservation. We also discuss the general properties of these correlators, including their analytic structure, consistency limits, and relation to Schwinger--Keldysh effective theories of diffusive fluctuations.

title: Irreducible representations of $SU(3)$ for nucleons in a oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$: Application to nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry
abstract: Applying some simple rules, established in group theory literature, generated are codes (easy to modify as required) for obtaining $SU(3)$ irreducible representations (irreps) for a given number of nucleons in a given oscillator shell $\eta$ with $\eta \le 8$. In this approach, first the $SU(3)$ irreps are obtained for spinless fermions in a given $\eta$ shell. Using the codes developed, tables of $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for identical nucleons (protons or neutrons) with a given total spin $S$. Similarly, the $SU(3)$ irreps are generated for nucleons with a given spin-isospin $SU(4)$ irrep. Some applications of these tables for $\eta=4$ shell for $52 \le \mbox{Z,N} \le 78$ nuclei with proxy-$SU(4)$ symmetry are presented. Also, the procedure used for the shell model $SU(3)$ limits is easy to be extended for the $SU(3)$ limit of various interacting boson models and some examples for these are also presented.

title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants
abstract: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are among the primary sites of the rapid neutron-capture (r-)process. In mergers with long-lived remnants, sustained neutrino irradiation raises the electron fraction of the disc wind ejecta, modifying the resulting nucleosynthesis pattern. Yields from numerical-relativity simulations with accurate neutrino transport are needed to quantify the contribution of BNS mergers to the Galactic production of heavy elements and to interpret kilonova spectra. We present and publicly release tracer trajectories and nucleosynthesis yields for eight BNS mergers forming long-lived neutron star remnants, obtained from general-relativistic simulations with M1 neutrino transport, spanning two equations of state (DD2 and SFHo), and a range of total masses and mass ratios. Passive tracer particles following the dynamical and wind ejecta were post-processed with the nuclear reaction network WinNet up to 1 Gyr. The yields and tracer trajectories are available on the MARTINI platform. At 1 day, the production of light and first-peak elements (He, Ni, Sr, and Y) is similar across models and is primarily enhanced by the neutrino-irradiated disc wind. The yields of heavy nuclei vary by more than one order of magnitude, with unequal-mass binaries producing the largest amounts owing to their more neutron-rich ejecta. Our He yields, particularly in the wind, exceed those of recent studies based on an M0 neutrino scheme, consistent with the stronger neutrino irradiation resulting from an M1 scheme. At 1 Gyr, all models reproduce the second and third solar r-process peaks, but differ in the first peak, the lanthanide region, the mass range between the first and second peaks, and the trans-lead region, reflecting the electron fraction distribution of the ejecta and the dynamical and wind contributions. Two equal-mass models provide a close match to the solar pattern.

title: Summary of the theory and modelling contributions at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025)
abstract: Abstract The contributions in magnetic fusion theory presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025) are summarized. This summary provides information on novel ideas and briefly reviews the most recent advances along the main avenues of the research, such as plasma integrated modelling, computational physics and application of artificial intelligence, fast ion instabilities, runaway electrons, disruptions, pellets, and some others. Given the current interest in bringing the magnetic fusion to the burning plasma state, the focus of the theory presentations was on burning plasma physics.

title: Prompt γ -ray production cross sections for neutron-induced reactions on Kr 86
New muon transfer cell for muonic x-ray spectroscopy on microgram-quantity targets based on liquid hydrogen
abstract: The muon transfer method allows access to radioactive/rare atomic nuclei for determining their charge radii via muonic x-ray spectroscopy. In this study we present a new muon transfer cell based on liquid hydrogen optimized for low-energy x-ray spectroscopy by employing a thin-walled Mylar cell for the container of the liquid hydrogen. Based on simulations, the present liquid hydrogen cell achieves competitive efficiencies compared to existing devices using the muon transfer method. Additionally, the liquid-hydrogen-based muon transfer setup provides a short timescale for the diffusion process of the muonic hydrogen atoms in the cell, well below 200~ns.

title: Neutron spectrometry of (p,n) based neutron fields at the University of Helsinki using the NCT-WES single-moderator directional spectrometer
abstract: A tunable-energy neutron beam produced with up to 1 $\mu$A / 10 MeV proton beam on a solid LiF target is available at the Department of Physics of the University of Helsinki for neutron metrology and research applications. This work presents the experimental characterisation of the neutron beams produced at the Helsinki Accelerator Laboratory, and the validation of the \texttt{MCNP6} and \texttt{GEANT4} radiation transport codes for simulating these neutron beams. The neutron spectra produced in the forward direction from 1960, 2040, and 2310 keV protons were measured using the NCT-WES single-moderator directional spectrometer. NCT-WES (Neutron Capture Therapy Wide Energy Spectrometer) is a recently developed single-moderator neutron spectrometer with a sharply directional response, and it is a very convenient instrument to characterise neutron facilities, as it determines the whole spectrum in a single exposure, and has a low sensitivity to room-scattering. The neutron fluence was also determined with the Berthold LB 6411 neutron monitor. The data acquired with NCT-WES were unfolded using the FRUIT unfolding code, starting from guess spectra obtained from \texttt{GEANT4} or \texttt{MCNP6} simulations. The unfolding analysis showed that both transport codes produced plausible spectra, \texttt{MCNP6} being more accurate for the 1960 and 2040 keV irradiations and \texttt{GEANT4} for 2310 keV. The measured values of energy-integrated neutron fluence agree satisfactorily with simulations as well as preliminary measurements with the LB 6411 neutron monitor.

title: Hyperonic equation of state for neutron stars: A systematic Bayesian comparison of density-dependent and nonlinear relativistic mean-field models
End-to-end Particle Reconstruction with Transformers in High-Granularity Calorimeters
abstract: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) will drastically increase the number of simultaneously interacting particles, posing a severe challenge to current particle reconstruction methods. While next-generation highly granular calorimeters offer unprecedented 3D measurement capabilities, reconstructing particles from heavily overlapping energy showers remains computationally difficult. This study investigates how raw detector hits can be accurately reconstructed using end-to-end transformer based methods on a simulated calorimeter dataset. We evaluate and compare three distinct machine learning frameworks, focusing on two generative architectures: diffusion and flow matching as well as query-based set prediction. Our results demonstrate that these advanced methods provide highly effective and scalable alternatives for resolving complex overlapping particle showers in conditions encountered in future calorimeters.

title: Summary of the contributions on magnetic fusion experiments (EX) to the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China
abstract: Abstract This paper summarizes the contributions presented in the ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’ category at the 30th IAEA fusion energy conference 2025, held in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China, from 13–18 October 2025. Conference materials are available at the FEC 2025 conference website ( www.iaea.org/events/fec2025 ), under the category ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’.

title: Radial transport of electric current by electromagnetic microturbulence in tokamaks
abstract: Abstract The turbulent transport of toroidal angular momentum helps determine the rotation profiles of tokamak plasmas, and thereby their confinement and stability. The electron contribution therein has an additional consequence: even a modest electron momentum flux can correspond to a substantial turbulent flux of toroidal current, whose divergence could in principle modify the safety-factor profile. Here, using nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations, we show that electromagnetic fluctuations qualitatively alter turbulent momentum transport. In microtearing-mode-driven turbulence, the total momentum transport is inefficient relative to that of heat, yet an electron contribution associated with the turbulent Maxwell stress dominates the momentum flux. We show that this contribution exceeds an estimated scale required for turbulent current redistribution to compete with the collisional processes maintaining the bootstrap current. In the case of kinetic-ballooning-mode-driven turbulence considered, the momentum transport is found to be stronger and remains dominated by the electrostatic ion contribution; nevertheless, retaining the Maxwell stress is essential for the electron momentum flux to exceed this bootstrap-based reference scale. To enable this study, we independently implemented complete electromagnetic momentum-flux diagnostics in the gyrokinetic codes GENE and CGYRO, and verified them through linear and nonlinear cross-code benchmarks. Taken together, these results suggest that electromagnetic momentum transport may potentially be important for the coupled evolution of the rotation, current, and safety-factor profiles in high-beta tokamak plasmas.

title: Pellet induced transition from low to high confinement in separatrix phase spaces of ASDEX Upgrade
abstract: Abstract The Separatrix Operational Space (SepOS) concept [T. Eich and P. Manz Nucl. Fusion 61, 086017 (2021)] describes the operational space of tokamaks with respect to MHD, density limits and the L-H transition in terms of density and temperature at the separatrix. It has been inspired by the phase space developed by Rogers, Drake, and Zeiler [Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 4396 (1998)] (RDZ). Their idea was contested by pellet-induced L-H transitions [P. Gohil et al. Phys. Rev. Lett. 86, 644 (2001)] evaluated inside the pedestal and subsequently this theory was widely dismissed. Whether the SepOS concept face similar challenges when applied to a pellet-induced L-H transition is studied. On the low-density branch of the L-H transition, the separatrix density is temporarily increased by pellet injection, thereby lowering the L-H power threshold in agreement with the SepOS model. The results will also be discussed in RDZ's phase space. We conclude that the basic idea of the plasma edge phase space proposed by RDZ, more precisely that an increase in plasma beta at low collisionalities has a beneficial effect on confinement and at high collisionalities has a detrimental effect on confinement, was discarded unjustly.

title: Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) at the 2025 IAEA Fusion Energy Conference
abstract: Abstract The paper provides a high-level summary of the contributions given at the 30 th International Atomic Energy Agency Fusion Energy Conference (FEC2025) held in Chengdu, China, from the 13 th to the18 th of October, 2025, under the category ‘Inertial Fusion Energy’.

title: Icosahedral-group beam layouts for highly uniform direct-drive laser fusion
abstract: Abstract We investigate irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser fusion using beam layouts generated from the full rotational icosahedral group. By expanding the incident intensity in spherical harmonics, we show the selection rules imposed by exact icosahedral invariance and identify the forbidden multipole degrees. These exclusions are independent of the single-beam profile and therefore remain valid for both delta-function and finite-width beams. Using flat-top and von Mises–Fisher beam profiles, we evaluate the resulting root-mean-square nonuniformity and compare an optimized 60-beam icosahedral layout with the conventional OMEGA 60-beam geometry. For smooth beam profiles, this model predicts substantially lower nonuniformity for the optimized icosahedral layout than for the OMEGA-60 geometry, because exact low-degree cancellation is combined with efficient high-degree attenuation by the beam-profile transfer coefficients. We further examine random beam-weight imbalance and show that optimized high-beam-count icosahedral layouts remain robust over the range studied. These results establish a symmetry-based design principle for low-mode control and improved irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser implosions.

title: High-Repetition-Rate Laser-Driven Fast Neutron Generation from Planar Liquid Heavy Water Jets
abstract: We demonstrate a high-repetition-rate, directional pitcher-catcher neutron source employing a continuously flowing, ambient-temperature liquid jet pitcher and a beryllium catcher target. Proton or deuteron beams are accelerated at 0.5 Hz from water (H$_{2}$O) or heavy water (D$_{2}$O) sheet jets using the $2\omega$ ALEPH laser at Colorado State University. Deuteron-induced neutron generation shows an average flux enhancement in the target normal direction of 13x compared to proton-induced neutron generation, achieving peak fluxes of $7.9\times10^{5}$ neutrons/sr. The experimentally predicted ion-to-neutron conversion efficiency of 1.5$\times 10^{-5}$ for protons and 1.1$\times 10^{-3}$ for deuterons indicates a significant yield contribution from the deuteron breakup reaction. High shot-to-shot stability neutron spectra up to 8.7~MeV ($^9$Be(d,n)$^{10}$B) are observed for more than 200 consecutive shots.
authors: G. D. Glenn (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
C. B. Curry (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory
D. P. DePonte (SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory

title: Comments on $\bf{\eta'}$ nuclei and on the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton
abstract: I briefly discuss two apparent puzzles: (i) is the observation of $\eta'$(958) bound states in $^{11}$C at GSI [1] compatible with a nearly vanishing real part of $\eta'N$ scattering length [2]? and (ii) is the $\Lambda$ binding energy of the hypertriton (${{_\Lambda}^3}$H), the lightest particle-stable hypernucleus, very small (63$^{+38}_{-31}$ keV, J-PARC E73 [3]) or very large (523$\pm$76 keV, MAMI [4])? Here, I suggest that MAMI's observed weak-decay pion momentum peak originates from ${{_\Lambda}^7}$He, not from ${{_\Lambda}^3}$H \cite{Gal26}.

title: Axisymmetric perturbations and vertical displacement oscillatory modes driven by fast ions in tokamak plasmas
abstract: Abstract Recent progress on the theory and numerical simulations of vertical displacement oscillatory modes (VDOM) in tokamak plasmas is reported. VDOM are driven unstable by energetic particles and can have an impact on plasma disruptions, plasma edge stability and confinement. These modes are a candidate, together with Global Alfvén Eigenmodes (GAE), to explain Alfvén-frequency n = 0 modes driven by fusion alpha particles recently observed on JET (Oliver et al 2026 Phys. Rev. Lett. 136 055101). Differences in the physical mechanisms underlying VDOM and GAE are discussed. An analytic dispersion relation that contains both VDOM and ideal-MHD unstable vertical displacements (VDs) is derived. Limits on plasma elongation for stable plasma operation against ideal-MHD VDs are discussed. While VDOM are generally immune against continuum damping, if the wall is brought very close to the plasma boundary and the plasma density remains relatively large up to the last-closed-flux-surface (as in the case of H-mode discharges), the VDOM oscillation frequency may interact with the Alfvén continuum spectrum, giving rise to continuum damping. Specific types of fast ion distribution functions that can provide an instability drive for n = 0 modes are considered. Numerical simulations of n = 0 modes obtained with the NIMROD code are shown, including a preliminary assessment of the fast ion instability drive for these modes.

title: Application of low- Z materials for enhancing H-mode plasma performance and pulse duration in EAST with full metal wall
abstract: Abstract Wall conditioning plays a key role in controlling impurity accumulation and fuel recycling for achieving long pulse, high-performance plasmas in fusion device. In this work, the effects of real-time wall conditioning using low- Z materials—boron (B) and lithium (Li) powders injection—are systematically investigated and compared in the EAST tokamak equipped with a full-metal wall. Continuous boron injection effectively suppresses high- Z impurity accumulation and maintains a low effective charge ( Z eff ), reducing the core W 44+ density peak by up to ∼40%, and enabling reproducible 105 s H-mode discharges. Lithium injection also significantly improves impurity and fuel recycling control, supporting a record-breaking 1066 s H-mode plasma under lithium coating. A rigorous statistical comparison via multivariate linear regression within a shared operational window reveals that real-time lithium conditioning delivers an approximate 26% enhancement in the confinement factor H 98 compared to the real-time boron conditioning baseline, while maintaining an equivalent core Z eff . This plasma improvement is accompanied by an order-of-magnitude reduction in lower divertor neutral pressure P low,div and suppressed edge D α emissions. Analysis of the plasma profile confirms that real-time Li injection enhances wall pumping to reduce edge density, which steepens the local density gradient within the narrow pedestal region. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of low- Z material-based wall conditioning in improving plasma confinement and extending discharge duration, offering important implications for ITER and future fusion devices.

title: A simple model for evaporation-driven migration of liquid metal between plasma pulses in a fusion reactor with liquid metal plasma-facing components
abstract: Abstract Liquid metal plasma-facing components are being considered for a variety of fusion power plant designs, and careful control of the liquid metal inventory will be essential in these systems to mitigate challenges with liquid metal corrosion and hydrogen fuel retention. Since many power plant designs and existing test facilities rely on pulsed plasma sources, it is critical to understand how liquid metal evaporation leads to material migration within a reactor over the periods of time when no plasma is present. This work addresses this question by developing a simple particle balance model to efficiently calculate liquid metal vapor transport patterns over indefinitely long time periods, using a particle redistribution matrix to capture the vapor transport details. After developing the mathematical model, characteristics of a future Liquid Metal Core-Edge (LMCE) research facility with liquid lithium divertors are used as a reference to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used. Examples of lithium migration during the cooldown period between plasma pulses show that the pattern of lithium deposition depends primarily on the system geometry. An important secondary effect in these scenarios is the relative cooldown rate of the lithium divertor with respect to other PFCs in the device. Examples are also provided to demonstrate how the particle balance model can be used to optimize the design of a cold finger to collect liquid metal condensation for extraction and reprocessing, with the results showing that a future LMCE facility may be capable of collecting all of the lithium evaporated between plasma pulses if the main chamber walls can be maintained above 350 C during operation.

title: A dynamical implementation of colour coherence for quenched jets in JEWEL
abstract: Colour coherence affects the radiation pattern of hard partons both in vacuum and in a dense coloured background formed in heavy ion collisions. In vacuum evolution it leads to the well-known phenomenon of angular ordering, and in heavy ion collisions the appearance of a medium resolution scale strongly affects the way in which a fragmenting hard parton interacts with the background medium. In this paper I present the implementation of colour coherence in the JEWEL event generator for jet evolution in a dense medium. In each interaction between a hard parton and the medium it is checked whether the momentum transfer of the scattering is sufficient to resolve the colour dipole. In this way it is dynamically decided which structures stay coherent. Importantly, scatterings that resolve an individual parton disrupt the colour coherence, which affects the next splitting via the loss of angular ordering. This leads to a suppression of hard radiation, and consequently a reduction in overall scattering rate, which is the dominant source of effects of colour coherence observable in reconstructed jets. I discuss these modifications using the examples of nuclear modification factor, jet fragmentation function and jet-hadron correlations.

title: Toward measuring the low-energy cosmic-ray spectrum with next-generation neutrino detectors
abstract: We investigate the capabilities of upcoming kiloton-scale neutrino detectors, such as Hyper-Kamiokande, in determining the primary cosmic-ray spectrum. These detectors provide full-sky coverage and long-term monitoring, unlike traditional satellite and balloon experiments that measure cosmic-ray flux at specific altitudes and locations. By analyzing the atmospheric neutrino flux generated by cosmic-ray interactions, we demonstrate that future detectors can differentiate between various cosmic-ray models with high statistical significance, even when accounting for uncertainties in neutrino cross sections and hadronic interactions. We introduce a technique for reconstructing the primary cosmic-ray spectrum using neutrino measurements, which reduces the flux uncertainty from approximately 20% to about 7%. We then show that Hyper-K has the potential to increase sensitivity to neutrino oscillation parameters, such as sin 2 θ 23 , by a factor of 2. Our results highlight the complementary role of neutrino detectors in cosmic-ray physics and their critical importance for precision measurements in particle astrophysics.

title: Performance Benchmarks for 2-View and 3-View Fiber-Projection Fine-Grained Particle Detectors
abstract: Fine-grained scintillator detectors are critical for precision measurements in nuclear and particle physics, where accurate reconstruction of interaction vertices and secondary particle directions enables separation of signal from background events. A well-known design choice is the fiber readout geometry: traditional 2-View systems use orthogonal X and Y fibers, while next-generation 3-View designs add a third Z-fiber layer that provides unambiguous 3D voxel identification. The 2-View approach suffers from combinatorial ''ghost hits'', which are false 3D candidates arising from fiber projection ambiguities, that degrade reconstruction performance in high-multiplicity events. This paper presents comprehensive simulation benchmarks quantifying the performance difference between 2-View and 3-View geometries across key metrics. We find that the 3-View geometry reduces ghost hits by 30 to 90% depending on event topology, provides robust vertex resolution across complex topologies, and maintains superior angular resolution for shower direction reconstruction. These benchmarks inform the design optimization of future detectors and provide quantitative guidance for reconstruction algorithm development across a broad range of experiments including neutrino physics, rare kaon/pion decays, and collider calorimetry.

title: Long-term scintillation light performance, calibrations, and triggering efficiency in the MicroBooNE detector
abstract: A detailed understanding of scintillation light in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs) is essential for the robust extraction of physics measurements from their data. This article presents the long-term performance of scintillation light production and detection using five years of data from the MicroBooNE LArTPC neutrino detector. We describe the MicroBooNE light simulation and light-based triggering schemes, and present the photomultiplier tube gain calibration and stability, light response stability, and light-based systematic uncertainties over the course of five years of data collection. We also make an in-situ measurement of the scintillation light triggering efficiency down to 30 MeV of visible energy. Finally, we discuss two notable observations in MicroBooNE's data, both reported here for the first time: an approximately 50\% decline in MicroBooNE's light yield over time, concentrated in the first two years of running; and a higher than expected O(200 kHz) rate of single photoelectrons (SPE). We present the first measurements of the dependence of the SPE rate on the TPC electric field strength and polarity. Together, the results presented in this article provide an important benchmark for the long-term performance of scintillation light systems in LArTPCs and their use in particle physics measurements.

title: Extending the limits of rotationally resolved mid-IR spectroscopy: an accurate model of trioxane derived from combining Fourier transform and sub-Doppler measurements
abstract: 1,3,5-Trioxane, a polyoxymethylene (POM) molecule relevant to prebiotic chemistry and astrophysics, exhibits a dense rovibrational spectrum that challenges high-resolution spectroscopic characterization. Here, we report an extensive study of its $\nu$ 5 CO symmetric stretching mode (960-1000 cm -1 ) by combining broadband high-resolution FTIR spectroscopy (0.001 cm -1 resolution, >2000 transitions) with SI-traceable sub-Doppler saturated absorption measurements using frequency-stabilized CO 2 lasers and a frequency-comb-referenced quantum cascade laser. The latter achieve lineposition uncertainties as low as 40 kHz, revealing inaccuracies in the FTIR frequency scale. A frequency-scale correction is determined by maximizing the global consistency of the complete spectroscopic data set. A global least-squares Hamiltonian fit combining the calibrated FTIR data, the SI-traceable sub-Doppler measurements and previously reported millimeter-wave rotational transitions yields a refined spectroscopic model. The resulting analysis significantly improves the precision of the rotational, quartic, and sextic constants for both the ground and $\nu$ 5 excited vibrational states. This work extends mid-infrared frequency metrology to the largest molecule studied to date (12 atoms), providing a dense set of reference transitions for frequency calibration around 970 cm -1 . The resulting spectroscopic parameters reach relative uncertainties as low as 3.7 x 10 -10 for the band origin, making them valuable for molecular databases used in astrophysics and atmospheric physics, as well as for precision measurements in fundamental physics. Additionally, the observed line shapes indicate the absence of significant intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution (IVR) within the investigated energy range, while a few discrepancies in the Hamiltonian fit suggest the onset of weak perturbations, demonstrating the sensitivity of the present approach to probe subtle intramolecular couplings in complex polyatomic spectra. Q P (31,10) 28 967 426 394.

title: Converting a superseded Raith electron beam pattern generator into an unattended Critical Dimension SEM
abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. This is shown for a Raith eLine Plus, and is expected to be applicable to other pattern generators running Raith's NanoSuite. Presented are results demonstrating its three use cases within a facility: accelerated calibration of two photoresists' process windows; chip-scale metrology of integrated photonic devices to track CD variation; and mass dataset acquisition for convolutional neural network training to predict process distortion. This methodology enables foundry-style, metrology-driven process calibration in academic cleanrooms, generalisable beyond photonics to any EBL nanofabrication that requires nanometre-scale CD control.

title: Absolute calibration of scintillators for laser-driven ion spectroscopy using in situ CR-39 sampling detectors
abstract: Quantitative studies of laser-driven ion acceleration and laser-induced nuclear fusion require accurate measurements of ion yields and energy spectra. Although scintillator screens integrated with Thomson parabola spectrometers provide real-time diagnostics, their nonlinear scintillation response requires absolute calibration. We present an in situ, single-shot cross-calibration method using a 2-mm-period CR-39 sampling mask to simultaneously record particle counts and scintillation signals from laser-accelerated proton beams. The method is applied to calibrate a 400-$\mu$m-thick CsI:Tl crystal and a 6-$\mu$m-thick P43 phosphor screen over a broad proton energy range. The measured scintillation responses are compared with a theoretical model combining Birks' law and simulated proton stopping powers. The calibration quantitatively reveals the distinct response characteristics of the two scintillators, including thickness-dependent punch-through effects and constraints on ionization quenching, and demonstrates a practical approach for the absolute calibration of scintillator screens used in laser-driven ion spectroscopy.

title: Numerical quality factor statistics for superconducting rf cavities with spatially inhomogeneous multilayer coatings modeled by Gaussian random fields
abstract: Bulk niobium has long been the material of choice for superconducting radio-frequency applications. An alternative approach is the superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) multilayer structure, which enables the use of brittle high- T c materials, such as NbTiN. At present, SIS coatings are limited to flat samples, with the single-cell TESLA cavity representing a key milestone. Extending coating processes to nonflat geometries is expected to introduce macroscopic inhomogeneities in coating thickness. We model these variations using Gaussian random fields parameterized by a spatial correlation length and generated by solving a stochastic partial differential equation. The resulting field is incorporated into the boundary condition of the cavity eigenvalue problem, from which quantities of interest—such as the quality factor—are computed. This procedure is repeated for eight correlation lengths, with 2048 samples per correlation length, where the resulting quality factors are recorded. Our results show that the quality factors follow a normal distribution. The standard deviation increases with the correlation length and can be statistically distinguished. In contrast, the mean values remain largely unchanged, with only a few significant differences. In extreme cases, depending on the correlation length, the quality factor may differ from the uniform case by 2%–6%.
