title: Global $\beta$-decay half-life predictions in a quasiparticle random-phase approximation based on relativistic Hartree-Fock Bogoliubov model with localized exchange terms
abstract: Abstract We present systematic calculations of nuclear $\beta^-$-decay half-lives for 5456 nuclei with $8\leq Z\leq120$, covering even-even, odd-$A$, and odd-odd ones, within the self-consistent proton-neutron quasiparticle random-phase approximation (pnQRPA) based on localized relativistic Hartree-Fock-Bogoliubov (RHFB) theory with the PCF-PK1 interaction. The Fierz transformation is employed to localize the exchange terms, ensuring a self-consistent treatment of the nuclear ground state and the particle-hole residual interaction for the calculation of excited states, while the isoscalar tensor coupling yields a relatively large Landau effective mass of $M_L^*=0.85M$. Spherical and allowed Gamow-Teller approximations are adopted, and the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing strength is determined as an isospin-dependent function of $N-Z$ by fitting experimental half-lives. The calculated half-lives reproduce the experimental systematics reasonably well, with about 80\% of the nuclei lying within one order of magnitude of the experimental data. The deviation decreases systematically toward shorter-lived nuclei, reaching standard deviation $\sigma=0.329$ for $T_{1/2}^{\rm Exp.}<0.1$ s, comparable to the corresponding RHB+pnQRPA calculations with D3C$^*$ and FRDM+QRPA results. Pronounced deviations are found around shell closures and in deformed regions, highlighting the importance of correlations beyond QRPA level, deformation effects and the first-forbidden transitions. Finally, the gated recurrent unit network, with PCF-PK1 results as inputs, reduces the overall standard deviation to 0.171 orders of magnitude for 690 nuclei whose experimental and calculated half-lives are both shorter than $10^{6}$ s, corresponding to a 83.6\% reduction relative to PCF-PK1 results.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF 2
abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: A Martian meteorite that formed ≳4.1 billion years ago samples Mars’ early crust and mantle
abstract: Martian meteorites provide a record of the planet’s geological history. However, most are geologically young samples that are not representative of Mars’ surface, which is dominated by ancient rocks. We describe the Martian meteorite Teghaza 001 (Teg 001), a slowly cooled igneous rock that formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. Its composition, mineralogy, and texture are distinct from other Martian meteorites. We determine that Teg 001 is a sample of ancient crust, which formed from a geochemically distinct mantle source with primordial composition. The presence of aqueously altered minerals, combined with bulk and mineral-specific oxygen isotope measurements, indicate that Teg 001 experienced reactions with fluids enriched in 18 O, before ejection into space by an impact.
publisher: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)

title: Effect of quark-hadron phase transitions on the neutron star mass distribution
abstract: The neutron star (NS) mass distribution serves as a crucial probe of the dense matter equation of state (EOS) and core-collapse supernova explosion mechanisms. Although observations reveal a bimodal NS mass distribution, existing theoretical simulations often struggle to naturally reproduce the high-mass peak, and the impact of the quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in high-density nuclear matter remains largely unexplored. Employing the 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamics code GR1D with hybrid EOSs incorporating a first-order PT (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2), we systematically simulate core-collapse supernovae for progenitors with zero-age main-sequence masses ranging from 13 to 120 $M_\odot$. Our results reveal a threefold impact of the PT onset density on the final supernova fate: in low-compactness progenitors, an early PT truncates accretion and produces less massive NSs; in the critical-compactness regime, it facilitates successful explosions; and in high-compactness progenitors, it accelerates black hole formation. Compared with the $\sim 1.4\,M_\odot$ peak typical of the conventional core-collapse scenario, the inclusion of the PT produces NSs with masses centered around $1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.1 and within $1.55$--$1.70\,M_\odot$ for RDF1.2. Furthermore, we identify a novel formation channel whereby low-compactness progenitors with failed initial shocks can form more massive NSs via a PT-induced second shock. Due to the fixed nature of the PT boundary, the final NS masses exhibit a pronounced clustering effect. This study elucidates the critical role of the quark-hadron PT in shaping the NS mass distribution, providing important astrophysical constraints on the properties of high-density nuclear matter and the formation mechanism of massive NSs.

title: Large scale shell model calculations for the shape coexistence at N = 40 and N = 50 island of inversion
abstract: Abstract Shape coexistence---the competition between near-degenerate spherical and deformed configurations---emerges as a pervasive feature of neutron-rich nuclei in and around the islands of inversion. Using a large-scale shell model (LSSM) with a realistic effective interaction, we systematically compute low-lying spectra, average orbital occupations, and particle--hole (p--h) excitation probabilities to investigate the candidate shape-coexistence states for even--even \(N=40\) and \(N=50\) isotones. Where data exist, our LSSM reproduces the observed systematics, including the benchmark \(E(2_1^+)\) in \(^{78}\)Ni and the characteristic shape-coexisting structure near \(^{68}\)Ni. Along the \(N=40\) chain, \(E(0_2^+)\) closely tracks \(E(2_1^+)\) with a minimum at \(^{64}\)Cr, signaling maximal collectivity. Along the \(N=50\) chain, both \(E(2_1^+)\) and \(E(0_2^+)\) follow a parabolic evolution from \(^{78}\)Ni to \(^{70}\)Ca with a common minimum at \(^{74}\)Cr; microscopically, the \(0_2^+\) states are predominantly \(2p\!-\!2h\) (with modest \(3p\!-\!3h/4p\!-\!4h\) admixtures), while \(^{74}\)Cr is a controlled exception exhibiting comparable \(0p\!-\!0h\) and \(2p\!-\!2h\) components. Extending the survey to neutron-rich Ti, Cr, and Fe isotopes, the LSSM captures the pronounced variation of \(E(0_2^+)\)---peaking at \(^{62}\)Ti and reaching minima at \(N=50\) (\(^{74}\)Cr, \(^{76}\)Fe), suggesting a widespread shape coexistence and its evolution in these regions.

title: Temperature dependence of the nucleon–nucleon inelastic cross section in an isospin-asymmetric nuclear medium
abstract: Abstract The nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) inelastic cross section plays an important role in constraining the nuclear equation of state at high baryon densities and in transport descriptions of heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the temperature dependence of $\Delta^{++}$ and $\Delta^{-}$ production cross sections in isospin-symmetric and asymmetric nuclear matter is investigated within the relativistic Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck (RBUU) framework. Two relativistic mean-field parameterizations are employed: the density-dependent parameterization (called DD-ME$\delta$) and the nonlinear-dependent parameterization (called OMEG). The cross sections generally decrease with increasing density, whereas their thermal enhancement becomes more pronounced. The two parameterizations predict comparable temperature effects at densities up to approximately $1.5\rho_0$, while OMEG exhibits a stronger temperature dependence at higher densities. In isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter, the cross section splitting results from the interplay between the effective mass splitting and vector self-energies and therefore depends on the mean-field parameterization. The temperature dependence of the splitting is relatively weak for $nn\rightarrow p\Delta^{-}$ but more pronounced for $pp\rightarrow n\Delta^{++}$. These findings provide quantitative information on the temperature dependence of the in-medium $NN\rightarrow N\Delta$ process and may be useful for future transport-model implementations.

versions.title: Temperature dependence of the nucleon–nucleon inelastic cross section in an isospin-asymmetric nuclear medium
versions.abstract: Abstract The nucleon-nucleon ($NN$) inelastic cross section plays an important role in constraining the nuclear equation of state at high baryon densities and in transport descriptions of heavy-ion collisions. In this work, the temperature dependence of $\Delta^{++}$ and $\Delta^{-}$ production cross sections in isospin-symmetric and asymmetric nuclear matter is investigated within the relativistic Boltzmann-Uehling-Uhlenbeck (RBUU) framework. Two relativistic mean-field parameterizations are employed: the density-dependent parameterization (called DD-ME$\delta$) and the nonlinear-dependent parameterization (called OMEG). The cross sections generally decrease with increasing density, whereas their thermal enhancement becomes more pronounced. The two parameterizations predict comparable temperature effects at densities up to approximately $1.5\rho_0$, while OMEG exhibits a stronger temperature dependence at higher densities. In isospin-asymmetric nuclear matter, the cross section splitting results from the interplay between the effective mass splitting and vector self-energies and therefore depends on the mean-field parameterization. The temperature dependence of the splitting is relatively weak for $nn\rightarrow p\Delta^{-}$ but more pronounced for $pp\rightarrow n\Delta^{++}$. These findings provide quantitative information on the temperature dependence of the in-medium $NN\rightarrow N\Delta$ process and may be useful for future transport-model implementations.

title: Prominence as a discriminator of gravitational wave signals
abstract: The concept of is familiar to signal engineers, topographers and mountaineers. We introduce Prominence P as a discriminator of gravitational wave (GW) signals. We treat black hole and neutron star binaries as astrophysical background sources, and show how P can be used to distinguish between GW spectra produced by first-order phase transitions, domain walls and cosmic strings, and combinations thereof. Prominence can also be used to discriminate between these and off-piste sources of GWs. The uncertainty in the measured energy density in GWs at pulsar timing arrays needs to be at the subpercent to percent level for P to achieve discrimination at 3 σ . LISA and ET data are expected to have sufficiently small uncertainties that Prominence can play a central role in their analysis. We define and apply a χ 2 statistic based on an inner product in signal space to show that sources indistinguishable at 2 σ using the signal-to-noise ratio can be distinguished using P with significances above and in some cases far above 3 σ .

title: Spectral Study of the Outburst Decay of the Accreting Millisecond X-Ray Pulsar SRGA J144459.2-604207
abstract: Abstract We study the spectra of the accreting X-ray millisecond pulsar SRGA J144459.2-604207 during the 2024 outburst using the Neutron star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER) and Swift observations. The spectra during the outburst decay, reflares, and quiescent state are explored using the absorbed Comptonized model. We find that the spectra during the quiescent state can also be explained using the absorbed power-law and absorbed blackbody model. The spectral evolution of the source is explored as the outburst decays into quiescence. We study the long-term quiescent X-ray activity of the source spanning roughly 45 yr and find that the long-term quiescent luminosity may be explained using the deep crustal heating model. We also find that the coronal activity of the companion star alone cannot power the quiescent X-ray luminosity of the source. We place the source on the radio-X-ray luminosity plane and compare its position with other sources. We estimate the propeller luminosity of the source and find that it is smaller than the estimated luminosity during reflares and the quiescent state during the 2024 outburst. Several reflares are detected during the outburst decay, one of which is near-simultaneous with the detection of an ultrafast outflow and radio emission. We explore plausible mechanisms that may power outflow, radio emission, and associated jet formation in this accreting binary.

title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
abstract: Abstract We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657−0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657−0406A is in a long-period ( P b ∼ 37 days) and eccentric ( e ∼ 0.12) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance ω ̇ = 0.00090 ( 13 ) deg yr −1 , which implies a total system mass of 2.5(6) M ⊙ by assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

title: Transition from Te-ITB sustainment with saturated m / n =1/1 activity to q =3/2 rational-surface-mediated collapse in EAST
abstract: Abstract A collapse of an electron internal transport barrier (Te-ITB) followed by a major disruption, is observed in electron-heating-dominant H-mode plasmas with a core- peaked Te profile on EAST tokamak. Before the collapse, the Te-ITB coexists stably with a long-lived saturated m / n = 1/1 mode, where m and n denote the poloidal and toroidal mode numbers, respectively. During this phase, the dominant electron- temperature information-transfer pathway identified by the transfer entropy (TE) analysis remains in the core region, consistent with barrier sustainment. In the pre-collapse phase, nonlinear coupling among core m/n = 1/1 modes, secondary destabilization of the saturated m / n = 1/1 mode and enhanced core impurity radiation are observed. The dominant TE response then shifts toward the q = 3/2 rational surface, while the inward-directed coupling is weakened. Although an m / n = 2/1 mode already exists before the collapse, it remains relatively passive until the heat perturbation propagates outward. The m / n = 3/2 mode emerges closest in time to the Te-ITB collapse and may participate in the final barrier degradation, which is followed by rapid outward thermal-perturbation propagation, fast-electron redistribution, enhanced impurity radiation, and finally a major disruption. These observations suggest that Te-ITB collapse is associated with the reorganization of electron-temperature information- transfer pathways and local rational-surface coupling, rather than with static magnetic- island topology alone.

title: CarMa0NL modelling of COMPASS halo currents
abstract: Abstract A vertical displacement event in the COMPASS tokamak is modelled using the CarMa0NL code, with the halo-current width treated as a free parameter. The simulations that best reproduce the experimental evolution are those in which the resulting safety factor at the last closed flux surface remains above unity. This result is consistent with the possibility that the interaction of the \(m/n=1/1\) mode with higher harmonics, and the associated formation of a stochastic magnetic field-line structure, may contribute to setting the halo-current width. The potential relevance of this observation to scrape-off-layer widening and divertor heat-load mitigation during normal operation is discussed.

title: Laboratory constraints on peV-scale mass splitting between ordinary and sterile neutron states
abstract: Sterile states of matter, represented by a parallel “mirror” sector, may contribute to the observed dark matter in the Universe. We investigated the parameter space of neutron ( n ) to mirror-neutron ( n ′ ) oscillations, in the case where the two states are not necessarily mass degenerate, taking into account interactions in the mirror sector. By tuning the magnitude of an applied magnetic field in the range 5 μ T < B < 360 μ T to corresponding resonance conditions for finite mass splitting, we derive exclusion limits for the n − n ′ oscillation time constant reaching about 20 s over the mass-difference range 0.3 − 22 p eV . In parts of this parameter range, our limits exceed the model-dependent neutron-star-cooling bound, providing the first experimental constraints in this scenario that are more stringent than this astrophysical estimate.

title: Influence of Δ resonances in hyperonic neutron stars on gravitational-wave inspiral signatures
Pulsar glitches due to triggered vortex traps
abstract: Abstract Pulsar glitches are thought to originate when angular momentum is transferred to the crust of the neutron star from the superfluid enclosed within, mediated by vortex avalanches. This idea has been qualitatively validated in the existing literature by simulating a star with a small number (∼103) of superfluid vortices, subject to deceleration and uniform pinning. Here, we employ the Barnes-Hut approximation to simulate up to 105 vortices in a reasonable time. Using the new setup, we probe glitches that originate in the presence of inhomogeneous pinning. The inner crust of a neutron star is expected to crack as the star spins down, relieving stresses and resulting in rearrangements within the crustal lattice. These regions become centres for pinning with large pinning energies. Many such vortex traps are expected to exist in mature pulsars like Vela. We simulate one such star and find that the rise of the glitch is now staggered, a clear signature of the trap network. In young to middle-aged stars like PSR J0537-6910, we expect quakes which result in new traps and also unpin the vortices in existing ones. We observe that such a configuration involving the simultaneous release of several traps could introduce a bimodality in the glitch-size distribution, a feature that has previously been reported for PSR J0537-6910. Our simulations also indicate that macroscopic inhomogeneities in the distribution of vortices could spontaneously develop in a star with uniform pinning sites.

title: Four-derivative corrections to the neutral-scalar Christodoulou threshold in charged de Sitter black holes
abstract: Abstract We study leading parity-even four-derivative corrections to the linear Christodoulou regularity criterion for a neutral, massless, minimally coupled spectator scalar in four-dimensional charged de Sitter black holes. We derive the corrected static solution, cold extremality relation, near-horizon geometry, Cauchy-horizon surface gravity, and neutral scalar quasinormal spectrum within Einstein-Maxwell effective theory. Near cold extremality, the scalar equation reduces analytically to the finite-temperature anti-de Sitter two-dimensional throat problem. We find that the dominant nonstationary spherically symmetric mode retains its cold-limit regularity ratio through first order, while higher angular sectors respond to the deformation of the relative throat radii. The finite-distance neutral-scalar Christodoulou boundary nevertheless shifts because the relevant exterior scalar spectrum and the unequal horizon surface gravities enter the regularity ratio. At smaller and intermediate cosmological scales, positive effective coefficients move the Christodoulou threshold to larger normalized separation of the Cauchy and event horizons. Toward the larger cosmological-scale part of the cold branch, the same coefficient directions move that threshold back toward the cold endpoint. The reversal accompanies a transition in the quasinormal family that supplies the spectral gap. We further show that the coefficient combination governing the fixed-charge extremal mass parameter differs generically from those governing the cold throat and the finite-distance neutral-scalar boundary. Extremality therefore does not determine a universal direction for the neutral-scalar Christodoulou-threshold correction. Our results identify cosmological scale and spectral-family competition as essential elements in relating effective gravity, black-hole extremality, and Cauchy-horizon regularity in this spectator sector.

title: Exhibiting Singularity-Free Ultra-Compact Stellar Models in Teleparallel \(f(\mathfrak{T})\) Gravity Under the MIT Bag \(EoS\)
abstract: Abstract In this paper, a relativistic model of anisotropic strange quark stars in the context of teleparallel $f(\mathfrak{T})$ gravity is presented, considering the fluid distribution in the interior of the star to be anisotropic. The analysis starts with the modified gravitational field equations in the light of a linear $f(\mathfrak{T})$ model in the context of static spherically symmetric spacetime geometry. Physically viable solutions are obtained by making use of the interior configuration modeled with the MIT bag model equation of state and the Finch--Skea spacetime ansatz, to get a self-consistent stellar solution. The exterior Schwarzschild spacetime is smoothly matched with the interior geometry at the stellar boundary, thus the model parameters can be determined by means of the continuity conditions. The obtained solution is further explored by different thermodynamic, energy and stability criteria on physical viability. It is applied to observational relevance, for compact stars SAX~J1808.4$-$3658 and 4U~1608$-$52. The derived solutions show that under appropriate parameter choices of the $f(\mathfrak{T})$ model, the proposed strange quark star configuration may be realized with higher value of the mass and compactness, which may have implications in the astrophysics in the context of modified teleparallel gravity. \textbf{\color{blue}The results indicate that \(f(\mathfrak{T})\) gravity can provide an effective description equivalent to General Relativity, accompanied by a modified coupling and a constant geometric contribution, thereby offering a possible framework for exploring the behavior of highly compact strange quark stars.}

title: Effective distance-duality deformations as a diagnostic oflate-time calibration tensions
abstract: Abstract The Hubble tension between the SH0ES-calibrated luminosity-distance scale and the CMB/BAO-inferred expansion history can be recast as an effective violation of the distance-duality relation (DDR), $\eta(z)\equiv D_L(z)/[(1+z)^2D_A(z)]$. Using the Fisher-bias formalism, we explore how an overall distance recalibration and a broad redshift variation can accommodate different cosmological responses. These diagnostic profiles guide a compact model of the distance deformation. We adopt a three-parameter tanh parameterization and perform full MCMC sampling with Planck, DESI-DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ with SH0ES, and cosmic chronometers. The tanh and constant-DDR models give $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm tanh/\Lambda CDM}=-35.1$ and $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm const/\Lambda CDM}=-31.5$, respectively; the additional redshift-dependent contribution is therefore $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm tanh/const}=-3.6$. Redshift dependence is marginally preferred ($\sim1.4\sigma$), while neither the Bayesian evidence nor the deviance information criterion provides meaningful support for the extension. We thus find no significant evidence for redshift-dependent DDR violation, while the dominant constant offset remains degenerate with a recalibration of the supernova absolute magnitude $M_B$ in the absence of an external calibration. The combined analysis returns $H_0=68.44\pm0.30$\,km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$ and $\Omega_m=0.301\pm0.004$. Finally, at the background level, the adopted SN-sector deformation is strongly degenerate with the specific evolving-dark-energy model considered here.

title: Re4: Scientific computing agent with rewriting, resolution, review and revision
abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are a promising class of generative artificial intelligence models and have demonstrated abilities to perform complex tasks in multiple domains, including mathematical and scientific reasoning. In this work, we construct a novel agent framework for solving representative problems in scientific computing. The proposed agent, incorporating a "rewriting-resolution-review-revision" logical chain via three reasoning LLMs (functioning as the Consultant, Reviewer, and Programmer, respectively), is integrated in a collaborative and interactive manner. The Consultant module endows the agent with knowledge transfer capabilities to link problems to professional domain insights, thereby rewriting problem descriptions through text augmentation. The Programmer module is responsible for generating and executing well-structured code to deliver the problem resolution. The Reviewer module equips the agent with the capacity for self-debugging and self-refinement through interactive feedback with code runtime outputs. By leveraging the end-to-end review mechanism, the executable code provided by the Programmer undergoes iterative revision. A comprehensive evaluation is conducted on the performance of the proposed agent framework in solving typical partial differential equations (PDEs), engineering-oriented flow past a cylinder, ill-conditioned linear systems, and data-driven physical analysis problems. Compared with a single-model approach, this collaborative framework significantly improves the bug-free code generation rate and reduces the occurrence of non-physical solutions, thereby establishing a highly reliable framework for autonomous code generation based on natural language descriptions. The review mechanism improved the average execution success (bug-free code and non-NaN solutions) rate of the modern reasoning model DeepSeek R1 from 59% to 82%, while ChatGPT 4.1-mini improved from 66% to 87% and Gemini-2.5 improved from 60% to 84%. Automatic code generation and review provide a promising workflow for scientific computing; analysis of solver-development trajectories further reveals recurring implementation difficulties in boundary treatment, array indexing, and the preservation of numerical constraints.

title: Cyclotron radiation signal characterization in resonant cavities for the Project 8 neutrino mass experiment
abstract: Many experimental methods in physics require understanding radiation from single particles into non-trivial electromagnetic mode structures. Such characterization is critical for Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy (CRES), an advancing new measurement technique that has the potential to greatly benefit fundamental physics measurements. In CRES, charged particles emit cyclotron radiation at frequencies that provide their energy measurement. As a notable example, the Project 8 experiment aims to kinematically infer the neutrino mass by measuring the energies of electrons emitted in tritium beta decay using CRES. In near-term realizations of Project 8, resonant cylindrical cavities will be used for CRES readout, in a configuration with a magnetic field oriented along the symmetry axis, and electrons following helical cyclotron trajectories confined to the cavity interior. The physics of electromagnetic radiation in these environments is complicated, since it involves both the motion of the emitting particle and the mode structure imposed by the cavity. In this work, we derive and validate an analytic model for how an oscillating, trapped electron radiates into cavity modes, and the power and frequency content of the radiation that can be read out from these events. These results can be used to guide the design of cavities for future CRES and other experiments.

title: r -process nuclei in the rare-earth region above N = 126 in relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory: A preponderance of shape coexistence in nuclei
abstract: The shell structure of nuclei beyond N=126 relevant to the third peak at A ~ 195 in r-process nuclear abundances in investigated. Within the framework of the relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in deformed space, a comparative study of the response of nuclei with three different model Lagrangians NL-SV1, SVI-2 and NL3 is made. Ground-state properties of even-even nuclei in the isotopic chains of Z=58-72 in the highly neutron-rich region are investigated. A comparison of binding energies with mass formulas shows that in the extreme region of the r-process path, the RMF model SVI-2 without nonlinearities of sigma and omega mesons shows an excellent agreement with the mass formula HFB-24. It is shown that in all the above Lagrangian models, in the neutron rich region between the shell closures N=126 and N=184, there is a preponderance of nuclides exhibiting coexistence of well-deformed prolate and oblate shapes in the ground state. A prolate ground state is shown to evolve smoothly to a coexisting oblate ground state via a near degeneracy with successive addition of neutrons. Induced by an onset of deformation for $N \ge 130$, nuclei approaching the r-process path are shown to exhibit enhanced stability in many isotopic chains (Z > 60). This has the effect of shifting the expected neutron drip line significantly farther into the neutron-rich region especially for the higher Z chains. Consequences of the enhanced stability, the shape co-existence and degeneracy of shapes in nuclei on the r-process nucleosynthesis are discussed.

title: Physics-guided residual correction of α -decay half-lives based on the effective liquid drop model
abstract: To improve the prediction accuracy of $α$-decay half-lives in heavy and superheavy nuclei, a physics-guided residual-correction framework combining the effective liquid drop model (ELDM) with machine-learning methods is proposed. The ELDM is first used as the macroscopic baseline for describing the barrier-penetration process, and XGBoost and TabPFN models are then employed to learn the residual deviations between ELDM predictions and experimental data. To incorporate microscopic nuclear-structure information, several physically motivated descriptors are constructed, including deformation-related quantities, Geiger--Nuttall-related features, and minimum orbital angular momentum. The results show that machine-learning residual correction significantly improves the predictive performance of the ELDM baseline. Among all models, TabPFN-term3 achieves the best accuracy, reducing the RMSE and MAE to 0.348 and 0.248, corresponding to improvements of 38.60\% and 40.46\%, respectively. Residual-distribution and feature-ablation analyses further indicate that the corrected predictions are closer to experimental values and that physically motivated descriptors play an important role in learning nonlinear residual structures. Overall, the proposed ELDM-based residual-correction framework can effectively compensate for missing microscopic nuclear-structure effects while preserving physical interpretability, providing a feasible strategy for high-precision $α$-decay half-life prediction.

title: Design studies of a pulsed quasimonoenergetic 2-keV neutron source for calibration of low threshold dark matter detectors
abstract: We describe design studies for a pulsed quasi-monoenergetic 2-keV neutron source for calibration of sub-keV nuclear recoils. Such a calibration is required for detectors sensitive to sub- GeV dark matter and also the coherent elastic scattering of reactor neutrinos. In our design, neutrons from a commercial deuterium-tritium generator are moderated to the keV scale and subsequently filtered to achieve a monoenergetic spectrum utilizing the antiresonance feature, characterized by a drop in neutron transmission spectra at 2-keV for scandium. The analyses and conclusions presented are primarily based on simulations, as this study represents a critical first step toward the final goal. We address challenges such as unmoderated high-energy neutrons and gamma backgrounds from neutron capture in the moderator materials. Through optimization of the moderator+filter and shielding geometry, we identify a configuration that achieves the target neutron flux at 2 keV while maintaining subdominant rates of background interactions in simulation. Lastly, we outline a future pathway to lower-energy (few eV scale) calibrations using time-of-flight and sub-keV neutrons

versions.abstract: We describe design studies for a pulsed quasi-monoenergetic 2-keV neutron source for calibration of sub-keV nuclear recoils. Such a calibration is required for detectors sensitive to sub- GeV dark matter and also the coherent elastic scattering of reactor neutrinos. In our design, neutrons from a commercial deuterium-tritium generator are moderated to the keV scale and subsequently filtered to achieve a monoenergetic spectrum utilizing the antiresonance feature, characterized by a drop in neutron transmission spectra at 2-keV for scandium. The analyses and conclusions presented are primarily based on simulations, as this study represents a critical first step toward the final goal. We address challenges such as unmoderated high-energy neutrons and gamma backgrounds from neutron capture in the moderator materials. Through optimization of the moderator+filter and shielding geometry, we identify a configuration that achieves the target neutron flux at 2 keV while maintaining subdominant rates of background interactions in simulation. Lastly, we outline a future pathway to lower-energy (few eV scale) calibrations using time-of-flight and sub-keV neutrons

title: Coulomb and nuclear polarization of the nucleon density in the dinuclear configuration of the Ca 40 + Pb 208 system
abstract: The change of the nucleon density distribution of a heavy nucleus caused by the presence of a second nucleus at a fixed center-to-center distance is studied in the framework of the deformed Woods–Saxon mean field. The single-particle problem of one nucleus has been solved by diagonalization in a cylindrical harmonic-oscillator basis with the external field of the partner nucleus included in the Hamiltonian before diagonalization. The external field consists of the Coulomb potential of the partner charge distribution and of the nuclear part obtained by double folding of the Migdal density-dependent effective nucleon-nucleon interaction, in the same form as used in the dinuclear system approach. The induced density change δ ρ ( r ; R ) and the corresponding changes of the quadrupole moment, of the mean-square radius and of the interaction energy have been calculated for the Ca 40 + Pb 208 system at separations R = 15.5 – 20 fm. The results are compared with the first-order (linear-response) treatment of the same external field. Because the mean field is anchored at the origin, the multipole moments are shown to require a translationally invariant definition: a displaced but undeformed distribution acquires a quadrupole moment second order in the displacement, and in this problem that kinematic term is comparable with the induced moment itself. Once it is removed, the intrinsic quadrupole response of Pb 208 agrees with the first-order one to better than half a percent, and remains so over the full range of the switching parameter for the Coulomb field at R = 20 fm, while that of Ca 40 retains a genuine higher-order contribution of 12% to 16 % . The polarization of both partners is dominated by the repulsive Coulomb tidal field, which produces an oblate deformation of the density, while the attractive nuclear field acts in the opposite sense and partially cancels the Coulomb contribution at the smallest separations. At the larger separations the induced octupole deformation is close to 40 % of the quadrupole one for Pb 208 and to 50 % for Ca 40 , and it is the more sensitive indicator of the breakdown of the one-center picture. The polarization energy is a dipole quantity, the induced quadrupole deformation contributing only a few percent of it; it is verified by coupling-constant integration and is quoted under several correction prescriptions for the spurious translational component and for the absence of the residual interaction. The sensitivity to the geometry of the folding densities and the limits of validity of the one-center description are established quantitatively.

title: Runaway electron induced explosions of graphite; modeling versus controlled DIII-D experiments
abstract: Abstract The state-of-the-art concerning the modeling of the thermomechanical response of graphite to runaway electron (RE) impact is based on one-way coupled linear thermoelasticity combined with Rankine’s strength-based failure criterion and limited to the onset of material failure. Here, the predictive capabilities are extended to the nonlinear damage phase characterized by material fragmentation and debris expulsion. This is achieved by introducing plasticity via the Johnson–Holmquist constitutive model, adopting an effective plastic strain-based failure criterion and coupling finite element analysis with smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. The extended thermomechanical model is successfully benchmarked against the results of two controlled RE-induced damage experiments recently carried out in DIII-D. This constitutes an important step towards the final objective of quantitatively describing the thermomechanical response of tungsten to REs.

title: Probing neutron skin through event-by-event pion asymmetry in heavy-ion collisions
abstract: In this work, we propose a novel approach for probing the neutron skin thickness of gold (Au) by analyzing the event-by-event distribution of $π^{-}$ and $π^{+}$ yield differences. This is achieved through SMASH simulations of ultra-peripheral Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=3$ GeV. Our results demonstrate that the mean value of $Δn_π = n_{π^{-}} - n_{π^{+}}$, along with the Pearson correlation and mutual information between $(π^{-}+π^{+})$ and $(π^{-}-π^{+})$, all scale linearly with the neutron skin thickness. Moreover, the slope of the line connecting two distinct $Δn_π$ values in the event-by-event distribution also exhibits a linear dependence on the neutron skin thickness. The most sensitive $Δn_π$ pairs are identified as $(-1, 1)$, $(-1, 2)$, $(0, 1)$, and $(0, 2)$. These findings establish a new pathway for determining the neutron skin thickness. Finally, by comparing SMASH and UrQMD simulations under identical initial conditions, we observe that individual slope values depend on the specific collision model. However, by extracting slopes from multiple $Δn_π$ pairs in experimental event-by-event data and inferring the corresponding neutron skin thickness, one can assess which model better aligns with the true physical value.

title: Investigation of transfer coupling strength in the N 14 + Hf 178 reaction
abstract: Disentangling the effects of nucleon transfer via Q value and deformation on fusion has been a longstanding objective. To address this, a comparative analysis of the barrier distribution, which is an alternative probe to fusion, for the N 14 + Hf 178 and O 16 + Hf 178 systems have been performed. The consistent alteration in deformation by choosing the same target Hf 178 mitigates its influence, thereby allowing for an explicit investigation of the effect of the Q value of nucleon transfer for these above systems. Consequently, the quasielastic scattering was measured for N 14 + Hf 178 at backward angles. The extracted excitation function and barrier distribution were analyzed in light of coupled-channel calculations, which indicated a significant contribution from the one- and two-neutron transfer channels, alongside the rotational degrees of freedom in the highly deformed Hf 178 nucleus. Furthermore, the coupling strength was extracted using the chi-square minimization method, yielding a value ≈ 0.201 . The extracted coupling strength of N 14 + Hf 178 system was compared with that of the two-neutron transfer in the O 16 + Hf 178 system, which indicates that the coupling strength for nucleon transfer decreases with an increase in the Q value. This observed behavior might be due to the spectroscopic structures of the O 16 and N 14 . The present study indicates that the spectroscopic properties play a significant role, along with Q values, in influencing the fusion reaction dynamics.

title: ISINN32: Saw-Tooth Mass Dependence of Fission-Fragment Angular Momenta in the Spontaneous Fission of \(^{252}\)Cf
abstract: Abstract The mass dependence of fission-fragment angular momenta is investigatedfor the spontaneous fission of $^{252}\mathrm{Cf}$ within thedinuclear-system (DNS) model. After penetration of the fission barrier,the system evolves through an ensemble of touching fragment configurationsin mass, charge, and deformation space, while the collective angular motionis treated quantum mechanically. The calculated fragment angular momenta reproduce well the experimentally observed mass-dependent trends and the pronounced minimum near $A\simeq132$. Thesaw-tooth structure persists after averaging over all charge partitionscontributing to a given fragment mass, demonstrating that it is a robustproperty of the scission ensemble rather than a consequence of theparticular isotope sequence selected experimentally. The results emphasizethe central role of shell-dependent fragment deformation in the generationof fission-fragment angular momentum. The same scission ensemble also reproduces the observed anticorrelation between the total kinetic energy (TKE) and the total prompt-neutron multiplicity, further supporting the calculated scission configurations.

title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei
abstract: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.

title: Nuclear Data Evaluation Utilizing Bayesian Monte Carlo Methods
abstract: While the body of experimental nuclear data continues to grow at a rapid pace, significant gaps persist. The lack of evaluated experimental data is far more pronounced in charged-particle reactions which are essential to a large portion of the isotope production community for vital medical, industrial, and national security interests. In the absence of experimental and evaluated data, isotope production relies on theoretical models that may result in low yield and isotopic impurities. This work investigates model and parameter adjustments in TALYS 2.0 to establish uncertainty bands on proton-induced cross sections, highlight influential parameters in calculations, and constrain adjustments within physically defensible bounds. The EXFOR dataset for proton-induced reactions on natural copper, comprised of 24 independent cross sections, was used for iterative Bayesian model updating. Upon convergence, parameters and their uncertainties were compared against 23 cumulative cross sections from EXFOR, highlighting the limitations of generalization. Various machine learning models were leveraged to predict TALYS performance, with a small neural network showing useful ranking capabilities across several generations, suggesting the use of a surrogate approach to screening for future evaluations.

title: Discovery of Kolmogorov-like Turbulence in the Inner Shell of the Supernova Remnant HB 9
abstract: Abstract We investigated the scaling relation of the magnetohydrodynamic turbulence in the inner and outer shells of the supernova remnant HB 9 using multitracers. For the eastern inner shell section, 1D structure function and power spectrum analyses of the radio total intensity, H α emission, and polarized intensity consistently show a Kolmogorov-like scaling l 2/3 over the inertial range. The 2D power spectrum for the entire inner region follows k −8/3 of all tracers, including the polarization gradient ∇ P . It indicates that fully developed, trans-Alfvénic Kolmogorov turbulence is present in the inner shell of HB 9. We estimated the strength of the random magnetic field therein from the low fractional polarization (∼5%) and obtained an upper limit of δB ∼ 18 μ G. The turbulence in the inner shock shell is most likely driven by the Richtmyer–Meshkov instability.

title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}\Sigma_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.

title: Optimization of 99mTc proton-induced production by means of cross-section measurements of technetium radioisotopes from molybdenum targets
abstract: $^{99m}$Tc [t$_{1/2}$=6.0072 h, IT: 99.9963%, E_${\gamma}$=140.51 keV (89%)] is the most widely used radionuclide for SPECT imaging. It is mainly obtained from $^{99}$Mo/$^{99m}$Tc generators, with $^{99}$Mo [t$_{1/2}$=65.924 h, $\beta^{-}$:100%] produced by fission of $^{235}$U in nuclear reactors. The aging of reactors dedicated to $^{99}$Mo production and increasingly frequent maintenance shutdowns highlight the need for alternative production routes. Among accelerator-based approaches, direct production of $^{99m}$Tc from enriched $^{100}$Mo targets using low-energy proton beams is particularly promising. Within a collaboration between the Laboratory for High Energy Physics (LHEP) of the University of Bern and the Department of Nuclear and High Energy Physics of Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv, we investigated $^{99m}$Tc production with medical cyclotrons. Cross sections of proton-induced reactions on solid molybdenum targets were measured to characterise the Tc radionuclides produced during irradiation and optimise production conditions. Based on these data, a proton energy of approximately 16 MeV and a highly enriched $^{100}$Mo target of about 0.5 mm thickness were identified as suitable conditions. For a 10 h irradiation, these parameters provide a calculated $^{99m}$Tc yield of approximately 1.7 GBq/$\mu$A while maintaining radionuclidic purity within European Pharmacopoeia limits. Production tests were subsequently performed to validate the measurements and demonstrate the feasibility of this production route.

title: Inverse-mapped density-dependent relativistic mean-field inference of the neutron-star equation of state with terrestrial nuclear, NICER, and gravitational-wave constraints
abstract: Abstract We perform a Bayesian inference of the cold dense-matter equation of state within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field (DD-RMF) model. The density-dependent couplings are reconstructed through an inverse mapping from a 12-dimensional set of nuclear-matter and high-density shape parameters. Two independent offsets, $\Delta d_\sigma$ and $\Delta d_\omega$, decouple the scalar and vector Typel--Wolter shift parameters from the isovector channel and provide a flexible isoscalar evolution at suprasaturation density. Thermodynamic consistency, beta stability, nonnegative core pressure, and the causal sound-speed condition are imposed on every accepted EOS.We analyze four likelihood combinations built from NICER mass--radius data, GW170817 tidal information, and heavy-ion collision flow constraints on the pressure of symmetric nuclear matter: NS-only, NS+HIC, NS+GW170817, and NS+HIC+GW170817. In the GW-conditioned comparison, the NS+HIC+GW170817 posterior gives $R_{1.4}=11.91^{+0.35}_{-0.35}~\mathrm{km}$, $R_{2.0}=11.40^{+0.42}_{-0.49}~\mathrm{km}$, and $M_{\max}=2.131^{+0.079}_{-0.068}\,M_\odot$ at 68\% credibility. Relative to the corresponding neutron-star baseline, HIC information narrows the high-density isoscalar sector, favors correlated scalar and vector density dependences, and reduces the high-mass stellar radius. The central microscopic response is therefore not only a narrowing of the pressure band, but a selection of the scalar-attraction and vector-repulsion balance that generates the pressure of symmetric matter. Evidence and sensitivity tests are used as diagnostics within the adopted likelihood construction: the results show a moderate dependence on the HIC uncertainty width, while using a fixed reference saturation density in the HIC likelihood leaves the conclusions essentially unchanged. These intervals should be read as conditional results within the adopted 12-parameter inverse-mapped DD-RMF family rather than as model-independent measurements.

title: Extracting the QCD speed of sound in the presence of quantum fluctuations
abstract: The equation of state of strongly interacting matter plays a %is one of the central quantities characterizing central role in characterizing quark--gluon plasma created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. It has recently been recognized that the QCD speed of sound is responsible for the linear correlations between the mean transverse momentum and charged-particle multiplicity in ultra-central collisions. In realistic collisions, however, this thermodynamic correlation is inevitably biased by quantum-initiated event-by-event fluctuations. In this work, we present a novel statistical framework to correct this bias by leveraging the Gaussianity condition of the quantum fluctuations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this approach can also serve as a probe of thermalization. Validated by the event-by-event hydrodynamic simulations, the extracted speed of sound in our framework is successfully consistent with the predictions from lattice QCD, from large to small collision systems.

title: Three-dimensional spatial modeling of nuclear de-excitation lines
abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are commonly thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants. Observations of ionization rates in the interstellar medium (ISM) have indicated an excess of low-energy CRs (LECRs) beyond that expected from standard propagation models. The LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV γ-ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can provide direct constraints on the LECR flux, its morphology, and its acceleration mechanisms. We aim to construct all-sky maps of de-excitation γ-ray emission from the Milky Way based on 3D CR distribution models. By comparing the predicted de-excitation line emission with the Galactic diffuse continuum, we assess the detectability of these lines. We calculated the de-excitation emission by combining 3D CR distributions obtained with the CR propagation code GALPROP and γ-ray production cross sections calculated with the state-of-the-art nuclear reaction code TALYS. Beyond the standard Galactic CR component, we constructed models including an additional LECR component motivated by the high ionization rates measured in the ISM. The predicted de-excitation emission is relatively weak when integrated over the broad regions commonly adopted in MeV γ-ray analyses (|l|łeq30^̧irc and |b|łeq15^̧irc), contributing only łesssim 1% above the leptonic continuum, even when considering the additional LECR component. The all-sky maps revealed that in the standard scenario, the de-excitation-to-leptonic flux ratio remains low over the entire sky, reaching at most ∼20% toward the Galactic anticenter. In contrast, models including an additional LECR component exhibited a pronounced enhancement toward the GC, where the ratio exceeds 100%, indicating favorable prospects for detection through spatially resolved analyses. We also find that the 6.1-to-4.4 MeV intensity ratio is particularly sensitive to the maximum energy of the injected LECR spectrum, varying by up to ∼ 30%. Our results demonstrate that the next generation of MeV observatories can already establish the presence of a distinct LECR component and constrain its origin, acceleration mechanism, and transport in the Galaxy.

title: Systematic calculations of \beta-delayed fission probabilities using a microscopic framework
abstract: The process of $\beta$-delayed fission ($\beta$DF) consists of a mother nucleus $\beta$-decaying to different states of a daughter isotope, followed by fission of the latter with a probability that strongly depends on the energy of the states populated in the $\beta$ decay. Studying this process experimentally can be challenging due to the typically small $\beta$DF probabilities. The theoretical framework presented in this work was developed to globally characterise $\beta$DF probabilities. This approach uses energy density functional based models to obtain the necessary inputs for the final probabilities, which are obtained through the nuclear reaction code TALYS. Calculations were performed for all isotopes with an experimentally measured value of $\beta$DF probabilities. Following the optimisation of the theoretical framework to better reproduce known data, a global RMS deviation of about two orders of magnitude was achieved, an accuracy that can be used to identify promising cases for future experimental $\beta$DF studies.

title: Probing massive star formation with intrinsic multiplicity constraints from TESS eclipsing binaries
abstract: Massive stars play a central role in stellar and galactic evolution as progenitors of supernovae, neutron stars, black holes, and gravitational wave sources. Despite their importance, the dominant formation mechanisms of massive binaries remain poorly constrained observationally. Our aim was to use a large homogeneous sample of eclipsing binaries to observationally constrain binary formation across a wide range of primary masses and to test predictions from various formation scenarios. We combined photometric time series data from TESS with distance measurements from DR3 and near-infrared photometry from 2MASS to analyze an all-sky sample of eclipsing binaries. By accounting for observational and geometric selection effects, we derived bias-corrected estimates of the binary fractions and orbital parameter distributions across different mass bins. Gaia We derived bias-corrected binary fractions and bias-corrected distributions of the orbital period and the radius-to-separation ratio for systems spanning primary masses from 1.1 M_⊙ to 47 M_⊙. For primary masses up to ∼5 M_⊙, the observed distributions show close agreement with theoretical predictions for systems formed via disk fragmentation followed by migration. At higher masses, we observed an apparent deficit of very short period systems relative to theoretical expectations, although this regime is also expected to be affected by incompleteness. Overall, the observed properties exhibit a gradual transition across the full range of primary masses. Within the orbital period range accessible to our sample, the results do not require a sharp transition in binary properties between F- and O-type stars. The observed continuity is consistent with disk fragmentation followed by migration acting across a broad range of stellar masses, although the present data do not uniquely require this formation pathway, and alternative channels may also contribute.

title: Identifying Kilonovae in the Presence of Optical Afterglow for the Wide Field Survey Telescope
abstract: Abstract Identifying kilonovae associated with binary neutron star mergers is often complicated by the presence of a dominant synchrotron afterglow. In this work, we evaluate the performance of the Wide Field Survey Telescope (WFST) in identifying kilonova signals in composite afterglow-kilonova transients. Using a numerical framework based on the Fisher information matrix, we simulate 10,000 realizations for each of two scenarios: an AT2017gfo-based template model and a physically sampled population that accounts for kilonova diversity. Our results indicate that kilonova identification is primarily limited by source distance. In both scenarios, the identification efficiency is largely insensitive to variations in afterglow microphysical parameters and exceeds 80% at distances within approximately 600 Mpc for AT2017gfo-like events. Under our adopted assumptions and a short gamma-ray burst (sGRB)-triggered target-of-opportunity (ToO) observational strategy, we estimate that the WFST could identify 0.1–1.2 kilonovae per year in the optimistic scenario. Furthermore, we find that the discriminating power of color-based filters rapidly saturates, reaching a stable plateau by the second night after the merger. We therefore propose a staged observing strategy that prioritizes high-cadence g - and r -band monitoring during the first night and incorporates the z band from the second night onward. This strategy improves the identification precision by exploiting the increasingly prominent red excess produced by the kilonova. Our results provide a physical basis for optimizing WFST observing resources to efficiently detect and characterize kilonovae in the multimessenger era.

title: Bayesian inference of the dense matter equation of state built upon extended Skyrme interactions: A generalization
abstract: The nonrelativistic theory of nuclear matter (NM) based on Brussels-Skyrme interactions is employed to develop models for dense and neutron-rich matter within a Bayesian framework. We employ the following set of constraints: the four best-known nuclear empirical parameters, the density dependence of the energy per particle in pure neutron matter (PNM), the density dependence of the Landau effective mass ($m_\mathrm{eff}$) of neutrons in PNM and symmetric NM, and a lower limit on the maximum gravitational mass that neutron stars (NSs) can support. In addition, a number of ``sanity checks'' are added: the values of the speed of sound, neutron and proton Landau effective masses, and Fermi velocities are constrained up to the central density of the most massive NS configuration and for isospin asymmetries $\delta=(n_n-n_p)/(n_n+n_p)$ ranging from 0 to 1. Our ensemble of models \emph{fully} explores the capacity of nonrelativistic Brussels-Skyrme effective interactions to describe NM at densities exceeding several times the nuclear saturation density. This is a necessary step toward a better understanding of the properties of dense matter and possible correlations between the parameters of NSs and the parameters of NM. Due to the pronounced U-shaped density dependencies of $m_\mathrm{eff}$, which qualitatively agree with the predictions of ab initio calculations featuring three-body forces, all our models exhibit a non-monotonic ``rise-and-fall'' behavior of the thermal pressure ($p_\mathrm{th}$) as a function of density, which in extreme cases leads to $p_\mathrm{th} < 0$. This work is a generalization of [Beznogov and Raduta, Phys. Rev. C 110, 035805 (2024)].
