title: Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement of the S 1 0 ↔ P 3 2 Transition and a Multitransition King-Plot Consistency Test
abstract: We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the ${^{1}S}_{0}\ensuremath{\leftrightarrow}{^{3}P}_{2}$ clock transition in neutral ytterbium (Yb) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at 905.4(2) nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than 100 Hz. The interleaved clock operation between isotopes allows us to determine isotope shifts of four bosonic isotope pairs at Hz-level uncertainties, which is combined with those of other four ultranarrow transitions in Yb and ${\mathrm{Yb}}^{+}$ to construct the King plot. We show that a rich dataset spanning multiple transitions enables a test of a restricted isotope-shift ansatz comprising the leading mass and field shifts, one effective factorized higher-order standard model contribution, and a new-particle contribution. Within this ansatz, the five-transition data are inconsistent with the new-particle contribution serving as the sole additional contribution over the mass ranges ${m}_{\ensuremath{\phi}}\ensuremath{\le}6.5\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{keV}$ and $18\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{keV}\ensuremath{\le}{m}_{\ensuremath{\phi}}<100\text{ }\text{ }\mathrm{keV}$, while the previous works rely on another bound set by the neutron scattering and $(g\ensuremath{-}2{)}_{e}$ measurements. This Letter paves the way for the effective use of precision isotope shift data in the King plot analysis and stimulates further measurements in Yb and other elements.

title: Analysis of CONUS+ run 2: Detector performance, background model and CE$\nu$NS measurement
abstract:
Coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CE$
u$NS) provides a uniquely sensitive probe of neutrino properties, but its detection requires pushing energy thresholds to the sub-keV scale while controlling backgrounds. The CONUS+ experiment, located at the Leibstadt nuclear power plant, reported the first observation of CE$
u$NS using reactor antineutrinos in 2025. Following a detector upgrade that replaced three of the original 1 kg high-purity germanium detectors with larger 2.42 kg diodes, this paper presents the analysis of the CONUS+ run 2 dataset, including the detector characterization, the background model, the signal prediction and expected sensitivity, and the extraction of the CE$
u$NS signal. The new detectors reach a background level per unit mass reduced by approximately a factor of two relative to the original detectors, while reaching energy thresholds between 140 and 170 eV$_{ee}$. With an exposure of 1296 kg$\cdot$days reactor-on and 86 kg$\cdot$days reactor-off, a blind likelihood analysis fitting directly the number of signal counts yields $N_s = 1555 \pm 152$ CE$
u$NS events, corresponding to a significance of 10.2$\,\sigma$. The result is in agreement with the Standard Model expectation of $1701 \pm 198$ events, with $N_s/N_{\mathrm{SM}} = 0.91 \pm 0.14$.

title: Physics-induced impact on the properties of Kepler /K2 solar analogs in light of PLATO requirements
abstract: Context. Solar analogs are stars whose fundamental properties closely match those of the Sun and, as such, they serve as useful laboratories for tests of stellar structure and evolution, particularly in the context of the upcoming PLATO mission. Aims. Our study is focussed on six seismic solar analogs observed by Kepler and K2, which have been characterised in detail in a former analysis. We investigate the impact of the model physical ingredients on these six targets to evaluate how well we can satisfy the PLATO precision requirements for stellar parameters with the data quality that is currently available. Methods. We used the stellar mass, age, and chemical composition obtained with the Forward and Inverse COmbination (FICO) procedure, based on OPAL opacities and a combination of NACRE II and Solar Fusion II (SFII) nuclear reaction rates, as our reference values. The efficiency of macroscopic transport was calibrated on lithium abundances derived from the analysis of HERMES spectra. Next, we carried out extensive tests of the physical ingredients with the help of a Levenberg-Marquardt local minimisation method, using both classical (luminosity, mean density, metallicity, and effective temperature) and seismic constraints (frequency separation ratios). In particular, we investigated the impact induced by the use of OPLIB opacities and SFIII nuclear reaction rates on the stellar fundamental properties, as well as the use of various seismic constraints. Results. We quantified the potential differences that changes in the modelling input physics might lead to and compared their extent with the requirements expected for the PLATO mission (15% in mass, 2% in radius, and 10% in age), providing crucial constraints on the accuracy and robustness with respect to systematics of the determination of fundamental properties for PLATO. For our sample of solar analogs, we were able to accurately retrieve the stellar masses within 2.5%. As for the stellar ages, we quantified the systematics of the order of 10–14% at most, but there are also very promising cases for which deviations remain within 4% depending on the stars and constraints considered.

title: Measurement of spectator fragment pseudorapidity distributions with the STAR Event Plane Detector
abstract: At sufficiently low center-of-mass energies, charged particles originating from the spectator region fall within the pseudorapidity acceptance ($2.14<|\eta|<5.09$) of the STAR Event Plane Detector (EPD). Measurements of the pseudorapidity distributions of helium spectator fragments are presented for Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair of $\sqrt{s_{_{\mathrm{NN}}}}=$ 19.6, 14.6, 11.5, 9.2, and 7.7 GeV. The helium fragment yields in each EPD ring are extracted from fits to the deposited energy spectra using convoluted Landau distributions while accounting for the contribution from singly charged particles. The effects of the EPD detection efficiency and interactions of the fragments with the STAR beam pipe are evaluated using Geant4 Monte Carlo simulations. The resulting pseudorapidity distributions are presented as a function of collision energy and collision centrality.
authors: Balazs Korodi for the STAR Collaboration

title: Investigating capture cross section and fusion probability of heavy-ion fusion reactions with the effective potential
abstract: Abstract We systematically examine the applicability of a recently proposed effective potential for describing heavy-ion fusion reactions within the dinuclear system (DNS) model. This potential reliably reproduces experimental barrier heights and capture excitation functions across a range of systems. For reactions with entrance channels near the Businaro–Gallone (B.G.) point, the predicted fusion probabilities agree well with experimental data, indicating that the potential captures the key dynamical effects relevant to such reactions. However, for reactions with entrance channels far from the B.G. point, the present treatment of dynamics is insufficient, and the evolution of the relative motion degree of freedom needs to be incorporated in future models. Overall, this effective potential offers a practical framework for near-barrier fusion reaction studies, balancing computational efficiency with dynamical realism, particularly for systems near the B.G. point.

title: Exploring differential two-particle correlations in $\gamma p$ and low-multiplicity pp collisions using PYTHIA8
abstract: A study of two-particle differential number ($B$) and transverse momentum ($P_{2}^\mathrm{CD}$) balance functions in photon-proton ($\gamma p$) and proton-proton (pp) collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 5.36 TeV is presented. The analysis focuses on inclusive charged hadrons within the pseudorapidity coverage $|\eta|<2.4$ and the transverse momentum interval $0.3 < p_\mathrm{T} < 3.0$ GeV and examines their correlations in terms of relative pseudorapidity ($\Delta\eta$) and relative azimuthal angle ($\Delta\phi$). The correlation functions are evaluated for same- and opposite-sign pairs, and their combinations are used to extract charge-dependent (CD) and charge-independent (CI) components. The evolution of the near-side peak of the CD correlations is investigated in terms of $\Delta\eta$ and $\Delta\phi$ as a function of charged-particle multiplicity ($N_\mathrm{ch}$) for $\gamma p$ collisions and compared to pp collisions at a similar multiplicity range. A clear multiplicity dependence of the balance function width is obtained. The width is found systematically lower in $\gamma p$ events than in pp collisions. This study provides valuable information on particle correlations and production mechanisms in low-$N_\mathrm{ch}$ regimes for upcoming measurements in small systems.

title: Radiative Corrections to Elastic Lepton-Proton Scattering with Focus on Two-Photon-Exchange Diagrams
abstract: Lepton (electron and muon) scattering experiments are excellent tools to gain insight into the nucleon structure. Elastic electron-proton scattering probes the spatial distribution of charge and magnetization inside the proton, and comparing electron-proton and muon-proton scattering data tests lepton universality. The availability of a plethora of scattering data with increased precision and observed discrepancies such as the proton form factor puzzle and the proton radius puzzle motivated a renewed effort to improve the theoretical framework. Realizing that the one-photon-exchange approximation (OPE), i.~e. the Born approximation, is not sufficient, radiative corrections in QED, especially the two-photon-exchange (TPE) diagrams, are under investigation. The TPE diagrams are of special interest among the radiative corrections, since their hadronic-structure-dependent contribution generates an additional dependence of the cross section on the virtual-photon polarization parameter beyond the Born approximation that is not captured by standard model-independent radiative correction procedures, and that directly impacts the extraction of proton form factors. In this work, we present a complete calculation of QED radiative corrections to elastic electron-proton and muon-proton scattering at next-to-leading order, taking into account loop-momentum-dependent form factors. In the discussion of their numerical impact on lepton-proton scattering cross sections, we pay special attention to the elastic nucleon contribution to the TPE diagrams and compare them with existing theoretical predictions and lepton-proton scattering data.

title: Higher-order strongly intensive observables for forward-backward multiplicity correlations
abstract: Forward-backward multiplicity correlations probe the longitudinal structure of particle production, but fluctuations in the number of emitting sources complicate their interpretation. Strongly intensive observables remove the contribution of source-number fluctuations at second order. Here we extend the construction to all cumulant orders. For independent identical sources whose emission law does not depend on the source count, we build a normalized hierarchy of strongly intensive observables with $n$ new algebraically independent quantities at order $n$. Every observable is normalized to unity for statistically independent particles, vanishes when both window multiplicities are fixed, and remains finite at equal positive window means. We give explicit expressions through fourth order and an all-order recursion. Analytical particle production models and PYTHIA calculations for $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=0.9$ and 13 TeV demonstrate the sensitivity to window geometry, event selection, and connected multiparticle correlations. Fits constrained by the mean multiplicities and second-order observables provide conditional higher-order benchmarks. Deviations of these benchmarks from the PYTHIA results test the assumed correlation hierarchy, subject to the quality of the lower-order fit. Preliminary ALICE measurements at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV are used to illustrate the corresponding model-dependent scenarios.

title: Chebyshev-expanded covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory
abstract: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component $U_V$ is incorporated at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $\sigma$, $\omega$, $\delta$, and $\rho$ channels. The density-dependent couplings are represented by cubic Chebyshev polynomials over the density range $0.08\leq\rho\leq0.48~{\rm fm}^{-3}$. A constrained thermodynamic calibration uses 199 RBHF energy-per-particle values from published microscopic computations at six isospin asymmetries, while maintaining positive, monotonic couplings. The Bonn-A RBHF saturation point, incompressibility $K_\infty=258$ MeV, symmetry energy $J=33.1$ MeV, and slope $L=65.2$ MeV are reproduced. The predicted curvature $K_{\rm sym}=33$ MeV differs from the published RBHF value of $-67$ MeV, illustrating the derivative sensitivity of the local reduction. The combined energy RMS is $0.613$ MeV, measuring model discrepancy rather than statistical uncertainty. Uniform matter remains mechanically stable and causal above saturation within the calibrated range. In cold charge-neutral $npe\mu$ matter, CE-ME1 reasonably reproduces the interpolated RBHF pressure and proton fraction over most of the interval, although the pressure discrepancy increases near its upper edge. The DD-ME2 benchmark is stiffer and predicts a lower proton fraction at high density.

title: Ancilla-recycled RODEO filtering for nuclear scattering: A cross-platform benchmark on quantum processors
abstract: Quantum computation of trapped spectra for nuclear scattering requires resource-efficient circuits and reliable energy inputs. We present a cross-platform benchmark of ancilla-recycled RODEO filtering for a four-dimensional effective Hamiltonian describing a trapped neutron--proton model. Static circuits on IonQ Forte-1 and dynamic circuits on IBM Aachen implement the same ideal ten-cycle all-zero accepted filter using twelve and three active qubits, respectively. Mid-circuit measurement and reset reduce the active qubit count by 75\% while retaining all controlled evolutions. The interleaved IBM peak-center offset from the exact level is $-0.017 \pm 0.507~\mathrm{keV}$, compared with $-0.568 \pm 0.694~\mathrm{keV}$ for IonQ (finite-shot bootstrap uncertainties). At \(\omega=3.7~\mathrm{MeV}\), the modified effective range expansion maps both centers to finite-confinement scattering inputs consistent with the exact reference within propagated uncertainties. Three IBM batches exhibit center variations beyond finite-shot uncertainties (\(p=0.015\)), despite comparatively stable postselection amplitudes. Calibration-derived noisy simulations do not consistently reproduce the measured centers. Complete sampled support enables sample-based quantum diagonalization to recover the exact effective-space level, whereas larger-space simulator tests expose substantial errors from omitted configurations. The calculation validates one finite-confinement input, not a free-space phase shift. This benchmark provides a reusable circuit and validation protocol separating spectral precision, hardware repeatability, and sampled-subspace completeness for multilevel nuclear-scattering calculations.

title: Radio ghosts: Radio polarimetry study of newly discovered cluster minihalo candidates or radio tailed galaxies
abstract: Extended diffuse radio emission in the central regions of galaxy clusters is commonly associated with non-thermal processes in the intracluster medium (ICM), but its origin and the mechanisms responsible for sustaining it remain uncertain. We present the discovery and multi-wavelength analysis of two diffuse radio sources, MKT,J0355--4237 and MKT,J0355--4230, to assess their nature and investigate their radio spectral and magnetic field properties through radio polarimetric analysis. We used deep MeerKAT L band (1.28,GHz) observations to perform spectral analysis of the diffuse emission and study its polarisation properties via rotation measure synthesis. We complement these observations with eROSITA X-ray data and DESI photometric redshift catalogues to characterise the host cluster environments. We confirm MKT,J0355--4237 as a cluster-scale minihalo with an extent of ∼ 400,kpc, while the nature of the other diffuse source, MKT,J0355--4230, remains uncertain; it could be associated with either a radio minihalo or a radio tailed galaxy. Both sources show steep spectra (α ≈ -0.7 to -0.8) that steepen towards the outskirts (α łesssim -2.5), consistent with spatial variations in electron ageing and re-acceleration. We detect polarised emission in both systems, with a fractional polarisation of sim1,% in the centres and an increase in the outer regions of MKT,J0355--4237. MKT,J0355--4230 is associated with a previously uncatalogued cluster and shows an X-ray morphology offset from the brightest cluster galaxy, indicative of dynamical activity. MKT,J0355--4237 exhibits a sharply bounded internal radio deficit without a corresponding X-ray counterpart, within current sensitivity limits. The spectral steepening supports turbulent re-acceleration as the origin of the diffuse emission. The detection of polarisation indicates partially ordered magnetic fields in the ICM. The internal radio deficit may trace local variations in particle re-acceleration or fossil active galactic nucleus (AGN) plasma embedded within the minihalo.

title: Proton Specific Entropy as a Proxy for the O 7+ /O 6+ Charge State Ratio over Heliocentric Distance
abstract: Abstract While the fast solar wind has well-established origins in coronal holes, the source of the slow solar wind remains uncertain. Compositional metrics, such as heavy ion charge state ratios, are set in the lower corona, providing insights into solar wind source regions. Prior to the launch of Solar Orbiter, in situ measurements of heavy ion charge state were limited to distances of 1 au and beyond. We investigate proton specific entropy as a proxy for the oxygen charge state ratio (O 7+ /O 6+ ), which generally becomes frozen-in below ∼1.8 R ⊙ , leveraging observations from Solar Orbiter’s Heavy Ion Sensor and Proton and Alpha Sensor covering 0.28–1 au. Our analysis confirms a strong anticorrelation between specific entropy and the oxygen charge state ratio that persists over a broad range of distances in the inner heliosphere. We categorize observations into fast solar wind, slow Alfvénic solar wind, and slow solar wind, identifying thresholds in specific entropy values and charge state ratios across these types that can be used to distinguish solar wind source regions. This work demonstrates the potential to use proton specific entropy as a classifier of solar wind source regions throughout the heliosphere. By establishing the S p –O 7+ /O 6+ relationship and quantifying its radial dependence, the specific entropy can be used as a quantity to identify the solar wind source region in the absence of in situ charge state measurements. This motivates future studies as to the applicability of this proxy to near-Sun observations, such as from Parker Solar Probe, and throughout the inner heliosphere.

title: Pion valence structure at intermediate x in the residual-field approach
abstract: We calculate the valence parton distribution function (PDF) of pion within the theoretical approach based on spectral function representation of valence quarks in the pion. In this approach we assume that the soft partonic structure of pion is defined by the valence q q ¯ cluster, consisting of current quarks, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The valence PDF is calculated using phenomenological light-front wave functions for the q q ¯ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF (xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the valence quark cluster and the mass of the residual system. Magnitudes of these parameters are obtained by fitting to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF evaluated at starting Q 0 . They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed to describe existing pion PDFs at intermediate x . They also indicate that the q q ¯ cluster is highly virtual and on average the interacting quark carries almost all of the momentum of the q q ¯ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF and practically describing ≈ ( 1 − x ) behavior observed recently at x → 1 limit. Our nontrivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at x → 1 limit.

title: Oncogenic modulation of MAPK signaling in leukemia via SPNS2-driven sphingolipid metabolism and membrane nanodomains remodeling
abstract: Abstract Lipid metabolism rewiring is an essential determinant of cancer progression, yet the key metabolic checkpoints which govern this process remain poorly defined. Using functional genomics in a mouse model of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), we identify the sphingosine-1-phosphate transporter SPNS2 as a critical sphingolipid checkpoint protein which modulates leukemia progression. SPNS2 expression is regulated by MYC and progressively declines during AML differentiation, highlighting its tumor-suppressive role in a subset of Core Binding Factor AMLs. By integrating steady-state and serine isotope-tracing lipidomics, RNA sequencing, flow cytometry, and high-resolution microscopy, with gain- and loss-of-function approaches, we show that SPNS2 modulation rewires sphingolipid metabolism by modifying sphingomyelin abundance. This remodeling alters membrane nanodomain organization, active RAS localization, and MAPK signaling. Exogenous reintroduction of SPNS2 decreases sphingomyelin levels, disrupts nanodomain organization, and limits leukemic progression in various AML mouse models. We further reveal in a cohort of patients with AML that low SPNS2 expression is associated with increased sensitivity to MAPK pathway inhibition, and demonstrate functionally in vivo that SPNS2 silencing sensitizes AML cells to MEK1/2 inhibition. Collectively, our data reveal a mechanism by which sphingolipid transport dynamics intersect with oncogenic signaling to control cancer progression.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Ketene as a gas phase intermediate in acetic acid ketonization on TiO2
abstract: Abstract Reactive gas-phase intermediates are often underappreciated in heterogeneous catalysis, despite their potential to control key catalytic steps. Here, we provide direct experimental evidence that ketene can act as an intermediate in acetic acid ketonization, a mechanism that has long been debated. Using faceted TiO 2 (101) nanoparticles assembled into layers of controlled thickness, we show that ketene, formed from surface acetate, migrates through interparticle voids via desorption-readsorption events before reacting with surface acetate to yield acetone. Surface science and reactor studies reveal a direct correlation between ketene and acetone production and the depth to which the particle layers are saturated. Ab initio calculations support ketene’s reactivity via low-barrier coupling pathways that converge on a common β-ketoacid intermediate. Here, we show that ketene can act as a mobile gas-phase intermediate and underscore the broader importance of spatially decoupled elementary steps in determining reactivity and selectivity in catalytic systems.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: A human erythropoietin-albumin fusion protein tailored for enhanced plasma half-life and delivery across mucosal surfaces
abstract: Abstract Erythropoietin (EPO) products stimulate production of erythrocytes in patients with anemia. The drugs are delivered intravenously or subcutaneously up to several times per week due to short plasma half-life. Improving the pharmacokinetic properties of EPO will allow less frequent administration, and thus impact therapeutic utility and patient compliance. In this study, we took advantage of an albumin variant (QMP) engineered for improved engagement of FcRn, a key regulator of the plasma half-life of albumin. After genetic coupling of EPO to QMP, the fusion protein shows favorable neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) binding, and 5.2-fold prolonged plasma half-life in human FcRn expressing mice upon intravenous administration, when comparing with EPO fused to WT albumin, with a similar half-life obtained following subcutaneous administration. Importantly, both fusions bind the EPO receptor with binding kinetics equal to that of the product darbepoetin alfa. After intravenous administration, mice receiving darbepoetin alfa experiences a faster drop in EPO levels compared to those given EPO-QMP, and moreover, we measure a prolonged increase in erythrocytes with EPO-QMP. Furthermore, intranasal administration results in 5-fold higher circulating amounts of EPO-QMP and a prolonged increase in erythrocytes compared to darbepoetin alfa. Thus, long-acting EPO-QMP could be an attractive design to explore for both invasive and non-invasive delivery to patients with anemia.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet
abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes the mean position of a spinning particle transform anomalously under a Lorentz boost, with an additional shift known as a side jump. In this work, we develop a trace method to derive an exact but compact transformation kernel for the probability center of a general three-dimensional Dirac wave packet under an arbitrary finite Lorentz boost. The expression includes the physics of finite momentum width, spin-momentum correlations, and coherent phase structure without a semi-classical expansion. We identify texture-dependent side jumps even at fixed initial mean momentum, spin, and orbital angular momentum, as well as a non-monotonic mass dependence for Gaussian packets at fixed momentum width. The explicit kernels further resolve the spin and orbital angular-momentum contributions for massive and massless fermions, providing a kinematic basis for covariant particle-based spin transport that retains wave-packet information.

title: Deriving the anomalous Lorentz transformation and side jump using a trace method
abstract: The side jump in the anomalous Lorentz transformation, arising from the spin-orbit interactions, plays important roles in various intriguing physics, such as chiral vortical effects and spin polarization. In this work, the side jump of the spin-half particles is visualized and evaluated ab initio within Dirac theory, through a comprehensive study of the density $\psi^\dagger\psi$ and position $\int d^3x\psi^\dagger \mathbf{x}\psi$ of a wave packet under Lorentz transformation. A compact gamma-matrix representation of the Lorentz boost matrix of a Dirac spinor, $S(\boldsymbol{\eta})= h_{\boldsymbol\eta}^{\mu}\gamma_\mu \check{u}^\nu \gamma_\nu$, has been found. Based on this expression, a trace method has been developed to derive the anomalous Lorentz transformation of the center of the probability density of a spin-half fermion wave packet, and a compact analytical expression for the side jump has been obtained through a transparent and tractable derivation. The momentum width plays an important role in the side jump. For example, for Gaussian wave packets, increasing the width suppresses the displacement, while the side jump at fixed width depends nonmonotonically on mass, reaching a maximum at a finite mass. In the zero-width limit, the side jump takes a compact form perpendicular to both the Pauli-Lubanski vector and the boost direction, recovering the known result for a chiral particle.

title: Density-Dependent Description of Clustering in Axially-Symmetric Nuclei
abstract: We present a microscopic description of the {\alpha}-decay processes from axially-symmetric superfluid nuclei in terms of proton ({\pi}) and neutron ({\nu}) single-particle (sp) degrees of freedom within a standard Woods-Saxon mean field (WSMF) and a density-dependent clustering potential centered around the average Mott point of the nuclear density, where the {\alpha}-particle is formed. In this way the clustering process is automatically enhanced on the nuclear surface. As an illustration of the method, a systematics of {\alpha}-decay from even-even emitters is presented.

title: Axions from Betelgeuse: Probing Axion Couplings with $^{23}\rm{Na}$ and $^{55}\rm{Mn}$
abstract: We investigate axion-like particle (ALP) production in the interior of Betelgeuse via nuclear de-excitation of thermally populated excited states of $^{23}$Na and $^{55}$Mn. As these ALPs propagate to Earth, they can produce photons either through their conversion in the Galactic magnetic field or through their decay. Using INTEGRAL-ISGRI and NuSTAR observations, we search for these photon signals, find no significant excess, and derive 95% CL exclusion limits on the ALP couplings. For magnetic-field conversion of ALPs, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}| < 4.1\times10^{-21}$ ($6.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ for $m_a < 10^{-10} \mathrm{eV}$. For ALP decays, the $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ ($^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$) line observed with INTEGRAL-ISGRI (NuSTAR) constrains $|g_{a\gamma}g_{ap}|$ down to $3.0\times10^{-22}$ ($2.9\times10^{-19}$) $\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a \simeq 400$ ($83$) keV, weakening in both cases as $m_a^{-3/2}$ for lower ALP masses, and as $m_a^{-2}$ for $^{23}$Na below $m_a \sim 1$ keV, with sensitivity extending to $m_a \simeq 440.2$ ($124$) keV. Although our $^{23}\mathrm{Na}$-based limits are the strongest for both channels, their larger transition energy makes them more sensitive to the precise evolutionary stage of Betelgeuse, whereas the $^{55}\mathrm{Mn}$-based limits are considerably more robust against such uncertainties.

title: Inclusive jet cross section in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 200$ and $510$ GeV
abstract: Jets are collimated clusters of particles formed by the hadronization of partons following a hard interaction. In proton-proton ($pp$) collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC), jet production is dominated by $gg$ and $qg$ partonic processes, allowing us to directly probe the gluon parton distribution function (PDF) in the proton in a way complementary to deep inelastic scattering. In this paper, we report the double-differential inclusive-jet cross sections as a function of jet transverse momentum, $p_{\rm T}$, and pseudorapidity, $\eta$, at center-of-mass energies $\sqrt{s} = 200$ and $510$~GeV, from $pp$ collisions studied with the STAR detector. The jet $p_{\rm T}$ is corrected for underlying event contributions by applying an off-axis cone method. At mid-pseudorapidity, $|\eta| < 0.9$, the kinematic coverage of our data extends to $0.07 < x_{\rm T} \text{ (}= 2p_{\rm T}{} / \sqrt{s} \text{)} < 0.5$ and $0.03 < x_{\rm T} < 0.31$ at $\sqrt{s} = 200$~and 510 GeV, respectively, where the gluon PDF is poorly constrained by the TeV-scale $pp$~($p\bar{p}$) colliders. The inclusive jet cross sections are compared to the next-to-next-to-leading order perturbative quantum chromodynamics calculations using several recent PDF sets as inputs. These results will further constrain the gluon PDF, help tune Monte Carlo generators, and provide critical reference data needed to study the quark-gluon plasma.
authors: M. Calder\'on de la Barca S\'anchez

title: From mergers to collapse: Scalarization dynamics in neutron star binaries
Boosted Dark Matter Directionality in Large Liquid Scintillator Detectors
abstract: Light dark matter can be boosted by cosmic-ray-dark matter interactions, which opens the possibility of direct-detection searches with large neutrino detectors. We consider the signal produced by boosted dark matter undergoing quasi-elastic scattering off carbon and knocking out a neutron in a large liquid scintillator detector. A distinctive delayed gamma ray from neutron capture can be reconstructed after $\sim 210$ $\mu$s, which is paired up with the prompt signal during neutron propagation. We find that 100 kt$\cdot$yr of data from the neutron-coincidence channel will be able to probe new parameter space compared to free proton signals found in previous work. We further consider the possibility of utilizing directional information from the displaced vertex associated with the capture of the final-state neutron. However, we find that directional information does not materially improve the sensitivity due to the large nucleon scattering angle.

title: Accelerator neutrinos as a probe of in-medium hyperon potentials
abstract: Charged-current (anti)neutrino interactions create Lambda and Sigma hyperons inside the nucleus, so the hyperons that reach a detector have crossed nuclear matter and carry the imprint of the in-medium potentials U_Y(rho) that also govern the appearance of hyperons in neutron stars. In the StrangeMC simulation of argon, the reconstructed Lambda yield and momentum and a kaon-vetoed Sigma+ tag respond to U_Lambda and U_Sigma at SBND and DUNE energies. A detector-level forecast, with the production cross sections, fluxes and efficiencies as nuisance parameters and the muon kinematics calibrating the production model, determines U_Lambda at rho* = 0.82 rho_0, independently of the low-density exponent of the potential, to 1.5 MeV statistically and +-31 MeV in total. The largest item, 18 MeV, is the convention by which the cascade applies the potential. The measurement is a check, with different systematics, of the hypernuclear constraint, +-3.3 MeV at rho*, for momentum-independent potentials; U_Sigma is not determined. In the relativistic mean-field equations of state GM1 and FSU2H, anchored to the hypernuclear and Sigma-atom depths, the maximum neutron-star mass depends on the Lambda NN repulsion, which these data do not constrain.

title: Phenomenology of strangeness-changing two-body currents in antineutrino scattering
abstract: Antineutrinos produce hyperons without kaons through Cabibbo-suppressed quasi-elastic scattering on a single nucleon. A two-body current acting on a correlated nucleon pair, nubar [NN] -> l+ Y N', gives the same hyperons plus a second nucleon. A companion paper constructs this current without fixing its size. StrangeMC, the only generator with the channel, set it to a flat 15% of the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section. We determine the ratio f = sigma_2p2h/sigma_QE of the two-body to the quasi-elastic hyperon cross section on carbon versus antineutrino energy, and the detector signatures of two-body events. The strange two-body current and its non-strange counterpart are computed on the same nucleon pair. Their ratio is converted into f with the Valencia non-strange 2p2h and quasi-elastic cross sections for carbon, assuming that nuclear effects missing from the pair are common to both. Under this assumption f rises from 0.14 at 0.6 GeV to 0.20-0.22 at 2-5 GeV. Averaged over the Booster antineutrino spectra it is 0.15-0.17, close to the 15% placeholder, which StrangeMC now replaces with f(E). The largest evaluated uncertainty comes from separating the two-body current from one-body production followed by rescattering: across the separation prescriptions explored, f at 1 GeV ranges from 0.12 to 0.22. Interference with one-body production is not calculated and could be as large as the two-body rate. In a simulated SBND antineutrino-mode exposure on argon with the carbon f, two-body events are about 11% of events that produce a strange hadron. They supply more than a quarter of the kaon-less Sigma+ events used to tag hyperon charge exchange, partly as Sigma+ made at the weak vertex. They reconstruct 12-30% low in energy under the quasi-elastic hypothesis. After final-state interactions half of them have a proton above 40 MeV at the vertex, against a fifth of quasi-elastic events.

title: Neutronics characterisation of the radiation environment for the qualification of magnetic sensors on DEMO
abstract: Abstract Magnetic sensors are a primary diagnostic tool for plasma control on DEMO, required to measure the local distribution of magnetic fields at multiple positions. As these sensors must be located between the Breeding Blanket (BB) and the Vacuum Vessel (VV), they will be exposed to a harsh radiation environment, with neutron fluences expected to exceed those of ITER by up to an order of magnitude. This paper presents a comprehensive assessment of the radiation environment at the expected locations of magnetic sensors in DEMO, for both the Helium-Cooled Pebble Bed (HCPB) and Water-Cooled Lithium Lead (WCLL) BB configurations. MCNP simulations were performed using heterogeneous reference models of both blankets. Neutron and gamma fluxes, nuclear heat loads, dose rates and displacements per atom were estimated at 60 in-vessel and 60 ex-vessel positions, distributed poloidally around the plasma. The HCPB configuration produces a maximum in-vessel neutron flux of 3.6×10 13 n cm -2 s -1 at the equatorial inboard positions, a factor 18 higher than the WCLL value at the same location. The WCLL maximum in-vessel neutron flux is 8.6×10 12 n cm -2 s -1 , found below the divertor, where the shielding is less effective. The impact of the Magnetic Strip (MS) – a modular structure proposed to integrate the sensors while ensuring compatibility with Remote Maintenance (RM) – was also assessed, through a parametric study in which the radial thickness of the MS envelope was varied between 5 and 11 cm. Overall, the results presented in this paper establish the boundaries of the radiation environment that must be sustained by the magnetic diagnostic front-end components over the plant lifetime, and provide the quantitative neutronics basis for the irradiation testing and qualification program required to advance the Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of the DEMO magnetic sensors from the proof-of-concept stage to full validation in a fusion-relevant environment.

title: Kinetic modifications to parallel transport in a low recycling scrape-off layer: A one dimensional gyrokinetic study
abstract: Abstract A liquid lithium boundary offers a route to improved energy confinement via reduced recycling, but the resulting low-density, high-temperature edge can become sufficiently collisionless that standard fluid models are no longer applicable. Experimental measurements of scrape-off-layer (SOL) parameters, including density decay length estimates presented here, can be used for simple analytic estimates of kinetic effects, but more complete models are needed. We present 1-D, two-velocity-space gyrokinetic simulations of low and higher-recycling LTX-beta SOL conditions using Gkeyll, an open-source continuum gyrokinetic code. The simulations follow a single open field line from the low-field-side midplane to the high-field-side limiter, evolving kinetic ion and electron distribution functions, electrostatic potential, collisions, sources, and sheath losses with experimentally constrained mid-plane parameters. The low-recycling case develops a hotter SOL, a larger electrostatic potential variation along the field line, and a density response not recovered with an adiabatic Boltzmann-electron closure. This indicates that kinetic-electron dynamics and the associated ambipolar potential are important for maintaining quasi-neutrality and reducing electron end loss. Collisionality scans show that as the ion neoclassical collisionality drops below unity, the ion distribution develops a stronger non-Maxwellian structure. The corresponding SOL particle and energy confinement times increase at low collisionality, especially for low recycling, because ions become mirror trapped and electron transport is suppressed by the ambipolar potential. These results suggest that low recycling lithium walls in LTX-beta access a SOL regime where mirror trapping and electrostatic modifications alter field-line residence times relative to fluid expectations, effects expected to amplify in larger, hotter tokamaks.

title: Hybrid magnetic diagnostics on DEMO: general concept and integration studies
abstract: Abstract As tokamaks advance towards steady-state fusion operation, most plasma diagnostics will have elements exposed to increasing nuclear and thermomechanical loads over the lifetime of the facilities. Since diagnostic failure due to neutron exposure is expected to occur in such environments, the approach on DEMO has been to develop a set of diagnostics with robust front-end components compatible with remote handling. This paper outlines a general concept of a magnetic diagnostic system for long plasma-duration operation, developed for DEMO but applicable to future full-scale fusion power plants and intermediate machines like the VNS. This is achieved by employing resilient enabling technologies, hybrid magnetic diagnostic chains and data fusion estimators. Following a detailed overview of the diagnostic subsystems under development, and the characterization of the radiation environment at the most exposed front-end locations, the main interfaces with other reactor systems are described and a remote handling classification scheme is developed, based on the one adopted on ITER. An in-depth discussion of the integration possibilities for in-vessel probes and cables on DEMO is then provided. To address the constraints identified in these studies, the Magnetic Strip concept is proposed, a modular structure conceived to house all the in-vessel magnetic probes and part of the cable looms that carry the signals to the vacuum vessel feedthroughs. The Magnetic Strip is designed to be attached to the inner surface of the vacuum vessel, anchored on the fixation bosses developed for ITER diagnostics, behind the breeding blanket. Integration with the remote maintenance procedures of the blanket is demonstrated through the development of a remote handling tool concept to manipulate the structure. Preliminary analyses underline the advantages of the Magnetic Strip concept, which allows the replacement of the front-end components and cabling in single remote handling operations while keeping temperatures and thermal gradients within the operating limits.

title: Circular-mode optics for high-intensity beams and high-luminosity colliders
abstract: We study circular-mode optics as a framework for transporting and accelerating intrinsically flat beams while maintaining a round transverse projection in physical space. Motivated by the strong degradation of flat beams under low-energy space-charge forces, we develop a coupled-optics description of circular modes, analyze their formation and preservation, and derive lattice design conditions for conserving canonical angular momentum and coupling phase. These conditions motivate rotationally invariant transport and ring cells based on solenoids, symmetric alternating-gradient structures, and indexed dipoles. We further derive space-charge tune-shift and tune-spread expressions for circular-mode beams in uncoupled and coupled lattices, showing that they preserve the leading-order space-charge behavior of round beams while retaining intrinsic eigenemittance flatness. Particle-in-cell simulations with TRACK and mpact confirm the generation, transport, and acceleration of circular-mode beams in representative lattices, including regimes with strong space charge. Circular-mode optics therefore provides a promising route toward high-intensity hadron beams and high-luminosity collider applications.

title: A Coupled Source Description of Pseudorapidity Distributions from RHIC to LHC: Emergent $1/\mu_B$ Scaling and Limiting Fragmentation
abstract: One of the most remarkable observations in heavy-ion collisions is the systematic regularity exhibited by pseudorapidity distributions of charged particles across collision energies. While single-source models fail at higher energies and independent multi-source approaches do not reproduce the central dip observed at LHC energies, a unified description across the full RHIC-LHC energy range remains elusive. These distributions from Au+Au collisions at RHIC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 19.6--200 GeV) and Pb+Pb collisions at LHC ($\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 2.76--5.36 TeV) are analyzed using a novel parametrization based on coupled Gaussian sources where the interaction strength is quantified by parameter $\lambda$. This coupled two-source model captures the interaction between forward and backward sources through the medium formed in the collision. Remarkably, $\lambda$ exhibits empirical scaling behavior resembling $1/\mu_B$, suggesting sensitivity to baryon stopping and the strongly-interacting medium. All fitting parameters follow systematic energy trends, with the peak-to-peak distance and chemical freeze-out temperature exhibiting identical exponential saturation patterns, indicating that geometric expansion and thermal evolution share a common underlying dynamics governed by QCD phase structure. Furthermore, the approach naturally preserves limiting fragmentation behavior across all energies, in contrast to independent source models that suggest its violation at LHC energies. Although the theoretical basis requires further investigation, these empirical correlations successfully unify charged particle production across nearly two orders of magnitude in collision energy, revealing fundamental connections to underlying collision dynamics.

title: Temperature-Dependent Performance of NaI(Tl) Crystal with Dual-Channel SiPM Readout for Low-Mass Dark Matter Searches
abstract: We report the first temperature-dependent characterization of a NaI(Tl) crystal readout by two silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) directly coupled to opposite ends of the crystal for rare-event searches. A $6 \text{ mm} \times 6 \text{ mm} \times 13 \text{ mm}$ NaI(Tl) crystal was directly coupled to two SiPMs and characterized in a liquid nitrogen-cooled cryostat over a temperature range of 94$-$293 K. The light yield, energy resolution, and scintillation decay time were measured using $\gamma$-ray peak from a $^{241}$Am source. After correcting for optical crosstalk contributions, the light yield increased, reaching $17.7 \pm 1.1$ photoelectrons/keV at 238 K, corresponding to a 34.5% enhancement relative to room temperature (293 K). Furthermore, dual-channel configuration effectively suppresses random thermal noise via coincidence triggers, which together with the observed increase in light yield, provides a critical pathway toward lowering the energy threshold for dark matter and coherent elastic neutrino$-$nucleus scattering searches.

title: Particle-dependent radioluminescence color response of Eu-doped CaF$_2$ associated with energy-loss density
abstract: Europium-doped calcium fluoride (Eu:CaF$_2$) exhibits characteristic blue Eu$^{2+}$ and red Eu$^{3+}$ emissions. In our previous study, the Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ radioluminescence intensity ratio under $\alpha$-particle irradiation was approximately twice that under X-ray irradiation. Here, we investigate the relationship between this emission ratio and energy-loss density using H, Li, C, and Ni ion beams produced by a tandem accelerator. Radioluminescence spectra were measured for each ion species, and the effective range-averaged energy-loss density was evaluated using SRIM simulations, spanning approximately 18 to 5900~keV/$\mu$m. The Eu$^{3+}$/Eu$^{2+}$ emission-intensity ratio increased systematically from H to C ions by approximately a factor of two, whereas no further systematic increase was observed for Ni ions at substantially higher energy-loss densities. Because the energy-loss density was varied mainly by changing the ion species, its effect cannot be fully separated from that of ion-specific track structure. The X-ray result, included for qualitative comparison, showed a lower emission ratio than the ion-beam measurements, although its effective energy-loss density was estimated only approximately. These results demonstrate a systematic variation in the emission color of Eu:CaF$_2$ across different ion-beam irradiation conditions and provide baseline data for future studies of wavelength-resolved particle discrimination.

title: Development of a real-time FPGA-based CNN trigger operating on full-granularity calorimeter images
abstract: We present a real-time field-programmable gate array (FPGA) implementation of a convolutional neural network (CNN) for event classification on full calorimeter images that retain crystal-level shower information. To meet the resource and latency constraints of trigger electronics, the network parameters and hidden activations were quantized to 8 bits with quantization-aware training, and a lossless space-to-depth reorganization rearranged the input image into fewer spatial positions, reducing the estimated CNN inference latency by more than an order of magnitude. The approach was evaluated with the J-PARC KOTO detector, recorded data, and data-acquisition (DAQ) constraints as a benchmark, targeting the online separation of the rare $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ decay from its dominant $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ background. As a proof of principle, the firmware was implemented and validated on an AMD Versal Premium VPK120 evaluation board. On 100,000 test events, inference on the board rejected $(99.34\pm0.04)\%$ of the recorded background sample enriched in $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{+}\pi^{-}\pi^{0}$ decays at a nominal $K^{0}_{L}\rightarrow\pi^{0}e^{+}e^{-}$ efficiency of 95%, with a measured CNN inference latency of 17.9 $\mu$s. Combining the measured image-assembly and CNN inference latencies with the estimated link-transfer and score-return times gives a projected end-to-end latency of 25.9 $\mu$s, within the adopted 32 $\mu$s DAQ latency budget. These results demonstrate the feasibility of using full-granularity calorimeter images for CNN-based event selection that achieves high background rejection while keeping the trigger latency within tens of microseconds.

title: Data-driven synthesis of high-fidelity triaxial magnetic waveforms for quantum control
abstract: We present a system for generating arbitrary, triaxial magnetic waveforms with a spectral content spanning from DC to tens of kHz, a critical capability for quantum control and spin manipulation. To compensate for amplifier-coil dynamics, we implement a data-driven approach to identify a numerical compensation model. The method parametrizes the system response using a Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter calibrated on the specific waveform to be generated. The application of a driving signal designed via frequency-domain inversion of the identified model enables the synthesis of complex field sequences with sharp transitions between static and single- or multi-frequency temporal segments. The work is validated with experimental results demonstrating waveform fidelity and transient performance, thereby showcasing the precision and feasibility of the method.

title: A Non-Foster Superconducting Broadband Matching Network
abstract: The nonlinear inductance of the Josephson junction has enabled the development of a wide range of continuous-variable amplifiers and qubit-based devices with unprecedented sensitivity. We present an alternative use of the Josephson junction in the context of broadband impedance matching. The idea poses a potential solution to a longstanding problem in the field of high energy particle physics. The axion, a compelling candidate for the dark matter, converts to a weak electromagnetic signal at an as-yet unknown frequency. As such, the ideal axion detector does not compromise bandwidth for sensitivity, a trade-off intrinsic to all linear, time-invariant and passive circuits. We propose a circuit that uses a Josephson junction in an impedance matching network to overcome these gain-bandwidth constraints and increase the scan rate of axion searches. The Josephson junction can be biased to exhibit negative inductance capable of canceling geometric inductance similar to a capacitor but across a wider frequency range.

title: Thermal evolution of neo-neutron stars. II. Temperature-dependent crusts
abstract: The neo-neutron star phase is an intermediate stage in the evolution from a hot, lepton-rich compact object, which is formed in the aftermath of a core-collapse supernova or an accretion-induced collapse of a white dwarf, to a cold deleptonized neutron star (NS). Alternatively, this phase can occur after a binary NS merger if the final compact object does not collapse immediately into a black hole. Radial temperature profiles provided by numerical simulations of proto-NS evolution suggest that the composition and mechanical structure of the star's core at the beginning of the neo-NS phase are approximately identical to those of a cold NS. In contrast, the composition and mechanical structure of the outer layers (i.e., the crust) are expected to change as the star cools. The thermal evolution of neo-NSs with temperature-dependent (inner) envelopes was considered by . Beznogov_ApJ_2020 Here, we investigate what happens if the equation of state (EoS) of the entire crust, including its composition, depends on temperature. We analyzed the thermal, mechanical, and chemical evolution of neo-NSs by further developing and employing , our NS thermal evolution code. neo-NSCool First, we show that thermally dripped neutrons slightly slow down the cooling during the early thermal relaxation stage. Then, we demonstrate that the EoSs featuring exotic light species in the deepest layers of the crust result in significantly slower cooling in the photon-cooling era compared to the EoSs that favor massive nuclei. The crust's composition also impacts the crystallization process as well as the contraction of the crust during cooling. The EoSs with light nuclei cause the innermost layers to remain liquid for a longer time than the EoSs with heavy nuclei.

title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I-type-II boundary: The low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$\kappa$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$\kappa$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

title: Spatiospectral conditioning of laser-plasma-accelerated electron beams using electromagnetic solenoids
abstract: Microcoulomb-class electron beams from laser-plasma accelerators (LPAs) driven by kilojoule-class laser systems can enable high-flux electron radiography and copious secondary particle production. However, electron beam spatial properties such as transverse beam nonuniformity and large spatial scale at application sites can limit their utility. In this work, we demonstrate spatial conditioning of microcoulomb-class electron beams using electromagnetic solenoids as focusing optics. By applying ∼ 10 T solenoidal fields, we focused the electron beam onto a detection plane and measured a fluence enhancement factor of 6 over unconditioned electron beams. The chromatic focusing of the solenoids improved the resolution of electron beam radiographs produced using the focused electron beam. We also demonstrate a method using angled electromagnetic solenoids to simultaneously condition LPA electron beam spatial and spectral properties. These features are attractive for applications because they enable the spatial separation of a narrow-energy-spread population of the electron beam from the bulk of the electron beam.

title: Ferrite-SiC axially graded absorber for broadband higher-order mode damping and thermal response in a 1.5 GHz TM 020 -mode cavity
abstract: The magnetic-field node of a TM 020 -mode cavity permits compact higher-order-mode (HOM) damping, but displacement of the coupling slots can expose the absorber to appreciable accelerating-mode leakage. A ferrite-SiC absorber is investigated numerically to combine broadband damping with improved thermomechanical response in a 1.5 GHz cavity. A transmission-line formulation relates material ordering to input impedance, and coaxial full-wave calculations show that placing SiC ahead of ferrite suppresses the pronounced low-frequency absorption dip of the reverse arrangement. The concept is integrated into a radially folded, six-sector absorber, with parameter sweeps resolving the effects of material dimensions, slot height, and sector angle. For the six higher-order modes (HOMs) tabulated, external quality factors are below 150, while the aligned accelerating mode has an external quality factor of 1.20 × 10 7 . Frequency-resolved loss maps show increasing SiC participation across the transition near 2 GHz. At the same imposed absorber load of 2.65 kW, the hybrid reduces peak temperature rise from 97.0 to 79.9 K and maximum first principal stress in ferrite from 146.0 to 78.6 MPa, reductions of 17.6% and 46.2%, respectively. These results connect electromagnetic loss redistribution to improved thermal and mechanical response and support the hybrid arrangement as a compact damping option for TM 020 -mode cavities.

title: Direct large-area observation of subsurface plastic activity in conditioned copper electrodes
abstract: High-field conditioning is the process by which radio-frequency structures in particle accelerators and other high-gradient devices reach their operating fields, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains an open question. Models and indirect measurements point to subsurface dislocation dynamics, but large-area structural measurements have been missing. We present electron backscatter diffraction measurements spanning millimeter-scale regions on a copper cathode conditioned at pulsed direct-current fields up to ∼ 80 MV / m in a sloped-anode geometry, which imposes a known gradient of field exposure across a single electrode. Across nine regions of interest spanning this exposure range, the mean intragrain misorientation of field-exposed regions exceeds that of unexposed references by ∼ 75 % ; the difference is reproduced by three independent misorientation metrics and confirmed by Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. To our knowledge, this is the first large-area observation of structural differences between conditioned and unconditioned regions of a high-field electrode. The misorientation separates into three tiers (high-field center and edge, low-field periphery, and unexposed reference) that match the spatial profile of the conditioning-state variable E S predicted by Monte Carlo simulations. These observations point to the evolving subsurface dislocation population as a candidate physical basis of conditioning.

title: Achievement of continuous-wave 100 kW radiofrequency transmission by a 1.3 GHz high-power input coupler
abstract: A high-power input coupler was developed at KEK to deliver 100 kW-class radiofrequency (rf) power in the continuous-wave (cw) mode at 1.3 GHz to a superconducting cavity. To mitigate thermal loads during high-power rf transmission, the coupler was engineered with active water cooling integrated into critical components, including a warm inner conductor, outer conductor, antenna, and rf window. The newly developed coupler underwent rf conditioning of up to 145 kW in the pulsed mode and 100 kW in the cw mode using a dedicated test stand at room temperature. The coupler successfully transmitted world-record cw 100 kW rf power at 1.3 GHz continuously for 10 h without any interlock event. During operation, the temperature rise of the warm inner conductor, the most thermally stressed component, was limited to 15 ° C whereas the maximum observed temperature increase was 19 ° C at the doorknob. Further power scaling was not constrained by the coupler itself. These results demonstrate that the newly developed coupler can reliably sustain cw rf transmissions exceeding 100 kW with excellent thermal performance.

title: Study of Multilayer TiNx/Ti/TiNx Films Formed In Situ for High-Efficiency Integrated Microheaters
abstract: A technology for the in situ formation of a three-layer TiN$_x$/Ti/TiN$_x$ functional material within a single vacuum cycle is presented, together with the results of investigations of its structural and electrophysical properties. The maximum critical power density reached approximately 140 MW/cm$^2$. Under continuous operation at 90% of the critical power, the structures remained operational for 24 h. The characteristics of microbridges without and with a protective SiO$_x$ layer were compared. The presence of the coating modifies the electrothermal operating regime of the structures and enables estimated temperatures of approximately 500-700 degrees Celsius to be reached.

title: Optical effects in Gaseous Electron Multipliers (GEMs)
abstract: Optical time projection chambers (OTPCs) are well suited for applications that require the highest spatial resolution for particle track reconstruction. The MIGDAL experiment uses a glass GEM-based OTPC and observes a systematic excess in both the intensity and width of particle tracks in its optical readout, when compared with charge readout simulations. One hypothesis is that scintillation light produced inside a GEM hole during the avalanche propagates through the GEM substrate and exits neighboring holes. We present lab measurements testing this hypothesized optical broadening effect in three types of GEM substrates: glass, ceramic, and FR4. Our observations quantify this optical broadening and demonstrate it to be strongest in glass GEMs. Additionally, we use Geant4 simulations to both reproduce our observations and quantify optical broadening effects in realistic charge avalanches. Applying our glass GEM effects to simulated particle tracks yields increases of track intensity and widths by up to approximately 26% and 31%, respectively. This may explain the larger-than-expected track intensities and widths observed in the MIGDAL OTPC. This effect may be relevant to GEM-based OTPCs, with its magnitude depending on the GEM structure and detector-specific optical configuration.

title: Observable signatures of a quarkyonic phase in neutron stars
Interferometry analysis of different pions at HIRFL-CSR energies
abstract: Due to differences in properties such as mass and charge among different pions, the magnitudes of Hanbury–Brown–Twiss (HBT) radii are affected. Therefore, we performed HBT interferometry analyses for [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], while also considering the influence of cross-terms on the HBT radii. Three different initial radii were selected. From the energy density distribution plots of the expanding source at different times, it can be seen that the expansion of the source is slower in the transverse direction than in the longitudinal direction. Interferometric analyses reveal that for [Formula: see text], a larger initial longitudinal radius leads to the larger HBT radius in the longitudinal direction [Formula: see text]. The cross-terms [Formula: see text] reduce the HBT radius in the out direction [Formula: see text], the HBT radius in the side direction [Formula: see text] and the reduction is most significant for [Formula: see text]. We considered the Chemical Freezing Out model (CFO), the Partial Chemical Equilibrium model (PCE) and the Thermal Freezing Out model (TFO). The CFO model yields the largest HBT radii while the TFO model yields the smallest. In the CFO and TFO models, the HBT radii of [Formula: see text] are larger than those of [Formula: see text], the opposite conclusion holds for the PCE model. For [Formula: see text], deviations from a Gaussian distribution are observed in both the y and z directions in the CFO model while deviations occur only in the z direction in the PCE and TFO models. title: Evidence of partonic collectivity in OO collisions through the measurement of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda$ elliptic flow
abstract: The first measurement of the elliptic-flow coefficient ($v_{2}$) of $\phi$, K$^0_{\rm S}$, and $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ hadrons performed in OO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV with the ALICE detector is presented as a function of transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) in central and semi-central collisions. For the $\phi$ meson, in particular, this is the first measurement of the elliptic flow in a small collision system. At low $p_{\rm T}$, a characteristic mass ordering of $v_{2}$ is observed, consistent with collective expansion of the system, in which heavier hadrons are shifted to higher $p_{\rm T}$ by a common velocity field. At intermediate $p_{\rm T}$, above 3 GeV/$c$, a baryon$-$meson splitting with a $10\sigma$ significance emerges, with the $\Lambda (\overline{\Lambda})$ baryon exhibiting larger $v_{2}$ values than mesons, while, despite its mass being close to the mass of the $\Lambda$, the $\phi$ follows the K$^{0}_{\rm S}$. The $\phi$ meson behavior disfavors a purely mass-driven interpretation of the observed patterns and supports the role of hadronization via quark recombination from a collectively flowing partonic medium. These results provide complementary evidence that key signatures of partonic collectivity observed in Pb$-$Pb collisions persist in light nucleus$-$nucleus systems.

title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
abstract: Electric-field-based actuators and machines lead the design space at the nanoscale and in biological systems, while having the potential to be used in favorable macroscale applications which prioritize minimal mass, performance in a vacuum, or performance in high temperatures. Electric-field induction motors consist of a set of stator electrodes which induce opposite charges onto a movable rotor surface. In earlier work, rotor surfaces for electric-field induction motors have been made of single continuum materials, which are limited in possible resistivity, permittivity and circuitry characteristics. To enhance design freedom, we develop a rotor for electric-field-based machines which may be constructed out of discrete circuit components between a finite number of conductive vanes. Magnetic-field induction motors, which are common in machinery, often utilize ``deep bar'' rotors, consisting of conducting bars which decrease the rotor time constant with increasing frequency using the skin depth effect. We propose, analyze, design and demonstrate a macro-scale electric-field induction motor which uses circuitry on the rotor surface to emulate the ``deep bar'' design, providing improved torque over a wide range of speeds.

title: Centrality and participant-number systematics of two-component standard-distribution parameters for identified hadrons in Au + Au collisions at sNN=77–624 GeV
abstract: Transverse-momentum ([Formula: see text]) spectra of identified hadrons are a powerful and precise phenomenological tool to study the collision-energy, centrality, and particle-species dependence of the matter created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. We report a systematic study of [Formula: see text], [Formula: see text], p and [Formula: see text] production in Au[Formula: see text][Formula: see text][Formula: see text]Au collisions as a function of the RHIC Beam Energy Scan (BES) range of [Formula: see text]–62.4[Formula: see text]GeV. The component inverse-slope parameters (effective temperature-like) [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text], the fractional contribution k, the weighted effective temperature-like parameter T, the mean transverse momentum [Formula: see text], the model-derived source-temperature parameter [Formula: see text], and the free normalization parameter [Formula: see text] are extracted and/or calculated within a two-component standard distribution, together with the fit-quality measure [Formula: see text]. The results are presented according to centrality, [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text]. For the particle species available, T, [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] drop from central to peripheral collisions and rise with [Formula: see text], indicating systematic spectral softening towards the smaller collision systems. Saturation-like behavior is observed as a descriptive pattern in both the energy scan and the centrality scan: from an energy of about [Formula: see text][Formula: see text]GeV and upwards, the growth of T, [Formula: see text] and [Formula: see text] weakens, and the centrality interval, where the parameters are nearly saturated, moves towards more peripheral collisions as the energy of the collisions increases. title: Spectral energy-loss bump and γ-ray pulsar halos
abstract: Abstract The parent electron spectrum of $\gamma$-ray pulsar halos is determined by continuous injection and radiative energy losses, with the nonlinear nature of the latter expected to produce an age-dependent energy-loss bump in the halo spectrum. We demonstrate that the broadband $\gamma$-ray spectrum of the Geminga halo measured by Fermi-LAT and HAWC is consistent with this expectation. Its energy-loss bump appears in the GeV region and is primarily produced by electrons injected at the earliest stage. Therefore, fitting the data allows us to constrain parameters governing early electron injection, such as the pulsar braking index $n$ and initial spin period $P_0$. In addition, we show that another crucial condition for explaining the Geminga halo spectrum is a power-law index of the injection spectrum close to $1$, consistent with the X-ray observations of the Geminga pulsar wind nebula. Currently, no significant energy-loss bump has been detected in the spectrum of the Monogem halo; based on this, we also place preliminary constraints on $n$ and $P_0$ for Monogem. This work demonstrates that pulsar halo spectra can be used not only to constrain electron injection parameters but also to provide independent estimates of certain intrinsic pulsar properties.

title: Searching for optical pulsations from spider millisecond pulsars with the fast photometer SiFAP2
abstract: Context. Optical pulsations from millisecond pulsars (MSPs) have recently been detected in a transitional MSP and an accreting MSP. Evidence for optical pulsations has also been found for a rotation-powered redback MSP. Observations suggest that optical pulsed emission is produced by different mechanisms depending on whether an accretion disk is present in the system. Aims. We explored a sample of rotation-powered MSPs in close binaries (P orb < 1 day; redbacks and black widows), searching for optical periodic signals with the SiFAP2 photometer mounted on the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo (TNG). Methods. We performed pulsation searches using the epoch-folding method with the most up-to-date (radio or gamma-ray) orbital solution for each system. These solutions were based either on previously published works or recent observations from Nançay, the Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope, the Parkes Observatory, and Fermi -LAT. Results. We update or confirm radio and gamma-ray ephemerides for five of the presented systems. No optical pulsations were detected with a significance exceeding a 3 σ confidence level in any of our searches, despite achieving sensitivities close to the instrument’s limit. This places correspondingly stringent upper limits on the systems’ optical pulsed magnitude and conversion efficiency. Our upper limits are consistent with the pulsed optical luminosity of optical pulsations from the redback PSR J2339-0533. Compared to accreting and transitional MSPs, redback and black widow systems show much lower efficiency in converting their spin-down power into pulsed optical emission. This supports the recent suggestion that the accretion disk around the neutron star plays a role in accelerating the particles responsible for producing bright optical pulsed emission.

title: Quasi-doublets in the $3\alpha$ Spectrum of $^{12}$C
abstract: Abstract Within the three-$\alpha$ cluster model of $^{12}$C, we perform configuration-space Faddeev calculations of the low-lying $0^+$ and $2^+$ states. Resonance states are treated using a variant of the analytic continuation in the coupling constant (ACCC) method. The phenomenological Hamiltonian includes both two-body and three-body interactions. The recently proposed effective-field-theory-motivated leading-order (LO) $\alpha\alpha$ interaction is approximated by a Gaussian-type (LO-simulating) potential to reproduce the experimental $\alpha$--$\alpha$ scattering phase shifts.The parameters $(V,\beta)$ of the three-body force,$V_{3\mathrm{bf}}(\rho)= V \exp\!\left[-\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\rho}{\beta}\right)^2\right],$are determined by fitting the experimental spectrum of $^{12}$C. We investigate the possibility of a universal set of two- and three-body interactions capable of simultaneously reproducing the energies of lowest $0^+$ or $2^+$ states. For the $2^+$ levels, we find that the condition $\beta > 3$ fm must be satisfied for such universality.The ACCC method, combined with the effective-mass approach, reveals level anticrossing and demonstrates coupling between the $0_1^+$ and $0_2^+$ states, as well as between the $2_1^+$ and $2_2^+$ states, which can be interpreted as quasidoublet structures in the $3\alpha$ spectrum.The calculated results are compared with those obtained using the Ali--Bodmer potentials and the next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) interaction. We find that the LO-simulating potential reduces the strength of the three-body force required to reproduce the low-lying spectrum.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Non-equilibrium trace of the energy-momentum tensor and bulk viscous pressure of a massive gas from kinetic theory
abstract: Abstract We investigate the far-from-equilibrium dynamics of a relativistic massive gas obeying Maxwell–Boltzmann, Bose–Einstein, and Fermi–Dirac statistics, undergoing a boost-invariant Bjorken expansion. We solve the relativistic Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation (RTA) using the method of moments. We focus specifically on the time evolution of the trace of the energy-momentum tensor Θ μ μ and the bulk viscous pressure Π , quantities that are crucial for understanding the breaking of conformal symmetry in the rapidly evolving fireball created in heavy ion collisions. Our results demonstrate that the non-equilibrium values of Θ μ μ / T 4 exhibit non-monotonic behavior, characterized by a local maximum at early times and a distinct dip around the characteristic collision time scale τ R . We find that the scaled bulk viscous pressure Π / P 0 ( P 0 isotropic pressure) depends significantly on the particle statistics. Along with this, we also observe that the magnitudes of both the bulk viscous pressure and Θ μ μ / T 4 are significantly enhanced by a larger initial chemical potential. We further find that increasing mass strongly enhances both the normalized trace and the magnitude of the bulk viscous pressure. Finally, for ensembles of randomly perturbed non-equilibrium moment initial conditions, the scaled bulk viscous pressure and pressure anisotropy lose sensitivity to the initial conditions and approach common late-time trajectories but scaled trace is not converging to a common late time trajectory.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: FRANZ: Framework for analytical one-zone blast-wave dynamics
abstract: Supernova remnants (SNRs) and super bubbles (SBs) evolve in complex galactic environments shaped by various different processes. While classical modeling approaches successfully describe blast waves in uniform media, a unified framework capable of treating these environmental effects simultaneously is lacking. We aim to develop a flexible analytical framework for modeling blast-wave evolution in arbitrary environments and use it to investigate how large-scale galactic structure affects the dynamics and morphology of evolved SNRs and SBs. We introduce FRANZ (FRamework for ANalytical one-Zone blast-wave dynamics), a modular thin-shell model that follows the local evolution of a shock-surface segment in environments characterized by arbitrary density, velocity and gravitational fields. After validating the model against well-established analytical results, we applied it to study the effects of vertical stratification, galactic shear, and dense galactic substructures on blast-wave evolution. FRANZ reproduces the classical evolution of blast waves in uniform media while extending to complex environments. We derive criteria for disk break out in stratified media, characterize the timescales on which differential rotation deforms blast waves, and identify a new mechanism, that can suppress the momentum coupling in continuously driven blast waves. Interactions with dense filaments modify both shock-surface morphology and dynamics and confound the interpretation of the expansion history of observed remnants, which depends on the density distribution prior to the onset of explosions; the latter is fundamentally inaccessible from the observed state. In highly structured media with a high diffuse-gas volume-filling factor, ages inferred from the observed state may be systematically overestimated. FRANZ provides a computationally inexpensive and extensible framework for studying blast waves in realistic galactic environments. It offers a useful complement to numerical simulations for interpreting observations of evolved SNRs and SBs and for developing improved models of stellar feedback in large-scale simulations.
