title: Physics-constrained graph closures and working-point conditioning for a fast surrogate of linac beam dynamics
abstract: When a graph neural network estimates a physical quantity, its frame, edge direction, aggregation and feature normalization decide which laws it can break, and wrong choices leave systematic errors the loss never registers. We build a linac beam-dynamics surrogate on this observation. Space charge, short-range wakefields and coherent synchrotron radiation enter as bounded closures on analytic kernels; the graphs carry a frame and a direction dictated by the interaction; and their symmetry makes the net space-charge self-force vanish for any weights. Verified without training, with randomized weights, the invariants break by five to eight orders of magnitude once the responsible feature is inverted. Per-working-point models constrained by the rms envelope equation are distilled into one model conditioned on 15 machine settings. On the 18.4~m L0+L1 section of the Shanghai soft x-ray free-electron laser linac, this model predicts the transverse beam envelope at 50 unseen settings to about $7\%$, together with the centroid trajectory and emittance, in 0.38~s on a single Quadro RTX 6000 GPU. Training is instead dominated by a normalization choice, a data-derived output range for the beam size: at all 16 working points it lowers the starting error 2.2- to 8.5-fold and fixes the convergence speed. The remaining accuracy differences between hybrid and data-driven architectures vary with the working point and with the density of observation. The held-out error scales roughly as $N^{-0.6}$ with the corpus size $N$. Whether the physics pays off where collective effects are strong, as in a magnetic bunch compressor, is in the next phase of our study.

title: A hierarchical adaptive Fourier-feature physics-informed neural network for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma discharges
abstract: Abstract Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) are difficult to train for radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF-CCP) fluid--Poisson systems because missing initial conditions, steep sheath gradients, and strongly imbalanced residuals can lead to unstable or nonunique reconstructions. We propose a Hierarchical Adaptive Fourier-feature PINN (HA-FPINN) for such coupled plasma models. The method combines Fourier feature mapping to improve the representation of small-scale sheath structures, sparse physical anchors to provide interior constraints, and a two-level adaptive weighting scheme to balance the PDE, boundary, and anchor losses as well as individual equation residuals. The framework is tested on an 8-equation helium discharge model and a 23-equation electronegative \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) model. In the helium case, HA-FPINN reconstructs the space--time evolution of the main physical variables with \(1\%\) anchors and converges for all tested network architectures, with convergence times of \(110\)--\(246\) s. In the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case, HA-FPINN achieves stable reconstruction with \(5\%\) anchors, whereas the non-adaptive Fourier-feature PINN and standard PINN fail to converge under the same setting. The best performance in both systems is obtained at the tested Fourier frequency parameter \(\sigma=2.20\). Noise-injection tests show that HA-FPINN maintains the lowest reconstruction error in the helium case and preserves the main space--time structures in the \(\mathrm{Ar}/\mathrm{O}_2\) case up to \(15\%\) anchor noise. These results show that HA-FPINN provides a robust PINN formulation for strongly coupled plasma fluid models with missing initial conditions.

title: Jet-like dihadron correlations in OO and Ne--Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV with ALICE
abstract: Heavy-ion collisions are primarily studied to investigate the properties of hot and dense primordial nuclear matter, known as the quark--gluon plasma (QGP). However, recent observations of hydrodynamic flow--like behavior in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC suggest the possible formation of QGP droplets even in the smallest collision systems. To bridge the multiplicity gap between small and large systems and to examine the applicability of hydrodynamic descriptions, light-ion collisions have been studied for the first time at the LHC. This contribution presents dihadron correlation measurements in OO and Ne--Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV recorded with ALICE to explore possible medium effects. The width of the near-side correlation peak has been studied as a function of charged-particle multiplicity at midrapidity, showing a multiplicity-dependent modification of the widths in various transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}$) intervals in OO and Ne--Ne collisions relative to pp and pO collisions. Further, the per-trigger normalized relative yields of near-side and away-side correlations, $I_{\rm AA}$, are measured in OO collisions for the first time, while in Ne--Ne collisions, the measurement is performed for the near side only. The observed suppression of the away-side associated yield in OO collisions relative to pp collisions is qualitatively consistent with jet--medium interactions, albeit with a weaker magnitude than in central Pb--Pb. However, the extent to which other effects, such as event-selection biases and cold-nuclear-matter effects, contribute to the observed suppression in the present kinematic regime remains an open question.
authors: Neelkamal Mallick (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)
Joonsuk Bae (on behalf of the ALICE Collaboration)

title: Constraining Twin-Star Existence in Four-Parameter Maxwell Equation of State
abstract: Twin stars (TSs) are predicted to exist in nature if the hadron-to-quark phase transition is strong enough to form a new branch of hybrid stars, separated from the branch of neutron stars. It is essential to study the hybrid equation of states (EoSs) that can form TSs, with a primary focus on estimating the onset of the phase transition and its strength. We systematically study the TS scenario by adopting a four-parameter Maxwell-CSS approach to construct a large ensemble of Maxwell-type hybrid EoSs. Within this framework, we report the conditions on our parameter space imposed by the TOV solutions. For a fixed transition energy density and speed of sound for quark matter, we define distinct ranges of transition pressures based on the allowed strengths of discontinuity. Below a maximum transition pressure, a range of discontinuity exists that increases as the transition pressure decreases. Thereby, we identify the loci of the limits on discontinuities as the TS existence boundaries. Based on the causality limit, the TS existence boundaries can be truncated. Strong constraints on this picture are drawn from the CET, GW170817 and NICER. Within our considered model, we computed conditional extrema surviving the adopted $2\sigma$ filters---the maximum mass for TSs to be $2.05~M_\odot$, the allowed strongest discontinuity in rest-mass density to be $7.76\rho_\mathrm{sat}$, and the upper bound on transition rest-mass density to be $4.03\rho_\mathrm{sat}$. Subsequently, we compute the implications of the stiffness of the quark matter EoS on this picture. Different confidence levels for observational constraints are considered to assess the extent to which Maxwell-type EOSs remain compatible with the observations.

title: A Barnett-Like Effect in Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: The Barnett effect refers to the spontaneous magnetization or polarization of rotating matter via spin-orbit coupling, a fundamental phenomenon observed across a multitude of physical systems down to atomic scales. Here, we demonstrate that this effect extends to subatomic regimes within relativistic heavy-ion collisions, where the most vortical fluid ever created in terrestrial laboratories is produced and the orbital angular momentum is transferred to emitted hadrons via spin-vorticity coupling. By performing transport simulations spanning a broad energy range, we discover a nearly-linear scaling relation between the global spin polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons and the source tilt angle extracted via two-pion femtoscopic correlations. This scaling reveals that global $\Lambda$ polarization induced by the local vorticity field is modulated by the inclined geometry of the produced strongly-interacting nuclear matter in these collisions. Supported by existing experimental measurements, our results unravel a geometry-modulated Barnett-like effect at the femtometre ($10^{-15}$ m) scale.

title: Tidal contributions to neutron star orbital precession around Sgr $A^*$
abstract: We investigate tidal contributions to the orbital precession of neutron stars around the supermassive black hole Sgr A*, using stellar configurations described by the Tolman - Oppenheimer - Volkoff equations. We examine the dependence of tidal precession on stellar compactness, pericentre distance, and the quadrupolar tidal Love number $k_2$, and compare its magnitude with general relativistic orbital precession. The calculated tidal angular shift decreases strongly with increasing pericentre distance and, for the stellar configurations considered, with increasing compactness. Larger Love numbers enhance the tidal contribution. This behaviour reflects the strong dependence of tidal precession on the stellar-radius-to-pericentre-distance ratio, $(R/r_p)^5$. Despite the enhancement during closer encounters, the predicted tidal shifts remain extremely small, reaching approximately $3.5 \times 10^{-18},\mu as$ within the displayed parameter range. The ratio of tidal to general relativistic precession spans approximately $10^{-33}$ - $10^{-28}$, indicating that relativistic precession overwhelmingly dominates. Our results suggest that direct detection of the neutron-star tidal contribution through orbital precession around Sgr A* would be exceptionally challenging under the assumptions of the adopted model.

title: Neutron Star--Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
abstract: The orbital evolution of a neutron star and a much lower-mass primordial black hole can differ strikingly from that of typical compact binaries. Dynamical tides, analogous to those in the Solar System's giant planet-moon systems, can accelerate inspiral or induce outspiral, depending on the orbital configuration. We show how gravitational-wave emission mediates this evolution when neutron star modes remain locked in resonance with the orbit. These effects may leave observable signatures in pulsar timing or gravitational waves.

title: Maximization of accelerated charge in multibunch-driven plasma wakefield accelerators
abstract: Driving the plasma wakefield with a train of multiple particle bunches has the potential to significantly increase the accelerated charge, provided that the witness bunches also form a train. In this scenario, the driver bunches can replenish the wave energy after the passage of the witness bunches, yielding comparable charges in both trains. However, implementing this method at high wakefield amplitudes is complicated by the reshaping of the driver bunches as they reach radial equilibrium with the wave. The witness bunches cannot preserve their quality during this process; nevertheless, they must load the wave to prevent it from reaching the amplitude at which the wakefield period elongates and the wave destroys the driver. The proposed solution is to form an equilibrium train of initially inefficient driver bunches, which becomes efficient upon the injection of the witness bunches. This concept is demonstrated using the example of a self-modulating driver beam. Several factors favoring a high witness charge are identified: injecting additional ``phaser'' bunches at the zero-accelerating-field points, suppressing the formation of an electron halo around the plasma, and operating at the highest possible wakefield amplitudes.

title: Loss Factor of Axisymmetric and Rectangular Tapered Collimators from Optical to Inductive Regimes
abstract: In this work, we investigate the loss factor of axisymmetric and rectangular tapered collimators over a broad range of bunch lengths and geometrical parameters using the electromagnetic simulation codes ECHO and GdfidL. The calculations are performed for Gaussian bunches of rms length $\sigma_s$, with the collimator geometry characterized by the minimum and maximum apertures $b$ and $d$, taper length $L$, and chamber width $W$ for rectangular structures. For short bunches and tapered collimators with $d-b>b$, we extend the phenomenological formula previously obtained for axisymmetric to rectangular tapered collimators, describing the dependence of the loss factor on bunch length and taper geometry through an arctangent function of the scaling parameter $\mu d^2/(\sigma_s L)$. We demonstrate that this parameter is related to a Fresnel number and, by combining diffraction theory with the electrodynamics of the beam-induced image charge, analytically explain the factor of two between the coefficients $\mu=0.2$ and $\mu=0.4$ for axisymmetric and rectangular collimators, respectively. The resulting expression is applicable to rectangular collimators with $W/(2d) \geq 1.8$, extending its validity beyond the idealized flat geometry. For longer bunches, we identify the transition from the optical to the inductive regime and derive an analytical expression for the loss factor based on the cutoff wavenumber of the lowest relevant electromagnetic mode.

title: Gaia DR3 Compact Binary Candidates Constrained by Radial Velocity Measurements
abstract: Astrometry enables the most direct determination of the orbital elements and component masses of compact binaries. The potential of the current Gaia data for this purpose has not yet been fully explored. In this work, we combine Gaia astrometric and radial velocity (RV) measurements to perform joint orbital fitting for 1,835 Gaia astrometric binaries with available RV data. Among the 518 systems with at least three effective RV epochs, we identify 171 compact binary candidates, including four with inferred dark companion masses exceeding 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 22 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. These candidates provide valuable targets for future follow-up observations and Gaia DR4 analyses. We also flag 1,317 additional potential compact binary candidates with effective RV epochs less than three, including 84 with inferred companion masses above 2.1 $M_{\odot}$ and 173 between 1.4 and 2.1 $M_{\odot}$. More importantly, our results point to a large, currently hidden population of black hole and neutron star binaries that can be further explored with the forthcoming Gaia DR4 data and complementary follow-up observations.

title: Femtosecond Three-Dimensional Imaging of Single-Protein with Hard X-ray Laser
abstract: The extreme intensity of X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses has enabled imaging of radiation-sensitive samples, such as macromolecular microcrystals, beyond radiation damage limits. These sources have the potential to enable biomolecular single-particle imaging, similar to cryo-electron microscopy but without the need for cryo-fixation and with temporal resolution from femtoseconds to milliseconds. While this possibility was recognized before XFELs were built, the biological single-particle imaging work flow has previously only been demonstrated on large virus particles. Building on improvements in X-ray beam focusing, particle delivery, diffraction detection, and advanced analysis, here we demonstrate imaging of a single molecular complex, the giant-hemoglobin erythrocruorin (Ery) with X-ray laser pulses. Two-dimensional classes of diffraction patterns could be reconstructed to 15 Angstrom resolution, and 3D images to ~20 to 30 Angstrom, even though the 3D merged intensity in reciprocal space extended beyond 20 Angstrom. The resolution discrepancy is likely due to heterogeneity caused by gas-phase compaction of the complexes. With increased throughput, this approach could be used to reveal in-situ structural details during mass spectrometry studies of biomolecules, while improvements in sample delivery may provide ultrafast snapshot imaging of biological single-particles in their native-state beyond the limitations of radiation damage.

title: Constraining Nuclear Matter from Finite Nuclei: the Ab Initio Perspective
abstract: This review surveys recent developments in ab initio calculations of finite nuclei aimed at constraining the nuclear matter equation of state. Particular emphasis is placed on observables that connect finite-nucleus structure to bulk properties of nuclear matter, including neutron-skin thicknesses, electric dipole polarizabilities, and monopole sum rules. We discuss how neutron skins and dipole polarizabilities provide information on the density dependence of the symmetry energy, while monopole observables constrain the incompressibility of nuclear matter.

title: The Pion Parton Distribution Puzzle in the High x Region
abstract: We developed a new theoretical approach in the description of partonic structure of hadrons based on spectral function representation of valence quarks. In this approach massless valence quarks are considered in the mean field of residual hadron. This approach initially was applied to the calculation of parton distribution function~(PDF) of nucleons that resulted in an observation of pion-cloud structure of nucleon. In this report we present our calculation of pion PDF in the valence region within the same approach. In this approach we describe the soft partonic structure of pion through the valence $q\bar q$ cluster, embedded in the residual field of the pion. The pion PDF is calculated using phenomenological Light-Front wave functions for the $q\bar q$ cluster and the residual field. Our result indicates that the peak position of the x weighted valence PDF~(xPDF) depends on parameters characterizing the virtuality of the $q\bar q$ cluster and the mass of the residual system. These parameters are evaluated by fitting the calculated PDF to the height and the peak position of empirical pion xPDF at starting $Q_0$. They indicate that unlike the nucleon case, very little residual mass is needed in the pion to describe existing pion PDFs in the valence region. They also require the $q\bar q$-cluster to be highly virtual with the interacting quark carrying almost all of the momentum of the $q\bar q$ cluster. This picture is consistent with the dominance of the Feynman mechanism leaving little room for the hard component in the PDF. The calculation practically describes the $\sim (1-x)$ behavior observed recently at $x\to 1$ limit. Our non-trivial observation is that the height and the peak position of xPDF define the analytic behavior of valence PDF at $x\to 1$ limit.

title: L\'evy-stable pion emission sources in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV from the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid model
abstract: Revealing the space-time evolution of the quark-gluon plasma created in heavy-ion collisions is a central challenge, as this information is encoded in the properties of particles emitted at freeze-out. We reconstruct the pion emission source in Au+Au collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 200 GeV (0-5% centrality), simulated with the vHLLE+SMASH hybrid framework, which combines a Glauber Monte Carlo initial state, (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics, and a hadronic afterburner describing resonance decays and hadronic rescattering. Hanbury Brown-Twiss (HBT) interferometry is used to characterize identical-pion pair sources, which can also be reconstructed directly from the last scattering points of final-state particles in simulations. The projected pair-separation distributions in the Bertsch-Pratt out, side, and long directions are analyzed using a three-dimensional Levy-stable parameterization. Over the investigated fit range, extending to approximately 100 fm, a single Levy-stable function provides a satisfactory description of the distributions. The extracted Levy index, alpha approximately 1.5-1.6, is below the Gaussian value of 2 and increases slowly with transverse mass mT. At larger pair separations, the total source deviates from the fitted distribution, consistent with a halo contribution from long-lived resonance decays. Short-lived resonance decays and hadronic rescattering may contribute to the non-Gaussian shape through the Levy-walk phenomenon. The HBT radii Rout, Rside, and Rlong decrease with mT, qualitatively consistent with collective expansion. These results demonstrate the utility of Levy-stable femtoscopy for connecting hadronic-stage dynamics in hybrid simulations with experimentally accessible observables.

title: Dilepton azimuthal anisotropy from coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction in hadronic Pb-Pb collisions
abstract: Hadron-based event-plane estimators can be affected by nonflow and autocorrelation biases, especially at low multiplicity. Coherent $J/\psi$ photoproduction offers a complementary geometry reference through the correlation between quasireal-photon polarization and the reaction plane. We calculate the second-order dilepton coefficient $A_2$ relative to the reaction plane in hadronic Pb--Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.36$ TeV within an equivalent-photon and generalized vector-meson-dominance Glauber framework. Nuclear diffraction and two-source interference produce a pronounced transverse-momentum dependence, while the rapidity dependence is weak. We also compare two treatments of coherent scattering in the overlap region of the two colliding nuclei. Suppressing the contribution from this region reduces the yield and strengthens the integrated polarization--reaction-plane correlation, with the largest differences in central and semicentral collisions and smaller differences toward peripheral collisions. Joint measurements of the coherent yield and $A_2$ can constrain how hadronic interactions disrupt nuclear coherence and clarify the photoproduction mechanism. With sufficient tagged yields, azimuthal correlations involving decay leptons from photoproduced $J/\psi$ mesons could complement studies of collectivity, with potential future applications to small systems.

title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
abstract: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO~J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source towards M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multi-mission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at $L_{0.5-8.0\rm~keV}\sim10^{38}-10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few $10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of $\sim0.5$ day ($\sim$6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and non-flare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with marginal evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the non-flare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate mass donor at a persistently high rate with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically-regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.

title: Probing In-Medium Neutron-to-Dark-Fermion Conversion with Multimessenger Neutron Star Observations
abstract: Neutron stars provide a natural environment for probing in-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion and its impact on the dense-matter equation of state (EOS). We use multimessenger neutron star observations to map excluded and not-excluded regions of dark-sector parameter space for an EOS ensemble within a non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) framework and determine their overlap across the ensemble. We include a fermionic dark component with repulsive self-interactions of strength $G_\chi$. We consider masses $m_\chi$ near the neutron mass and heavier states accessible in neutron star cores at sufficiently large neutron chemical potentials. To reduce sensitivity to the nucleonic EOS within this framework, we scan $m_\chi=939$--$1500$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$100$ fm$^2$ across 21 nucleonic EOSs: a main baseline set of 13 EOSs and soft and stiff limiting cases. Stellar sequences are tested against the requirement that the EOS support at least $2M_\odot$ neutron stars, GW170817 tidal-deformability bounds, and NICER mass--radius constraints, considering the Illinois--Maryland and X-PSI/Amsterdam inference sets separately. For the full ensemble of 21 EOSs, both NICER analyses identify similar regions excluded by all EOSs, with approximate minimum--maximum extents of $m_\chi=939$--$1300$ MeV and $G_\chi=1$--$11$ fm$^2$. Unlike the full 21-EOS ensemble, the main baseline set has a common not-excluded region whose extent depends on the NICER analysis. The soft and stiff limiting cases show how these regions shift when the nucleonic EOS predicts a maximum neutron star mass near $2M_\odot$ or large tidal deformabilities. Across these 21 calibrated nucleonic RMF EOSs, weak dark-sector repulsion is robustly disfavored across a broad dark-fermion mass range, while the extent of the remaining not-excluded region depends on the NICER analysis and baryonic EOS stiffness.

title: On the assessment of the disk truncation and detection of type-II-like bursts from the accreting millisecond X-ray Pulsar IGR J17062-6143
abstract: We present a spectral analysis of the NuSTAR and NICER observations of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar IGR J17062-6143, performed in 2022. The source remained in the hard spectral state during these observations, with a luminosity of about $\sim$0.13-0.14 percent of the Eddington luminosity. The continuum emission of the NuSTAR spectrum is entirely dominated by a power-law component or by Comptonized emission of disc photons by a plasma with a high electron temperature ($\gtrsim100$ keV). The NuSTAR spectrum also reveals clear evidence of disc reflection, a broad Fe K line around 6-8 keV, and a Compton hump peaking at 20 keV, irrespective of the choice of the continuum models. Our spectral studies suggest a disk extending close to the neutron star surface ($\sim$6-20 $R_{\rm g}$) at low inclination angle ($\sim41$ degrees), as revealed by the self-consistent relativistic reflection model, relxill. In addition, we detected type-II-like bursts for the first time in the NICER observation of this source. Light curve profiles of type-II-like bursts exhibit different patterns, mostly associated with the so-called mode-0 and transition from mode-0 to mode-1 type-II bursts. The energy spectra of the persistent (pre-burst) and burst emission are well described by an absorbed Comptonization component, scattering disk- and blackbody-distributed photons, respectively, by a corona with a temperature of 1-3 keV. Although the origin of the type-II-like burst is not very clear, it has been possibly linked to disk-magnetosphere interaction of the accretion flow.

title: Core-Collapse Supernovae from Single and Binary-Stripped Massive Stars - I. Explodability and Nucleosynthesis
abstract: Binary interaction can substantially alter massive-star evolution and pre-supernova structure, changing core-collapse outcomes and nucleosynthetic yields. We compare explodability and nucleosynthesis in 66 non-rotating, solar-metallicity single-star and binary-stripped progenitors spanning zero-age main-sequence (ZAMS) masses of $11$-$45\,{\rm M}_\odot$, using the spherically symmetric PUSH framework and nucleosynthesis post-processing. Both populations explode up to $22\,{\rm M}_\odot$, with binary stripping altering explodability at higher ZAMS masses. Successful explosions span similar energies ($\sim$0.4-1.3$\,$B) and remnant masses ($\sim$1.4-2.0$\,{\rm M}_\odot$). The largest nucleosynthetic differences occur at low ZAMS masses, particularly for material undergoing explosive O and Si burning. The $^{56}$Ni yields and iron-group abundances broadly agree with observations of core-collapse supernovae and the metal-poor star HD 84937. When compared with calculations using time-dependent mixing-length theory and a two-parameter explodability criterion for the same progenitors, our results reveal substantial differences in explodability, with agreement on successful explosions for only 5 cases across all three approaches. Nevertheless, elemental yield patterns can remain broadly similar for models that explode successfully across treatments. Salpeter initial-mass-function-weighted yields of most elements differ by $\sim$20% between populations, with K enhanced by a factor of $\sim$3.4 in the binary-stripped population, driven by increased production in the lowest-mass progenitors. Binary-stripped models show closer agreement with empirical core-collapse S, K, and Ca abundance ratios relative to Mg inferred from APOGEE, while Na remains overproduced in both populations. Together, our results highlight the need to account for binarity when interpreting supernova abundance patterns.

title: Contributions of massive stars and classical novae to Galactic 26Al
abstract: The radioactive isotope 26Al is believed to be mainly produced by massive stars and ejected into the interstellar medium through their winds and supernovae. Due to its lifetime of 1.04 Myr, it traces recent nucleosynthesis and star formation. 60Fe is a similarly long-lived (lifetime 3.8 Myr) isotope, and only originating in ccSNe. Stellar evolution models in combination with Galactic Chemical Evolution (GCE) models tend to over-predict the 60Fe/26Al ratio. Population synthesis models that attempt to explain both, the 26Al mass in the Galaxy and its spatial distribution, only match the observational constraints with an enhanced star formation rate (SFR) of >5 Msun/yr. Classical novae may contribute to the 26Al production, potentially lowering the SFR inferred from massive stars and alleviating tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio. However, previous studies suggest their contribution is negligible or < 10%. In this work we aim to determine the mass distribution of 26Al as a function of Galactocentric radius and estimate the contribution of (very) massive stars and classical novae to the 1.8 MeV signal. We are using 20 yr of INTEGRAL/SPI observations of the gamma-ray line at 1.8 MeV to test different assumptions on the radial structure of 26Al and compare the resulting mass distribution to different GCE models. For our baseline analysis, all tested source models prefer substantial nova contributions, with best-fit fractions of 77-84%. This alleviates tension in the 60Fe/26Al ratio and lowers the SFR from 26Al measurements accordingly to 1-2 Msun/yr. While it is difficult to gauge both contributions directly, next generation MeV telescopes can potentially identify individual massive stars, such as Gamma-2-Velorum.

title: $El\ Ascua$: An ultra-luminous, radio-loud, Compton-thick AGN at $z\sim 3.8$ hiding in plain sight revealed by MINERVA multi-band MIRI observations
abstract: Heavily dust-obscured active galactic nuclei (AGN) are crucial for understanding supermassive black hole growth. Using multi-band MIRI photometry from the MINERVA survey, we report the discovery in the UDS field of an extremely mid-infrared bright Compton-thick AGN (CT AGN) at $z \sim 3.8$, \textit{el Ascua} (the Ember). The AGN and/or its host galaxy is detected at 870\,$\mu$m with ALMA and at 1.4\,GHz with the VLA. With UV-to-radio spectral energy distribution modeling, we estimate that the dusty host galaxy has a stellar mass of $\log\left( M_\star / M_\odot \right)=10.82 \pm 0.57$ and a star formation rate of ${\rm{SFR}} =157 \pm 8 \,M_\odot\,{\rm yr^{-1}}$, and we confirm the presence of a powerful dusty AGN with an intrinsic accretion luminosity of $\log\left( L_{\rm{acc}} /{\rm erg\,s^{-1}} \right)=47.12 \pm 0.58$. CT obscuration is revealed by comparing the upper limit on the X-ray luminosity over $2-10 \,{\rm{keV}}$ with the $6 \,{\rm\mu{m}}$ mid-IR AGN luminosity. We additionally find evidence for a radio excess by comparing its total IR-to-radio ratio to those of typical star-forming galaxies and radio-quiet AGN, implying that \textit{el Ascua} could be a rare radio-loud CT AGN. With an extremely high ratio between black hole accretion rate and SFR, the AGN is likely nearing the peak of a deeply obscured phase of black hole growth before AGN feedback blows away the obscuring material. Our work demonstrates the power of MIRI to reveal heavily obscured AGN missing from our supermassive black hole census.

title: PeV Diffuse Neutrinos from Magnetically Arrested Disks in Low-Luminosity Active Galactic Nuclei
abstract:
Radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAFs) in low-luminosity active galactic nuclei (LLAGNs) are promising candidates for the PeV astrophysical diffuse neutrino background (DNB), but how the magnetically arrested disk (MAD) state affects their neutrino output and what fraction of LLAGNs are in this state remain unclear. We present a comprehensive study of diffuse neutrino emission from the inner accretion flows of LLAGNs in the MAD state, including all three flavors and both hadronuclear ($pp$) and photohadronic ($p\gamma$) production channels. Assuming that $\sim 5\%$ of the accretion power is transferred to nonthermal protons, current IceCube data allow at most $2.3	imes10^{-3}$ of LLAGNs to have their inner accretion flows in a MAD state that can produce high-energy neutrinos. A lower fraction of the accretion power transferred to nonthermal protons would allow a proportionally larger fraction of such LLAGNs. Assuming that the comoving number density of low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) approximately matches that of LLAGNs in the MAD state, we also estimate a MAD fraction of $\simeq 1.6	imes10^{-3}$. The corresponding diffuse intensity is compatible with current IceCube data and testable by IceCube-Gen2. For this MAD fraction, the all-flavor diffuse intensity peaks at $E_
u\simeq1.5\,{m PeV}$ with $E_
u^2\Phi_
u\simeq2.6	imes10^{-9}\,{m GeV\,cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,sr^{-1}}$. Current IceCube data are beginning to challenge several predictions from previous LLAGN RIAF models, and the MAD component can become the dominant contribution from LLAGN accretion flows beyond the cutoffs of most earlier RIAF spectra considered here.%%%This constraint suggests that only a small fraction of LLAGNs are supplied with sufficient coherent net poloidal magnetic flux.

title: Differential measurements of $\gamma\gamma\to\tau\tau$ and constraints on $\tau$-lepton electromagnetic moments in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{_\text{NN}}} = 5.02$ TeV with ATLAS
abstract: This paper presents the first differential fiducial measurements of $\gamma\gamma\to\tau\tau$ using 1.93 nb$^{-1}$ of Pb+Pb data at $\sqrt{s_{_\text{NN}}} = 5.02$ TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector. Events in which one of the $\tau$-leptons decays into a muon and two neutrinos $\tau\to\nu_\tau\bar{\nu}_\mu\mu$ are selected and are categorized into three regions by the presence of an electron or either one or three charged-particle track(s) from the second $\tau$-lepton decay. The measurement is performed in events where both Pb ions remain intact and no neutrons are emitted. Differential cross-sections are measured for seven variables in three fiducial regions at particle level. The measurements are compared to theory predictions with different photon flux models and spin correlation effects. For the fiducial region with one muon and one electron in the final state, comparisons to next-to-leading-order electroweak predictions are also made. The transverse momentum ($p_\text{T}$) of the decay muon, the $p_\text{T}$ of the visible decay particles of the other $\tau$-lepton, the total $p_\text{T}$, invariant mass, and pseudorapidity of the visible particles from the di-$\tau$ system, and the rapidity and acoplanarity of the visible decay particles from either $\tau$-lepton are measured. A maximum-likelihood fit to the muon transverse-momentum distributions in the three regions before unfolding is performed to extract the $\tau$-lepton anomalous magnetic moment $a_{\tau}$ and electric dipole moment $d_{\tau}$, the latter for the first time in heavy ion collisions. The observed 95% confidence level intervals are $-0.057 <a_{\tau}< 0.035$ and $|d_{\tau}|< 2.7 \times 10^{-16}~e\text{cm}$.}

title: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
abstract: Nonlinear tides couple stellar oscillations and reshape the gravitational wave (GW) signal from inspiralling binaries. We present hydrodynamic simulations of nonlinear tides in inspiralling neutron-star binaries and, within a mode-coupling model, derive a semi-analytic quadrupolar fundamental mode-frequency shift through second order in the tidal strength. The two approaches agree in the perturbative regime, but diverge at stronger tidal fields, where perturbation theory breaks down. In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response. These effects make nonlinear tides a promising target for next-generation GW detectors.

title: Anisotropic flow measurements in OO and Ne-Ne collisions with ALICE
abstract: The LHC results have demonstrated that small collision systems can exhibit collective behavior reminiscent of that~observed in heavy-ion collisions, opening a new frontier for exploring the connection between nuclear structure and collective dynamics at ultra-relativistic energies. However, the interpretation of collectivity in small collision systems is limited by understanding the proton subnucleonic structure. The ${}^{16}$O and ${}^{20}$Ne collisions delivered by the LHC offer an opportunity to study the influence of nuclear geometry on anisotropic flow in systems where the nuclear structure is well-constrained. In this proceeding, measurements of the anisotropic flow of charged particles, $v_n$, in OO and Ne-Ne collisions involving up to eight-particle correlations are presented, using the multi-particle cumulant method. Furthermore, the first reconstruction of the probability distribution function of elliptic flow $P(v_2)$, and the first measurement of the ratio $v_3\{4\}/v_3\{2\}$ in light-ion collision systems are reported. These measurements provide deeper insight into the role of nuclear geometry-driven flow in light-ion collisions.

title: Updating GEANIE 239 Pu prompt γ -ray experimental data using a modern Hauser-Feshbach fission fragment decay model
Unfolding the low-energy reactor neutrino flux from CE$\nu$NS data with a finite Dirac sum
abstract: We present a novel method to analyze coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) data to extract the reactor antineutrino spectrum below the inverse beta decay threshold of 1.8 MeV, where it remains unmeasured. Adapting halo-independent analysis techniques developed for direct dark matter detection, we show how to obtain a best-fit and a pointwise confidence band for the integrated neutrino flux, without assuming a parametric form or smoothness prior for the spectrum. In our approach, which follows from convex geometry arguments, the differential neutrino rate is written as a linear combination of Dirac delta functions -- a finite Dirac sum (FDS) -- with a maximum number of terms determined by the number of data points. We apply our "FDS method" to mock CE$\nu$NS data for a low-threshold Ge detector and compare it with Tikhonov-regularized unfolding.

title: The renormalization of the shell-model neutrinoless double-beta decay operator starting from effective field theory at next-to-next-to-leading order
abstract: This paper is the continuation of a previous study, where shell-model calculations of the matrix elements for the neutrinoless double-beta decay were performed within a fully-consistent framework, starting from expressions of the nuclear Hamiltonian and decay operators which have been derived through chiral perturbation theory. The decays under our investigation are those involving 48Ca, 76Ge, and 82Se, as in our earlier analyses of electroweak nuclear decays with Hamiltonians and operators derived within effective field theory. In this work we focus on perturbative properties of the chiral expansion of the decay operator, namely in assessing the weight of terms beyond the leading order on the nuclear matrix elements of medium-mass candidates. To this end, we have constructed effective shell-model decay operators starting from two-body currents up to next-to-next-to-leading order and, for the first time, we introduce for nuclei of experimental interest contributions of the three-body current operators, which emerge at next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order of the chiral perturbation theory. Our investigation is aimed to evaluate the theoretical uncertainties affecting the calculated nuclear matrix elements of the neutrinoless double-beta decay, by conjugating the estimate of the inaccuracy related to the finiteness of the degrees of freedom of the nuclear model and the truncation of the chiral expansion of the decay operator.

title: Is XTE J1814-338 a dark matter-admixed neutron star?
abstract: We explore the possibility that the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338 is a dark matter-admixed neutron star (DNS) based on a general-relativistic two-fluid approach, in which one fluid describes ordinary nuclear matter and the other dark matter. The equations of state of nuclear matter and dark matter are described by the Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) theory with realistic three-body forces and a generic bosonic self-interacting dark matter model, respectively. Based on the observational data, we determine the parameter space for XTE J1814-338 as a DNS, and find that only a halo stellar configuration with a high dark matter fraction is allowed. Furthermore, we predict other observable properties of XTE J1814-338 and provide robust lower bounds for these quantities.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian Inference on the Intrinsic Event Rate of Type I Gamma-Ray Bursts from the Fermi/GBM Catalog
abstract: Abstract The intrinsic event-rate of Type I gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) as a function of redshift, provides a probe for the binary neutron star (BNS) merger population. However, the abovementioned inference is complicated by instrumental selection effects, the lack of redshift measurements for the majority of GRBs, and uncertainties in jet geometry. In this work, we applied a hierarchical Bayesian inference framework to the Fermi/GBM Type I GRB catalog to reconstruct the underlying event-rate population. This framework accounts for the selection effects and marginalizes over the limited-information posteriors of individual GRB redshifts and jet structures. The population model uses the parameterized luminosity function, distribution of jet structure parameters, the Madau-–Dickinson star formation rate and a delay-time distribution of BNS mergers. The posterior distribution of the hyperparameters in the model are to be inferred, using a GPU-accelerated MCMC algorithm. The intrinsic event rate density as a function of redshift is constrained up to z = 5, which a local rate density of R 0 = 22 . 6 − 10.6 + 15.0 Gpc − 3 yr − 1 , which is consistent with the latest gravitational-wave measurements.

title: From binding and saturation to criticality in nuclear matter with lattice effective field theory
abstract: We investigate the interaction dependence of the liquid-gas critical point of symmetric nuclear matter in finite-temperature lattice effective field theory. Building on the pinhole-trace algorithm, we benchmark a first-order perturbative treatment for representative Hamiltonian splittings and then compute the finite-temperature equation of state for a sequence of sign-friendly lattice Hamiltonians ranging from an SU(4)-symmetric interaction to Hamiltonians with physical S 0 1 and S 1 3 channel dependence and three improved leading-order Hamiltonians. The finite-temperature analysis is complemented by zero-temperature calculations of the symmetric-matter saturation point and the binding energies of selected nuclei within the same lattice framework. We find that the benchmarked perturbative strategy is quantitatively reliable in the thermodynamic regime studied. Across this Hamiltonian sequence, the leading order Hamiltonians improve the overall description of finite-nucleus binding energies and move the zero-temperature saturation point toward the empirical region, while lowering the critical temperature from 15.33(6) to 13.50 ( 17 ) – 13.71 ( 19 ) MeV. These calculations show that finite-temperature criticality is not fixed by zero-temperature saturation and binding alone, and they provide a complementary benchmark for future lattice interaction development.

title: CREMA: Collinear Resonance for Exotic Molecules and Atoms
abstract: The Collinear Resonance for Exotic Molecules and Atoms (CREMA) setup has been developed and commissioned at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology's Laboratory for Nuclear Science. The instrument combines the Doppler-suppressed resolution of the collinear fast-beam geometry with the selectivity of resonance ionization, for precision measurements of hyperfine structure and isotope shifts in atoms and molecules. We describe the setup, including the ion-optical simulations in which a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm provided the starting settings for the beam transport, and report commissioning measurements of the hyperfine structure of 133Cs. The extracted hyperfine constants agree with literature values within one standard deviation, demonstrating the operational readiness of the setup. CREMA mirrors the Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy Experiment at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams and serves as its offline counterpart for the development of laser ionization schemes and techniques for future studies of exotic atoms and molecules.

title: Analysis of the elastic scattering cross-sections within the halo and non-halo configurations of 8 B and 11 Be projectiles
abstract: Abstract The optical model (OM) formalism inherently omits the structural properties of weakly bound nuclei, owing to its restriction to an effective two-body description. By assuming the halo and non-halo configurations of 8B and 11Be projectiles on two quite different mass targets, 64Zn and 208Pb, we introduce an approach that explicitly incorporates the ground-state structure of a weakly bound projectile by embedding its wave function into the projectile-target nuclear potential through a double-folding formalism. The resulting potential successfully reproduces the suppression of the Coulomb-nuclear interference peak observed in elastic scattering, which is commonly attributed to coupling with breakup channels. Moreover, incorporating the halo structure into the OM significantly improves the agreement with experimental elastic-scattering data. These results for weakly bound nuclei demonstrate that an accurate description of elastic scattering requires an OM that explicitly accounts for the projectile's structure.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Revised analysis of the strengths of the contact potential at N4LO through nuclear and neutron matter
abstract: We examine the contact three-nucleon force at N4LO expressed as a density dependent potential. In Ref. [1], the necessary couplings (13, including two that appear in the leading three-nucleon force), were extracted from nd scattering observables. The contact strengths obtained through the three-nucleon continuum, without ?ts to the triton, seem incompatible with the energy of nuclear and neutron matter. We take the opportunity to revisit the role of the cD, cE couplings of the leading three-nucleon force in nuclear matter and nuclei. We close with a discussion about recent ?ttings of three-nucleon scattering observables using a spectroscopic basis for the subleading contact three-nucleon force. Using the errors given for the couplings in the spectroscopic basis, we derive uncertainty bands for the strengths in the operator basis and their contributions to the leading and subleading three-nucleon contact interactions.

title: Quantum Complexity and Stabilizer-State Expansions: From Pairing to Deformation in Fermionic Systems
abstract: Understanding how collective phenomena such as pairing and deformation emerge in interacting fermionic systems, and how the correlations underlying them shape the resources required for their simulation, is a central challenge in many-body physics. We investigate various aspects of quantum complexity in a fermionic system exhibiting two main forms of collectivity, specifically deformation and pairing, through entanglement, non-stabilizerness, and fermionic non-Gaussianity. In the deformed phase, high entanglement coexists with low non-stabilizerness, while the superfluid pairing phase, by contrast, exhibits substantial multipartite entanglement and non-stabilizerness, together with maximal fermionic anti-flatness. In a second step we examine how to describe the phase diagram of the system in a classically scalable and symmetry-preserving way, by combining stabilizer-state expansion and variational basis optimization. A physics-guided decomposition of the Hamiltonian identifies the relevant stabilizer states, which can be constructed from graph states. A single stabilizer state captures the deformed phase to a large extent, and, although the number of stabilizer states required to describe the pairing phase grows exponentially with system size, a symmetry-preserving basis rotation yields a high-fidelity approximation using far fewer states. This rotated state can then serve as a practical starting point for quantum refinement.

title: Probing the Dependence of Partonic Energy Loss on the Initial Energy Density of the Quark Gluon Plasma
abstract: Considerable evidence now exists for partonic energy loss due to interaction with the hot, dense medium created in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. A primary signal of this energy loss is the suppression of high transverse momentum $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ hadron yields in A-A collisions relative to appropriately scaled $pp$ collisions at the same energy. Measuring the collision energy dependence of this energy loss is vital to understanding the medium, but it is difficult to disentangle the medium-driven energy loss from the natural kinematic variance of the steeply-falling $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ spectra across different $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}$. To decouple these effects, we utilize a phenomenologically motivated spectrum shift model to estimate the average transverse momentum loss $\Delta p_{\mathrm{T}}$ imparted on high $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ partons in A-A collisions, a proxy for the medium induced energy loss. We observe a striking correlation between $\Delta p_{\mathrm{T}}$ and Glauber-derived estimates of initial state energy density $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{Bj}}$, consistent across two orders of magnitude in collision energy for a variety of nuclear species. To access the path-length dependence of energy loss, we couple our model to geometric event shape estimates extracted from Glauber calculations to produce predictions for high-$p_{\mathrm{T}}$ hadron elliptic flow $v_2$ that agree reasonably with data.

title: Newtonian I-Love-Q relations: An enthalpy-based approach
abstract: We present a pedagogical introduction to the I-Love-Q relations within Newtonian gravity using an enthalpy-based formulation of stellar structure. Introducing the specific enthalpy converts Euler's equation into a first integral of hydrostatic equilibrium and recasts the equation of state as a relation between the mass density and the enthalpy. Together with Poisson's equation, these relations provide a unified description of spherical equilibrium and deformations induced by rotation and tides. We illustrate the formalism with polytropic equations of state and a relativistic free Fermi gas. In Newtonian gravity, slow uniform rotation and a weak tidal field excite the same linear quadrupolar response, yielding the exact identity $\bar I^{\,2}\bar Q/\bar\lambda\equiv1$ for the dimensionless (``bar'') observables---independently of the equation of state. This exact identity is distinguished from the approximate universality of the pairwise I-Love-Q relations, whose residual dependence on stellar structure is illustrated by the models considered in this work.

title: Accessing exotic hadronic states via charmed-meson femtoscopy in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
abstract: The two-particle correlation function measured in femtoscopic analyses provides access to the interaction potentials between emitted particles. This offers a unique opportunity to investigate interactions among charmed mesons and to explore the nature of possible exotic hadronic states. In this Letter, we study femtoscopic correlations of various charmed-meson pairs in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The dynamical evolution of the system and charm hadron production are described within the Parton-Hadron-String Dynamics (PHSD) transport approach, while the correlation functions are computed using the Correlation Analysis Tool using the Schrödinger equation (CATS). We demonstrate that heavy-ion collisions provide a significantly more favorable environment than $pp$ collisions for accessing charmed meson femtoscopic correlations. This arises from enhanced charm-quark production, reduced relative momenta due to in-medium energy loss, and a strong suppression of initial-state correlations. Our results indicate that femtoscopic measurements in heavy-ion collisions offer a sensitive probe of charmed meson interactions and possible hadronic molecular states.

title: Systematic Study of Neutrino-Nucleus Interactions for the DUNE Experiment
abstract: The recent generation of high-precision neutrino oscillation experiments, such as the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE), relies on the accurate reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to determine fundamental parameters like Charge-Parity (CP) violation and the neutrino mass hierarchy. The use of Liquid Argon, introduces significant theoretical complexities. This dissertation provides a investigation into neutrino-nucleus scattering phenomenologies, connecting fundamental electroweak theory with computational simulations using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. The study evaluates the limitations of traditional frameworks, such as the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model, specifically addressing the Axial Mass parameter and its impact on the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel. By comparing baseline RFG predictions against experimental data from MicroBooNE, this research quantifies the necessity of advanced many-body nuclear frameworks. The implementation of the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) model, Random Phase Approximation (RPA) screening, and the SuperScaling Approximation (SuSAv2) are systematically analyzed to resolve kinematic biases. Additionally, the impact of modernized phenomenological constraints, including the updated $M_A^{RES} = 0.96$ GeV for resonant pion production and the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates for Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), is evaluated. Furthermore, this research integrates university extension initiatives by developing and presenting macroscopic 3D-printed educational models, consisting of a Linear Accelerator (LINAC) analog and a scattering experiment, and finally presenting it into the festival "Mais Ci\^encia Por Favor".
authors: L. F. B. M. Rodrigues (Federal University of Alfenas
F. G. Gardim (Federal University of Alfenas

title: Local correlation formula based on the liquid-drop model for the energy released in proton radioactivity
abstract: Based on the liquid-drop model, we propose and refine a local formula for the released energy of proton radioactivity ( Q p ) . The calculated results for 44 proton emitters with 71 ≤ Z ≤ 91 are in good agreement with the experimental data. For comparison, the WS4 [Phys. Lett. B 734, 215 (2014)] and FRDM [At. Data Nucl. Data Tables 125, 1 (2019)] nuclear mass models are also employed. The root-mean-square (rms) deviations between the experimental data and theoretical results obtained from this work, WS4, and FRDM are 0.071 MeV, 0.144 MeV, and 0.348 MeV, respectively. These results demonstrate that the present approach reproduces the experimental Q p values well in the considered region. The formula is further employed to predict the released energies for candidate proton emitters, and the predictions are broadly consistent with those of the other models.

title: Flavored $S_{3}$ Non-Minimal Left-Right Symmetric Model
abstract: In this work we investigate fermion masses and flavor mixings in a non-minimal left-right symmetric model endowed with the non-Abelian discrete symmetry $S_3$. The scalar sector contains three Higgs bidoublets, while one left-handed and one right-handed triplet generate Majorana neutrino masses. Assigning the first two fermion families to an $S_3$ doublet and the third family to a singlet, together with a specific alignment of the bidoublet vacuum expectation values, leads to a common and analytically tractable structure for the fermion mass matrices. We study both the pseudomanifest and manifest left-right realizations, in which the fermion mass matrices are complex symmetric and Hermitian, respectively, and derive analytical expressions for the left- and right-handed CKM and PMNS mixing matrices. A numerical likelihood test shows that the model successfully reproduces the observed quark and lepton mixing patterns for both normal and inverted neutrino mass orderings at the level of oscillation data. Remarkably, the manifest scenario emerges as a more restrictive realization of the pseudomanifest one, with the main distinction residing in their CP-phase structure. We further explore the phenomenological consequences for the neutrinoless double-beta decay, the muon anomalous magnetic moment, and the lepton-flavor-violating decay $\mu\to e\gamma$. The right-handed contribution exhibits the characteristic dependence on the heavy-neutrino and $W_R$ mass scales, while flavor corrections are found to be subleading over most of the allowed parameter space. These results show that an $S_3$ flavor symmetry can simultaneously organize fermion mixing and lead to distinctive low-energy signatures within left-right symmetric theories.

title: Strangeness-changing two-body weak currents from SU(3) chiral dynamics
abstract: We know of no microscopic calculation of the semileptonic strangeness-changing 2p2h current. We construct it at tree level for nubar [NN] -> l+ Y N' from vertices of the lowest-order SU(3) chiral Lagrangian: contact, meson-in-flight, baryon-pole and kaon-exchange families, both pn line assignments summed coherently, and decuplet poles with N -> Delta transition form factors and SU(3) route signs. The undressed vector current is the Noether current of the flavour rotation and satisfies the SU(3)-limit Ward identity pointwise. The axial current has a vertex-level kaon-pole completion fixed by the Goldberger-Treiman relation, whose divergence equals (m_s+m_u)P_su by construction; we omit the axial contact operator, its kaon-pole partner, and the remaining inverse-propagator and mass-splitting terms, and the form factors break the vector identity. The flavour routes allow a primary kaon-less Sigma+ n final state from a pp pair that no one-body weak vertex reaches; antisymmetrised, it is 1.13-1.20% of the isolated two-body hyperon rate over the seven charge channels. In a factorised free-pair benchmark, octet baryon poles carry 77% of the Lambda-channel incoherent family sum at 0.6 GeV but 43-58% at 1-5 GeV, where the decuplet carries 26-48%; the line assignments interfere destructively. The isolated two-body current is 0.81-0.87 times as Lambda-rich as the quasi-elastic one at 1-5 GeV (0.67-0.95 across prescriptions); the axial contact operator with its kaon-pole partner at the Lagrangian coefficient lowers this by 2-6%, and a Ward-compatible form-factor dressing changes it by about 4%. A correlation on every meson changes the composition by under 3%; a Landau-Migdal contact on the pions alone leaves kaon exchange unscreened and roughly triples Lambda/Sigma0. The KNY couplings carry the axial N -> Y flavour combinations, so the composition is not the quasi-elastic one rescaled.

title: Orientational average in nuclear shape imaging: densities, correlations, and eccentricity in Ne-20
abstract: The orientational treatment of deformed nuclei in high-energy nuclear collisions have two ways, a rigid rotor and a wave-function rotor, in which nuclear densities in laboratory frame are constructed differently. We calculate the one- and two-body densities (including Pauli blocking effects), body-axis contour multipoles, and geometric eccentricity variances under a leading-order ultracentral mapping for Ne-20 in a deformed harmonic-oscillator model in the rigid and wave-function rotors. At fixed deformation parameter $\kappa$ in the model, the two constructions can give different laboratory radial moments and pair correlations. The body-axis transition-kernel contours in the wave-function rotor are generally more compact along the symmetry axis, and $\beta_{20}$, $\beta_{40}$, $\langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle$ and $\langle\varepsilon_4^2\rangle$ lie below the rigid-rotor results in a wide range of $\kappa$. The relations among these quantities in each rotor are nevertheless similar in most scanned parameter space: $\beta_{40}$ and $\langle\varepsilon_2^2\rangle$ depend linearly on $\beta_{20}^{2}$, while the hexadecapole baseline-subtracted variance follows an approximate quadratic trend in the quadrupole one. The method can be extended to seek more sensitive quantities for rotational effects in the wave-function rotor.

title: Bayesian analysis of the Coulomb breakup of C19
abstract: Coulomb breakup is a common experimental technique to study the structure of halo nuclei. Coupling a halo effective field theory (Halo-EFT) description of these nuclei to accurate reaction models provides an ideal tool to analyze such experiments. In particular, it enables us to sample the space of the low-energy constants of this EFT within a Bayesian approach. This allows us to infer nuclear-structure information from the reaction data in a systematic and reliable way. Moreover, it provides an estimate of the uncertainty on those structure observables. We apply this to re-analyze the Coulomb breakup of $^{19}$C measured on Pb at 67 MeV/nucleon in RIKEN [T. Nakamura et al. Phys. Rev. Lett. 83, 1112 (1999)]. We obtain a new and more accurate value for the one-neutron separation energy $S_n(^{19}\mathrm{C}) = 0.60 \pm 0.02$ MeV and an improved estimate of the asymptotic normalization constant of its bound state $C_{1/2^+} = 0.85 \pm 0.02$ fm$^{-1/2}$. In addition, we estimate the uncertainty related to other model inputs at about 15% on both structure observables.

title: Photoproduction of K 0 Σ + off protons in the resonance region
Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering Simulation Using GENIE Event Generator
abstract: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) relies on the precise reconstruction of incident neutrino energy to extract oscillation parameters. The use of Liquid Argon introduces significant theoretical complexities due to nuclear effects. This work evaluates neutrino-nucleus scattering models using the GENIE Monte Carlo event generator. We demonstrate the limitations of the Relativistic Fermi Gas (RFG) model in the Charged Current Quasi-Elastic (CCQE) channel and its reliance on an inflated Axial Mass to match experimental data from MicroBooNE. We show that transitioning to advanced many-body frameworks, specifically the Local Fermi Gas (LFG) supplemented with Random Phase Approximation (RPA), is needed. Additionally, we evaluate the impact of the 2021 Bodek-Yang parameter updates on Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS), concluding that modernized constraints are a prerequisite for mitigating systematic biases in DUNE.

title: Exploring the influence of microscopic nuclear densities and collective excitations on 16 O-induced fusion cross sections
A Unified Model for Radioactive Signatures and Source Identifiability in Neutron Star Mergers
abstract: Late light curves of neutron star mergers can contain substantial fission power while remaining compatible with different radioactive inventories. We develop a unified source attribution model in which a common bounded response formulation links nuclear heating, radiation transport and isotope identification. Within particle dependent deposition and gray photon escape, matched luminosity comparisons show how long alpha and fission responses become aligned. Explicit competing inventories then reproduce a light curve with a substantial $^{254}$Cf contribution, with smooth evolution of the beta luminosity response providing an important source of compensation. We derive optimization certificates and collective likelihood bounds that quantify the resulting limits on identification under specified source and ejecta constraints. We also introduce an energy conserving model with two radiation frequency groups to resolve the information carried by color at fixed total luminosity precision. Its exact response modes identify the source adjustments that absorb color contrast, while a residual color floor characterizes the contrast retained by the permitted family. Late observations of AT~2023vfi with the James Webb and Hubble Space Telescopes provide an observational benchmark: the reference and retained alternatives predict bolometric declines about 1.5 quoted uncertainties shallower than the reconstruction, while differences between inventories containing and excluding $^{254}$Cf remain within the reported decline uncertainty. The unified model provides a quantitative basis for connecting nucleosynthesis predictions, gravitational wave constraints and the temporal and spectral information in merger observations to radioactive source attribution.

title: QubiC 2.0: An Extensible Open-Source Qubit Control System Capable of Mid-Circuit Measurement and Feed-Forward
abstract: Researchers manipulate and measure quantum processing units via the classical electronics control system. We developed an open-source FPGA-based quantum bit control system called QubiC for superconducting qubits. After years of qubit calibration and testing experience on QubiC 1.0, we recognized the need for mid-circuit measurement and feed-forward capabilities to implement advanced quantum algorithms, and upgraded the system to QubiC 2.0 on an AMD ZCU216 RFSoC evaluation board with all these enriched features. The system uses portable FPGA gateware with a simplified processor to handle commands on-the-fly. For design simplicity and straightforward scaling, we adopted a multi-core distributed architecture, assigning one processor core per qubit. The pulses combine the unique pulse envelope and carrier information specified in a command. Each pulse envelope is pre-stored in the FPGA's block RAMs, ensuring speed and reusability throughout the quantum circuit, while pulse parameters including amplitude, phase, and frequency can be updated from pulse to pulse. The software stack is developed in Python, running on both the FPGA's ARM core and a host computer via XML-RPC. Quantum circuits can be described in a high-level language supporting both pulse-level and native-gate-level programming with high-level control flow constructs, and are compiled into binary commands loaded into the FPGA. With QubiC 2.0, we achieved multi-FPGA synchronization and low-latency data communication, and demonstrated feed-forward experiments on conditional circuits. The system also serves as a platform for artificial intelligence and machine learning driven quantum control, such as FPGA-based real-time quantum state discrimination. The enhanced QubiC system provides researchers with powerful tools to explore and implement advanced quantum algorithms and applications.

title: Synchrotron-based Photonuclear Neutron Source for Energy, Medicine and Radiation Testing
abstract: Neutron source availability is constrained by the declining number of research reactors and the challenging cost of spallation facilities, while compact accelerator-based sources remain limited to beam powers below 100~kW due to severe thermal loads from charged particle-target interactions. Here we demonstrate that synchrotron-driven photonuclear production overcomes this fundamental limitation through architectural decoupling: electrons circulating in a storage ring generate MeV-range synchrotron radiation that drives external neutron production targets, completely isolating targets from primary charged-particle power. This separation enables continuous-wave photon beam powers exceeding 200~kW per beamline while drastically reducing localized heating and reducing thermal shocks. Through systematic Monte Carlo optimization across three independent codes (OpenMC, MCNPX, FLUKA), we identify optimal target configurations delivering single-beamline neutron intensities of $3$--$13 \times 10^{14}$~n/s with inherent spectral tunability: low-Z targets (Be, D$_2$O) produce epithermal-to-thermal spectra for medical applications, while high-Z converters (W, U) generate fast neutrons for subcritical reactors. Multi-beamline architecture enables facility-scale outputs exceeding $6 \times 10^{16}$~n/s, being competitive with research reactors, while supporting simultaneous parallel

title: Radiation damage and recovery of SiPMs exposed to low-momentum muon beams for innovative scintillation-based muon beam monitors
abstract: Silicon PhotoMultipliers (SiPMs) are among the standard devices for light detection in scintillator detectors. Some detector designs require these devices to be placed in radioactive areas or directly exposed to particle beams. Specifically, the damage from exposure to low-momentum muons is particularly important, as they have a high energy deposit and they have several applications in material science and particle physics. Eight SiPM models from different manufacturers were exposed to 29 MeV/c positive muons, with an intensity of O(10^6) muons/s for 13 hours, maximising the charge deposited in the depletion region. I-V curves were measured before/after irradiation and annealing; DCR and crosstalk analyses are ongoing, to extract dark count rate and optical crosstalk. Despite showing a measurable increase in dark current, the devices preserved operational stability. Thermal annealing has also been tested by heating the devices at 125{\deg}C, showing a recovery of the optimal SiPM features. This work is part of a collaboration between the University of Pavia and ISIS, to develop detectors for low-momentum muons (< 40 MeV/c), based on thin scintillators.

title: Initial performance of the Radar Echo Telescope for Cosmic Rays: Pathfinder for a next-generation neutrino detector
abstract: The Radar Echo Telescope for Cosmic Rays, a pathfinder instrument for the radar echo method of ultrahigh energy neutrino detection, was initially deployed near Summit Station, Greenland, in May 2023. After a four-week commissioning period, nine days of data were taken before the instrument went offline. In this article, we describe the instrument as it was deployed, and the initial performance of the detector. We show that the technical aspects of running a radar-based particle cascade detector in the ice have been demonstrated. Analysis of the 2023 data informed improvements that were incorporated into the May–August 2024 deployment, which has just concluded at time of writing. Results from the 2024 run will be presented in forthcoming publications.
