In symmetric matter at saturation density and zero temperature, the peaks of the three $u$ quark distributions move toward larger $x$ and fall least for the unpolarized distribution and most for the transversity distribution, so the spin-dependent $u$ quark distributions are modified more strongly. Between vacuum and saturation density, the axial charge of the proton drops from $1.28$ to $0.844$, and the tensor charge of the $u$ quark decreases while that of the $d$ quark grows in magnitude. At the center of each nucleus, the axial charge of the proton rises from $0.699$ in $^{40}$Ca to $0.817$ in $^{208}$Pb as the central baryon density decreases, which suggests that the modification at the center follows the central density rather than the mass number.

title: Parameter Constraints on $f(R^{1+\epsilon},T_{\mu\nu}T^{\mu\nu})$ Gravity from Exotic Compact Objects
abstract: According to General Relativity (GR), gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Although GR has been highly successful in describing gravitational phenomena, exotic compact objects with high mass and strong gravitational fields, as well as low-mass objects, have motivated the study of modified theories of gravity. One of the modified gravity frameworks is $f(R,T^2) = R^{1 + \epsilon} + \alpha \kappa^2 T_{\mu \nu} T^{\mu \nu}$, which provides an extension of GR by introducing modifications to both the geometric and matter sectors. In this study, we investigate the mass-radius structure, physical viability, and stability of quark stars in $f(R,T^2)$ gravity using the MIT Bag Model equation of state. We compare results from the exact $f(R,T^2)$ model, its first-order Taylor expansion, and GR. The values of the gravity parameter $\epsilon$ and $\alpha$ are constrained by evaluating the ability of the model to reproduce the observed mass-radius configurations of compact objects, including HESS J1731-347 with a mass of $M = 0.77_{-0.17}^{+0.20} \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 10.4_{-0.78}^{+0.86}$ km, GW190814 with a mass of $M = 2.6 \, M_{\odot}$, PSR J1614-2230, with a mass of $M = 1.928 \pm 0.017 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R > 10$ km, and PSR J0437-4715, with a mass of $M = 1.418 \pm 0.037 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 11.36_{-0.63}^{+0.95}$ km. We assess the physical viability and stability of the stellar configurations using the energy conditions (strong, weak, null, and dominant) and the speed of sound. Overall, the $f(R,T^2)$ gravity model can accommodate quark star configurations and reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects, particularly those associated with GW190814 and the lightest compact object observed, HESS J1731-347, respectively.

title: Formation and Detectability of PSR J0653+0443-like Extremely Eccentric Binary Neutron Stars in the Milky Way
abstract: Recently, the Five-hundred-meter-Aperture-Spherical-radio-Telescope (FAST) Galactic Plane Pulsar Snapshot (GPPS) survey discovers an extraordinary binary neutron star (BNS) system, PSR J0653+0443, possessing the highest known orbital eccentricity ($e\approx0.992$) among Galactic BNSs (Yang et al., 2026), which provides a unique probe into the formation and evolution of BNSs. In this Letter, we perform compact binary population synthesis calculations with self-consistent neutron star spin evolution to model extremely eccentric BNS population detectable by the FAST GPPS survey, explicitly incorporating observational selection effects. We find that BNSs with $e>0.99$ constitute only $\sim0.6\%$ of the detectable population, with an expected detection number of $\lambda_{\mathrm{GPPS}}\approx0.31$ over the full planned footprint. Thus, although rare, systems as eccentric as PSR J0653+0443 are compatible with standard binary evolution. We further demonstrate that extremely eccentric BNSs arise preferentially from core-collapse supernovae, whereas imposing $P\lesssim0.1$ s select older, more frequently recycled systems, which naturally reproduce the observed properties of PSR J0653+0443. We further predict that the completed GPPS sample has a $\sim15\%$ chance of finding another $e>0.99$ BNS, but a much higher $\sim88\%$ chance for $e>0.90$ systems. By contrast, future facilities are expected to enlarge the detectable highly eccentric BNS population, with SKA potentially detecting PSR J0653+0443-like systems and sub-mHz gravitational-wave detectors probing a larger population with $e>0.9$, enabling much more in-depth population-level constraints.

title: Exploring PSR J0901-4046 as an ultra-slowly rotating neutron star versus a white dwarf
abstract: The source PSR J0901-4046 shows a very long rotational period, of $\approx 75.88$ s. In fact, its long period suggests that it could be a white dwarf. We examine the properties of the source and compare the outcomes under the hypotheses of the source being a highly magnetized white dwarf (B-WD) and neutron star. We find that assuming it to be a B-WD with a surface field $\sim 10^{10}$ G explains many properties, including its storage/rotational energy, explaining luminosity. On the contrary, the neutron star-based idea, particularly if examined under the conventional spin down mechanism, requires an unusually high surface magnetic field $\gtrsim 10^{14}$ G, even exceeding $10^{16}$ G, depending on the obliquity angle and emission mechanism. The source also sits very close to AR Sco, a white dwarf pulsar, in the period and period-derivative plane. We suggest that the source is a B-WD. Along with AR Sco, it being a B-WD constrains the death line model. B-WD hypothesis alleviates the necessity of an unusually high magnetic field hindering pair production for PSR J0901-4046 under the neutron star hypothesis. We argue that some rotation-powered pulsars with extreme properties may possibly be white dwarfs rather than neutron stars.

title: Chandra and Multiwavelength Study of Pevatron Candiate HESS J1702-420A
abstract: Aims: HESS J1702-420A is a promising Galactic PeVatron candidate whose physical nature remains unknown. Previous XMM-Newton observations revealed hard, apparently extended X-ray emission from XMMU J170147.3-421407, offset from the center of the TeV source, suggesting a possible pulsar wind nebula (PWN) association. We aim to resolve its X-ray morphology, investigate compact-object candidates in the field, and assess their possible association with HESS J1702-420A. Methods: We obtained three new ACIS-I observations from the Chandra X-ray observatory (CXO) with a total exposure of 50.4 ks. We performed imaging, source detection, spectral and variability analyses, and multiwavelength (MW) machine-learning (ML) source classification. Neutron star (NS) candidates were further investigated using deep near-infrared and radio imaging. Results: The Chandra observations resolve XMMU J170147.3-421407 into a faint point-like source, Src11 (CXO J170144.5-421415), and asymmetric diffuse emission comprising eastern and western lobes. The X-ray spectral, variability, and MW properties of Src11 and the diffuse emission are consistent with those commonly observed in pulsar/PWN systems, further supported by the ML classifications. However, the asymmetric diffuse morphology is unlike a typical bow-shock/tail or jet/torus PWN, and the $\sim7'$ offset from HESS J1702-420A makes a firm physical association difficult to establish. A possible shell-like radio structure north-west of Src11 may indicate a more complex PWN/SNR environment. Other NS candidates are less consistent with a pulsar/PWN interpretation, making Src11 the most compelling candidate in the field.

title: Axial Perturbations of Extended Tolman III in the New $f(R,T)$ Theory
abstract: We investigate compact objects using the extended Tolman III equation of state in the framework of $f(R,T)=R+2\chi T$ gravity. In the matter sector of the Lagrangian density, we employ a new formalism based on the evaluation of the second-order derivative of the matter Lagrangian with respect to the metric \cite{Jayawiguna:2026das}. We analyze the corresponding observational signatures through axial gravitational perturbations including stellar stability and gravitational echo. We find that the effective potential in $f(R,T)$ gravity is wider and deeper than its counterpart in general relativity (GR). The quasinormal-mode (QNM) frequencies are calculated using the Bohr--Sommerfeld (BS) fitting and both the lower- and higher-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB) approximations. For the ultracompact configurations considered, trapped modes can tunnel through the potential barrier, giving rise to gravitational-wave echoes. The imaginary parts of the QNM frequencies are found to be negative, $\Im(\omega_n M)<0$, indicating that the perturbations decay exponentially with time. Our results show that the echo train in GR contains more echoes than that in $f(R,T)$ gravity. Finally, assuming that the stellar object is a neutron star and adopting a stellar radius consistent with measurements by the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), we find that the $f(R,T)$ gravity model yields a characteristic frequency consistent with the estimated frequency associated with GW170817 for $\beta= 4.663\times10^{-1}$ and $\chi=0.96\pi$, whereas the corresponding GR model does not exhibit comparable agreement.

title: $\gamma$hosts from the past: reheating neutron stars with supernova-sourced ALPs
abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) can be copiously produced in the hot and dense environment of a core-collapse supernova. If their mass is within an order of magnitude of the supernova temperature, a non-negligible fraction of them will remain gravitationally bound to the neutron star remnant. This basin of ALPs can then decay to photons over the lifetime of the neutron star, thereby reheating it. Using the measured luminosities of several neutron stars, we close multiple windows in ALP parameter space while also satisfying the SN 1987A cooling constraint on the ALP-nucleon coupling. In particular, using the 35000 K upper limit on the temperature of the coldest neutron star observed, PSR J2144$-$3933, we derive the strongest upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling for 1$-$400 MeV ALP masses. Ceilings on these limits arising from ALP decays occurring within the neutron star lifetime may be overcome by using younger neutron stars such as the one in Cas A, probing couplings orders of magnitude higher. Observations of a $2000 \, {\rm K}$-hot neutron star in infrared observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope could reach ALP-photon couplings three orders lower and ALP masses one order lower than our current limits.

title: Machine Learning Neutrino-Nucleus Cross Sections II: More Leptons
abstract: Neutrino-nucleus cross sections are essential inputs for long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, yet remain challenging to model with high precision. Recent work demonstrated that fully black-box data-driven cross-section models cannot accurately generalize between near- and far-detector fluxes, but imposing Standard-Model symmetries via structure-function parameterizations provides a well-posed learning problem in a simplified DUNE-inspired muon-neutrino disappearance analysis. Here, we extend this framework to multiple lepton flavors and both neutrino and antineutrino beam modes, incorporating the electron appearance channel and enabling a simultaneous determination of $\sin^2\theta_{23}$, $\Delta m^2_{31}$, and the CP-violating phase $\delta_{\rm CP}$. We find that the learned cross section model recovers the injected oscillation parameters without significant bias, with constraints comparable to those obtained using the exact underlying cross section. Flux uncertainties have more significant effects in the multi-channel case, and incorporating flux nuisance parameters into the learning problem is required for accurate results. Our results demonstrate that this data-driven approach can be extended to the multi-channel measurements needed for long-baseline neutrino oscillation analyses.

title: ULTRAMAN: A Proposed ultrasound detector for macroscopic dark matter
abstract: We propose ULTRAMAN (ULTRAsound Macro ANalyzer), a passive ultrasound array experiment designed to search for macroscopic dark matter (macros) through coherent acoustic disturbances generated as compact objects traverse a controlled target medium. Unlike existing dark matter detectors that primarily rely on scintillation, ionization, or other signatures of energy deposition, ULTRAMAN exploits the acoustic response of matter to reconstruct individual highly supersonic trajectories using synchronized multielement ultrasound arrays. The framework connects macro stopping power and interaction cross section to the resulting acoustic pressure, while the expected event rate probes the macro mass and abundance. A genuine candidate would appear not as an isolated radio frequency spike, but as a correlated multichannel track consistent with a single highly supersonic passage through the target. Representative macro, nuclearite, axion quark nugget, and primordial black hole benchmarks are shown to occupy distinct regions of the resulting acoustic observable space. Existing ultrasound technology offers a realistic route to an event-level terrestrial search for macroscopic dark matter, with null observations translating into complementary constraints on its parameter space.

title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
abstract: Turbulence in magnetically confined plasmas is inherently quasi-two-dimensional and can exhibit both inverse and forward energy transfer across scales. Experimental evidence for cross-scale energy transfer in the hot plasma core has, however, remained scarce. Understanding such energy transfer is crucial because it governs turbulent transport, which directly impacts confinement quality of fusion plasmas. Here we report experimental evidence consistent with forward energy transfer associated with core-edge coupling in tokamak turbulence. We combined multichannel collective Thomson scattering (CTS) and radially localized Doppler backscattering (DBS) to resolve cross-scale fluctuation dynamics. The results reveal that a quasi-coherent mode (QCM) originating from the edge is also present in the core and resonantly couples with broadband turbulence, producing significant forward energy transfer and characteristic secondary instabilities. These combined measurements indicate that quasi-two-dimensional tokamak turbulence can support a net energy transfer from ion to electron scales through cross-scale wave-wave interactions, contrary to the inverse cascade paradigm of idealized two-dimensional turbulence. Such a plasma regime is attractive for fusion reactors, as it avoids large edge-localized modes (ELMs) that damage first-wall components and maintains high confinement quality even in the presence of high-Z impurities.

title: Ongoing and Post-Mass-Transfer Binaries: A Living Catalog and Unified Review of Binary Mass Transfer Products
abstract: Mass transfer is arguably the most defining interaction in binary stellar systems, yet many aspects of its physics remain poorly understood, from stability to endpoints and observable products. Comparing theory and observations is challenging because post-mass-transfer systems are studied across largely independent communities with different methods, nomenclature, and evolutionary frameworks. % We present a unified review and catalog of ongoing and post-mass-transfer binaries spanning the full stellar mass range, but restricted to systems likely to have experienced only a single episode of mass transfer (i.e., only one component is evolved). We review 16 observational classes of binary interaction products and compile a curated sample of 5,452 systems into a publicly available, community-driven catalog at https://binary-observations.github.io/post_mt_catalog/. % Using this catalog, we investigate global trends in orbital periods, eccentricities, masses, and mass ratios across post-mass-transfer binaries. We find I) non-zero eccentricities are common at all periods and system classes, with both median values and scatter increasing with period, II) the $e(\log P)$ relation depends on donor progenitor mass, with neutron-star and black-hole binaries showing the highest median eccentricities, likely reflecting effects of natal kicks, III) period distributions are broad and overlapping across evolutionary channels, and IV) the Gaia BH and NS systems are extreme in mass ratio but otherwise consistent with the general post-mass-transfer population. Together, these results support a unified empirical view of post-mass-transfer binaries that highlights several tensions between theory and observations.

title: Charting the Galactic Underworld II: Strategies for Identifying BHs and NSs with LISA
abstract: Stellar-mass black holes (BHs) and neutron stars (NSs) observed by space-based gravitational-wave detectors offer constraints on binary stellar evolution that are complementary to those from ground- based detectors. The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to detect hundreds of double compact objects (DCOs) containing a BH or NS, but distinguishing these sources from the far more numerous double white dwarfs (WDWDs) may prove challenging. We use adaptive importance sampling with COSMIC to synthesise large populations of BHBH, BHNS, NSNS, BHWD, and NSWD binaries. We combine these binaries with a Milky Way star-formation history and integrate their Galactic orbits with cogsworth, repeating our simulations for a grid of variations in uncertain (binary) stellar physics. We find that LISA detections are largely insensitive to the changes in Galactic position resulting from natal kicks. We then assess how well chirp mass, eccentricity, distance from the Galactic plane, and orbital frequency distinguish BH- and NS-hosting DCOs from WDWDs, accounting for LISA measurement uncertainties. Using chirp mass alone distinguishes only 50-60% of BHBHs and BHNSs, and ~40% of NSNSs, but combining this with orbital frequency recovers 90-100% of BHBHs and BHNSs and around ~50% of NSNSs, with eccentricity further improving the recovery of NSNSs to around 60-70%. Distance from the Galactic plane adds little discriminating power, though it can recover a handful of NSWDs that are missed otherwise. These methods will help identify a significantly larger number of BHs and NSs in LISA data that would be missed by a chirp mass cut alone.

title: Dihadron Transverse-Spin Asymmetries in Muon-Deuteron Deep-Inelastic Scattering
abstract: In 2022, the COMPASS collaboration performed semi-inclusive measurements of deep-inelastic muon-scattering on a transversely polarized deuteron ( LiD 6 ) target. From these data, transverse-spin-dependent dihadron asymmetries are extracted using pairs of oppositely charged hadrons. These asymmetries are directly sensitive to the quark transversity distributions and provide an independent handle on these fundamental quantities with respect to the Collins asymmetries measured in single-hadron production. The present results significantly improve upon the previous COMPASS deuteron measurements, which were the only available deuteron data worldwide, and reach a statistical precision comparable to that of the existing proton results from COMPASS. A small but nonzero asymmetry is observed at large Bjorken- x , consistent with theoretical expectations. A point-by-point extraction of the valence-quark transversity distributions yields, in particular, a substantially improved determination of the d -quark transversity. These measurements represent a major step towards a complete flavor mapping of the transverse-spin structure of the nucleon.

title: Real-time CXRS analysis on HL-3 tokamak with reliable neural networks and cross-device transfer learning
abstract: Abstract We present a neural network-based method for real-time charge exchange recombination spectroscopy (CXRS) analysis on the HL-3 tokamak. To enhance model performance and reliability, we tailor the network architecture to the physical characteristics of CXRS spectra: the receptive field matches the Doppler-broadened line width, channel embedding encodes spatial awareness across diagnostic channels, and attention pooling focuses on the most informative spectral regions. These designs yield millisecond-level inference (0.56 ms per 32-channel) with accuracy comparable to conventional methods ( R 2 _ T i = 0.93, R 2 _ v t = 0.98). Furthermore, the model’s reliability is established through interpretability and uncertainty analysis. Interpretability analysis confirms that the model focuses on the Doppler-broadened wings of C VI for T i and tracks line shifts for v t , consistent with physical principles. Uncertainty estimates show that the model appropriately expresses higher uncertainty in regions where predictions are inherently more challenging. To address data scarcity on new devices, transfer learning from HL-2A tokamak markedly boosts performance in low-data regimes while retaining a modest advantage even with full HL-3 data, provided that the spectra are properly aligned and baseline subtracted. This work establishes a real-time, reliable, and data-efficient AI framework for CXRS analysis, offering a practical path to deploy machine learning approaches in plasma control on future fusion devices.

title: First observation of anisotropic distribution evolution of hydrogen fast ions heated by ICRF in EAST
abstract: Abstract The continuous energy and pitch-angle distribution of hydrogen fast ions generated by ion cyclotron range of frequencies (ICRF) minority heating is measured in EAST using an imaging neutral particle analyzer (INPA). The measured two-dimensional fast-ion distribution exhibits a triangular structure: as energy increases, the pitch-angle distribution becomes progressively narrower, with its peak located around 0.4 < | v ∥ / v | < 0.5 . This behavior is consistent with resonance localization theory, which associates the pitch-angle peak with trapped orbits whose turning points are close to the ion cyclotron resonance layer. Through diagnostic response correction, the reconstructed spectrum shows a progressive enhancement of the high-energy minority-ion tail with rising ICRF power. A clear anisotropic evolution of the fast-ion distribution is also observed between discharges with different electron-temperature profiles. In the discharge with higher core electron temperature, the signal enhancement appears mainly for fast ions at energies above 100 keV and | v ∥ / v | ⩾ 0.5 , together with a broader measured pitch-angle distribution. This behavior is interpreted as the combined result of collisional pitch-angle scattering, fast-ion accumulation, and finite-orbit-width effects. The enhanced signal region corresponds to wide-orbit fast ions whose inner orbit legs extend to the hotter inner plasma region, making them more sensitive to changes in the electron-temperature profile. These results demonstrate the capability of INPA to resolve the anisotropic evolution of ICRF-heated fast ions and provide experimental insight into the optimization of ICRF heating schemes in EAST and future fusion devices.

title: Proton and neutron elastic scattering on He targets from ab initio symmetry-adapted no-core shell model optical potentials
Prospects For A New Light Nuclei, Fission Fusion Energy Cycle
abstract: Future advanced nuclear rocket propulsion, and the availability of new nuclear power cycle designs, will benefit substantially from the large current investment in alternative nuclear energy that is underway today. We propose a new nuclear cycle which includes the primary fission of lithium-6, followed by secondary fusion of deuterium and tritium, and a secondary fission of lithium-7 by tritium. This cycle does not produce nuclear waste from its nuclear fuel, since all byproducts of these cascade reactions are stable, provided that the triton production during the primary reaction is fully consumed in the secondary reactions. This cycle may, however, activate surrounding technical materials from its neutron flux. This light-element nuclear fuel is readily obtained through the ongoing expansion of the lithium mining industry and electric vehicle (EV) battery recycling industries.

title: Helium Detection in Technical Materials
abstract: Materials used to study nuclear fusion can retain atmospheric helium unless pretreated before an experiment. Understanding helium outgassing is important for accurate diagnostics in experiments surrounding nuclear fusion. The presence of helium is often cited as the primary evidence that a nuclear reaction has occurred, so it is imperative that known sources of helium are mitigated prior to proceeding with novel nuclear experiments. It is also necessary to ensure hermiticity when transferring gas aliquots from an experiment to a mass spectrometer. In this article, we present studies of detecting helium leak rates in systems used in novel nuclear experiments. We also present studies of helium retention in materials subjected to various heating profiles and atmospheric concentrations. Without pretreatment, stainless-steel 316 retains between 15 $\unicode{x2013}$ 240 pmol of $^{ 4}$He or an areal outgassing amount of 0.07 $\unicode{x2013}$ 1.20 pmol/$cm^{ 2}$. It also may reabsorb $^{ 4}$He from the atmosphere in time. These studies also demonstrate that it is necessary to pretreat most materials prior to performing experiments where the presence of $^{ 4}$He is being used as an indicator for novel nuclear reactions.

title: B$_{4/2}$ anomaly related to the shape coexistence in $^{94}$Zr
abstract: Solutions of the Bohr-Mottelson Hamiltonian with a sixth-order anharmonic oscillator potential, for both axially-symmetric and $\gamma$-unstable deformations, are applied to investigate the lowest states of the $^{94}$Zr nucleus. The experimentally observed $B_{4/2}$ anomaly is explained, within the present approach, by the presence of a coexistence between an approximately spherical shape ($2_{1}^{+}$) and an axially-symmetric deformed one ($4_{1}^{+}$). On the other hand, the energies of the $0_{2}^{+}$ and $2_{2}^{+}$ states and their associated electromagnetic transitions fit better a dynamical triaxial deformation configuration ($\gamma$-unstable). This overall picture of the lowest states in $^{94}$Zr corresponds to a triple shape coexistence scenario.

title: Radiative decay and electromagnetic moments in 229 Th determined within nuclear density functional theory
Astrophysical constraints on hadron-quark crossover in hybrid neutron stars
abstract: We investigate astrophysical constraints on hybrid neutron-star equations of state constructed by combining an extended linear sigma model description of quark matter with several representative hadronic equations of state through a smooth hadron--quark crossover. Four different hadronic models are examined in order to explore the model dependence of the resulting hybrid equations of state. After imposing stability, causality, perturbative QCD matching, tidal deformability, and maximum-mass constraints, only the eLSM+GMSR(BSK16) construction remains fully consistent with current astrophysical observations. The surviving parameterizations are further constrained using Bayesian inference based on NICER mass--radius measurements and the GW170817 gravitational-wave event. The posterior distributions favor a broad hadron--quark crossover occurring at relatively high baryon densities, while the formation of extended pure quark cores is strongly disfavored. Instead, the current observations favor neutron stars containing an extended mixed hadron--quark transition region. We also investigate the implications of the inferred maximum-mass distribution for the secondary object of GW190814 and find that, within the present model and adopted observational constraints, its interpretation as a neutron star is unlikely.

title: The FAST tool for synthetic SXR calculations and determination of impurity density and effective charge ( Z eff )
abstract: Abstract A new soft x-ray (SXR) synthetic tool has been developed: it is called FAST for FLYCHK-based Atomic physics and SXR Tomography. It is based on FLYCHK SXR emissivity spectra calculated for a variety of elements, from deuterium to tungsten. FAST creates 2D plasma emissivity for arbitrary plasma compositions and plasma profiles. It computes line-integrated SXR profiles based on a specific detector geometry and response. This tool is used to reproduce signals from an absolutely calibrated multi-energy SXR (ME-SXR) camera at WEST. Thanks to its energy-resolved measurement capability, the ME-SXR camera is able to separate spectral regions dominated by impurity line emission from others containing only continuum emission. At WEST, FAST and the ME-SXR camera are employed to determine impurity density profiles for tungsten and nitrogen (used as a proxy for low- Z impurities), as well as the plasma effective charge ( Z eff ), through SXR measurement reproduction at different energies, from 2 to 14 keV. Tungsten density is determined in two plasma scenarios at WEST: lower hybrid heating in the X -point radiator regime and lower hybrid heating with modulations of ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH). In the first scenario the tungsten profile is found to be moderately peaked in the core with a concentration of 0.8–1 × 10 −4 . This concentration is found to increase up to 1.4 × 10 −4 during ICRH. Tungsten peaking factor in steady-state conditions is also retrieved and compared to theoretical predictions. It is found to be slightly lower than the combined neoclassical and turbulent transport prediction.

title: Global polarization of $\Lambda$, $\Xi^{-}$, and $\Omega^{-}$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions at RHIC BES-II energies
abstract: We investigate the global spin polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons and the multi-strange hyperons $\Xi^{-}$ and $\Omega^{-}$ in Au+Au collisions across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan II (BES-II) energy range, $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=7.7$--$27$ GeV. The polarization is computed using the modified Cooper--Frye formula, which includes contributions from thermal vorticity, the thermal shear tensor, and the gradient of the baryon chemical potential, combined with the (3+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic framework CLVisc with SMASH initial conditions. We present the global polarization as a function of collision energy, centrality, transverse momentum, and rapidity. We find that the global polarization of $\Omega^{-}$ is systematically larger than those of $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^{-}$ because of its larger spin quantum number, but it remains below the central value of the recent STAR measurement. This discrepancy may suggest that additional mechanisms, such as spin correlations among strange quarks inside the $\Omega^{-}$, could contribute to the observed $\Omega^{-}$ polarization. We also find that the global-polarization splitting between hyperons and anti-hyperons increases toward lower collision energies and is dominated by the chemical-potential-gradient contribution.

title: Experimental determination of the double $K$-shell vacancy creation probability in the electron-capture decay of $^{55}$Fe with a microcalorimeter
abstract: The probability of double \(K\)-shell vacancy production following electron-capture decay is determined for $^{55}$Fe using a high-resolution microcalorimeter. The \(K\)-hypersatellite lines arising from double \(K\)-shell-vacancy filling are directly resolved within the measured spectra of X-ray emissions which are dominated by Mn \(K\)-X-ray diagram lines. The energies of the Mn \textit{K}-hypersatellite lines, \(K\alpha_2^h\), \(K\alpha_1^h\), and \(K\beta_{1,3}^h\), are measured as $(6143.5\pm0.5)$ eV, $(6162.1\pm1.5)$ eV and $(6811.9\pm2.6)$ eV, respectively. The relative intensities of \textit{K}-hypersatellite to diagram X-rays are measured to be $(1.30 \pm 0.07) \times 10^{-4}$. From the relative intensities together with established fluorescence yield values, the probability of double-vacancy creation per \(K\)-shell capture ($P_{{KK}}$) is determined as $(1.22 \pm 0.09) \times 10^{-4}$. Comparisons with previous experimental results and theoretical calculations are discussed.

title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.

title: Reformulation of the pionless effective field theory for practical few- and many-body applications
abstract: The effective field theory (EFT) of contact forces which describes few-nucleon systems at distance scales larger than the pion Compton wavelength ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ can be defined in terms of momentum-dependent potentials that contain a fixed number of simple poles and generate the effective-range expansion to a given fixed order. These potentials provide a practical generalization of the standard ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ power-counting scheme which, for instance, naturally accounts for the large effective ranges in the s-wave channels. Nucleon-nucleon phase shifts computed in this formulation of ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ are compared to modern phase-shift analyses, and effective-range parameters are tabulated. The ${\rm EFT}({\pi\hskip-0.54em /})$ potentials, which provide a rational approximation of the S-matrix, are easily extended into the regime of pion physics through the inclusion of additional S-matrix poles and zeros, and provide an accurate description of data up to pion-production threshold. The potentials in this scheme are in an important sense weak over all relevant distance scales, and are therefore of utility for systematic calculations of many-nucleon observables.

title: Nuclear lattice effective field theory as a testing ground for $\alpha$-cluster structures in ${}^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$
abstract: The framework of nuclear lattice effective field theory (NLEFT) is applied to $^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$, with the perspective of obtaining a model-independent density map of the geometry of a sample of excited states of the nucleus. The Hamiltonian incorporates Wigner SU(4)-symmetric nuclear forces as well as the Coulomb interaction. The coupling constants of the spin-isospin symmetric nucleon-nucleon potentials have been adjusted in order to reproduce the experimental ground-state (g.s.) energy of $^{24}\mathrm{Mg}$ as well as the experimental Tjon ratio between the binding energies of $^3\mathrm{H}$ and $^4\mathrm{He}$. The ensuing parameter set turns out to be capable of capturing the experimental trend of the binding energy per nucleon, reproducing simultaneously within 1% deviation the measured values for $^{18}\mathrm{F}$, $^{22}\mathrm{Na}$, $^{26}\mathrm{Al}$, $^{28}\mathrm{Si}$, $^{30}\mathrm{P}$ and $^{32}\mathrm{S}$. Considerations based on the convergence rate of Euclidean-time extrapolations for the two lowest energy eigenvalues highlight the dual nature of the $0_1^+$ and $2_1^+$ states, of hybrid mean-field and $\alpha$-cluster type. For the latter, triaxial $\alpha$-cluster configurations seem to be favoured over the axially-symmetric ones, whereas oblate superdeformation might characterize a rotational band at $20$ MeV excitation energy.

title: Magnetization by Rotation: Spin and Chiral Condensates in the NJL Model
abstract: The role of spin degrees of freedom in the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) has attracted significant interest in recent years. Spin hydrodynamics extends conventional hydrodynamics by incorporating spin via the spin tensor. In the mean-field limit of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model under rigid rotation, spin degrees of freedom manifest naturally as axial-vector, or spin, condensate. We investigate the interplay between chiral and spin condensates in this framework. While rotation typically suppresses the formation of a chiral condensate, the presence of a spin condensate may counteract this effect, enhancing the chiral condensate. Moreover, it can alter the nature of the chiral transition from second to first order.

title: Anisotropic flows of light-flavor and charmed hadrons in Pb+Pb collisions at energies available at the CERN Large Hadron Collider
abstract: We apply a constituent quark equal-velocity combination (EVC) model to study the elliptic flow ( v 2 ) and triangular flow ( v 3 ) of light-flavor and single-charmed hadrons in Pb+Pb collisions at s N N = 2.76 and 5.02 TeV. v 2 , 3 of hadrons in the EVC model can be expressed as a linear superposition of the v 2 , 3 of quarks at the same velocity as that of the hadrons. We find that available experimental data for v 2 and v 3 of p , Λ , Ξ , and Ω as a function of transverse momentum ( p T ) can be consistently explained by the EVC formula using the v 2 of up/down quarks and the v 2 of strange quarks. In comparison with v 2 data of ϕ at s N N = 2.76 TeV, which can be naturally explained by the v 2 of strange quarks, explanation of the data of ϕ mesons at s N N = 5.02 TeV requires an additional contribution of two-kaon coalescence, which indicates approximately 20% influence of final-state hadronic rescattering on v 2 of ϕ at s N N = 5.02 TeV. Using v 2 and v 3 of light-flavor quarks obtained in studying light-flavor hadrons and v 2 and v 3 of charm quarks determined from D 0 meson data, we apply the EVC model to predict the anisotropic flows of D s + , Λ c + , Ξ c 0 , and Ω c 0 and compare them with the available experimental data. The preliminary data for v 2 of D 0 , D s + , and Λ c + at s N N = 5.36 TeV are found to be naturally described by the EVC model.

title: A Reproducible Benchmark and Evidence-Retrieval Software Framework for Silicon Detector R&D Literature
abstract: Silicon pixel detector R&D depends on a large and rapidly growing technical literature, including beam-test and irradiation studies, performance measurements, simulation, and design reports. Locating the supporting evidence passage for a measurement, operating condition, or design decision is therefore a computing and data-science challenge for detector-development workflows. General-purpose language models are insufficient unless grounded in traceable primary sources, particularly in a domain with specialised terminology, configuration-dependent measurements, and rapidly evolving experimental results. We address this with a reproducible, general-purpose framework for evidence-grounded retrieval over technical literature, using silicon pixel detector R&D as a demanding validation domain. The framework combines sparse lexical retrieval, dense semantic retrieval, and hybrid reciprocal-rank fusion, with an optional graph-guided exploration layer and grounded, abstention-aware response generation. The accompanying benchmark provides manually curated chunk-level evidence annotations, source-level diagnostics, semantic relevance checks, and negative-query abstention tests over two detector query sets. We evaluate six retrieval configurations across 378 source documents and 8,442 indexed chunks. Hybrid sparse-dense retrieval gives the strongest strict evidence recovery, achieving Hit@5 of 0.917 on the core benchmark and 0.951 on the curated extension benchmark, while graph-based methods are more effective for literature exploration and source discovery. Graph expansion is therefore best employed as a discovery layer over the hybrid retrieval backbone. The framework provides reusable software for traceable, 1 evidence-grounded knowledge access in silicon detector R&D and high-energy physics instrumentation.

title: Recent upgrades to the CRIS Decay Spectroscopy Station: Accessing $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy on pure isomeric beams
abstract: The Decay Spectroscopy Station (DSS) of the Collinear Resonance Ionization Spectroscopy (CRIS) experiment at ISOLDE-CERN has been upgraded to perform isomer-selective $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy, including a new tape system to perform spectroscopy, free from residual activity. The baseplate of the detection chamber was redesigned to incorporate the tape, a MicroTOF detector for beam diagnostics, and a custom-made, high-vacuum-compatible plastic scintillator. The vacuum operation reached a stable pressure of $10^{-7}$ mbar in the detection chamber, overcoming vacuum issues from the previous design. Around the detection chamber, up to three high-purity germanium (HPGe) detectors and four LaBr detectors can be installed, giving a total photopeak efficiency of the HPGe detectors of 7% at 200 keV. The implementation of a 24-channel digital DAQ system combines the detection array with the CRIS setup to perform laser-assisted $\beta$- and $\gamma$-ray spectroscopy. A commissioning experiment with isomeric beams of $^{106g,106m}$In, purified by narrow-band laser resonance ionization, showed complete removal of activity from the $\beta$ detector and full separation of the ground and isomeric state of $^{106}$In. An average $\beta$-detection efficiency of 19(2)% was determined from the experiment.

title: Cryogenic scintillation veto for $0\nu2\beta$ bolometric experiments: from a concept to BINGO prototypes
abstract: Achieving a very low, ideally zero, background level, along with ensuring high energy resolution and detection efficiency, are the main tasks in the development of the next generation of experiments to search for neutrinoless double beta ($0\nu2\beta$) decay. Cryogenic scintillating bolometers meet these basic requirements perfectly. The main ideas pursued in the BINGO (Bi-Isotope $0\nu2\beta$ Next Generation Observatory) project are the use of a cryogenic scintillation anti-coincidence veto, the minimization of the detector array passive materials, and the use of advanced cryogenic light detectors to reduce backgrounds from surface radioactivity and random signal coincidences. This article presents simulation results for detectors based on Li$_2$MoO$_4$ or TeO$_2$ surrounded by a 5-cm-thick active Bi$_4$Ge$_3$O$_{12}$ scintillation veto, demonstrating the potential to reduce the background by up to a factor of $10^3$, depending on the source location and the type of radionuclide. We further present results from the first cryogenic tests of a small scale prototype with respect to the feasibility of this proposed veto.

title: Spatial asymmetry of neutron pairing:A distance-resolved study of $^{46}\mathrm{Ti}$
abstract: Distance integration can conceal the spatial organization of neutron pairing in a reflection-asymmetric intrinsic configuration. We resolve the spin-singlet pairing tensor by relative distance and signed pair-center position along a prescribed $\alpha$+$^{42}$Ca-like path in $^{46}$Ti, using density-constrained Skyrme Hartree--Fock plus Bardeen--Cooper--Schrieffer calculations. Compact and extended components have oppositely signed shifts relative to the normal-density product conditioned on the same distance interval. At a reference center separation of 6 fm, the distance-integrated difference is 0.010, whereas the compact--extended contrast is 0.439. For the baseline surface-pairing prescription, this contrast increases between reference center separations of 6 and 7 fm while the extended anomalous weight decreases and the average neutron gap increases. Endpoint partitions locate an excess of extended neutron weight with both nucleons on the core side. An interference-retaining analysis in the stored canonical representation links the anomalous redistribution to $f_{7/2}$-weighted branches gaining core-side support with distinct amplitude responses. Changes in the normal-density reference contribute separately to the growing contrast. The conditional neutron pattern persists under the tested functional and pairing variations. Distance-conditioned distributions thus reveal intrinsic pairing structure hidden by scalar measures and distance integration.

title: Relative geometry of nuclear mean fields through differential forms
abstract: Proton and neutron densities can have similar multipole moments while differing locally. We use differential forms to measure and locate such differences between nuclear mean fields. A pair invariant measures the angle between two density gradients, weighted by their magnitudes, and the coarea formula resolves its contribution over level surfaces. A triple invariant factorizes exactly into a weighted pair term and a directional term that measures the variation of a third field along the level-surface intersections. We test these quantities in 98 magnetized Wigner-Seitz solutions, five static Hartree-Fock configurations, an illustrative $^{16}$O + $^{34}$Mg collision, and periodic nuclear pasta (a slab and a connected network). The pair invariant distinguishes cell solutions with comparable proton quadrupole moments and is 253 times larger in $^{34}$Mg than in $^{24}$Mg; refinement to 0.6 fm changes it by at most 1.3% in the four configurations recomputed. The directional factor separates the sampled triaxial configurations from the prolate ones. In the collision, it accounts for the 7.3-fold rise of the triple before the first recorded low-density connection, while the weighted pair term changes by at most 3%. In nuclear pasta, slab and network configurations have similar integrated proton-neutron misalignment but different distributions over density levels; their triple invariants differ by a factor of about 370 on the finer grid, mainly due to the variation of the Coulomb potential along joint density levels. These comparisons require no preferred origin or axis. A resolved nonzero triple excludes a common symmetry axis, but zero does not establish one. The pasta results require further convergence studies.

title: Nuclear Geometry-Driven Femtoscopic Correlations in Light-Ion Collisions
abstract: Recent anisotropic flow measurements in $^{16}\rm O{+}^{16}\rm O$ and $^{20}\rm Ne{+}^{20}\rm Ne$ collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.36~TeV provide evidence for nuclear geometry-driven collectivity. In this Letter, we investigate the femtoscopic signatures of nuclear geometry in these light-ion collision systems, using a hybrid simulation framework that couples \textit{ab initio} nuclear configurations to viscous hydrodynamics and hadronic transport. We show that the $\rm Ne{+}Ne/O{+}O$ ratio of the freeze-out eccentricity, extracted from azimuthally sensitive femtoscopy, reaches 1.5-1.8 in central collisions for deformed nuclear configurations, compared with about unity for a spherical baseline. This enhancement is significantly larger than that of elliptic flow in the same simulations, and remains stable when pre-equilibrium free streaming is omitted, even though the absolute source radii change considerably. Confronting these predictions with future data will provide new, complementary constraints on nuclear structure and initial-condition modeling.

title: Two-dimensional transport mechanisms in the vicinity of the X-points in snowflake divertors
abstract: Abstract Snowflake divertor (SFD) experiments show enhanced radial transport near the X-points, more than may be explained by standard two-dimensional edge transport models without drifts. Here we investigate transport mechanisms in SFDs through two complementary approaches: i) modelling of recent SFD experiments performed at MAST-U with the edge transport code UEDGE with ExB and ∇B drifts enabled, and ii) reduced modelling of transport and turbulence in the vicinity of the X-points with a model developed here and implemented in BOUT++. Through these two approaches we assess the two leading candidates for this transport: equilibrium ExB drifts driven by strong poloidal gradients near the primary X-point, and the 'churning mode' (CM), a toroidally-symmetric plasma vortex close to the X-points. UEDGE modelling shows that equilibrium ExB drifts do play a role in increasing particle and energy transport across the primary separatrix, increasing the proportion of heat flux delivered to secondary strike points (SPs) and reducing peak heat fluxes at the primary SPs. This mechanism is less effective in the upper divertor due the reversed drift directions in combination with the device geometry. Including drifts in the model is also shown to improve agreement with the experimental radiated power profiles.To self-consistently compare the impact of drifts and the CM we develop a reduced-MHD model which includes both effects, and which is implemented in BOUT++. We find that equilibrium ExB drifts are dominant when the ratio of plasma pressure in the null region to poloidal magnetic pressure at the midplane is low, β pm ≤ 0.5-1.0%, which were the conditions obtained in the MAST-U experiments. The CM was found to be dominant for β pm ≥ 1.0%, leading to increased transport across the null region and activation of secondary divertor legs.

title: The influence of ELM-like loading on tungsten under slow transient conditions in Magnum-PSI
abstract: Abstract ITER is anticipated to operate with occasional slow transients, resulting in an increase in expected heat loads to the divertor from 10 to 20 MW m − 2 and thus in the surface temperature increasing to > 2000 ∘ C. At the same time mitigated ELMs may be expected to strike the surface. To investigate the consequences of this, two sets of experiments were carried out in Magnum-PSI, representing the first experiments to explore this regime. In the first set, seven ITER-like tungsten monoblocks were exposed to either hydrogen plasma, or impurity-seeded hydrogen plasma at a surface temperature of 2050 ∘ C. Simultaneously five of the seven monoblocks were exposed to 10 5 ELM-like pulses using a 1 ms duration laser at an energy density of 0.1 − 0.19 MJ m − 2 . Very strongly roughened and cracked laser exposed areas with localized melted regions were observed. These areas protruded several hundreds of micrometers above the original surface. In the second experiment, three tungsten plates, with either small, large or no castellations cut into the surface, were exposed to a hydrogen plasma at 2100 ∘ C with a wider range of ELM-like pulse numbers ( 10 2 − 10 5 ) and energies ( 0.13 − 0.31 MJ m − 2 ). The surface was found to evolve by roughening and pre-crack formation towards similar strongly protruding roughened structures as pulse number increased, while increasing the transient energy resulted in increasing the fraction of surface melting observed in the loaded region. Mass loss measurements of the plates indicated that erosion was significant, between 0.05–0.13 nm per pulse for the different plates. Extrapolating these results to ITER suggests that this mass loss rate would be relatively high and would constitute a significant tungsten source.

title: Reawakening of GS 1843+00: A multiwavelength study of its 2026 giant X-ray outburst
abstract: GS 1843+00 (Ginga 1843+009) is a poorly studied Be/X-ray binary system that underwent a major X-ray outburst in 2026 February-May after nearly sixteen years of quiescence. We present an X-ray, optical, and radio study of GS 1843+00 during this outburst, focusing on the evolution of the neutron star emission geometry, Be-disk connection, and possible outflow activity. We analyzed three νstar observations obtained at different stages of the outburst, complemented with archival and data, optical spectroscopy and imaging with the Nordic Optical Telescope, and a MeerKAT radio observation. νstar observations reveal coherent X-ray pulsations around 29.7 s with a spin-up rate of (-5.1 $ during the outburst. The pulse profiles show strong evolution with energy and outburst phase, with distinct morphologies even at comparable luminosities. The pulsed fraction varies between 1 and 16% and exhibits a complex reversal in energy dependence above 7 keV, increasing with energy during the first two observations and decreasing during the third. The 3-79 keV broadband spectra are described by thermal Comptonization with a blackbody and an Fe Kα emission line, with no evidence of a cyclotron absorption feature. Phase-resolved spectroscopy reveals variations in the Comptonization and blackbody parameters, indicating changes in the accretion-column structure. Optical spectroscopy confirmed the presence of a Be-circumstellar disk through Hα and Paschen-series emission lines. No radio counterpart was detected, with a 3σ upper limit of 36 μJy beam$^ s s -1 -1 at 1.28 GHz. The observed pulse profile evolution, spectral variability, and reversal of the pulsed-fraction energy dependence suggest substantial changes in the accretion-column geometry during the outburst. Weaker Hα emission compared with previous epochs indicates that the Be-circumstellar disk was in a different state during the current episode, while the radio non-detection suggests that any associated outflow activity was faint or below the detection limit. Together, these results reveal a complex interplay between Be-disk evolution, outflows, and neutron-star accretion geometry in GS 1843+00.

title: Oscillation modes, Decoherence, Beam Transfer Functions, and Instabilities for a Beam Subjected to Space-Charge Forces
abstract: Based on the oscillation modes of a bunch subject to the space-charge force, we discuss the decoherence of the dipole oscillation, the beam transfer function, and the beam instability. The longitudinal phase space is discretized into \(n_l\times n_J\) grids in the azimuthal and radial directions, respectively. The transverse dipole moment in the longitudinal phase space is represented by a vector of length \(n_l n_J\), and the transformation given by the Vlasov equation is represented by a matrix transformation of size \(n_l n_J\times n_l n_J\). Solving the eigenvalue problem of this matrix gives the \(n_l n_J\) eigen-oscillation modes of the bunch. Using the resulting eigenvectors within a standard linear-algebraic treatment, we analyze these three phenomena. The analysis was performed for the Rapid Cycling Synchrotron (RCS) of the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS) using \(n_l=41\) and \(n_J=40\), and it visualizes the features related to the continuous distribution of the tune, Landau damping, and isolated modes separated from the continuous tune region.

title: Optimization of room-temperature targets for laser direct-drive fusion
abstract: Abstract Fusion ignition is a critical milestone toward the realization of fusion energy. For laser direct-drive fusion, the cryogenic deuterium–tritium (DT) targets encounter considerable fabrication and delivery challenges, such as the survival of cryogenic targets during the injection and flight in a reactor chamber. To mitigate the cryogenic bottlenecks, we explore the potential of room-temperature solid targets composed of low- Z elements and hydrogen isotopes via machine-learning optimization. In this work, a multi-fuel module is developed with the one-dimensional hydrodynamics code (MULTI-IFE) to simulate multiple room-temperature fuels. By optimizing the target structure and laser waveform parameters, a calculated fusion energy gain of 10.18 can be achieved with 2.35 MJ of laser energy, despite the additional radiative and conductive losses that may arise from the low- Z ions in the room-temperature target. A thicker target driven by a laser energy of 9.4 MJ is able to produce 109.7 MJ fusion energy with a maximum in-flight-aspect-ratio smaller than 17. During the fusion burning, tritium breeding via neutron–lithium reactions increases the fusion energy output for the LiBD 2 T 2 target by 5.2%. This work provides a reference for the ongoing development of direct-drive repetition-rate laser fusion energy.

title: Off-normal simulations of radiative collapse events in Alcator C-Mod
abstract: Abstract In preparation for ARC, supplementary offline tools are being developed alongside a real-time warning system in order to reduce its disruptivity. This paper introduces Off-Normal SIMulations (ONSIMs) to the MOSAIC pulse-simulating framework with that intent in mind. These modules probe simulated equilibria with a library of distinct perturbations, and can characterize disruptivity based on the scenario’s resiliency to them. This paper addresses the development of a module for simulating radiative collapses, with a specific focus on validating for the first time the power balance dynamics characteristic of these events. The simulations are performed using the TORAX transport simulator and are benchmarked against radiative collapse precursors on Alcator C-Mod. It is found that transport models that include sufficient turbulence effects, like a surrogate of the QuaLiKiz (Bourdelle et al 2015 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 58 014036; Citrin et al 2017 Plasma Phys. Control. Fusion 59 124005) transport model, are capable of reproducing the relevant radiative collapse dynamics for an L-mode discharge. It is also found that these dynamics are relatively insensitive to the shape of the collapse-inciting impurity profile, which bodes well for the robustness when probing various equilibria. The benchmarking reported here is part of a larger ongoing validation effort, which lays the groundwork for radiative collapse ONSIMs. Future work will be done to translate validations like this to a general implementation of ONSIMs to SPARC and ARC scenarios.

title: Metaheuristic physics-informed extreme-learning machine for initial orbit determination of near-Earth asteroids from too-short arcs
abstract: Modern wide-field astronomical surveys are substantially increasing the volume of observational data and the discovery rate of near-Earth asteroids (NEAs), placing growing demands on efficient and automated initial orbit determination (IOD). The physics-informed extreme-learning machine (PIELM) is an artificial intelligence (AI)-based algorithm for IOD that reconstructs orbital trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. However, optical survey observations often span arcs that are too short to provide sufficient geometric constraints, making it difficult for the standard PIELM to determine a reliable initial orbit. New IOD methods capable of handling too-short arcs (TSAs) are therefore increasingly needed. We develop a new AI-based method for determining the initial orbits of NEAs from TSAs. It yields reliable initial estimates for subsequent least-squares refinement. We propose a metaheuristic PIELM method, termed MH-PIELM. An artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm explores candidate solutions defined by a single line-of-sight range, with PIELM embedded directly within the search to reconstruct the corresponding trajectories under observational and dynamical constraints. The resulting PIELM loss serves as the fitness function, guiding the ABC algorithm toward promising candidate solutions. The method was tested on the initial optical observations reported for several NEAs. The MH-PIELM solutions enabled successful least-squares refinement, whose results closely agreed with the Jet Propulsion Laboratory reference solutions. The refined orbits were then used to predict the astrometric positions on the following day. Comparisons with the corresponding observations showed a useful short-term predictive capability for follow-up observations and target recovery, demonstrating the feasibility of the MH-PIELM approach. MH-PIELM offers a new AI-based strategy for initial orbit determination from TSAs by combining metaheuristic global search with physics-informed machine learning. It extends the applicability of the standard PIELM to challenging TSA observations.

title: Estimating global energy fluxes during COMPASS disruptions via magnetic measurements
abstract: Abstract During tokamak disruptions, a significant amount of poloidal magnetic energy is converted into other energy forms within the plasma, contributing to the thermal load on the first wall and the surrounding plasma facing components. The amount of magnetic energy converted to plasma thermal losses depends on the duration of the current quench as compared to the electromagnetic time of surrounding conductors. We implement a first-principle method to estimate plasma thermal losses during disruptions for the tokamak COMPASS. The method assumes the plasma evolves through MHD equilibrium states during the disruption, but it does not require any equilibrium reconstruction, elaborating exclusively raw magnetic measurements. The robustness of the method is validated against numerical simulations and different diagnostic measurements. An extensive analysis of energy fluxes during COMPASS disruptions is considered, showing how the poloidal magnetic energy influx contributes to losses and the role of halo currents in the task.

title: Effects of tungsten radiative cooling on impurity, heat and momentum transport in DIII-D plasmas
abstract: Abstract A first-of-its-kind experiment was conducted in the DIII-D tokamak under WEST similarity constraints on plasma shape and core parameters. This work presents a detailed transport study comparing a reference regime dominated by intrinsic carbon radiation and a high-radiation regime resulting from controlled tungsten (W) injection using the laser blow-off system, with a core tungsten concentration n W / n e ∼ 3 × 10 − 4 and a radiated-power fraction f rad > 0.5 . The W-induced radiative cooling lowered the electron temperature, thereby decreasing T e / T i and stabilizing trapped-electron-mode (TEM) turbulence. This transition in turbulence regime reduced momentum and ion thermal diffusivities, yielding ion temperature peaking and a factor-of-two increase in toroidal rotation. At the outer plasma region, enhanced E × B shear and increased collisionality further suppressed ion-scale turbulence, causing a sharp drop in ion heat flux. Consequently, impurity transport, predominantly turbulent in the low-radiation regime, acquired a strong neoclassical inward W convection during radiative cooling, bootstrapping the cooling cycle. Despite f rad > 0.5 , radiative collapse was not observed, likely owing to collisional ion-to-electron energy exchange acting as an electron-energy reservoir, together with 1 / 1 MHD activity modulating the radiated power through core impurity neoclassical T i -screening. These results support preparation for a tungsten wall change in DIII-D by elucidating tungsten-induced turbulence stabilization. They also provide key insights for interpreting plasma performance in WEST and are relevant to future reactors expected to operate with radiating tungsten-walled plasmas.

title: Core-edge integrated modeling of ARC: on the effect of impurity transport and detachment conditions
abstract: Abstract Integrated modeling of the flat-top phase of ARC H-modes has been conducted to assess the feasibility of high-performance scenarios compatible with divertor detachment. The analysis incorporates self-consistent evolution of impurity radiation and density profiles, demonstrating that fusion power levels approaching a GW can be achieved while maintaining divertor temperatures below 2 eV with Ar seeding. Sensitivity studies reveal a strong dependence of fusion power on the separatrix density, with performance spanning 750–1000 MW, and a weaker dependence on enrichment factor and pedestal density. Alternative seeding strategies using Neon have also been explored. Plasmas with Argon seeding consistently access H-mode, providing the highest fusion power and detached divertor operation, whereas Neon seeding leads to lower performance (600–850 MW) and less robust H-mode access, due to excessive core impurity accumulation. A small W impurity peaking has been found, with decreasing values at higher Z eff . Further analyses incorporate reduced momentum transport modeling, and sensitivity studies of neoclassical impurity transport, confirming the robustness of the results. Overall, these findings support the viability of high-performing H-mode operation in ARC, ensuring divertor protection, enabled through Argon and Neon impurity seeding.

title: NTL amplification in a SuperCDMS-style detector fabricated from a University of South Dakota-grown germanium crystal
abstract: Neganov-Trofimov-Luke (NTL) amplification enables eV-sub-keV detection thresholds for low-mass dark-matter and coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering experiments. We evaluated two University of South Dakota (USD)-grown germanium crystals fabricated as SuperCDMS-style four-channel athermal-phonon detectors and operated near 10 mK. The crystals had electrically active impurity concentrations near $10^10~\mathrm^-3$ and etch-pit densities of $300$-$7000~\mathrm^-2$. Contact-free biasing produced no resolvable amplification. However, after depositing a 600 nm aluminum bias contact, Detector~2 exhibited clear voltage-dependent NTL gain. The reconstructed channel-B energy increased from approximately 3.9 keV at 0 V to 34.9 keV at 40 V, corresponding to an 8.9-fold enhancement. Statistical centroid uncertainties were below 0.3%, while low-bias fits yielded effective prompt- and NTL-phonon response coefficients of $(6.77\pm0.82)%$ and $(4.77\pm0.20)%$, respectively, excluding systematic uncertainties. These results demonstrate the feasibility of USD-grown germanium for SuperCDMS-style high-voltage phonon detectors and highlight the importance of both crystal quality and contact fabrication in achieving NTL amplification.

title: Generalized parton distributions of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model: Sum over all quark states at nonzero skewness and momentum transfer
abstract: We compute the combinations $E_M=H^{u+d}+E^{u+d}$ and $H_E=H^{u-d}+tE^{u-d}/(4M_N^2)$ of unpolarized generalized parton distributions (GPDs) of the nucleon in the chiral quark soliton model at nonzero skewness $\xi$ and nonzero momentum transfer $t$. The combinations contain the GPDs $H^{u-d}$ and $E^{u+d}$, which are subleading in the expansion in the inverse number of colors. Both combinations are double sums over the quark states. A multipole expansion of the light-cone operators makes the sums computable at every $\xi$ and every $t\le0$. The contribution of the Dirac continuum is summed over the quark states, without an interpolation formula and without a gradient expansion. The first moments satisfy the form-factor sum rules, and the second moments satisfy polynomiality.

title: A Broadband Room-Temperature Design for the Einstein Telescope
abstract: The unique underground location of the Einstein Telescope (ET) is expected to substantially suppress seismic and gravity-gradient noise, providing a favorable environment for gravitational-wave detection at low frequencies compared with surface-based observatories. The baseline ET design aims to achieve broadband sensitivity through a xylophone configuration, in which separate cryogenic and room-temperature interferometers are optimised for low- and high-frequency gravitational-wave detection. However, achieving the target low-frequency sensitivity introduces substantial technical complexity caused by vertical suspension thermal noise, vibrations of the cryocooler, and detuned optical configuration. In this paper, we demonstrate an alternative, entirely room-temperature, fully resonant, single-interferometer architecture that addresses these challenges and achieves broadband sensitivity superior to that of the conventional ET xylophone configuration. Using mature fused-silica suspension technology, recent advances in optical coatings, and novel inertial isolation, we show that 4-m-long fused-silica fibres can meet the required suspension thermal-noise performance. We further demonstrate that vibrations, optical rigidity, and quantum back-action noise can be controlled through appropriate design of the interferometer, test mass suspensions, optical seismometers, and quantum states.

title: PSR J0653+0443: An Eclipsing Millisecond Pulsar in an Extremely Eccentric Double Neutron Star System
abstract: Double neutron star (DNS) systems emit gravitational waves (GW) as they orbit each other, with waveforms dependent on their orbital properties \cite{Poisson+2014grav.book.....P}. The number of DNS systems surviving binary star evolution in the Milky Way and the distribution of their orbital parameters are fundamental questions for GW astronomy and binary evolution studies. Here, we report the discovery of a new Galactic field DNS system, PSR J0653+0443, comprising two ~1.4 $M_\odot$ components in an extremely eccentric orbit $e=0.992387$, $P_{\rm orb}=79.084$ d. Its unique orbital dynamics include a 46-minute transit from true anomaly $\theta=-90^\circ$ to $90^\circ$ and striking periastron relative motion (maximum acceleration 1.11~km~s$^{-2}$, peak speed 1.14$\times$10$^6$~m~s$^{-1}$. The pulsar undergoes an 85-second conjunction eclipse, indicating a nearly edge-on binary orbit. Short-term variations in the periastron advance induce significant pulse arrival time modulation spanning -2.91 to +2.49 ms --- at least an order of magnitude larger than that observed in any other DNS system. From this modulation, the non-relativistic periastron advance rate is constrained to $-1.5^{+0.9}_{-0.8}\times10^{-4}$ deg yr$^{-1}$. The extreme orbital eccentricity can only be attributed to a large kick velocity imparted during the iron-core collapse supernova of the progenitor of the second component. The predicted detection probability of such a PSR J0653+0443-like DNS system is $\lesssim 5 \times 10^{-3}$, implying that our discovery of this system challenges current understanding of binary evolution. This extraordinary DNS system emits periodic gravitational wave bursts, with the GW energy flux peaking at 0.357 mHz. This makes it an ideal target for the future LISAmax mission.

title: remage: a Geant4-based simulation framework for low-background experiments
abstract: Monte Carlo simulations are an essential tool for data modeling and experimental design in low-background physics. These simulations typically demand a considerable effort, with each collaboration developing and maintaining its own complex Geant4 application. In this paper we present the design and validation of remage, which is an open-source framework designed to standardize these simulations and significantly reduce this effort. Its design separates the geometry, built with dedicated Python tools, from the compiled application. It provides a physics list and event generators tuned to radiogenic and cosmogenic backgrounds, output tailored to the most common detector types, and robust validation backed by modern software development practices. The software is distributed ready to use and scales efficiently with the computing resources that demanding simulations require. remage has been primarily developed for the LEGEND experiment, but is applicable to a wide variety of experiments.

title: Simulations of MAPS designs for FCC-ee
abstract: Future electron-positron colliders such as the future circular collider require vertex detectors with excellent spatial resolution and a low material budget. Monolithic active pixel sensors (MAPS) are a leading candidate technology because they integrate the sensing volume and readout electronics within a single thin silicon substrate and can operate at power densities compatible with air cooling. This paper presents the design and optimization of a high-voltage MAPS (HV-MAPS) pixel structure with a thickness of 25 $\mu\text{m}$ and a pitch of 50 $\mu\text{m}$, developed using TCAD process and device simulations. The implantation energies and doses of the top-side implants are optimized with respect to the maximum electric field, sensor capacitance, and signals induced at each contact by minimum-ionizing particles. The optimized design reaches full depletion at a bias voltage of approximately -3 V and has an estimated breakdown voltage magnitude of 300-390 V. At a bias voltage of -100 V, the simulated charge-collection efficiency is approximately 90% outside the well regions and 80% within them and remains nearly independent of the angle of incidence.

title: Monte Carlo study of extending the BM@N tracking acceptance toward midrapidity with the Vertex Silicon Plane
abstract: The Vertex Silicon Plane (VSP), installed close to the target in BM@N Run 9, can extend the tracking acceptance of the central tracking system toward larger polar angles. Using Monte Carlo simulations of Xe+Sn collisions at 3 AGeV, we reconstruct short tracklets from the primary vertex, one VSP hit, and hits in the first two Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) stations. These tracklets extend the reconstructed primary-proton coverage toward midrapidity and higher transverse momenta. For the 10-30% centrality interval of the independent validation dataset, the conditional reconstruction efficiency for reconstructible high-$p_T$ primary protons after BDT selection is 67.0%, while the tracklet purity reaches 86.5%. For $p_T>1.2$ GeV/c, the VSP-assisted tracklets increase the number of reconstructed primary protons by 17.5% relative to standard BM@N tracking. Of these additional protons, 84.6% lie within $|y|<0.3$, where the relative reconstruction gain reaches 45.5%. The added acceptance is concentrated in the high-$p_T$, near-midrapidity region relevant for identified-proton observables. Its use in data requires particle identification in the same region.

title: Charged-current neutrino-nucleus scattering off 129 Xe and 131 Xe including the meson-exchange contributions
Cavity optomechanical magnetometer actuated by substrate bending
abstract: We describe a magnetic field sensor based on a monolithic Fabry-Perot cavity. The cavities were fabricated in a thin-film buckling process at one surface of a fused silica chip, and the chip was subsequently bonded to a giant magnetostrictive material (GMM). External magnetic fields drive flexural modes of the assembly and the associated bending stresses are efficiently mapped to changes in the cavity height, with enhanced response at kHz-range mechanical resonance frequencies. A key attribute of this platform is that the size of the transducing material is decoupled from the size of the optical cavity. The buckled cavity operates in low mode order and with moderate Q ~ 103, providing a high optomechanical coupling coefficient while also enabling a straightforward tuned-to-slope readout technique. Peak sensitivity ~ 2 pT/Hz1/2 was achieved in an unshielded laboratory environment, limited by laser phase and electronics noise in the readout system. With future reductions in these noise sources, we predict that a broadband thermomechanical-noise-limited sensitivity in the ~ 0.1 pT/Hz1/2 range is feasible.

title: Background-Limited Silicon Telescope Methodology for Weak Internal Pair Creation Transition in Low-Energy Deuteron-Deuteron Reactions
abstract: A background-constrained silicon-telescope methodology has been developed to investigate recently observed internal electron-positron pair creation in low-energy deuteron-deuteron fusion. The decay of the near-threshold $0^+$ resonance in $^4$He produced in DD fusion results in an $e^-e^+$ pair sharing a total energy of 22.84 MeV. These high-energy leptons traverse thin silicon detectors and deposit only part of their kinetic energy. The resulting partial-absorption peak structure overlaps with the natural-radiation background of cosmic-ray secondaries and terrestrial gamma rays. The silicon detector telescope used in the present experiments is characterised against this background through a component-by-component model that combines a GEANT4 cosmic-ray simulation, a large-volume NaI(Tl)-constrained terrestrial-gamma propagation, and a beam-correlated neutron response. Long-duration measurements in multiple orientations and shielding configurations are used to quantify the run-to-run variability of the background and to translate it into an explicit systematic envelope on the extracted signal. The framework is then applied to the beam-on singles spectrum and the two-dimensional coincidence response, yielding a quantitative branching-ratio measurement under background-limited conditions. The methodology is directly transferable to other weak-channel searches in surface laboratories where continuum-like signals overlap with natural-radiation backgrounds.

title: Agentic AI Detector Co-design and Optimization in Vertically Integrated Differentiable Full Simulations
abstract: We present the first implementation of AI agents into the design and optimization of detectors in high-energy physics experiments via a bi-level optimization framework that vertically integrates detector geometry, front-end digitization, and high-level reconstruction algorithm parameters in differentiable full simulations. Using the example of a dual-readout, segmented crystal EM calorimeter with a baseline resolution of $3\%/\sqrt{E}$, we investigate the capabilities and value propositions of AI agents in the identification and reduction of key detector parameters and in the nonlinear traversal of design space. We find that frontier LLM reasoning-models today, without being given additional experiment-specific context, are able to effectively execute complex workflows and proactively suggest generic but relevant avenues for further study or improvement. Here, we demonstrate an AI agent's ability to find an optimal design point amidst three competing performance criteria, showing that effective integration of agents into the complex workflows of frontier research areas can yield higher performance for key physics goals while reducing labor and compute. This study establishes the foundation for a future demonstration of the first fully AI-designed detector for future scientific facilities.

title: Will a supernova explode in CD-3011223?
abstract: Accretion of He-rich matter onto a low-mass carbon-oxygen white dwarf in a binary system with a He-rich donor may lead to an explosive event at the level of a type Ia supernova ( albeit with a low peak luminosity and peculiar nucleosynthesis. Recently, the possibility of this occurring in the context of certain binaries with He-accreting white dwarfs has been questioned, with the suggestion that if the effects of rotation are accounted for in the evolution of the accretor, the latter would not explode. It could instead become a white dwarf with a massive He-buffer. We investigate the expected evolution of the currently detached binary ̧dth harboring a 0.74, carbon-oxygen white dwarf and a 0.47, donor with a He-burning core and a very thin H-envelope (Δ M_H=6 , 10^ -4 We used the stellar evolution code FuNS to compute the evolution of ̧dth up to the epoch when the two components come into contact and through the RLOF phase of the donor. With respect to our earlier study of the system PTF J2238+743015.1, we also included the transport of angular momentum due to magnetic instabilities in the accretor interiors (`magnetic model'). During the H-accretion phase, the effects of rotation in the accretor are negligible.
