In the `magnetic model', the angular momentum deposited by the accreted matter is very efficiently redistributed along the whole WD due to magnetic instabilities, so that the angular velocity of the accreted layers remains very low. During the He-accretion phase, the accretor experiences two very strong He-flashes, which result in the ejection from the binary system of a large part of the matter previously accreted. The system ends its life as a carbon-oxygen core capped by a massive He/C/O-envelope (Δ M_ ̊m env ≃ 0.194, and an extremely low-mass companion that is remnant of the donor, as in the rotating model, and not including the effects of magnetic field. The system ̧dth cannot be regarded as the potential progenitor of an SN Ia. This conclusion is equally applicable to all detached binary systems having similar component masses and orbital periods.

title: A bright X-ray flaring event from the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient IGR J00370+6122 observed with NuSTAR
abstract: We present an analysis of a long νstar observation of the intermediate supergiant fast X-ray transient (SFXT) IGR,J00370+6122, obtained around the peak of its orbital modulation. The observation has a net exposure ∼93,ks. During the observation, the source displayed a bright flaring event that was resolved into numerous short flares with durations of 10-10^3,s. The 3-70,keV luminosity spanned a dynamic range of ∼200, from to -1 $; the maximum was reached for only $ /BAT monitoring, we refine the orbital period of the system to P_ in total. The spectrum is well described by an absorbed double-Comptonisation model, with parameters consistent with those found in other X-ray pulsars accreting at similarly low luminosities. This is the first detection of a double-hump continuum in which extends this spectral state to the class of intermediate SFXTs. We searched for the previously reported sim346,s and sim674,s periodicities and find no significant signal at either period, which makes their interpretation as the neutron star spin period less likely. Using sim21,yr of Swift ̊m orb =15.6654 Finally, we discuss the observed flaring activity in the framework of quasi-spherical settling accretion, which is expected at the observed luminosities.

title: Evaluation of Transverse Incoherent Tune Shifts in the Electron-Ion Collider
abstract: Achieving the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) peak luminosity goal of 10 to the power of 34 per square centimeter per second requires high average currents, flat beams, non-circular vacuum chambers, and large transverse orbit offsets in the Hadron Storage Ring (HSR) and Electron Storage Ring (ESR). These conditions can generate collective effects and incoherent tune spreads that drive particles across low-order betatron resonances, causing emittance growth, halo formation, and reduced beam lifetime. We quantitatively evaluate incoherent transverse betatron tune shifts from beam-beam interactions, direct space charge, and beam-environment interactions associated with image forces and vacuum chamber geometry. Xsuite and PyHEADTAIL simulations validate the analytical calculations for beam-beam and direct space-charge effects, respectively. For indirect space-charge effects, we review and compare several analytical formalisms and apply the Laslett image-charge formulation to rectangular vacuum chambers with off-axis beams. The analysis accounts for transverse orbit offsets of up to 20 mm in the HSR and 10 mm in the ESR. The results establish baseline parameters and provide quantitative guidance for EIC design, optimization, and operation. The comparison of indirect space-charge formalisms also offers an accessible reference and methodology for studies of high-intensity beam dynamics.

title: A Hybrid Neural Network Emulator for M1 Neutrino Reaction Rates in Binary Neutron Star Merger Simulations
abstract: We present a neural network emulator for the bns_nurates library, which computes neutrino reaction rates used in binary neutron star merger simulations. Following a hybrid strategy, we emulate only the computationally dominant two-dimensional reactions---pair processes, bremsstrahlung, and inelastic neutrino-electron scattering---while evaluating the inexpensive one-dimensional processes still with bns_nurates. We find that the emulator reproduces the opacities to within a few percent across the relevant thermodynamic conditions and accelerates their evaluation by roughly an order of magnitude. When deployed in a global Athenak binary neutron star merger simulation, it recovers the remnant structure, neutrino luminosities, and ejecta composition of a reference run using the full bns_nurates library, at approximately half the overall cost

title: Impact of non-standard neutrino-electron interactions on Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
abstract: Neutrino non-standard interactions (NSI) with electrons, predicted in many extended theoretical models of particle physics, are known to alter the picture of neutrino decoupling from the cosmic plasma. We update previous analyses of neutrino decoupling in the presence of NSI with electrons, extending the parameter space and assessing their impact on the primordial light-element abundances produced during Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN). We show that tracking the NSI-induced modifications of the neutrino distributions is necessary to accurately predict the helium-4 abundance, which cannot be derived from a pure $N_{\rm eff}$-driven change. BBN therefore provides additional observables that are complementary to $N_{\rm eff}$. We then derive cosmological constraints on non-universal and flavour-changing NSI parameters, using different dataset combinations, and compare them with bounds from terrestrial experiments. We find that the cosmological limits are significantly less stringent than the terrestrial ones, but they provide an independent probe of neutrino interactions in the early universe.

title: Hybrid Stars with a Crossover Equation of State
abstract: The possible occurrence of a phase transition in superdense nuclear matter remains an open problem in nuclear physics. In particular, the transition from purely hadronic matter to the hypothesized deconfined quark matter is a subject of considerable interest. Beyond its fundamental significance, this transition has important implications for the physics of compact objects, including neutron stars, quark stars, and hybrid stars. The conventional approaches to this problem involve the Maxwell and Gibbs constructions, both of which have been extensively studied and applied. In the present study, we focus on a third, alternative approach based on a smooth transition from hadronic to quark matter through the so-called switching function. More specifically, the present work focuses on two main objectives. The first is to systematically investigate the influence of the symmetry energy on the transition densities and chemical potentials associated with the transition to quark matter. Subsequently, we attempt to physically constrain and parametrize the two parameters characterizing the switching function, ensuring that the transition from hadronic to quark matter is not merely continuous but also consistent with relevant physical requirements. The main conclusion is that, with an appropriate choice of the aforementioned parameters, the phenomenological model becomes more physically motivated and can serve as a useful tool for investigating the structure and properties of hybrid compact objects. Moreover, this approach offers the flexibility to predict the properties of compact objects that lie beyond the scope of standard neutron-star theory, such as objects characterized by relatively low masses and small radii, which have recently attracted considerable attention in observational studies.

title: General Relativistic Simulations of the Nonlinear Evolution of r-modes in Rapidly Rotating Neutron Stars
abstract: The r-modes in rotating neutron stars are a promising source of continuous gravitational waves, and may grow or be excited to amplitudes $\alpha\lesssim1$. We perform general relativistic simulations of nonlinear $l=|m|=2$ r-modes in a rapidly rotating neutron star with spin frequency $f_{spin}\approx792$ Hz, relaxing the Cowling and small-$\alpha$ approximations. The star is idealised as an unmagnetised, one-component, perfect fluid with a polytropic equation of state. The r-mode frequency is measured to be $f_{r-mode}=1014$ Hz for initial amplitude $\alpha_0=0.2$. The dimensionless frequency $\kappa\approx0.7197$ agrees with an estimate from linear perturbation theory to within 1.7%. $f_{r-mode}$ increases quadratically with amplitude, and $\kappa$ decreases by 3.4% across simulations where $\alpha_0$ is varied through the range $0.2\leq\alpha_0\leq1.2$. The gravitational wave strain calculated from the Newman-Penrose scalar implies $h_{r-mode}\approx9.7\times10^{-22}$ at $10$ kpc for $\alpha_0=0.2$, which agrees with Einstein's quadrupole formula to within 35%. We also report on nonlinear phenomena observed in our simulations, e.g. differential rotation, amplitude decay, and signatures of nonlinear mode coupling in the spacetime oscillations.

title: Development of a Prototype Superconducting Radio-Frequency Multicell Cavity for Compact, Conduction-Cooled Accelerators
abstract: Jefferson Lab and General Atomics are jointly advancing compact, high-power irradiation systems capable of delivering electron-beam powers in the hundreds of kilowatts based on superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) technology. A critical step toward deploying SRF accelerators in industrial environments is replacing traditional liquid-helium cryogenic systems with conduction-cooled cryomodules powered by commercial cryocoolers. This paper reports recent progress in the design, fabrication, and testing of a prototype three-cell SRF cavity developed at Jefferson Lab and evaluated in a dedicated horizontal test cryostat at General Atomics. Peak surface magnetic fields up to 18.4\,mT, corresponding to accelerating gradients of approximately 4.3\,MV/m, were achieved in one of the cells. The results provide key insights into cavity preparation, thin-film coating, mechanical robustness, and cryogenic integration, offering guidance for the continued maturation of compact, conduction-cooled SRF accelerators for industrial irradiation applications.

title: Neutron Star-Main-Sequence Star Collision: Formation and Long-Term Evolution of Thorne-\.Zytkow Objects
abstract: Thorne-$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$ytkow objects (T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$Os) are stars containing a neutron-star (NS) or black-hole (BH) core embedded in a stellar envelope and powered primarily by mass accretion onto the core. Classical evolution models of T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$Os begin with an assumed equilibrium configuration and predict chemical anomalies in the stellar envelope resulting from nuclear burning in the vicinity of the NS core. Here we connect dynamical formation to long-term evolution by combining a three-dimensional simulation of a post-supernova collision between a $1.4M_\odot$ NS and a $10M_\odot$ main-sequence star with a subsequent stellar evolution calculation using MESA. The collision successfully produces a bound, quasi-spherical T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$O with the NS settled at the center of the stellar envelope. In contrast to the classical picture, the collision heats a substantial fraction of the star and leads to widespread nuclear burning during the subsequent thermal-relaxation phase. As the envelope becomes convective, material processed by the carbon-nitrogen cycle is transported to the surface, leaving a potentially observable chemical imprint of formation that persists after the star attains the standard accretion-supported T$\dot{\mathrm{Z}}$O structure. At the end of our simulation, the stellar luminosity greatly exceeds Eddington in the outer envelope, suggesting that significant mass ejection will occur, leaving behind an isolated NS or BH.

title: Can we constrain the binary neutron star merger time from kilonova light curves?
abstract: The joint observation of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary neutron star (BNS) merger (GW170817), together with a short Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB 170817A) and a kilonova (KN, AT2017gfo), marked the birth of multimessenger astronomy with GWs, and demonstrated the informative power of multimessenger observations. More BNS merger and KN detections are expected , thanks to the increasing sensitivity of GW detectors and the advent of new electromagnetic facilities such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. However, the association between a BNS merger and a KN might not be trivial: the detection of a KN might not coincide with the onset of the EM emission, making it difficult to define a temporal window to assess the coincidence with a GW event. In this work we investigate the possibility to constrain the BNS merger time from KN light curves, exploring different observing conditions and with focus on the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. We used different KN models and different inference frameworks to simulate and fit KN light curves. We explored different cadences and wavelength coverages for observations, to investigate how the different observing conditions can affect the capability to recover the BNS merger time. The tests performed also include real data related to AT2017gfo, plus a few GRBs that have been associated to possible KN candidates. We find that, under realistic observing conditions with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, the BNS merger time can be recovered with a precision of 5.5 days (90\% CI) with a best-case scenario with an accuracy of 0.18 day and a precision of 0.74 day (90 \% CI). Results can slightly improve (by $\sim$ 5 \%) if the source redshift is available. Upper limits near the merger time can also improve the results, reducing the width of the posterior by $\sim60$ \%. The BNS merger time estimate could also benefit from EM follow-up observations with other telescopes.

title: Radiative corrections to double-$\beta$ decay and their impact on experimental analyses
abstract: We present a comprehensive study of the $\mathcal{O}(\alpha)$ radiative corrections to two-neutrino and neutrinoless double-$\beta$ decay within a heavy-nucleus effective field theory. We compute all virtual and real-emission corrections for intermediate nuclear states of arbitrary excitation energy, including new closed-form expressions for the required one-loop integrals with heavy-nucleus propagators. For excitation energies large compared with the lepton energies, the corrections factorize into the tree-level rate times a universal double-weak Sirlin function, which differs substantially from the sum of two single-$\beta$ Sirlin functions used so far in the literature. We discuss the impact of the radiative corrections on the analysis of measured spectra in terms of ratios of nuclear matrix elements, $\xi_{31}$, and show that neglecting radiative corrections can significantly bias the extraction. Real-photon emission, not considered in previous analyses, plays a central role and the impact of radiative corrections depends crucially on the detector setup. We provide the photon spectrum, fully differential in the photon energy and direction, and recommend that experiments simulate the photon explicitly. For $0\nu\beta\beta$ decay, the radiative corrections increase the inclusive rate by about $5\%$, independently of the nuclear matrix elements or the neutrino Majorana mass.

title: On the nature of fully-charmed four-quark exotic state $X(6900)$ from its photoproduction off nuclei
abstract: The possibility to study the nature of fully-charmed tetraquark state $X(6900)$ from its inclusive photoproduction off nuclei near the kinematic threshold is investigated within the collision model based on the nuclear spectral function. The model accounts for $X(6900)$ production in direct photon--nucleon interactions as well as three different scenarios for its internal structure: compact tetraquark, molecule of the two hidden-charm $J/\psi$ and $\psi(3770)$ mesons and the mixture of both of them. We calculate within these scenarios the absolute and relative excitation functions on $^{12}$C and $^{184}$W nuclei at near-threshold photon energies of 30--40 GeV, the absolute momentum differential cross sections and ratios of them for the $X(6900)$ meson production off these target nuclei at laboratory polar angles of 0$^{\circ}$--5$^{\circ}$ and for photon energy of 35 GeV as well as the A-dependences of its transparency ratios at photon energy of 35 GeV. We show that these observables reveal a definite sensitivity to the $X(6900)$ intrinsic structure. Therefore, they might be useful for the determination of this structure from the comparison of them with the experimental data from the future experiments at the upcoming experimental facilities, such as the planned electron-ion colliders in the United States and China.

title: Exploring the origin of slow-rotating pulsars: Emission from STARS simulated white dwarfs
abstract: An increasing number of slow-rotating pulsars and long-period transients have been observed in recent years. The periods of these sources can be significantly longer than typical pulsar sources, ranging from ~ 100 - 1000 s, or even longer. The observed periods and period derivatives predict high magnetic fields, higher than the Schwinger field, when we consider conventional pulsar models of dipole-driven emission from neutron stars. Interestingly, the periods of these sources are consistent with the current observations of white dwarfs (WDs). We explore the possibility of magnetic WDs, simulated using the stellar evolution code STARS, as the origin of some of these unusual pulsar observations. We simulate WDs with enhanced magnetic fields due to accretion after their formation. We also briefly touch on the more exotic possibility of super-Chandrasekhar WDs as the origin for these sources. We find that expanding the parameter space to include the possibility of a WD origin provides an alternate and viable explanation for these unusual observations.

title: Direct Access to Nuclear Photon TMDs with In Situ Probes in Ultraperipheral Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: Resolving local structure in photon distributions is an important goal in probing strong coherent electromagnetic fields. We propose using electron--positron pairs produced in situ in ultraperipheral heavy-ion collisions as dynamical probes to directly extract photon distributions. We define a theoretical reference cross section using the complete tree-level amplitude for two-photon-induced radiative lepton-pair production. When background effects factorize into a scalar Bose-enhancement factor, the ratio of the background-modified to reference differential cross sections, minus unity, yields the photon occupation number at a fixed momentum. Finite bins yield averages weighted by the reference cross section. We specify the conditions under which kinematic selections, acceptance, and radiative corrections preserve this local inversion.

title: Lowest-radiation environments in the Solar System: New opportunities for underground rare-event searches
abstract: We study neutrino, muon, and gamma-ray fluxes in extraterrestrial environments in our Solar System via semianalytical estimates and Monte Carlo simulations. In sites with negligible atmosphere, we find a strong reduction in the cosmic-ray-induced neutrino and muon fluxes relative to their intensities on Earth. Neutrinos with energies between 50 MeV and 100 TeV show particularly strong suppression, by as much as 10 3 , even at shallow depths. The solar neutrino suppression increases as the square of the site’s distance from the Sun. Natural radiation due to nuclear decay is also expected to be lower in many of these locations and may be reduced to effectively negligible levels in liquid water environments. The sites satisfying these characteristics represent an opportunity for greatly extending the physics reach of underground searches in fundamental physics, such as searches for weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) dark matter, neutrinoless double-beta decay, the diffuse supernova neutrinos, and neutrinos from nearby supernova. As a potential near-term target, we propose a measurement of muon and gamma-ray fluxes in an accessible underground lunar site such as the Mare Tranquillitatis pit to perform a first measurement of the prompt component in cosmic-ray-induced particle production, and to constrain lunar evolution models. Although the focus of this work is on fundamental physics, the finding of this work—that the existence of an atmosphere in a planet enhances cosmic-ray-induced radiation in its underground—could be relevant for a broader range of sciences, such as radiobiology deep underground and searches for extraterrestrial life.

title: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of superheavy Z = 124 isotopes with the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum
abstract: Shell structure and spontaneous decay of $Z = 124$ isotopes are systematically investigated using the deformed relativistic Hartree-Bogoliubov theory in continuum (DRHBc) with the PC-PK1 density functional. By accounting for deformation and continuum effects, the neutron drip line is predicted to be located at $N = 320$, and eight potential multi-neutron emitters beyond the neutron drip line are identified. The results, compared with the spherically constrained case, highlight the critical role of deformation effects in determining the ground-state properties of superheavy nuclei. In addition, potential neutron shell closures emerge at $N = 258$ and $350$, alongside subshell closures at $N = 232$ and $320$. The results disfavor $Z = 124$ as a possible proton magic number and suggest $Z = 120$ and $138$ as more favorable candidates for proton shell closures in the superheavy region. Finally, the competition between $\alpha$ decay, $\beta$ decay, and spontaneous fission is analyzed by calculating half-lives within various semi-empirical formulas. The results indicate that $\alpha$ decay is the predominant mode on the proton-rich side, whereas spontaneous fission and $\beta^-$ decay gradually become dominant with increasing neutron number.

title: First Simultaneous Analysis of Transverse Momentum Dependent and Collinear Parton Distributions in the Proton
abstract: We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, W + charm, and jet production involving PDFs, as well as TMD Drell-Yan and Z -boson production data from fixed target and collider experiments sensitive to both TMD and collinear distributions. The analysis is performed at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for QCD resummation in TMD observables and next-to-leading order for observables described in collinear factorization. The combined analysis improves knowledge of both TMD and collinear PDFs, particularly in the sea-quark sector, providing a consistent simultaneous description of the aforementioned observables.

versions.title: First Simultaneous Analysis of Transverse Momentum Dependent and Collinear Parton Distributions in the Proton
versions.abstract: We present the first simultaneous global QCD analysis of unpolarized transverse momentum dependent (TMD) and collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the proton. Our Letter incorporates data from deep-inelastic scattering, Drell-Yan, inclusive weak boson, W + charm, and jet production involving PDFs, as well as TMD Drell-Yan and Z -boson production data from fixed target and collider experiments sensitive to both TMD and collinear distributions. The analysis is performed at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy for QCD resummation in TMD observables and next-to-leading order for observables described in collinear factorization. The combined analysis improves knowledge of both TMD and collinear PDFs, particularly in the sea-quark sector, providing a consistent simultaneous description of the aforementioned observables.

title: New universal relations for magnetized neutron stars
abstract: Unlike the neutron-star mass--radius relation, which depends sensitively on the internal stellar structure through the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, certain neutron-star properties obey approximately universal relations that exhibit only weak dependence on the equation of state. In this paper, we explore new universal relations for magnetized neutron stars. We focus on a purely poloidal dipolar magnetic-field configuration and treat the effects of the magnetic field perturbatively to second order in the field strength. After appropriately normalizing the relevant quantities by the stellar mass and the magnetic-field strength at the pole, we first identify an exact universal relation between the magnetic dipole moment and stellar compactness. We then find approximate universal relations among the magnetic dipole moment, magnetically-induced stellar quadrupole moment, and ellipticity, with fractional variations due to the equation of state at the level of O(10%). We support these numerical findings with analytic estimates for Newtonian polytropes, which reproduce the observed behavior. Among the newly discovered relations, the one connecting the magnetic dipole moment and stellar quadrupole moment may be particularly useful for the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from binaries containing magnetized neutron stars.

title: Measurements of local polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons with event shape engineering in Au+Au collisions at RHIC-STAR
abstract: Anisotropic flow is expected to generate local vorticities along the beam direction, which in turn lead to local polarization of produced particles. Although the local polarization of hyperons has already been observed at RHIC and the LHC, its mechanism is not yet understood: model calculations indicate that the shear-induced and vorticity-induced contributions can have opposite signs and may substantially cancel, so that the resulting polarization depends sensitively on the theoretical implementation. Since both are driven by the anisotropic flow, we employ the Event Shape Engineering (ESE) method, which selects events with different flow magnitudes within a narrow centrality range, to measure the local polarization as a function of the elliptic flow at a fixed multiplicity. We report the measurements of the elliptic flow ($v_2$) and the local polarization ($P_{z,2}$) of $\Lambda$ and $\bar{\Lambda}$ as a function of the reduced flow vector magnitude $q_2$ used for the ESE event selection, in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 19.6~{\rm GeV}$ from the STAR experiment. The $v_2$ shows a clear positive dependence on $q_2$, while $P_{z,2}$ indicates a weak positive dependence on $q_2$ and $v_2$. This is the first measurement to directly investigate the relation between anisotropic flow and local polarization, providing new insight into the origin of local polarization.

title: An exact time-dependent generator coordinate method with projection for spontaneous fission reactions
abstract: Microscopic descriptions of fission dynamics through the barrier rely on different theoretical frameworks depending on the fission regime, with the time-dependent generator coordinate method (TDGCM) commonly used for induced fission and semiclassical approaches such as the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) method widely employed for spontaneous fission. In this work, we develop a fully microscopic approach to spontaneous fission based on an exact formulation of the TDGCM, avoiding both the Gaussian overlap approximation and semiclassical treatments. By combining the exact TDGCM with new projection tools and a quasistatic description of spontaneous fission, we derive spontaneous fission half-lives from a one-dimensional potential energy surface. A detailed analysis of the model parameters shows that they do not introduce uncontrolled phenomenological effects. Remaining discrepancies with experimental half-lives are related to possible limitations of the underlying microscopic interaction and to the choice of basis states in the generator coordinate method. The new framework provides a microscopic description of spontaneous fission with reduced empirical input and offers a pathway toward improved predictions through future developments of nuclear interactions, collective coordinates, and the handling of many-body dynamics.

title: Next-to-Next-to-Next-to-Leading-Order QCD Corrections to Photon-Pair Production
abstract: The production of two isolated photons at the Large Hadron Collider has applications in Higgs-boson phenomenology and in new-physics searches. In fact, measurements would provide more insight if a percent-level theoretical prediction were available. We account for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order strong-interaction effects in the cross section for the first time. This is not only necessary to demonstrate the convergence of perturbation theory, but also results in a reduction of the theoretical uncertainty by a factor of 3 down to 3%. With this, we pave the way to improved analyses.

title: Examining Temporal Characteristics of Galactic Cosmic Rays in the AMS-02 Era
abstract: Abstract The energy spectra of Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) serve as critical probes of their astrophysical origins and propagation mechanisms through the interstellar medium. Among the key physical processes shaping the observed spectra, solar modulation, driven by turbulent heliospheric magnetic fields and the variability of the solar wind, plays a dominant role in modifying GCR fluxes within the inner heliosphere. The recent release of time-dependent flux measurements for He, Li, Be, B, C, N, and O by AMS-02 provides unprecedented precision to investigate solar modulation phenomena. In this study, we demonstrate that Li, Be, B, C, N, and O nuclei exhibit solar modulation parameters consistent with those of protons (p) and He within a modified force-field approximation (FFA) framework incorporating rigidity-dependent modulation potentials. By positing that GCRs with the same charge sign share solar modulation parameters, we further forecast daily fluxes of Ne, Mg, and Si from 2011 to 2020.

title: Reconciling anomalous quadrupole deformation in $^{200,202}$Hg with Coulomb excitation
abstract: Stable isotopes of mercury, with two fewer protons than magic lead, are found experimentally to exhibit oblate deformation, similar to neighbouring platinum isotopes. These isotopes are of special interest due to the use of $^{199}$Hg as an experimental laboratory for electric dipole moment searches, which are a powerful test of charge-parity ($CP$) violation and the interpretation of which depends critically on the quadrupole and octopule shapes of the underlying nucleus. It is observed that the ratio between experimental quadrupole moments and electric quadrupole transition strengths exceed physical limits, placing uncertainty on this underlying shape. In an effort to resolve this situation, a Coulomb excitation experiment was performed to remeasure the spectroscopic quadrupole moment ($Q_s(2^+_1)$) of $^{200}$Hg and $^{202}$Hg utilising $^{48}$Ti and $^{120}$Sn targets. The values obtained were $Q_s(2^+_1)$ $^{200,202}$Hg = $0.52(14)$, $0.63(10)$ eb, lying within physical limits defined by $B(E2)$ values but still consistent with near axially-symmetric oblate deformation. A systematic study of nuclei indicates that, as with neighbouring Pt isotopes, $^{200,202}$Hg are strongly oblate deformed, albeit without fully developing into an axial rotor.

title: Dynamical Triaxial Correlations in the Charge Radii of Neutron-Rich Ruthenium Isotopes
abstract: Nuclear charge radii are fundamental observables that track changes in nuclear structure. Recent measurements of neutron-rich Ru isotopes, interpreted using mean-field density-functional calculations, have highlighted the sensitivity of charge radii to static triaxial deformation. Whether dynamical shape fluctuations involving triaxial configurations---known to affect both nuclear ground- and excited-state properties---can reshape the charge-radii evolution remains unresolved. In this Letter, we investigate the charge radii of even-even neutron-rich $^{106-114}$Ru within a nuclear density-functional framework that combines three-dimensional angular-momentum projection with the generator-coordinate method. Including dynamical triaxial shape fluctuations yields charge radii in good agreement with experiment, without introducing additional adjustable parameters. By successively incorporating static triaxial deformation, dynamical axial shape fluctuations, and dynamical triaxial shape fluctuations, we trace how the predicted charge radii change at each step. These results demonstrate that triaxial shape dynamics can leave a substantial imprint on charge radii. They also inform the interpretation of experimental charge-radius measurements used to trace the evolution of nuclear structure, since charge radii alone cannot uniquely determine the underlying nuclear shape.

title: Deciphering Entangled Fission at Finite Excitations via Thermal Subspace Projection
abstract: The sharing of particles and energy between entangled fission fragments is known to contribute considerably to final observable distributions. This work unravels this sharing mechanism at finite excitations, which exhibits an intriguing quantum-thermal interplay relevant to long-standing open questions in induced fission. We formulate a thermal double particle-number projection onto spatial subspaces, using the Balian-Brezin representation and Grassmann integrals, to derive the projected partition function and observables. Based on finite-temperature dynamical fission calculations of 240Pu, the formalism explains the puzzling energy dependence of odd-even staggering in charge yields and of sawtooth neutron multiplicities. The present framework also provides a general projection tool for probing entangled thermal many-body systems.

title: Quasilinear Theory of Fast Flavor Instabilities
abstract: Dense neutrino plasmas can develop instabilities that drive collisionless flavor exchange, equivalent to the emission of flavomons, the quanta of flavor waves. We treat these waves as independent linear degrees of freedom and develop a quasilinear theory, including backreaction on the neutrino distribution and nonresonant neutrino-flavomon interactions, while neglecting wave-wave processes. In a statistically homogeneous, axisymmetric model, the saturated neutrino and flavomon distributions agree closely with periodic-box solutions of the original quantum kinetic equation. Our results provide the first theoretical interpretation for the numerical observations. They also show that flavomon phases have little influence on the final state, supporting the quasilinear theory as a framework for capturing flavor evolution without resolving nonlinear small-scale dynamics.

title: Deep learning search for gravitational waves from compact binary coalescence
abstract: Gravitational-wave searches rely on a combination of methods, including matched filtering, coherent analyses, and more recent machine-learning–based pipelines. For compact binary coalescences—where signals originate from the relativistic dynamics of compact objects—matched filtering remains a central element, but its computational cost will increase substantially with the data volumes and parameter-space coverage required by next-generation interferometers such as the Einstein Telescope. Developing complementary strategies that reduce computational load while preserving detection performance is therefore essential. We investigate a hybrid approach that combines matched-filtering concepts with convolutional neural networks, enabling efficient signal searches without relying on the usual χ 2 rejection test. Using simulated datasets that include injected signals in Gaussian noise, transient noise, and physical effects not represented in the template bank—such as eccentricity, precession and higher-order modes—we show that the method achieves a detection efficiency comparable to or better than a standard matched-filtering search while offering a more resource-efficient pipeline in all the cases where the physics included in the signals were not represented in the template bank or when glitches were affecting the data. Conversely, the analysis also reveals some loss of detection capability for standard binary neutron star and binary black hole searches in pure Gaussian noise. These results indicate that deep-learning–assisted searches can support sustainable gravitational-wave data analysis in future detector eras.

title: Hamiltonian framework for Chiral Gauge Theories on a Disk Boundary
abstract: I propose a Hamiltonian framework for chiral gauge theories (CGT) based on an existing Euclidean formulation, that uses 2n dimensional chiral fermions on the boundary of a 2n+1 dimensional disk. In the original Euclidean formulation, boundary gauge fields were extended into the bulk using $2n + 1$ dimensional gauge field equations of motion (EOM). This creates a bottleneck for constructing a Hamiltonian. I present an alternate proposal for extending the gauge fields into the bulk that is compatible with both a Hamiltonian framework and a Euclidean path integral. Applying this to Abelian gauge fields produces exact expressions of interior fields as a functional of the boundary fields, which can be directly used in a Hamiltonian formulation. Euclidean analysis of the new gauge field extension shows that it can preserve the non-perturbative content of the original construction, including the behavior of topological charge, associated chiral fermion zero modes and an absence of the strong CP problem when applied to the Standard Model. This construction opens up a route to a Hamiltonian treatment and future quantum simulation of CGTs on a disk boundary.

title: Peripheral nucleon-nucleon scattering with explicit vector mesons in chiral perturbation theory
abstract: Background: In chiral perturbation theory (ChPT), heavy degrees of freedom are integrated out, with their contributions absorbed into low-energy constants. Keeping the $\rho$ and $\omega$ explicit within ChPT retains the finite-range momentum dependence associated with these mesons. Purpose: We study how explicit $\rho$ and $\omega$ mesons affect peripheral $NN$ phase shifts. Methods: We incorporate the vector mesons by counting their masses as hard and the momentum they carry as soft. The next-to-next-to-leading-order nuclear force includes, in addition to one- and two-pion exchange, one-vector-meson exchange with dressed propagators and vertex functions. The vector propagators and vertex functions are fixed from the mesonic sector and the nucleon electromagnetic form factors. We calculate neutron--proton scattering with $J=3$--$5$ up to $T_{\rm lab}=300$ MeV and examine the sensitivity to one-pion-exchange iteration and the spectral-function regularization scheme. Results: The vector-meson contribution falls rapidly with $J$. In several $J=3$ waves it moves the phase shifts toward PWA93, while in other waves the change is small or moves the phase shift away. In ${}^{3}\mathrm{G}_{3}$ the change toward PWA93 persists under variations of the spectral cutoff, and its size is nearly independent of the treatment of one-pion exchange. The ${}^{3}\mathrm{D}_{3}$ wave is strongly cutoff dependent, and there the $\omega$ contribution outweighs the opposing $\rho$ contribution. The tensor and spin-spin components of the $\rho$ interaction play the dominant roles in moving $\epsilon_3$ and ${}^{1}\mathrm{F}_{3}$ toward PWA93, respectively. Conclusions: The effect of the explicit vector mesons on the peripheral phase shifts is channel dependent. The $\rho$ meson gives the dominant shifts toward PWA93, particularly in $\epsilon_3$ and ${}^{3}\mathrm{G}_{3}$.

title: Heavy-quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma via a fractional Langevin equation
abstract: The dynamics of heavy quarks in the quark-gluon plasma is commonly described within a standard Langevin equation framework. In this work, we extend the conventional framework by using a fractional Langevin equation based on the Caputo derivative of order $\alpha$ with $1<\alpha\leq 2$. We solve the fractional Langevin equation and derive the corresponding {\textit {fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem}} for the heavy quark thermalization in the quark-gluon plasma medium. We calculate the time evolution of the mean-squared momentum, mean-squared displacement, momentum distribution, energy loss, longitudinal momentum loss, transverse momentum broadening, and the nuclear suppression factor of the heavy quarks. The mean-squared momentum thermalizes to the same value for all $\alpha$ at late times, in agreement with the fractional fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and the nuclear suppression factor shows a systematic $\alpha$-dependence. The energy loss of an energetic heavy quark grows strongly with $\alpha$. The time evolution of the heavy quark momentum distribution provides additional sensitivity to the fractional dynamics of the heavy quarks in the QGP medium.

title: Sharpening the Mass Measurement of PSR J1048+2339 via High-cadence Photometry
abstract: Abstract Neutron stars are among the densest objects in the Universe, and mass measurements are crucial to the understanding of their equations of state. Pulsars in tight binaries can be weighed dynamically, but accurate mass estimates are often hampered by uncertainties in orbital inclinations. In this paper, we report on multiepoch optical monitoring of the pulsar binary, PSR J1048+2339, using the 0.5 m RIFT telescope at Lulin Observatory. Our observations reveal frequent optical flares with eclipses caused by the companion. Using the eclipse duration with archival photometric data and orbital ephemeris in the literature, we constrain the inclination to 78 . ° 0 ± 1 . ° 0 and the pulsar mass to 1.7 9 − 0.08 + 0.09 solar masses. This measurement is among the most precise for any redback system to date, demonstrating a novel way to improve the pulsar mass measures with small-aperture optical telescopes. Furthermore, the optical eclipse duration is significantly shorter than that measured in M/GeV γ -rays, possibly suggesting that a fraction of the eclipsed γ -ray emission originates from the apex of the intrabinary shock. Based on these constraints, we estimate the magnetic field strength of the companion to be 30–170 G. This is consistent with the high field strength implied by the X-ray orbital modulation observed.

title: Multi-phonon wobbling excitations as a probe for dynamical quasiparticle alignment
abstract: The multiple and very extended triaxial strongly deformed bands of the $^{163,165}$Lu nuclei are used to ascertain the spin dependence of the odd quasiparticle alignment. The band heads are found to favor a tilted alignment geometry which gradually evolves into a transverse configuration. Distinct dynamical regimes are thus identified in specific bands and spin intervals, which are discussed in terms of wobbling excitations based on the analysis of the wave functions and $E2$ transition probabilities.

title: Investigating three-body resonances in $\alpha\alpha\Omega/\Omega_{ccc}$ clusters within the $^{9}_{\Omega/\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ nucleus
abstract: We investigate the bound and resonant states of the $\alpha+\alpha+\Omega$ and $\alpha+\alpha+\Omega_{ccc}$ three-body systems, corresponding to $^{9}_{\Omega}{\mathrm{Be}}$ and $^{9}_{\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$, within the Gaussian expansion method combined with the complex scaling method. The $\alpha\Omega$ and $\alpha\Omega_{ccc}$ interactions are constructed by folding the $N\Omega$ and $N\Omega_{ccc}$ potentials obtained from lattice QCD calculations by the HAL QCD Collaboration with the nucleon density distribution of the $\alpha$ particle. The uncertainty associated with the $\alpha$-particle matter radius is also examined. For the $\Omega$ sector, the strong $N\Omega$ attraction generates deeply bound $0_1^+$, $2_1^+$, and $4_1^+$ states in $^{9}_{\Omega}{\mathrm{Be}}$, accompanied by a pronounced contraction of the $\alpha\alpha$ core, demonstrating a strong gluelike effect of the $\Omega$ baryon. An unconventional inversion between the $0_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ levels is also predicted. In contrast, the $\Omega_{ccc}$ baryon produces considerably weaker attraction: the $0_1^+$ state of $^{9}_{\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ is weakly bound, whereas the $2_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ states remain resonances. Their resonance energies and widths exhibit a clear dependence on the strength of the $\alpha\Omega_{ccc}$ interaction. These results reveal qualitatively different gluelike behaviors of the $\Omega$ and $\Omega_{ccc}$ baryons and provide predictions for the spectroscopy of exotic multistrange and triply charmed hypernuclei.

title: Pfaffian and minor formulas in number-conserved pairing theory
abstract: In this work, I present closed-form formulas for the norm and many-body density matrices between wave functions with exact particle numbers in pairing theory. The expressions, written as sums of Pfaffians and minors, apply to both even and odd particle-number systems and to pair condensates as well as broken-pair configurations. This formalism facilitates calculations using the generator coordinate method and symmetry restoration techniques, such as angular momentum projection. I apply these formulas to $^{70}$Ge and $^{69}$Ge using the angular-momentum-projected number-conserved BCS theory. The calculations describe low-lying collective bands and provide an interpretation of their intrinsic structures.

title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
abstract: We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.

title: From Harmonic Oscillators to Multiplicity Distributions in Particle Production Processes
abstract: We propose an oscillator framework of studying multi-particle production processes using the information theory approach. For a system of degenerate oscillators, we derive the negative binomial distribution (NBD) and its nonadditive generalization represented as gNBD. We observe that gNBD derived from nonadditive statistics describes data in higher multiplicity region, thereby providing an alternative for the multi-component distributions used in phenomenological studies. We also generalize our framework for non-degenerate oscillators and encounter a Lerch-type generalization of the Barnes zeta function that, to the best of our knowledge, has not been studied in the context of nonadditive statistics and multiplicity studies before.

title: Fano formula for resonance poles in the Jost--random-phase approximation: Breit--Wigner-type peaks, Fano dips, and Fano-type peaks in $^{16}$O and $^{208}$Pb
abstract: Fano's formula is derived for a resonance pole of the strength function in the continuum random-phase approximation formulated within the Jost function framework (Jost-RPA). At a pole, the residue of the transition-amplitude vector of the open channels lies along the Takagi vector of the pole for every external field. Of the background, the amplitude vector without the pole term, only the component along the Takagi vector therefore interferes with the resonance, and the strength function can be written exactly in Fano's form for several continuum channels. In this form $q$ is complex and energy dependent, and the modulus $p$ of the cosine of the angle between the Takagi vector and the background serves as Fano's $|\rho|$. In an idealized form of Fano's model, $q$ and $p$ reduce to Fano's $q$ and to the overlap $|\rho|$ of Fano and Cooper. A second exact form separates a Fano term and a Breit-Wigner term, the part of the resonance that does not interfere with the background. Three patterns follow: Breit-Wigner-type peaks for $p^2\simeq0$, Fano dips, and Fano-type peaks for $p^2\simeq1$. A negative real part of the complex transition probability, the residue of the response function at the pole, is equivalent to Fano's condition $|q|<1$ for a dip at the resonance energy, evaluated at the complex conjugate of the pole energy. Earlier Jost-RPA analyses were made only for $^{16}$O. The analysis is applied to $^{16}$O and to $^{208}$Pb, with up to 62 open channels. It attributes the dips found earlier in $^{16}$O to the interference of single poles with their backgrounds, and it shows in both nuclei Fano dips, Fano-type peaks, and poles whose pattern changes with the field. In $^{208}$Pb, narrow poles near the broad poles of the giant dipole resonances produce Fano-type peaks with dips in the field of each resonance. The patterns are not determined by the collectivity indicators of the poles.

title: Ab initio-guided optical potentials for semi-magic nuclei from Gorkov self-consistent Green's functions
abstract: We construct ab initio-guided nonlocal optical potentials for semi-magic nuclei from the self-consistent Gorkov-ADC(2) one-body Green's function. This extends ab initio self-consistent Green's function approaches to open-shell targets and to proton projectiles. The starting point is the NNLO$_{\rm sat}$ chiral interaction, whose three-nucleon component is included as an effective two-body interaction. The self-energy is computed in a harmonic-oscillator basis, transformed to coordinate space and used in the scattering code SIDES. Its imaginary part relies on a phenomenological energy-dependent width, hence the label ab initio-guided. Differential and integral (total and reaction) cross sections are compared with data for n,p+$^{40}$Ca and p+$^{42}$Ca. Forward angles are well reproduced. Backward angles reveal a lack of absorption, which calls for larger model spaces and many-body truncations beyond Gorkov-ADC(2).
