title: Impact of Eccentricity on the Population Properties of Neutron Star–Black Hole Mergers
abstract: Abstract We revisit the population properties of neutron star–black hole (NSBH) mergers using low-mass compact binary coalescences reported through GWTC-4. Employing pyEFPE , an inspiral-only waveform model that captures both orbital eccentricity and spin-induced precession, we reanalyse all binary neutron star (BNS) and NSBH events observed via gravitational waves. The BNS systems GW170817 and GW190425 are fully consistent with quasi-circular inspirals, while GW200105 stands out among the NSBH binaries as the only system exhibiting significant residual eccentricity at 20 Hz, strengthening evidence for dynamically driven formation pathways. The remaining NSBH events show no measurable eccentricity and appear broadly compatible with low-spin binaries formed through isolated stellar evolution. Using hierarchical Bayesian inference, we obtain the first joint constraints on the mass, spin, and eccentricity distributions of NSBH binaries. Our results also yield the first simultaneous constraints on spin precession and orbital eccentricity in NSBH mergers, while the inferred merger rates remain fully consistent with previous LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA measurements. Treating all NSBH systems as a single population yields results compatible with formation in hierarchical triples, whereas the quasi-circular population remains broadly consistent with isolated evolution. Our results highlight the emerging role of eccentricity as a key discriminator between formation channels. As the number of NSBH detections grows, joint constraints on masses, spins, and orbital eccentricities will enable increasingly sharp tests of dynamical versus isolated binary evolution, establishing NSBH systems as powerful probes of compact-object astrophysics.

title: FINESSE: A Versatile Beamline for Fundamental Interactions with Neutrons at the European Spallation SourcE
abstract: FINESSE (A Versatile Beamline for \textbf{F}undamental \textbf{I}nteractions with \textbf{N}eutrons at the \textbf{E}uropean \textbf{S}pallation \textbf{S}ourc\textbf{E}) is a proposed versatile beamline for fundamental interactions with neutrons at the European Spallation Source. Building on the HIBEAM design studies, FINESSE extends the original concept into a dual-guide beamline capable of operating either in a high-flux configuration or in a low-background configuration within a single ESS beam port. The high-flux branch is optimized for rare-process searches, including neutron--antineutron oscillations, neutron--sterile-neutron transitions, axion-like-particle searches, neutron charge measurements, and rare neutron decays. The low-background branch is designed for precision measurements requiring strong suppression of prompt and line-of-sight backgrounds, with a cryogenic neutron electric-dipole-moment experiment used as a benchmark case. A baseline exchangeable-guide concept has been developed in which only short guide sections inside the ESS bunker are exchanged, while the upstream extraction system and chopper positions remain fixed. A staged implementation, Short FINESSE, would use the upstream section of the high-flux beamline together with a compact magnetically controlled experimental region, enabling an early physics and R\&D programme before completion of the full facility. This paper summarizes the scientific case, beamline concept, guide simulations, chopper and timing system, magnetic-field control, detector developments, and staged implementation strategy. FINESSE would establish a long-term particle-physics infrastructure at ESS, providing a beamline for both discovery-driven searches and precision neutron measurements throughout the lifetime of the facility.

title: Cross-shell excitations and the impact of the high- j intruder orbital in 94 Tc
abstract: Abstract The high-spin level structure of the N = 51 nucleus 94 Tc has been investigated using large-scale shell-model calculations with different effective interactions. Calculations including neutron excitations across the N = 50 shell gap reproduce the main features of the experimental level scheme and identify neutron core excitation as an important mechanism for generating high-spin states. An extended model space including the 1 h 11 / 2 neutron orbital provides improved agreement with experiment. Wave-function analyses show that 1 h 11 / 2 configurations dominate over a broad spin range, while N = 50 core excitations are largely suppressed. The results reveal the evolution of the competition between 1 h 11 / 2 excitation and N = 50 core breaking with increasing spin.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Contribution of incomplete fusion to the evaporation residue cross sections in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction
abstract: The formation of the evaporation residues in the $^{30}$Si$+^{186}$W reaction leading to the compound nucleus $^{216}$Ra$^*$ has been studied in the framework of the dinuclear system (DNS) model. The capture, complete fusion, quasifission, and incomplete fusion cross sections have been calculated at the collision energies $E_{c.m.}=107.6-172.2$MeV by averaging over the orientation angles of the axial symmetry axes of the deformed $^{30}$Si and $^{186}$W nuclei. The incomplete fusion is considered as the breakup of the DNS with the emission of the $\alpha$ particle from its very mass-asymmetric configuration, which is populated by the nucleon transfer in collisions with large orbital angular momentum. The survival probabilities of the excited $^{216}$Ra and of the conjugate nucleus $^{212}$Rn formed after the $\alpha$-particle emission have been calculated using the statistical model. It is shown that the complete fusion is the main source of the evaporation residues at the lower collision energies, while above $E_{c.m.}=128$MeV the Rn isotopes formed in the incomplete fusion give more than half of the calculated evaporation residue cross section. The sum of both contributions describes the slow decrease of the measured total evaporation residue cross section at these energies, where the yield of the Ra isotopes decreases by an order of magnitude. The calculation of the de-excitation of $^{216}$Ra$^*$ with the emission of protons and $\alpha$ particles shows that the contribution of the complete fusion to the cross sections of the isotopes $^{212}$Rn and $^{211}$Rn is negligible, and these isotopes are formed in the incomplete fusion. The fusion probability calculated for the partial waves $\ell\leq30\hbar$ is about 0.75 in comparison with the value $0.57\pm0.08$ extracted from the experimental data at the same collision energies.

title: Scattering phase shifts from overlap relations in the $J$-matrix method
abstract: We present an approach to the quantum mechanical scattering problem in which computation of a wave function and determination of scattering parameters are separate steps. This approach is built on the $J$-matrix formalism, but in place of the usual $J$-matrix procedures, we introduce a novel formula that extracts phase shifts accurately from scattering states computed in a square-integrable basis. This formula is closely analogous to existing integral relations or overlap integrals in a (continuous) position basis. We then demonstrate the extraction of phase shifts from wave functions in single-channel potential scattering. For a soft but realistic nucleon-nucleon potential, Daejeon16, we obtain good phase shifts with as few as six oscillator basis states, using the Lippmann-Schwinger equation to obtain scattering states at arbitrary energies even in this highly truncated space. These results constitute a step towards calculations in which scattering observables are extracted from scattering states generated in a many-body framework with square-integrable basis functions, such as the configuration-interaction shell model.

title: Research on phase detection technology for synchrotron accelerator RF system based on TDC feedback
abstract: Abstract During long-term operation of the RF system in the Hefei Light Source II (HLS II) storage ring, a prescribed phase relationship must be maintained between the reference signal (Ref) and the cavity-voltage sampling signal (Pt). After the RF system is powered on or recovers from a fault, this phase relationship must be rapidly and reliably restored to support low-level RF (LLRF) closed-loop control. Conventional phase-detection circuits based on dedicated detector chips may provide insufficient phase resolution for this application and require additional circuitry to determine the phase-lead or phase-lag relationship. To address these limitations, an FPGA-based tapped-delay-line time-to-digital converter (TDC) is developed for direct phase detection of the 204.030 MHz Ref and Pt signals. The proposed design combines three staggered CARRY4 chains with multiple-measurement averaging and directly determines the relative phase direction. Code-density characterization gives an average TDC bin width of 3.82 ps, corresponding to a theoretical phase resolution of approximately 0.28 ∘ . In bench tests with known input phase settings, the average phase-measurement root-mean-square error (RMSE) is 0.2065 ∘ . The system was further evaluated using actual accelerator RF signals over a continuous 75 h interval. The directly measured RF phase difference exhibits an RMS deviation of 0.6319 ∘ about its mean value. This value characterizes the aggregate long-term phase fluctuation under actual operating conditions and remains below the 1 ∘ RMS phase-stability requirement of the HLS II LLRF system. The results demonstrate that the proposed detector satisfies the requirements for online Ref-Pt phase-difference measurement and phase-direction discrimination.

title: Neutrino Emissivity in Δ -Direct-Urca Processes inside Neutron Stars
abstract: Observed massive neutron stars may contain heavier baryons such as $Δ$ isobars and hyperons in their interiors. In the presence of $Δ$ isobars, the neutrino emitting nucleonic Urca processes can be accompanied by $Δ$-direct-Urca processes involving nucleons and hyperons. Over the past three decades, significant theoretical effort has been dedicated to understanding the thermal evolution of neutron stars with the nucleonic and hyperonic Urca processes emerging as dominant cooling mechanisms. While recent studies have proposed the presence of $Δ$ isobars in the dense core of neutron stars, the specific contribution of the $Δ$-direct-Urca process to neutrino emissivity has not been explicitly quantified. In this work, we address this gap by deriving the neutrino emissivity associated with $Δ$-direct-Urca processes in dense matter inside neutron stars. We show that once $Δ$-direct-Urca processes become kinematically allowed, their emissivities are comparable to those of nucleonic-direct-Urca processes.

title: Experimental Demonstration of Soft-Tissue Muon Scattering Tomography
abstract: Muons have fascinated physicists since their discovery in cosmic rays almost a century ago. Their large mass and relatively long lifetime allow relativistic muons to traverse large amounts of matter, a property that has been exploited to probe otherwise inaccessible structures, from volcanoes and archaeological monuments to shielded nuclear materials. Here, we experimentally demonstrate for the first time that muon scattering tomography can be extended to biological soft tissue. We image an anthropomorphic thorax phantom using a 2 GeV/c muon beam at the CERN Proton Synchrotron and reconstruct its three-dimensional scattering density from the measured deflections of individual muons. Despite the weak scattering produced by tissue-equivalent materials, the reconstructed density agrees with the expectation from simulation at the percent level. Our results extend muon imaging into a previously unexplored regime and open the possibility of using muons as a complementary probe for medical imaging.

title: Asteroseismology of Neutron Stars with Axion-Like Particle Mediated Dark Matter
abstract: We examine the impacts of dark matter (DM) on the observables of the neutron star (NS). The interaction of DM with nucleons intermediate by axion-like particles (ALPs), and the DM-admixed NS (DNS) is formulated in the framework of the relativistic mean field (RMF) formalism. The effects of the DM on the NS are characterized by two parameters: DM Fermi momentum ($q_f$) and DM mass ($m_\chi$). By varying these two parameters, we investigate how the NS's mass, radius, and tidal deformability are altered. Furthermore, we study how the ALP-mediated DM impacts the stability of the NS through the analysis of radial oscillations. In addition, the nonradial oscillation has been investigated by calculating its fundamental mode frequency in the DNS and analyzed how the ALP-mediated DM modifies its behavior.

title: A 4D $T^\prime$-expanded lattice QCD equation of state with a multi-dimensional 3D-Ising-type critical contribution
abstract: Inferring the possible existence and location of a critical point on the QCD phase diagram through experimental observations requires equations of state that include both lattice QCD constraints and critical behavior. In this manuscript, we present the first four-dimensional equation of state in the $(T,\mu_B,\mu_Q,\mu_S)$ space combining the lattice 4D $T^\prime$-Expansion Scheme with a critical contribution mapped from the 3D Ising model. We extend the earlier two-dimensional construction, the so-called Ising 2D-TExS in the $(T, \mu_B)$ plane, promoting the critical point to a parametrizable critical surface in the full four-dimensional thermodynamic space. Our framework provides a family of equations of state to systematically study the effects of criticality in realistic hydrodynamic simulations with $BQS$ conserved charges, going beyond the case of strangeness neutrality, by varying the geometry of the critical surface and the strength of criticality at finite $\mu_B$, $\mu_Q$ and $\mu_S$ separately.

title: Evidence of Nuclear Urca Process in the Ocean of Neutron-Star Superburst MAXI J1752$-$457
abstract: We propose that the rapid cooling of the neutron star following its X-ray superburst in MAXI J1752$-$457 over a period of 4 days, observed by two Japanese satellites, MAXI and NinjaSat, is due to enhanced neutrino emission from cycles of electron capture and $\beta^{-}$ decay involving odd-$A$ nuclei (or Urca pairs) in the ocean. Hence, this work provides the first indication of the possible existence of such a ``nuclear Urca process". The observation of MAXI J1752$-$457 implies a hot ignition layer with a maximum temperature of $\sim 4~{\rm GK}$, located near the Urca shell in the ocean, such that the nuclear Urca process becomes dominant for up to $\sim 2$ days after the superburst. This behavior is distinct from that of normal Type-I X-ray bursts, which are triggered by hydrogen or helium burning in much shallower layers than those of superbursts. Our findings enable probing of superburst ashes through Urca pairs via long-term monitoring of crust cooling on day-long timescales.

title: Signal-to-noise problems in fault-tolerant quantum computation
abstract: Quantum computation offers a promising alternative to classical Monte Carlo methods by naturally avoiding sign problems through unitary evolution. A common misconception follows from this: because quantum simulation sidesteps the sign problem, it is often assumed to be an essentially perfect substitute for classical sampling. This is false---quantum measurements are intrinsically stochastic, and estimating observables often requires a number of samples that grows exponentially with system size, time separation, or inverse temperature, exactly as in the classical signal-to-noise problem. In this work, we analyze the origin and structure of signal-to-noise problems in quantum computation, drawing parallels with classical Monte Carlo, and demonstrate that such noise persists even in sign-problem-free regimes. We discuss strategies to mitigate it, in particular a quantum generalization of Stein control variates construction, in which unbiased estimators are built from operator commutators $[X,A]$ and their discrete diagonal counterparts, and validate the approach with exactly solvable numerical examples that quantify the achievable variance reduction. Our results underscore that variance reduction, not merely sign-problem avoidance, is required to make quantum algorithms practically viable for many-body physics.

title: Separating entanglement at emission from femtoscopic correlations
abstract: We investigate how femtoscopic correlations modify the relation between the spin entanglement of emitted particle pairs and that of pairs selected at a given relative momentum. For two spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ particles, we show that the momentum-selected spin state can be entangled even when the corresponding state at emission is separable. We derive a momentum-dependent separability criterion that determines whether the observed spin correlations require entanglement at emission. As an application, we consider a pair of identical $\Lambda$ hyperons, for which quantum statistics and final-state interactions affect the singlet and triplet spin channels differently at low relative momentum. Our results provide a framework for using experimentally accessible spin correlations to investigate entanglement at emission.

title: Factorization in quasifree breakup reactions with two bodies left behind
abstract: We consider scenarios in which a shallow bound state undergoes breakup by a probe whose energy is high compared to the binding energy. The first two scenarios, which serve as warm-up exercises, involve a single heavy particle bound to a light particle, analogous to a core nucleus bound to a neutron. We show that in quasi-free kinematics, the leading effect comes from the heavy particle being knocked out by the probe, with corrections suppressed by inverse powers of the probe momentum. This formally justifies extracting neutron form factors from high-energy deuteron breakup in quasi-free kinematics. In Scenario 1, the probe is a local current; in Scenario 2, it is hadron scattering. In Scenarios 3 and 4 we consider, respectively, a local current and hadron scattering, but now on a three-body bound state of a heavy particle and two light particles. Hard knockout of the heavy particle leaves two low-energy particles behind, which can interact with one another. In all four scenarios, we prove that the amplitude is dominated by the nearby on-shell pole of the heavy-particle propagator and derive a closed-form expression for this contribution. When two bodies are left behind, the leading amplitude is the product of the scattering of the two light particles, a dynamical function depending on the probe, and a real function related to the bound-state wavefunction. Thus, quasi-free removal of a core nucleus from a system with halo neutrons provides access to on-shell data on multi-neutron interactions. The resulting amplitudes are relativistic and satisfy unitarity for the remnant subsystem exactly. We also provide complementary non-relativistic derivations. While the derivations are for spinless particles, the generalization to spin is straightforward, since the results depend only on quasi-free knockout kinematics; we make no assumptions about the inter-particle dynamics.

title: Evidence for low-energy electron contribution to vacuum Compton detector intrinsic sensitivity under bias fields
abstract: Abstract Intrinsic sensitivity is a key parameter for vacuum Compton detectors (VCDs), enabling the quantitative analysis of pulsed γ-radiation fields. Since VCDs are insensitive to the emitted electron energy, traditional calibration of intrinsic sensitivity has generally neglected the contribution of low-energy electrons. In this work, a zero-bias Monte Carlo (MC) simulation with and without low-energy electron transport using the Geant4 toolkit gave nearly the same net yield and intrinsic sensitivity. To test whether an applied electric field can still enhance the detector response beyond this zero-bias baseline, an experimental VCD system incorporating bias electrodes was designed. By applying an electric field across the emitter, the signal was enhanced by over 10% under 60 Co irradiation, with Al reaching a maximum increase of 15%. Further analysis of the derivative of the signal-voltage curve revealed that this enhancement mainly originated from electrons below 20 eV, which is consistent with the energy range of true secondary electrons. When the vacuum bias field is included in the Monte Carlo calculation, the predicted sensitivity remains essentially unchanged relative to the zero-bias case. The measured gain is therefore attributed to near-surface processes that are not included in the present vacuum-transport framework. This study provides experimental evidence that low-energy secondary electrons can measurably enhance VCD intrinsic sensitivity under bias-assisted conditions, identifies a concrete modeling gap at the surface under bias, and suggests a practical route for sensitivity enhancement.

title: Comment on arXiv:2604.27678
abstract: Shuang-Jie Liu et al. (arXiv:2604.27678) reported that the momentum-dependent nuclear mean field (MDI) with $K_0 = 230$ MeV 'can fit fairly' the experimental data for Au + Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 3$ GeV, whereas the momentum-independent nuclear mean fields (MID) with $K_0 = 230$ MeV and $K_0 = 380$ MeV 'can only partially describe' the experimental results. We quantify these statements by performing $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit tests for the comparison between the theoretical calculations and the experimental distributions presented in that work. For the complete set of data, all three calculations show highly statistically significant disagreement with the experimental data, with (p-value) p < 0.001. For the $0-10\%$ centrality class, however, the MDI calculation with $K_0 = 230$ MeV gives p = 0.49, indicating no statistically significant disagreement with the experimental data for the proton transverse-momentum distributions and the rapidity dependence of the mean transverse momentum, whereas both MID calculations give p < 0.001. For the $10-40\%$ centrality class, the analysis of the directed flows of protons, $K^+$ mesons, and $\Lambda$-hyperons gives the largest p-values for MDI with $K_0 = 230$ MeV and MID with $K_0 = 380$ MeV, with p = 1.00 and p = 0.97, respectively. In contrast, the analysis of the corresponding elliptic flow data gives p < 0.001 for all three calculations. Our results demonstrate that the qualitative statements 'fit fairly' and 'only partially describe' depend substantially on the particular observables and centrality classes considered and cannot by themselves establish statistically acceptable agreement between the calculations and the experimental data.

title: Anisotropic chromo-field fluctuations and spin alignment of quarkonia
abstract: Spin correlations are believed to contribute significantly to vector-meson spin alignment. In this work, we study the generation of spin correlations through fluctuations of the chromomagnetic field in the quark-gluon plasma. We show that anisotropic fluctuations generically lead to finite vector-meson spin alignment. We study two sources of anisotropic chromomagnetic-field fluctuations: one arises from the motion of a vector meson relative to the medium, which makes isotropic fluctuations in the medium anisotropic in the meson rest frame; the other arises from QGP shear flow through viscous corrections to the chromomagnetic field fluctuations. The linear HTL estimates indicate sensitivity to the nonperturbative magnetic sector; we treat the full field correlators as phenomenological inputs.We apply the mechanism to study spin alignment of $J/\psi$ in heavy ion collisions. With QGP evolution modeled by Bjorken flow, we obtain negative spin alignment from both sources, with the shear induced contribution numerically suppressed compared to the motion induced contribution.

title: Vacancy-mediated ultrafast oxide-ion conduction in excess-oxygen Sillén oxybromides
abstract: Abstract Solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs) require electrolytes with high oxide-ion conductivity at low temperatures (200–400 °C) to reduce costs. Here, we report that Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br exhibits oxide-ion conductivity of 0.01 S cm⁻¹ at 233 °C within the “Norby gap” in dry atmospheres. This performance exceeds that of leading proton conductors, such as BaZr 0.8 Y 0.2 O 2.9 and BaZr 0.4 Ce 0.4 Y 0.1 Yb 0.1 O 2.9 , as well as representative oxide-ion conductors, including yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ), LaGaO 3 -based phases (LSGM), and Bi 2 V 0.7 Sb 0.3 O 5.5 . Bi 1.9 Te 0.1 LaO 4.05 Br also exhibits negligible chemical expansion and high chemical stability under oxidizing, reducing, and CO 2 -containing atmospheres. The high conductivity is associated with a layered Sillén structure composed of Bi-containing triple fluorite-like slabs and Br layers, together with oxygen vacancies that enable vacancy-mediated oxide-ion migration. Despite the presence of excess oxide ions, oxide-ion transport predominantly occurs via a vacancy mechanism, as revealed by ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, static density functional theory calculations, and neutron diffraction analyses. These findings establish a design principle for high-performance oxide-ion conductors based on vacancy-mediated oxide-ion transport in excess-oxygen Bi-containing Sillén oxyhalides.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Probing eV-scale sterile neutrinos with neutrinoless double-beta decay and beta decay
abstract: An eV-scale sterile Majorana neutrino can suppress neutrinoless double-beta decay through destructive interference with the active-neutrino contribution, weakening the resulting constraints on sterile-neutrino parameters. We investigate how complementary beta-decay information restricts this cancellation in the 3+1 framework. Using updated oscillation parameters that include the first JUNO results, we determine the allowed sterile-neutrino mass and mixing regions for both normal and inverted ordering. We show that an upper limit on the effective beta-decay mass $m_\beta$ of the three light neutrinos strengthens the constraints from neutrinoless double-beta decay alone. The beta-decay bound restricts the light-neutrino masses and hence the cancellation between the active and sterile contributions to $m_{\beta\beta}$. We derive analytic expressions for the resulting boundaries and use complex-plane geometry to explain the allowed values of the sterile Majorana phase $\alpha_4$ for a finite $|m_{\beta\beta}|$ limit. For the mixing considered, normal ordering allows a broad range of $\alpha_4$ at small sterile masses, whereas inverted ordering favors values near $\pi$. The allowed phase range narrows as the sterile mass approaches its upper bound or the limit on $|m_{\beta\beta}|$ becomes more stringent.

title: Particle Correlations in Jets
abstract: We study particle correlations in high energy jets by comparing the measured energy-energy correlator with that constructed from two individual energy flows with respect to the jet axis. This comparison demonstrates that the genuine correlations are stronger at moderate or large angles across all jet energies, indicating that they are coming from correlated splitting. Meanwhile, at small angles, they increase with jet energy, exhibiting a peculiar pattern that can be used to explore jet energy loss in heavy-ion collisions. This method will provide a unique tool to disentangle different physics by comparing the genuine correlations in jet energy-energy correlators between heavy-ion collisions and proton-proton collisions.

title: Inclusive breakup of three-body projectiles: A unified four-body framework for pair-detection and single-particle observables
abstract: Inclusive breakup measurements detect only part of a projectile while the remaining fragments interact with the target. For a projectile with three constituents, these measurements can probe correlations that are lost when the projectile is treated as two preformed clusters. I derive cross-section sum rules within the distorted-wave Born approximation for detecting either a pair or a single constituent, retaining the full three-body projectile wave function. For pair detection, the detected state is projected from this wave function. Comparing the resulting reaction source with its factorized limit tests, at the amplitude level, what the preformed-cluster approximation omits. For single-particle detection, both unobserved constituents can interact with the target, and their absorption includes a contribution mediated by target excitation that is absent from an independent-fragment description. The optical reduction recovers the Carlson-Frederico-Hussein absorption kernel [Phys. Lett. B \textbf{767}, 53 (2017)]; explicit coupling of the detected particle to target excitation adds further contributions. The ${}^6\mathrm{Li}=\alpha+n+p$ example shows how neutron-proton states beyond the bound deuteron enter the reaction source. I give a route for calculating the single-particle spectrum using inelastic target transition form factors and three-body propagation.

title: Feeding the Little Monster: An Accreting Intermediate-mass Black Hole in a Minor Merger Secondary Galaxy
abstract: Abstract We report the discovery of a luminous supersoft X-ray source associated with the secondary galaxy in a 10:1 minor merger at z = 0.216. We identified the system in the 3D-HST survey and observed it serendipitously in more than 100 Chandra observations, providing a combined exposure of 6.6 Ms. The secondary galaxy ( log ( M * / M ⊙ ) = 8.24) exhibits X-ray emission detected exclusively below 2.0 keV, with no significant hard-band photons. Because the source is low count, we characterize its spectrum using Bayesian hardness-ratio analysis combined with simulations of physically motivated spectral models folded through the Chandra response files. The observed count rates and hardness ratios are reproduced by a thermal accretion-disk spectrum with rest-frame inner-disk temperatures kT in = 0.18–0.30 keV and luminosities log( L X /erg s −1 ) = 40.5–41.2. Interpreted using a standard thin-disk framework, these properties imply a black hole mass of M • ≈ 8 × 10 2 –5 × 10 3 M ⊙ accreting at ≈0.2–0.5 of the Eddington rate. Alternative interpretations involving ultraluminous X-ray supersoft sources are disfavored by the source’s luminosity, temperature, and lack of variability, and the host galaxy’s low star-formation rate. Numerical simulations predict that black holes in smaller, secondary galaxies could experience episodic rapid growth during minor mergers. This discovery provides observational support for this scenario and suggests that minor interactions may be an important channel for assembling supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dwarf galaxies.

title: COOL-LAMPS. IX. A Rare Duo of Quasars Each Lensed by a Single Massive Galaxy Cluster
abstract: Abstract Wide-separation lensed quasars (WSLQs) are rare systems that arise from the chance alignment of two objects: a galaxy cluster and a background quasar. After two decades, only seven WSLQs have been found. Here, we report the discovery of COOL J1153+0755 by the COOL-LAMPS collaboration in DECaLS imaging and its confirmation with follow-up observations with the Magellan Telescopes and the Nordic Optical Telescope. This system features two multiply imaged quasars each lensed into four images by the same z = 0.4301 cluster: a classic broad-line Type I quasar at z = 1.524 (COOL J1153A) and a dust-obscured Type II quasar at z = 1.939 (COOL J1153B), with maximum image separations of 25 . ″ 6 and 26 . ″ 0 , respectively. We construct a lens model to estimate a projected cluster mass of M ( < 500 kpc) ∼ 3.3 × 10 14 M ⊙ and relative time delays between the three brightest images of each quasar of Δ t A3, A1 ∼ 800, Δ t A2, A1 ∼ 1200, Δ t B1, B3 ∼ 800, and Δ t B2, B3 ∼ 1000 days. COOL J1153A resides in a dense environment with three nearby galaxies, two of which are also strongly lensed. We identified COOL J1153+0755 without making a morphological cut in the DECaLS catalog; none of its multiple images are classified as point sources in those data, implying that morphology-based selection would miss such systems. COOL J1153+0755 expands the WSLQ sample from seven to eight systems (nine individual quasars), adding two powerful laboratories for probing black hole-galaxy coevolution at Cosmic Noon and for time-delay cosmography constraints on the Hubble constant, H 0 .

title: The $\Sigma N$ threshold structure in the $K^-d\to\pi^-\Lambda p$ reaction
abstract: The $\Lambda p$ invariant-mass spectrum near the two physical $\Sigma N$ thresholds in the $K^-d\to\pi^-\Lambda p$ reaction is studied as a probe of the low-energy $\Sigma N$ interaction. The reaction is formulated up to two-step processes, and the coupled $\Lambda p$, $\Sigma^+n$, and $\Sigma^0p$ channels are described within a constant-$K$-matrix model constrained by spin-triplet scattering lengths. The dependence of the $\Sigma N\to\Lambda p$ conversion amplitude on these scattering lengths is examined, and the relation between its line shape and nearby pole positions is investigated. The resulting invariant-mass spectra are studied at different incident kaon momenta and compared qualitatively with existing experimental data. The effects of the spin-singlet $YN$ amplitude and the deuteron wave function are also examined. The line shape near the $\Sigma N$ thresholds is found to be particularly sensitive to the complex spin-triplet $I=1/2$ $\Sigma N$ scattering length, indicating that measurements of this spectrum can provide useful constraints on the low-energy $\Sigma N$ interaction.

title: Shear viscosity from fluctuations in linearized relativistic hydrodynamics
abstract: In this work we incorporate thermal fluctuations into fluid-dynamic simulations with the vHLLE code, in linear approximation. The fluctuations are built in following the fluctuation-dissipation theorem. The effect of space discretization into cells in numerical hydrodynamics on the spatial correlation of fluctuations is studied with the help of static structure factor. A difference from the continuum result is pointed out and systematically investigated. Time evolution of the ensuing fluctuations is examined and the Green-Kubo formula is used for the extraction of shear viscosity from the fluctuations. The extracted value is demonstrated to be the same as the input value of the shear viscosity for the simulations using Israel-Stewart equations. It is also shown that numerical regulators commonly used in the codes to ensure stability of the calculation severely spoil the fluctuations and break the fluctuation-dissipation theorem.

title: Relativistic Covariance from Hamiltonian Hydrodynamics in the Chiral Limit
abstract: We derive the covariant equations of nondissipative chiral hydrodynamics from their equal-time Hamiltonian formulation and identify the Lie--Poisson structure implicit in the chiral brackets. This structure combines fluid motion with local chiral transformations. For a parity-invariant Hamiltonian quadratic in chiral charge densities and pion gradients, without external backgrounds, we derive and solve the constraints imposed by Lorentz boosts. Their coupled nonlinear sector is equivalent to the linear boost transformation laws of a symmetric tensor, which determine the velocity dependence from rest-frame data. For finite, positive rest-frame coefficients, finite ordinary-fluid energy density and thermodynamic derivatives, and a momentum--velocity relation that can be solved in either direction, the chiral Hamiltonian coefficients remain finite at every fluid speed below light speed if and only if the rest-frame pion propagation speed does not exceed the speed of light. This formulation makes symmetry constraints explicit and provides a starting point for future thermodynamically consistent dissipative extensions.

title: Investigating Exotic Phenomena of Neutron-Rich Nuclei in the Light-Mass RegionUsing RMF+CMR
abstract: Abstract The exploration of exotic nuclear phenomena constitutes a central theme in nuclearphysics. In this work, the exotic structures of neutron-rich phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and argonisotopic chains are systematically investigated using the relativistic mean field combined with thecomplex momentum representation (RMF+CMR) approach. Based on the calculated two-neutronseparation energies, the neutron drip-line positions of the four isotopic chains are predicted. Inaddition, the single-particle levels of these four isotopic chains are examined. The increasing dif-ference between the neutron and proton rms radii indicates an enhanced neutron-skincharacter in the neutron-rich region. Finally, diffuse density distributions manifest throughoutthe P, S, Cl, and Ar isotopic chains.

title: Gravitational-Wave Propagation in Quadratic Einstein--Cartan--Dirac Gravity: A Conditional Tensor-Sector Analysis
abstract: We study leading tensor propagation in a specified first-order Einstein--Cartan--Dirac theory with the parity-even quadratic torsion invariant $\zeta T_{\lambda\mu\nu}T^{\lambda\mu\nu}$. Eliminating the nondynamical Lorentz connection on the regular algebraic branch gives a metric description containing the Einstein--Hilbert term, the Dirac action, and a $\zeta$-dependent axial--axial fermion contact interaction. We evaluate the transverse-traceless (TT) Hessian under an explicit factorized mean-field closure, with vanishing connected-current TT response, vanishing first- and second-order TT response of the factorized current scalar, and zero intrinsic TT anisotropic stress. Under these imposed conditions, the leading two-derivative tensor action has $Q_T=M_{\rm Pl}^{2}$ and $c_T=1$, with no leading dispersion or propagation-induced polarization splitting. These conditions do not follow from isotropy of the one-point axial current, and the present calculation does not derive them from a microscopic fermionic state. The result is therefore conditional and does not establish a general Einstein--Cartan--Dirac no-go theorem. We identify the connected-current TT response that must be calculated to extend the result beyond this closure. Published NANOGrav summaries are used only to check consistency with the GR-like prediction; no new timing-data likelihood or constraint on $\zeta$ is obtained.

title: $S$ factor of $^{13}$C($\alpha$,$n$)$^{16}$O at low energies in cluster effective field theory
abstract: The $^{13}$C($\alpha$,$n$)$^{16}$O reaction at low energies is studied by constructing an effective field theory. We choose a separation scale at $E=1$~MeV, where $E$ is the initial $\alpha$-$^{13}$C energy in center-of-mass frame, just below the sharp resonant $5/2^+$ state of $^{17}$O, and include two open channels, $\alpha$-$^{13}$C and $n$-$^{16}$O, and resonant $1/2^+$, $5/2^-$, $3/2^+$ states of $^{17}$O in the study. Parameters of the theory are fitted to experimental data, $S$ factor of $^{13}$C($\alpha$,$n$)$^{16}$O at the energies below $E=1$~MeV, including the data sets recently reported by the LUNA and JUNA collaborations, and the $S$ factor of $^{13}$C($\alpha$,$n$)$^{16}$O is extrapolated to the Gamow peak energy $E_G= 0.19$~MeV in the low mass AGB stars. We discuss an uncertainty in the estimate of the $S$ factor and confirm that the main part of the uncertainty emerges from the model assumptions about the near-breakup threshold $1/2^+$ state of $^{17}$O.

title: Covariant approach to allowed beta decay
abstract: We propose a Lorentz-covariant on-shell formalism for allowed nuclear beta decay. Nuclear matrix elements are organized in a systematic effective field theory expansion in the recoil momentum, with the dependence on nuclear spin and polarization encoded in little-group-covariant structures. In this language, we construct the most general standard and exotic currents for allowed transitions through first recoil order. We then derive the differential decay distribution encoded in a set of Lorentz-invariant form factors. Specializing to the rest frame of the parent nucleus, we relate our parameters to those used in the traditional beta-decay literature and in nucleon- and quark-level effective field theories. The formalism provides a natural framework for extensions to higher recoil orders, radiative corrections, and forbidden transitions.

title: Half-Life Measurements of $^{110}$Sn, $^{113}$Sn, $^{117\mathrm{m}}$Sn, and $^{123\mathrm{m}}$Sn Produced via Photon Activation of Natural Tin
abstract: We report independent determinations of the ground-state half-lives of $^{110}$Sn, $^{113}$Sn, and the isomeric states $^{117\mathrm{m}}$Sn (J$^{\pi} = 11/2^{-}$) and $^{123\mathrm{m}}$Sn (J$^{\pi} = 3/2^{+}$), produced via photon activation of natural tin using a TT-300HE Rhodotron accelerator. The activated samples were monitored over several months using a high-purity germanium (HPGe) detector. Time-dependent $\gamma$-ray spectra were analyzed using Gaussian peak fitting for the \SI{280.49}{keV}, \SI{391.697}{keV}, \SI{158.56}{keV}, and \SI{160.34}{keV} transitions, yielding half-lives of \SI{4.165(25)}{h} for $^{110}$Sn, \SI{116.08(94)}{d} for $^{113}$Sn, \SI{13.95(1)}{d} for $^{117\mathrm{m}}$Sn, and \SI{39.95(12)}{min} for $^{123\mathrm{m}}$Sn. Agreement with Nuclear Data Sheets (NDS) recommended values is generally observed for $^{110}$Sn, $^{113}$Sn, and $^{123\mathrm{m}}$Sn, with deviations consistent within combined uncertainties when quantified using standardized differences (z-scores). In contrast, $^{117\mathrm{m}}$Sn exhibits a statistically significant deviation from the evaluated value of \SI{13.76(4)}{d}, with a z-score indicating a discrepancy well beyond expected statistical fluctuations. This result suggests a systematic difference warranting further investigation, with potential implications for applications relying on precise decay data, including calibration, dosimetry, and astrophysical modeling.

title: Bayesian exploration of weakly interacting models of dark matter admixed neutron stars based on multi-density constraints
abstract: We present a unified Bayesian analysis of Higgs-portal, neutron-decay, and axion-like-particle (ALP)-mediated dark matter in neutron stars within the single-fluid approximation. Using a common relativistic mean-field description of hadronic matter, we combine finite-nucleus and heavy-ion collision data, chiral effective field theory, NICER measurements of four pulsars, and GW170817. The individual dark-sector parameters remain weakly determined, while model-dependent shifts in nuclear skewness reveal the sensitivity of the inferred hadronic equation of state to the assumed dark-matter mechanism. The three scenarios yield substantially overlapping mass-radius and tidal-deformability predictions, with median maximum masses near $2.1\,M_\odot$. For $1.4\,M_\odot$ stars, the Higgs-portal model predicts higher $f$-mode frequencies and shorter damping times than the neutron-decay and ALP models, although their credible regions overlap. Comparison with three consistently reanalysed two-fluid models gives the largest Bayesian evidence to neutron decay: under the adopted priors, its Bayes factors relative to the Higgs-portal and two-fluid alternatives are approximately $24$-$37$, but only $2.2$ relative to ALP. This ranking concerns complete dark-matter models and does not establish a general preference for either fluid description or evidence for a dark component itself. Improved nuclear constraints and future gravitational-wave asteroseismology could provide complementary information to disentangle the hadronic and dark-sector contributions.

title: The trigger for plasma detachment bifurcation in the edge divertor region of tokamaks
abstract: Abstract We identify a new trigger and dynamical pathway of plasma detachment bifurcation in tokamak divertors using steady-state and time-dependent UEDGE simulations. We report two key findings: first, the existence of a regime in which the direction of the E × B flow in the private-flux region reverses to point from the inner to the outer divertor in a deeply detached divertor plasma; and second, that this E × B flow reversal provides the causal mechanism for the abrupt drop in electron temperature (Te cliff) observed at the outer target in DIII-D. Specifically, in DIII-D H-mode plasmas with the ion B × ∇B drift driven into the active divertor, the Te cliff arises from a bifurcation-induced Te drop above the magnetic X-point accompanied by reversal of the E × B flow pattern in the private-flux region. Time-dependent simulations reveal a two-phase transition mechanism: the inner-divertor radiation front first extends across the last closed magnetic flux surface and stabilizes above the X-point, causing the local Te to drop from ∼ 70 eV to ∼ 10 eV and inducing an E × B flow reversal in a thin layer below the X-point in less than 0.5 ms (Phase I); this flow reversal subsequently triggers the sharp drop in outer-divertor target temperature on a timescale of 1–2 ms (Phase II), establishing deep plasma detachment a few ms thereafter. We show that a bifurcation transition occurs when the high-field-side radiation front crosses the separatrix while the outer divertor remains attached, with the Te cliff manifesting distinctly when the outer-target Te ≳ 10 eV prior to the bifurcation transition, implying that the bifurcation is fundamentally linked to in–out divertor asymmetry and asymmetric radiation-front evolution.

title: TD-Link: A Daisy-Chain Optical Architecture for Integrated Data Readout and Deterministic Timing Distribution in Large-Scale Detector Systems
abstract: TD-Link is an optical communication architecture that combines high-throughput data readout and sub-nanosecond timing synchronization over a single fiber for large-scale detector systems. It adopts a multidrop daisy-chain ring topology connecting a Data Concentrator to up to sixteen FERS front-end boards per link, with up to eight links per concentrator. Operating at 3.125 Gb/s, TD-Link carries data, synchronization, and control traffic in the same serial stream through a token-based streaming protocol that minimizes per-hop latency and supports on-the-fly payload fragmentation. Deterministic latency is enforced at two levels. On the concentrator, transmitter lanes are aligned by using the half-full flag of the multi-gigabit transceiver (MGT) elastic buffer as a one-bit phase detector: a firmware state machine steps the transmit phase interpolator (PI) until the buffer pointer difference crosses half-depth, locking every lane to the same phase condition. On each front-end board, where the synchronization pulse must also cross from the recovered-clock to the transmit domain, the residual three-to-five-cycle ambiguity of the synchronizer is removed by a calibration-free multiphase oversampling time-to-digital converter (TDC) with 0.8 ns bins, which time-stamps the incoming edge on the transmit time base so that a scheduler regenerates it at a fixed, programmable latency. A Digital Dual Mixer Time Difference (DDMTD) circuit measures the inter-concentrator phase. Tests with CERN PicoTDC-equipped FERS boards show a board-to-board synchronization $\sigma$ of 24 ps on the same ring, 27 ps across transceiver quads, and 28 ps across two cascaded concentrators, against an intrinsic front-end floor of 7 ps. Over more than one thousand cold boots without re-calibration, the boot-to-boot spread of the board-to-board skew stayed below 20 ps, consistent with the 18.6 ps phase-interpolator step.

title: Prediction of the thermal neutron response of grain-boundary impedance in Gd-doped ceria based on the radiation-ionic effect
abstract: The radiation-ionic effect was recently reported in 3 mol% Gd-doped CeO$_2$ (3GDC): under $^{60}$Co gamma irradiation at 35 Gy/min, the grain-boundary (GB) ionic resistance of a bulk pellet decreased 680-fold at room temperature, because electrons trapped at the GB core lower the space-charge potential. The effect has been demonstrated only with photons. Gd has the largest thermal-neutron capture cross section of any stable element and is also the dopant that creates the GB barrier in GDC, so the same mechanism could link GB impedance to thermal-neutron sensing; whether it does, and under what conditions, has not been examined. Here the thermal-neutron response of 3GDC is modelled with the gamma-calibrated Mott-Schottky/Seager framework, with unmeasured parameters carried as intervals and propagated jointly. Each capture deposits about 50 keV by conversion and Auger electrons within 1 $\mu$m, the remaining 8 MeV leaving as prompt photons; Gd segregation to the GBs adds a factor of only 1-2 because the electron range exceeds the grain size. A thermal flux of $8\times10^{9}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ (6-12$\times10^{9}$) matches the GB-effective generation rate of the 35 Gy/min calibration, and the predicted room-temperature GB resistance ratio is 110 (70-170) at $10^{9}$ and 970 (600-1500) at $10^{10}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, falling to 2 at 61 (55-68) and 81 (73-92) $^\circ$C. The neutron case differs from gamma irradiation in three respects: capture events are discrete, so the continuous-source approximation depends on the unmeasured trapped-charge lifetime; self-shielding (mean free path 0.27 mm) makes the response thickness dependent; and capture photons absorbed in the pellet add a gamma term comparable to the local term for pellets of 0.3 mm or more. The intervals are conditional on the model and exclude its structural error. The conditions under which the prediction can be tested are given.

title: Population pumping of vibrational and rotational quantum states in the triatomic hydrogen ion observed by electron-beam-assisted high-resolution spectroscopy
abstract: We present a technique to observe the optical manipulation of individual quantum states of H 3 + ions stored inside a heavy-ion storage ring, where the excitation is detected by electron-beam-assisted action spectroscopy. The transitions addressed here are chosen to enable multicolor spectroscopy of states far above the energetic barrier, where this molecule—with a triangular ground state—can sample linear geometries. This region of the spectrum has so far been inaccessible due to extremely weak direct transition strengths from the ground vibrational level. Our experiments pave the way for spectroscopy of the simplest polyatomic molecule in a previously unexplored energetic territory, which would benchmark theoretical data crucial for the understanding of this fundamental molecular system. Our results also demonstrate laser pumping to vibrationally and rotationally excited states of H 3 + , gaining model-dependent access to their relative dissociative electron recombination rates.

title: Plasma-neutral collision operators for hydrogen isotopes: kinetic and gyrokinetic descriptions, comparison to fluid
abstract: Plasma-neutral interactions critically affect the edge dynamics of magnetically confined fusion devices. Neutral atoms modify ion and electron velocity distributions, potentially affecting local instabilities Standard fluid models simplify these processes (namely charge exchange, ionization and recombination) using Maxwellian assumptions and linearized source terms. We revisit these assumptions for a hydrogen plasma interacting with hydrogen atoms. We derive plasma-neutral interaction terms in the kinetic and gyrokinetic frameworks. Accounting for velocity-dependent differential cross-sections, the model captures the kinetic impact of inelastic collisions on ions and electrons beyond energy and momentum exchange. We demonstrate that the fluid moments of the kinetic model reduce to standard fluid source terms under the appropriate assumptions of Maxwellianity and linearity. We compare the kinetic model with fluid models through their effects on distribution functions and fluid moments. Substantial discrepancies are observed, even for Maxwellian distributions. For charge exchange, the kinetic model yields momentum and energy exchange rates up to twice those predicted by fluid descriptions. We show that a fluid treatment of ionization greatly overestimates the mean kinetic energy of the produced electrons. These results highlight the limitations of fluid descriptions and the importance of kinetic effects in edge-plasma momentum and energy exchange.

title: Femtoscopic parameters of pion emission sources in EPOS4 Au+Au collisions from 7.7 to 200 GeV
abstract: Three-dimensional femtoscopy probes the space-time structure of particle-emitting sources in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision-energy dependence of L\'evy source parameters may reveal the evolution of strongly interacting matter and possible signatures of the QCD phase diagram. We previously studied the excitation function of three-dimensional L\'evy source parameters for pion pairs in Au+Au collisions with EPOS4, analyzing the pair-distance distribution \(D(\rho)\) through one-dimensional projections. Here, we analyze the full three-dimensional source distribution and correlation function directly. We construct \(D(\rho_{\rm out},\rho_{\rm side},\rho_{\rm long})\) as a 3D histogram, transform it into \(C(q_{\rm out},q_{\rm side},q_{\rm long})\) using a Fast Fourier Transform, and fit the correlation function with the analytic L\'evy formula. This approach can reduce biases arising when one-dimensional projections are used to describe a non-elliptical source. We apply the method across the RHIC Beam Energy Scan range and compare the extracted energy dependence with results from the projection-based method and recent UrQMD calculations. We focus on the out-side observables \(R_{\rm diff}^{2}=R_{\rm out}^{2}-R_{\rm side}^{2}\) and \(R_{\rm out}/R_{\rm side}\), whose different energy dependences in EPOS4 and UrQMD may illuminate the roles of emission duration and source dynamics. This work establishes a direct three-dimensional framework for comparison with future femtoscopic measurements and for exploring possible non-monotonic structures associated with the QCD phase diagram.

title: Performance and Radiation Damage of the Heavy-Ion Silicon Beam Tracker in the BM@N Experiment
abstract: The Silicon Beam Tracker (SiBT) of the BM@N experiment at the NICA complex (JINR, Dubna) is designed to reconstruct trajectories of beam ions upstream of the target. It consists of three stations based on double-sided silicon strip detectors (DSSDs) installed directly in the relativistic heavy-ion beam. The SiBT performance and radiation damage were studied using data from the 2026 experimental run with $^{124}$Xe beams at~$1.6$,~$2.2$, and~$3.0$~AGeV. During the run, the leakage current of the DSSD of the third station of SiBT increased by $28.95~\mu\mathrm{A}$, while the charge collection efficiency in the beam center decreased to approximately $68\%$ at the nominal bias voltage of 30~V. Increasing the bias voltage to 90~V restored the charge collection efficiency to approximately $95\%$. Despite the radiation-induced signal degradation, the tracking efficiency remained close to $99\%$. The accumulated radiation damage was also used to reconstruct the spatial distribution of the integrated beam fluence from strip-by-strip leakage-current measurements, yielding an average fluence of approximately $1.3\times10^{12}~\mathrm{n_{eq}/cm^2}$.

title: Finite-Temperature Equations of State for Neutron-Star Mergers within the Quark Mean-Field Model
abstract: We extend the quark mean-field (QMF) model to finite temperature and systematically investigate the thermodynamic properties of uniform nuclear matter, using the relativistic mean-field (RMF) model as a reference. For each model, we consider two parameter sets calibrated to the same selected nuclear-matter saturation properties but with different nucleon Dirac effective-mass ratios at saturation. We examine the effective nucleon mass and the composition of $\beta$-equilibrium matter, together with the free energy, energy density, pressure, entropy, and heat capacities of symmetric nuclear matter, pure neutron matter, and $\beta$-equilibrium matter. The QMF and RMF models exhibit similar qualitative trends, but their predictions increasingly differ at high density, where the effective masses have distinct density dependences. These differences are particularly evident in the thermal pressure and thermal index. For the two parameter sets considered in this work, we further provide compact analytical representations of the thermal index, $\Gamma_{\rm th}(\rho_{\rm b},T,\beta)$ over baryon densities of 0.08-1.0 $\rm fm^{-3}$, temperatures of 5-100 MeV, and isospin asymmetries of 0-1. The fits reproduce the numerical results with an accuracy better than $2\%$ and can be directly implemented in binary neutron-star merger simulations. This study establishes a finite-temperature extension of the QMF framework and provides a basis for future assessments of how a quark-structure-based description of nuclear matter affects thermal support and post-merger dynamics in binary neutron-star mergers.

title: Cryogenic characterisation of the FBK NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers for the DarkSide-20k dark matter experiment
abstract: Liquid Argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly promising detectors for dark matter searches due to their uniform response, scalability to large target masses, and compatibility with ultra-low background conditions. The DarkSide-20k (DS-20k) experiment, currently under construction at Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN) Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS), aims to achieve unprecedented sensitivity to Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs), approaching the neutrino fog. At the heart of the detector is a dual-phase TPC filled and surrounded by low-radioactivity argon from underground sources (i.e. Underground Argon (UAr)), functioning both as the WIMP target and detection medium. The experiment employs Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) NUV-HD-cryo Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs) as the chosen photon sensors for its optical planes. Key SiPM properties such as dark noise rate, gain and direct crosstalk were measured using specialized test setups at 77 K. The photon detection efficiency (PDE) was measured under vacuum at 77 K over the wavelength range 350-820 nm. Secondary photon emission, which can give rise to external optical crosstalk, was measured under vacuum at 86 K over the wavelength range 550-1020 nm.

title: Characterizing the energy resolution of the MicroBooNE LArTPC at the MeV scale using monoenergetic features of $^{208}$Tl decays
abstract: A detailed understanding of the capabilities and fidelity of low-energy reconstruction is crucial for taking advantage of MeV-scale neutrino physics opportunities in liquid argon time projection chambers (LArTPCs). This study presents a measurement of the resolution of reconstructed energy in the MicroBooNE LArTPC at $\approx 1.5$ MeV. The characterization is performed using monoenergetic signals generated by $2.614$ MeV $\gamma$-rays from $^{208}$Tl decays undergoing pair production in the detector. The resolution is found to be ($7.52 \pm 0.78 \text{(stat)} \pm 0.92 \text{(syst)}$)%. This value is consistent with the MicroBooNE simulation prediction of ($9.70 \pm 0.65 \text{(stat)}$)% at the $1.6 \sigma$ level. This study represents the first ever measurement of LArTPC energy resolution at the MeV scale and provides a pathway for monoenergetic energy calibrations in future experiments using LArTPC detectors.

title: Numerical calculations of neutron star mountains supported by crustal lattice pressure
abstract: Gravitational waves may set the spin frequencies of neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs). One mechanism for facilitating such emission is the formation of a mass asymmetry - or `mountain' - supported by elastic strains driven by thermal gradients. Most studies have focused either on the origin of the elastic strains or the temperature asymmetry in isolation, and have not considered the entire formation process. In previous work, we showed that anisotropic heat transport in magnetised accreting neutron stars can source a significant temperature asymmetry, and made rough estimates that suggested temperature-induced perturbations in the pressure supplied by the crustal lattice may be competitive with the widely known model of temperature-induced capture-layer shifts. In this paper we carry out detailed calculations to properly explore this scenario. We self-consistently calculate the temperature asymmetries, the perturbations in crustal lattice pressure, and the mass asymmetries within a single framework. For the first time, we make use of the set of realistic equations of state from the Brussels-Montreal nuclear energy-density functionals BSk19, BSk20, and BSk21 which describe all regions of accreting neutron stars in a thermodynamically consistent, unified way. We find these mountains are too small to dictate the spin-equilibrium of LMXBs, and estimate the level of gravitational wave emission they produce.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: High-efficiency klystrons from a dream to a reality
abstract: During the past decade, a comprehensive research and development (R&D) program on high-efficiency klystrons has been carried out in collaboration with industry. Initial prototypes have undergone testing, with experimental results showing significant promise. This paper is an extended and updated version of the work presented in Catalan-Lasheras [ , FRYD1 (2024)]. After a brief overview of the R&D program, it presents the latest experimental findings and discusses future developments, including novel vacuum tube topologies aimed at next-generation collider applications.

title: ENGRAVE follow-up of a type IIb supernova spatially coincident with the sub-threshold gravitational wave trigger S250818k
abstract: The candidate gravitational wave (GW) event S250818k was one of only three non-retracted LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA public alerts issued during the fourth observing run of the network (O4) with a binary neutron star (BNS) merger classification probability exceeding one percent. This triggered a prompt search for a potential electromagnetic (EM) counterpart in the large localization error region (949 deg 2 projected in the sky at the 90% credible level). The transient supernova (SN) 2025ulz discovered by the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) during the search, attracted a great deal of attention due to a potential spatial and temporal coincidence, and due to its initial fast decay and featureless spectrum. Here, we report on the follow-up of this transient by the Electromagnetic counterparts of gravitational wave sources at the Very Large Telescope (ENGRAVE) Collaboration. We conducted an extensive multi-wavelength observational campaign, which led to the spectral classification of the transient as a type IIb SN, indicating that it is unrelated to the candidate GW event. In this article, we describe our observing strategies, data reduction, and interpretation. All of our results confirm and strengthen our classification of the source, and also show that shock-cooling tails associated with type IIb SNe are one of the most prominent contaminants in kilonova searches.

title: Beam transient studies in high-intensity linacs
abstract: Space charge is one of the main challenges for high-intensity linear accelerators (linacs). To overcome this, most linacs have adopted the space charge compensation (SCC) scheme at the low-energy beam transport (LEBT). However, SCC is a buildup process that produces beam transients, i.e., nonoptimal beam conditions, which can lead to significant beam degradation and losses. Furthermore, most LEBTs are equipped with a chopper to provide a beam structure intended for the downstream sections and for the gradual ramp-up of power. However, operation of the chopper will destroy the SCC, leading to additional beam transients. SCC studies on beam transients focus primarily on the LEBT section, resulting in insufficient analysis of the downstream section, where beam transients can cause significant losses. This work addresses this gap by analyzing beam transients generated in the LEBT and their propagation throughout the linac to assess beam losses. This analysis challenges conventional notions by revealing that the worst-case scenario does not occur when the SCC is zero, but rather within twice the compensation time ( τ * ). This is because, although mismatch and emittance growth are at their maximum at the beginning, 80% and 450%, respectively, the current transmitted to the superconducting linear accelerator is minimal (30%); consequently, beam instabilities caused by the mismatch are less severe. Most nonoptimal beams were intercepted by the cone collimator and the radio-frequency quadrupole at energies below the activation threshold (2.16 MeV), with a peak power loss density that remained within cooling capacity limits. Furthermore, any residual risk was safely eliminated by the collimators in the medium-energy beam transport. As a result, transient losses in the superconducting linac were estimated to be below 1 W / m and were confined to the low-energy section.

title: The Energetic Particle Detector Instrument on ELFIN
abstract: We present the design methodology, implementation, and data products of the Energetic Particle Detector (EPD) instrument on-board the Electron Losses and Fields Investigation (ELFIN) dual SmallSat mission. ELFIN was designed to study the time-evolution of energetic particle distributions in Earth's magnetosphere, having operated in polar Low Earth Orbit (LEO) from 2018 to 2022. Each satellite's instrument payload contained a pair of detector heads to sense differential-directional fluxes of 50 keV to $\sim$5 MeV electrons (EPDE), and 50 keV to $\sim$2 MeV atomic ions (EPDI), with an energy resolution better than 50% ($\Delta E/E<0.5$). The satellites were spinning with a nominal period of 2.8 s in a plane containing Earth's background magnetic field, with particle counting intervals subdivided into 16 consecutive spin sectors. Each EPD was paired with a three-axis Fluxgate Magnetometer (FGM) sampled at 80 Hz for local pitch-angle determination. Each detector head operated on the principle of pulse-height analysis (PHA) in solid state media, collimated by a rectangular 22.5$^\circ$ field of view and entrance aperture. The EPDE contained a stack of 6 silicon detectors (0.7 cm total thickness) with 0.15 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with ion contamination mitigated by an aperture foil and digital coincidence logic. The EPDI contained a stack of 2 silicon detectors (0.1 cm total thickness) with 0.03 cm$^2$ str geometric factor, with electron contamination mitigated by a magnetic broom stage and digital anti-coincidence logic. The total assembled mass, volume, and power required for the EPD detector heads and circuit boards were 939 g, 10$\times$9.8$\times$8.4 cm$^3$, and 2.3 W, respectively. We describe each EPD design element alongside instrument data products and processing.

title: Response of GAGG(Ce) scintillators to different charged particles
abstract: Charged-particle telescopes play an essential role in studies of nuclear clustering, which require high-resolution detection of charged breakup fragments. GAGG(Ce) is a promising scintillator for charged-particle detection at high counting rates because of its high light yield, fast response, and non-hygroscopic nature. However, systematic data on its light-output response to different charged particles remain scarce. In this work, we present a systematic study of the scintillation light-output response of GAGG(Ce) crystals to various charged particles and quantify the associated quenching behavior. The relationship between the scintillation light output and the deposited energy is established over a broad range of particle species and energies, providing essential experimental input for response modeling and energy calibration of GAGG(Ce)-based charged-particle detector systems.

title: Non-contact lens metrology from optical flow and differentiable ray tracing
abstract: Accurate lens surface metrology is essential to determine the manufactured geometry of refractive optical elements and their deviation from the specified design. We demonstrate a transmission metrology method that reconstructs refractive lens surfaces from the displacement of a wavelet-noise-patterned mask. Lens-induced distortion is represented by a dense displacement field. A differentiable ray tracer fits the lens geometry using a calibrated near-telecentric camera model with an effective finite ray origin. We validate the method on commercial lenses. The recovered geometries agree with nominal specifications, and the plano-aspheric reconstruction is compared with chromatic confocal profilometry.

title: Impact of errors in the shape function of rotating neutron stars in the oblate Schwarzschild approximation
Feasibility demonstration of a high-momentum, high-purity muon beamline at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility
abstract: Abstract We have established and characterized a novel high-purity muon beam delivery scheme, designated as the μ20 mode, at the high-momentum hadron beamline (B-line) of the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility. This scheme delivers tertiary muons produced via the in-flight backward decays of secondary pions in the straight section of the beamline, inherently suppressing parent hadron contamination. In a systematic performance evaluation, the muon beam achieved a standalone intensity of 1.7 × 103particles/spill with a spatial spread (standard deviation, σ) of approximately 15mm at the downstream detector position.A systematic attenuation analysis utilizing an iron absorber verified a high muon purity of 98.0 ± 0.6% for the 3GeV/c muon beam mode. Crucially, this work marks the first successful feasibility study of a pure multi-GeV/c muon beamline operation at an experimental facility in Japan.
source: Progress of Theoretical and Experimental Physics

title: Energy, vertex, and time response of a LiquidO detector with an opaque-scintillator target to Compton-tagged electrons
abstract: LiquidO detectors confine scintillation light near its point of production by stochastic scattering in an opaque medium and collect it with a lattice of wavelength-shifting (WLS) fibers. The elementary signal of such a detector is the point-like sub-MeV energy deposition, yet the response to that signal at the center of the detector volume has not been measured against an event-by-event ground truth. To close this gap, we couple BPULSE, a 4-liter prototype LiquidO detector, to a Compton-coincidence calibration setup that selects electron recoils of known energy on a constrained beam axis. The prototype is a 160 mm cube of opaque scintillator with 64 WLS fibers in alternating orthogonal layers at a 20 mm pitch, read out by silicon photomultipliers. Compton scatters of collimated gamma-ray beams from $^{137}$Cs and $^{60}$Co sources are tagged by a NaI(Tl) spectrometer. For 373.4 keV electrons, tagged from $90^{\circ}$ scatters of the $^{137}$Cs beam, the detector collects $19.04 \pm 0.07$ photoelectrons (p.e.). Across four operating points, the two sources at two scattering angles, it responds linearly at $48.3 \pm 1.5$ p.e./MeV. The energy resolution of $(23.4 \pm 0.4)\%$ matches the Poisson statistics of the detected photoelectrons. Collection at both fiber ends and larger sensors would raise the light yield of this target to an estimated 108-124 p.e./MeV. Center-of-mass reconstruction locates each recoil to the width of the delivered 20 mm beam spot, which bounds the intrinsic localization of the detector from above. The arrival time response sets a lower bound of 1.5 ns on the single-scatter start time at the observed $\approx 19$ p.e. light level. This single-scatter response is the building block for reconstructing multi-site events. It constrains the light collection, confinement, and timing models on which reconstruction in future LiquidO detectors will rest.

title: Dual deconvolution multifocal fluorescence response matrix microscopy for aberration-free high-throughput super-resolution imaging
abstract: Fluorescence response matrix imaging enables separate computational correction of excitation and emission aberrations through dual deconvolution, but single-focus acquisition requires a large number of camera frames, limiting its practical use. Multifocal excitation can accelerate acquisition by recording many illumination positions in parallel, but denser foci also increase inter-focus crosstalk, which can bias the estimated excitation and emission optical transfer functions and degrade aberration correction. Here, we introduce high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging with adaptive multifocal illumination, in which the inter-focus spacing of the multifocal lattice is adjusted according to specimen-dependent crosstalk. A programmable digital micromirror device generates multifocal excitation lattices, and the resulting detector-resolved fluorescence responses are assembled into a two-coordinate fluorescence response matrix. Dual deconvolution separately estimates and corrects the excitation and emission optical transfer functions, and the aberration-corrected matrix is then combined in the spatial-frequency domain to reconstruct the aberration-free image. This strategy reduces the number of required camera frames by approximately three orders of magnitude, allowing response matrices with $\sim 10^6$ illumination positions to be acquired within seconds to a few minutes. The accelerated acquisition preserves the aberration-correction capability of dual deconvolution and achieves an estimated lateral resolution of $\sim$100 nm. Applied to heterogeneous mouse brain and kidney tissue, the method enables high-resolution, depth-resolved volumetric imaging while correcting specimen-dependent aberrations. Together, these results establish adaptive multifocal illumination as a practical route to high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging.

title: Broadband 600- and 1200-GHz Subharmonically Pumped Schottky Diode Mixers
abstract: A subharmonic mixer topology is introduced that uses quarter-wave stubs to create virtual RF/LO grounds and provide impedance matching in close proximity to the antiparallel Schottky barrier diode pair, thereby reducing the electrical length and enabling broadband operation. The RF/LO matching topology is demonstrated at 600 GHz and 1200 GHz, with good agreement between measured and simulated performance. The 600-GHz mixer demonstrates approximately 20% RF bandwidth with a DSB receiver noise temperature below 1300 K across most of the measured band, while the 1200-GHz implementation achieves DSB receiver noise temperatures below 3000 K over a broad frequency range. Both mixers are characterized at room temperature with approximately 2 mW of LO power. The 600-GHz mixer is used in the Submillimeter Wave Instrument (SWI) onboard ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer. Overall, these results demonstrate state-of-the-art room-temperature performance for broadband receiver front ends targeting atmospheric research and remote-sensing applications.

title: A Low-Temperature Tool for Acousto-electric Detection
abstract: We have developed an apparatus for the measurement of the acousto-electric effect (AEE) from room temperature to liquid nitrogen temperatures. The AEE is excited by bulk acoustic waves (BAWs) for which a lithium niobate piezoelectric actuator is employed. A very low background noise level is realized through careful electrical and mechanical design of the setup. The validity of the setup is tested by measuring the AEE in heavily doped P-type and N-type silicon. The opposite sign of the AEE signal was seen for both samples, showing dependence of the signal on the type of charge carrier being dragged by acoustic waves. The signal showed quadratic dependence on the driving voltage, which is consistent with the AEE literature. Further, a temperature dependence of the AEE signal was measured, which exhibits a monotonic increase with a rise in temperature. The ability to probe the AEE in bulk samples at low temperatures makes this setup a promising tool to investigate the AEE and related phenomena in different materials at cryogenic temperatures.

title: Theoretical study of multinucleon transfer reactions with a 208 Pb target using master equation
abstract: Abstract Combining with the dinuclear system concept, we developed the traditional master equation approach by incorporating the nucleon transfer probability influenced by the optimal Q -value. That approach was applied to calculate the production cross sections of the fragments in the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb, 136 Xe+ 208 Pb, and 136 Xe+ 198 Pt reactions and the mass distributions in 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 136 Xe+ 208 Pb reactions. The calculated results are in favorable agreement with the available experimental data. For the observed asymmetry in the production cross sections of the fragments for 58 Ni+ 208 Pb and 40 Ca+ 208 Pb systems, it is attributed to the constraint of the optimal Q -value window on the transfer process. Due to the small difference between Q -value of nucleon transfer and optimal Q -value, the projectile 58 Ni and 40 Ca tend to pickup neutrons and strip protons. Furthermore, owing to the shell effect, the Q -values for the 40 Ca+ 208 Pb reaction in the proton pickup and neutron stripping channels are farther from the optimal Q -value than those for the 58 Ni+ 208 Pb reaction, making it harder for 40 Ca to lose neutrons and gain protons than for 58 Ni.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Pressure-induced unconventional charge-density-wave states in kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 ( A = K , Rb, Cs)
abstract: Since the discovery of charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity, kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 ( A = K , Rb, Cs) provides a new platform for exploring novel many-body quantum phenomena. In CsV 3 Sb 5 , a stripelike CDW with commensurate wave vector q = 3 / 8 was observed under moderate pressures, which leads to a peculiar superconducting double-dome behavior in pressure-dependent phase diagram. Previous density functional theory (DFT) calculations indicate that the pressure-induced stripelike CDW is beyond conventional phonon softening scenario, suggesting a nontrivial role of electronic correlations. However, an in-depth understanding for the pressure-induced unconventional CDW remains elusive. Here, we performed pressure-dependent V 51 nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) measurements on KV 3 Sb 5 and RbV 3 Sb 5 . Although the superconducting double-dome behavior is absent in pressurized KV 3 Sb 5 and RbV 3 Sb 5 , a pressure-induced CDW phase, ascribed to a possible incommensurate triple- Q CDW, is identified by NMR spectra in both materials, indicating that the pressure-induced unconventional CDW beyond DFT calculations is a common feature for kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 . In contrast to the stripelike CDW, the pressure-induced incommensurate triple- Q CDW does not strongly suppress the superconducting temperature ( T c ) but coincides with an almost plateau behavior at intermediate pressure regime in the pressure-dependent superconducting phase diagram.
