Furthermore, by systematically analyzing the Korringa relation between Knight shift and nuclear spin-lattice relaxation rate in AV 3 Sb 5 , Van Hove singularity-driven electronic fluctuations are revealed as an effective knob for the pressure-induced unconventional CDW. Finally, our present findings underscore the pressure-induced unconventional CDW as a novel correlated quantum state in kagome metal AV 3 Sb 5 .

title: IViS: Interferometric Visibility-domain inversion Software. A GPU-accelerated Python framework for joint deconvolution with ASKAP
abstract: Wide-field spectral-line imaging with modern radio interferometers remains challenging when the emission is extended, multiscale, and distributed over many overlapping pointings. In this regime, accurate reconstruction requires a joint treatment of the calibrated visibilities, control of image-domain regularity, and, when necessary, recovery of missing short spacings from single-dish data. We present of Galactic foreground emission and LMC emission with reduced residual side-lobe structure and realistic multiscale morphology. A comparison with using multiscale CLEAN shows that, for this specific target and a single observing block, (Interferometric Visibility-domain Inversion Software), a GPU-accelerated Python framework for visibility-domain joint deconvolution, and assess its performance for wide-field ̋I imaging with the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder (ASKAP). The current model, reconstructs a nonparametric sky cube directly from calibrated visibilities by minimizing a regularized least-squares criterion. The forward model relies on a nonuniform fast Fourier transform (NUFFT), supports joint deconvolution across all mosaic pointings, and allows positivity constraints through bounded optimization. Short-spacing information can be incorporated through a fusion term that models single-dish data from the same sky estimate. We validate the method using synthetic point-source, noise-only, and multiscale diffuse-emission simulations, and apply it to ASKAP full-survey observations toward the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). The simulations show that recovers point-source flux accurately in the absence of regularization and that the regularization strength sets the trade-off between noise suppression and effective resolution. Relative to linear mosaicking of independently deconvolved pointings, joint deconvolution can recover more large-scale power. When single-dish information is included, the reconstructed power spectra closely reproduce the input sky statistics over a broad range of spatial frequencies. Applied to ASKAP data, yields 10,h mosaics with an effective resolution of 22 ASKAPSoft exhibits fewer residual side-lobes and recovers substantially more power at low spatial frequencies. provides a flexible visibility-domain framework for joint deconvolution of large spectral-line mosaics, and illustrates the potential of regularized inverse-problem approaches as an alternative to traditional CLEAN-based imaging for next-generation radio surveys.

title: Exact Traversable Wormhole Solutions in Finsler--Randers Gravity: Geometry, Physical Viability, and Equilibrium
abstract: Abstract We construct a static, spherically symmetric traversable wormhole in Finsler--Randers (FR) gravity using the osculating-Riemannian formulation, in which the spacetime anisotropy is encoded by a weak time-like vector field $\zeta_a(r)$ rather than introduced by hand at the matter level. Starting from the general FR field equations for a static spherically symmetric line element, we specialize to a zero-tidal-force Morris--Thorne wormhole and derive closed-form expressions for the energy density, radial pressure, and tangential pressure sourcing a fixed shape function $b(r)=r_0^2/r$. Adopting a decaying weak-field ansatz for the anisotropy field, $\zeta_0(r)=\zeta_c\,r_0/r$, we show that the amount of null-energy-condition (NEC) violating matter required to hold the throat open decreases monotonically with $\zeta_c$, and that the radial extent of the NEC-violating region shrinks from the entire spacetime (the general-relativistic limit $\zeta_c\to0$) to a compact neighbourhood of the throat. We further derive the generalized hydrostatic-equilibrium (TOV-type) equation for this geometry and identify an explicit geometric force $F_\zeta$, sourced by the gradient of $\zeta_0(r)$, that supplements the usual hydrostatic and anisotropic forces. The model reduces smoothly to the general-relativistic Morris--Thorne wormhole as $\zeta_0\to0$, and all reported effects remain within the weak-anisotropy regime $|\zeta_0|\ll1$ under which the field equations were derived. We further examine tidal forces (finding the radial component vanishes identically for every observer), sound speeds and the Herrera cracking criterion, a corrected convergent exotic-matter measure, a Herrera-type complexity factor adapted to the wormhole geometry, an analytic classification of the critical anisotropy strength across the shape-function and anisotropy-decay parameter space, a thin-shell realization with reduced surface exotic density, the absence of a photon sphere with the corresponding light-deflection angle, and a linearized generalization to a nonzero redshift function.

title: Anomaly Detection in Bunch Oscillations for Early Warning of Sudden Beam Loss at SuperKEKB
abstract: Sudden beam loss (SBL) events at the SuperKEKB collider result in the loss of a large fraction of the stored beam within just a few revolutions, on a timescale comparable to or shorter than the 20-30 {\mu}s latency of the existing abort system. Such events have damaged collimators and threaten Belle II subdetectors. Bunch Oscillation Recorders (BORs) capture transverse bunch positions at each revolution, which often show sizable oscillations that precede significant beam current loss. We test whether these precursors can be detected earlier than a charge-based reference that mimics the existing abort sensors. We apply several oscillation-based anomaly detection algorithms to 208 SBL events recorded in the low-energy ring during the 2024 run period, ranging from simple rolling statistics to machine learning models trained to forecast bunch oscillation. On 173 events not used for training or calibration, the best-balanced model (DeepLSTM) triggers before the charge-based reference in 86-90% of events across five training seeds, with a mean lead time of 25-30 {\mu}s. The only trigger classified as a false alarm fires on an oscillation that begins about 60 turns before the abort and persists until the beam is lost, making it more likely an early precursor than a spurious trigger. These results establish bunch oscillations as a viable early abort trigger and motivate a shadow-mode deployment to measure the false-alarm rate in continuous operation.

title: Two-body scattering observables from finite-volume real-time evolution
abstract: Abstract We study two-body scattering observables from real-time evolution in a finite periodic box. The system consists of two distinguishable particles on a two-dimensional lattice interacting through pointlike s - and p -wave interactions. We evolve their wave packets in real time, define detector observables through angular wedges in the relative coordinate, and attach infinite-volume labels obtained from the bound-state pole equation and the low-energy scattering amplitude. We train a convolutional neural network on this data and test its performance on previously unseen finite volume scattering data and find that is able to predict the total magnitude and angular shape of cross sections for previously unseen Hamiltonians.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Radii and Scaling Relations of Dark-Matter-Admixed Neutron Stars
abstract: The radius of a neutron star is closely related to the equation of state (EOS) of asymmetric nuclear matter, particularly to the nuclear symmetry energy. At fixed stellar mass, the neutron-star radius and the nuclear-matter pressure near saturation density approximately satisfy a pressure--radius (R-P) scaling relation, linking stellar geometry to strong-interaction matter. In the presence of dark matter (DM), changes in the stellar geometry can modify this relation. We investigate how GeV- and sub-GeV-scale DM affects the R-P relation in DM-admixed neutron stars (DANSs) within a gravity-only two-fluid framework. We extend the Buchdahl analytic solution to a two-fluid configuration to demonstrate this scaling and then use 21 nuclear EOSs to fit the relation $R_{\rm NM}=\bar C P_{\rm NM}^{\eta}$ for $1M_\odot$ and $1.4M_\odot$ DANSs. The exponent $\eta$ and coefficient $\bar C$ jointly quantify the DM-induced modification and depend on the DM particle mass, stellar DM content, and self-interaction strength. For bosonic DM, changes in $\eta$ and $\bar C$ occur mainly in the sub-GeV range, whereas significant fermionic-DM effects persist up to about 1.5 GeV. Increasing the DM content or strengthening a repulsive self-interaction generally increases $\eta$ and decreases $\bar C$. The modified R-P relation therefore encodes information about the DM particle mass, abundance, and self-interaction, and affect the extraction of the nuclear EOS from celestial observations. At DM masses of several hundred MeV, both fermionic and bosonic DM can also produce DM-dominated low-mass ($1M_\odot$) DANSs with large radial extensions, for which the conventional scaling relation ceases to apply.

title: AI Acceleration of Muon Collider R&D: A Report from the AI4MuC Workshop
abstract: A Muon Collider is one of the most attractive routes to multi-TeV lepton collisions, but it requires the accelerator and detector communities to solve a tightly coupled set of problems that have no close precedent in an operating collider. Muons must be produced, captured, cooled, accelerated, and collided before they decay. The detector must then extract clean physics from an environment dominated by decay products from the beamline. Artificial intelligence is not a substitute for accelerator physics, detector design, or engineering validation. It is, however, unusually well matched to several of the central obstacles: high-dimensional design spaces, expensive simulations, coupled subsystem trade-offs, and workflows that are currently too slow or too fragile to support broad design exploration. This report distills the AI4MuC workshop into a summary of AI use cases with the potential to change the pace of Muon Collider R&D, organized around the following physics bottlenecks: muon production and capture, ionization cooling, magnet and RF technology, detector design in beam-induced background, background simulation and generation, reconstruction, and software.

title: Phase Memory Controls Radiative Depolarization Near an Isolated Spin Resonance
abstract: Radiative depolarization near spin resonances in electron storage rings is conventionally described by correlated-sideband and local resonance-density theories, but a quantitative description of the crossover between them has remained lacking. Here we derive a unified finite-memory response from stochastic spin dynamics near an isolated resonance. By separating the coherent resonance contribution from stochastic fluctuations, we show that the connected correlation of the accumulated resonance-relative spin phase determines the leading off-center weak-resonance depolarization rate. Both conventional theories emerge as controlled asymptotic limits of this response, which also captures the surviving synchrotron phase memory governing the crossover. Monte Carlo spin tracking validates the predicted rates throughout the crossover and reproduces the recurrence-induced generalized-sideband structure. More broadly, the connected-correlation formulation provides a basis for extending radiative depolarization theory to more general stochastic spin-orbit dynamics in storage rings.

title: Observational evidence of black hole event horizon from ultra-compact X-ray binaries
abstract: The event horizon is the most crucial feature that distinguishes black hole (BH) from all other objects in the universe. However, since no radiation can escape from the event horizon, its direct observational evidence remains lacking. Although both are compact objects, the event horizon leads to differences in the radiative behavior between black hole and neutron star (NS) X-ray binaries. Historically efforts to probe the existence of event horizons revealed that the BH X-ray binaries are fainter than NSs with similar orbital periods in their quiescent states. Here, we use a special class of X-ray binaries namely the ultra-compact X-ray binaries (UCXBs), to reveal the existence of the event horizon near stellar-mass black holes. In short-period UCXBs, gravitational radiation dominates the orbital angular momentum loss, allowing us to accurately determine their accretion rates. Based on five UCXBs with orbital periods shorter than 40 min, located in globular clusters, and identified accretors (NS or BH), we obtained their accretion rates. Combining their accretion rates and X-ray luminosities, we calculated the X-ray radiative efficiencies of NS and BH. The radiative efficiency of BH is about two to three orders of magnitude lower than that of NS systems, indicating the accretion energy is swallowed by the BH, thereby indirectly probe the presence of the event horizon.

title: Nonlinear Photoemission for Bright Beams in X-Band Photoinjectors
abstract: The ongoing development of low-cost and compact x-ray light sources is vital for increasing the number of experiments that can be performed at the atomic scale. One option for a compact and simple photoinjector is to operate in blow-out mode, in which a high-charge, short-bunch length electron beam self-expands by space-charge forces into a uniformly ellipsoidal shape. This mode necessitates a photoinjector whose initial electron pulse has a pulse duration on the order of $100$ fs. A photoinjector utilizing linear photoemission with an ultraviolet laser in this regime presents significant technical challenges, as many optical substrates degrade at these wavelengths. In this paper, we present an alternative design that uses nonlinear photoemission to produce electron beams with high charge and short bunch length in an X-band (9300 MHz) photoinjector. This photoinjector design produces an electron beam with a bunch charge of up to $200$ pC, an RMS bunch length of $291$ fs, a normalized transverse emittance of $1$ to $1.4$ mm$\cdot$mrad, and an energy spread of $10^{-4}$. This results in a beam brightness of $10^{18}$ A/m$^2$, which is bright enough for our beamline's purposes. We also present ongoing efforts are aimed at further increasing the electron beam brightness by using a spatial light modulator to shape the laser profile at the cathode.

title: Non-accumulation of background-enhanced neutrino forces in proto-neutron stars
abstract: In a neutrino background, the vacuum two-neutrino exchange potential $V \propto G_F^2 /r^5$ acts as a much longer-ranged interaction, scaling as $V\sim1/r$ for a directional background. A proto-neutron star (PNS) hosts one of the densest astrophysical neutrino environments known, and naturally provides a setting in which to test whether this pairwise enhancement produces a macroscopic Hartree contribution. We show that this does not happen. In the spin-independent sector, averaging over pair orientations projects the background onto its angular monopole. The bulk Hartree contribution then saturates instead of growing with system size. We also find that the spin-dependent parity-conserving and parity-violating terms do not generate macroscopic growth under the PNS mean-field conditions considered here. Thus, although the pair potential can be strongly enhanced, the resulting bulk interaction remains very small. The suppression comes from the angular and oscillatory structure of the kernel, not from screening. Within the Standard Model mechanism considered here, the effect is not important for the PNS equation of state or for events like pulsar kicks.

title: Multi-Objective Design of C-Shaped Targets for Energy--Divergence Control in Laser-Driven Proton Acceleration
abstract: We optimize the energy-divergence trade-off of laser-driven protons from a C-shaped target using two-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations and constrained multi-objective Bayesian optimization. Five geometry and focusing parameters are varied to maximize proton cutoff energy and minimize the RMS divergence of forward protons with E_k >= 5 MeV under a proton-only conversion-efficiency constraint of eta_H >= 9%. Of 82 designs, 60 are feasible and 15 Pareto-optimal. The Max-Energy and Min-Divergence endpoints yield 28.64 MeV at 52.51 degrees and 11.47 MeV at 11.13 degrees, respectively; a representative compromise yields 21.44 MeV at 38.44 degrees. Matched-stage diagnostics link these regimes to optical-field buildup, electron energization, charge separation, and outer-sheath organization. Numerical tests support the principal trends. Reflection timing does not support a monotonic trapping-duration law, and the charge-sheath relation remains non-local. These results establish a design-resolved route to controlling proton energy and angular quality.

title: Learn the Dynamics, Enforce the Physics: Generative Latent Operators for High-Dimensional Beam Evolution
abstract: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation is indispensable for modeling beam dynamics in particle accelerators, but its computational cost limits many-query workflows, such as configuration exploration, virtual diagnostics, and controller design. We introduce GLOBE, a physics-constrained Generative Latent Operator for Beam Evolution, modeling the nonlinear, control-dependent, multiscale evolution of 3D beam--field dynamics covering $10^7$ spatial cells. GLOBE compresses beam--field states into a compact latent space and factors their evolution into two components. A control-conditioned neural operator learns the dominant dynamics, while an amplitude-normalized generative model captures the residual distribution, recovering fine-scale structures and conditional variations. GLOBE enforces field constraints by regime-specific, parameter-free operators: a Poisson solve reconstructs the electric field in the electrostatic regime, and a spectral projection imposes Gauss's law and a divergence-free magnetic field in the electromagnetic regime. On two high-resolution 3D particle-accelerator benchmarks, bunched-beam transport and plasma-wakefield acceleration, GLOBE lowers relative-$L_2$ error by 9\% and 13\%, low-frequency spectral error by 69\% and 51\%, and mid-frequency spectral error by 54\% and 20\% relative to the strongest baseline (DPOT), satisfies field constraints, and reduces hours of PIC simulation to a minute per rollout.

title: HOM Mitigation
abstract: Higher Order Modes (HOMs) in accelerating structures are resonant electromagnetic fields excited and left behind by charged particle bunches. They can severely degrade the beam quality in accelerators, such as the multi-bunch energy spread and transverse emittance, and therefore one must carefully study and mitigate them. In this lecture, various methods of HOM mitigation are reviewed. On one hand, one tries to avoid their existence, for example by careful design of the accelerating structures and damping systems. On the other hand, one can reduce the effect of the excited HOM fields, for example by means of fast feedbacks or beam alignment. Additionally, a few ways to make HOM signals useful are referred to, such as diagnostics of the beam or of accelerating structures.

title: Generalized Beth--Uhlenbeck entropy formula from the $\Phi-$derivable approach
abstract: We derive a generalized Beth-Uhlenbeck formula for the entropy of a dense fermion system with strong two-particle correlations, including scattering states and bound states. We work within the $\Phi-$derivable approach to the thermodynamic potential. The formula takes the form of an energy-momentum integral over a statistical distribution function times a unique spectral density. In the near mass-shell limit, the spectral density reduces, contrary to na\"{i}ve expectations, not to a Lorentzian but rather to a "squared Lorentzian" shape. The relation of the Beth-Uhlenbeck formula to the $\Phi$-derivable approach is exact at the two-loop level for $\Phi$. The formalism we develop, which extends the Beth-Uhlenbeck approach beyond the low-density limit, includes Mott dissociation of bound states, in accordance with Levinson's theorem, and the self-consistent back reaction of correlations in the fermion propagation. We discuss applications to further systems, such as quark matter and nuclear matter.

title: Equation of State Classification of Core-Collapse Supernovae with a Network of Gravitational-Wave Detectors
abstract: Gravitational waves from core-collapse supernovae may provide a unique probe of the equation of state (EOS) of dense nuclear matter. In previous work, we assessed the potential of machine-learning methods for EOS classification for rapidly rotating supernovae using individual gravitational-wave detectors. Here, we extend the framework to detector networks and investigate the impact of detector configuration, source distance, arrival time, and sky location on the classification. Using convolutional neural networks, we perform 10-class EOS classification directly from noisy detector data for both second- and third-generation observatories. We find that detector geometry strongly influences classification performance. For Galactic events, current detector networks can achieve promising classification performance, but the reach depends sensitively on the detector network antenna response. Adding detectors improves time-averaged performance and produces more uniform classification across the sky. Third-generation observatories extend the classification reach to 100 kpc for favorable source orientations but do not remove the dependence on detector geometry.

title: A modern particle-in-cell code for beam-beam simulations of future colliders
abstract: A key challenge in the design of next-generation colliders is predicting the effects of beam-beam interactions and using these predictions to optimize machine performance. Beam-beam interactions are characterized by strong focusing forces, radiative effects, and the generation of background particles. While analytical formulas provide insight into the dynamics of beam-beam interactions, these nonlinear, coupled effects are most accurately described with numerical methods. In this paper, we introduce the open-source particle-in-cell code WarpX as a modern tool for modeling the interaction point in future lepton colliders. WarpX provides high-performance execution on distributed GPU architectures within an open-source and actively maintained code base. We present convergence scans and benchmarks against the established beam-beam codes GUINEA-PIG (v1.2.2) and CAIN (v2.42) for luminosity spectra, photon emission, and secondary-particle production under a wide range of beam parameters corresponding to different collider concepts. Our results show that WarpX (v26.09) reproduces the benchmark beam-beam observables while enabling GPU-portable, extensible simulations. These results establish WarpX as a scalable platform for high-fidelity beam-beam modeling in future collider studies.

title: Undiscovering Quark-gluon Plasma
abstract: Quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is a conjectured state of matter wherein the quarks and gluons of QCD theory, usually confined within the nucleons in atomic nuclei, are deconfined under conditions of extremely high temperature and pressure. According to the current understanding of big-bang evolution, conditions compatible with QGP formation existed for a brief early period as the universe expanded and cooled. In that scenario present matter in the universe in some sense emerged from ``freezeout'' of the primordial QGP. This article describes the rise and fall of a community effort to create QGP in the laboratory and study its properties.

title: System-size dependence of jet quenching from light to heavy-ion collisions at LHC
abstract: Single inclusive hadron suppression in high-energy heavy-ion collisions provides a sensitive probe of parton energy loss and jet transport coefficient in quark-gluon plasma (QGP). System size dependence of jet quenching can provide further constraints on the dynamics of jet quenching and parton energy loss. Motivated by recent experiments on light-ion collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), we perform a systematic study of single-inclusive hadron suppression in O+O, Ne+Ne, Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions at the LHC energies. The calculations are carried out within the next-to-leading-order perturbative QCD model, incorporating the nuclear modified initial-state parton distributions, final-state parton energy loss in the higher-twist approach and the temperature dependence of the jet transport coefficient $\hat q/T^3$ from the Bayesian analyses of previous experimental data at the Relativistic Heavy-ion Collider (RHIC) and LHC. Our model calculations can simultaneously describe the measured single-inclusive charged hadron $R_{AA}$ in O+O, Ne+Ne, Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions over a broad range of event centralities and in the minimum-bias events. We further illustrate the system size dependence of jet quenching through the ratio $R_{\mathrm{NeNe}}/R_{\mathrm{OO}}$ and the modification factors $R_{AA}$ as a function of $\langle N_{\mathrm{coll}} \rangle$ which follow a common behavior at fixed $p_{\rm T}$, indicating the formation of QGP even in the smallest collision systems.

title: Holographic light quark jet quenching in flavor resolved QCD plasmas
abstract: We study light quark energy loss in a quark-gluon plasma using the holographic falling-string framework on a machine-learning-calibrated Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton background for three flavor configurations: pure glue, two-flavor QCD, and full QCD with strangeness. Stopping distances are computed from null geodesics as functions of reduced temperature $T/T_c$ and baryon chemical potential $\mu$. For $T/T_c>1.03$, the flavor ordering of the integrated stopping distance stabilizes to $N_f=2+1>N_f=2>N_f=0$, corresponding to the quenching hierarchy $N_f=0>N_f=2>N_f=2+1$. This agrees with the flavor ordering obtained from the shooting-string $dE/dx$ when both are expressed in the reduced-temperature framework, providing a cross-check between local and integrated observables within the same holographic background. Near $T/T_c\simeq1$, the behavior is more complex due to the interplay between the $a$ and $b$ terms in $A(z)$ and the different $T_c$ values of the three systems. Finite baryon chemical potential monotonically shortens stopping distances and enhances quenching, with enhanced sensitivity near the QCD critical endpoint, consistent with expectations from RHIC beam energy scan measurements. We discuss the geometric origin of the high-$T/T_c$ flavor ordering and possible extensions to heavy-ion transport simulations.

title: Exploring Collective Effects in Small Collision Systems via Light-Flavour Particle Production in High-Multiplicity pp Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=$ 13 TeV in ALICE
abstract: High-multiplicity pp and p-Pb collisions show signatures of radial and anisotropic flow, as well as the enhanced production of strange hadrons. These observations resemble phenomena seen in heavy-ion collisions, where a quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is formed, although their origin in small systems remains under discussion. This contribution presents ALICE Run 2 results on light-flavour hadron ($\pi$, K, p) production in high-multiplicity (HM) pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV, where the charged-particle multiplicity reaches values comparable to peripheral or semi-peripheral Pb-Pb collisions. The multiplicity dependence of $\pi$, K, and p transverse momentum spectra, $p_{\rm T}$-differential and $p_{\rm T}$-integrated particle ratios, and mean transverse momenta ($\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$) is presented and compared with published results from other collision systems and energies, as well as with PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4 model calculations.
authors: Rajendra Nath Patra for the ALICE Collaboration

title: Effect of Thermal Broadening on Light Hadron Production in Heavy-Ion Collisions
abstract: The measured hadron yields in heavy-ion collisions are well described by thermal particle production at temperatures close to the QCD pseudo-critical transition. However, if particles are produced in thermal equilibrium, then the in-medium effects, e.g., broadening of their spectral functions, must be taken into account. In this work, we study for the first time the effect of the thermal broadening of the light vector-meson spectral functions on light hadron production in heavy-ion collisions. We generalize the efficient resonance decay framework FastReso to resonances with finite-width spectral functions. We then compute the pion, kaon and proton spectra from the decays of hadron resonances for in-medium and vacuum spectral functions. We perform a simultaneous blast-wave fit with decay feed-down to measured particle spectra in central Pb-Pb and Xe-Xe collisions at the LHC. We find an increase in pion spectra at low momenta, from including thermally broadened $\rho$ and $\omega$ mesons. Additional pion yield from finite-resonance widths reduces the commonly observed discrepancy between models and data, but does not completely resolve the soft pion puzzle in heavy-ion collisions.

title: Radio and Gamma-Ray Timing of a Newly Discovered Millisecond Pulsar
abstract: We report the discovery and timing of PSR J2147-3604, a fully recycled millisecond pulsar with a spin period of 3.2 ms, discovered in a reprocessing of the 350-MHz Green Bank North Celestial Cap (GBNCC) survey and later serendipitously confirmed by the MeerKAT TRAPUM UHF survey of Fermi-LAT unidentified sources. We followed up this pulsar with Murriyang/Parkes radio telescope and obtained a phase-connected timing solution spanning one year, revealing a 4.5-day binary orbit with very low eccentricity (e ~ 1.9 x $10^{-5}$). A follow-up search in LAT data revealed gamma-ray pulsations, allowing for a joint radio and gamma-ray timing analysis. Assuming a neutron-star mass of 1.5 Msun, the inferred median companion mass (~0.2 Msun) is consistent with a helium white dwarf. The pulsar has a low dispersion measure of 17.0 pc cm$^{-3}$ and shows strong scintillation, leading to it being detected in ~72% of the observations covering the 704-1174 MHz band with Murriyang. The pulsar has a narrow duty cycle of ~6.5%, which leads to individual time of arrival (ToA) uncertainties of ~4.5 us for a 10 min integration with MeerKAT, suggesting this pulsar is well suited for inclusion in PTA experiments.

title: Internal Nucleon Properties and the Equation of State of Ultra-Dense Matter
abstract: The question of the link between the nucleon properties and the equation of state of ultra-dense matter, both being composed of quarks and gluons, is investigated by adopting a soliton model to describe internal nucleon properties and a direct mapping between nucleon and quark matter to obtain the equation of state of ultra-dense matter. We compare $\pi+\omega$ and $\pi+\omega+\rho$ soliton models and analyze the presence of a pressure singularity at the nucleon center due to the $\rho$ field. This singularity impacts the equation of state in ultra-dense matter. Only the pressure derived from the canonical energy-momentum tensor has a singularity, while the Belinfante pseudo-gauge transformation of the energy-momentum tensor generates an internal pressure without a singularity. We then investigate predictions for the equation of state of ultra-dense matter based on different prescriptions for the nucleon pressure. It is shown that none of the prescriptions agree with the thermodynamical pressure defined in uniform matter. The mismatch between any equation of state and the thermodynamical one questions the simplicity of the direct mapping between finite-size nucleon properties and uniform matter as well as the role of the nucleon surface in the internal energy density and the pressure.

title: Fast Radio Bursts from Monster Shocks and Flares of Inspiraling Binary Neutron Stars: A Kinetic Model for Double Pulsar
abstract: The coalescence of binary neutron star systems offers unprecedented possibilities for multimessenger observations, including the detection of gravitational waves, gamma-ray bursts, kilonovae, and potentially fast radio bursts. For a detailed investigation of the latter, one requires a kinetic plasma model to describe the interacting magnetospheres of the stars. We present a three-dimensional particle-in-cell kinetic simulation of the combined magnetosphere of a binary neutron star in which the two stars physically orbit one another so that the orbital motion itself twists the magnetic loops. We find that the stellar magnetic-field intensity ratio controls the emergence of flares, while the stellar spins set the direction and modulation of the flare. We identify four spatially and dynamically distinct regions of strong electromagnetic energy release: (i) an expanding fast magnetosonic wave that steepens into a monster shock, (ii) a plasma flare being pushed by (iii) an expanding fireball and containing (iv) a reconnecting current sheet. The fast magnetosonic wave is a promising source of coherent radio emission. It is released when orbital motion cuts a closed plasma loop. The electric and magnetic wave amplitudes are similar and reach that of the background magnetic field. Our kinetic treatment yields particle spectra and plasma structures that can be used to assess coherent emission in kinetic-scale simulations. In conclusion, the stellar orbital motion constitutes a driving channel distinct from models with spin-driven magnetospheric twisting.

title: Energy Extraction from Rotating Black Hole in Effective Quantum Gravity via Comisso-Asenjo Magnetic Reconnection Process
abstract: Abstract We investigate the energy extraction from a rotating quantum corrected black hole in effective quantum gravity through the Comisso-Asenjo magnetic reconnection mechanism. We determine the allowed parameter space for the energy extraction and evaluate the extraction efficiency for both circular and combined plasma streamlines. For circular streamlines, increasing the quantum parameter generally shrinks the allowed parameter space. For combined streamlines, the plunging phase significantly expands the accessible radial range and broadens the extraction domain, while the relative influence of quantum corrections diminishes. Our results indicate the existence of a critical quantum parameter, above which energy extraction ceases. In contrast to circular streamlines, the allowed parameter space for combined streamlines exhibits asymmetry relative to the orientation angle, suggesting a preference for positive optimal angles. We show that the quantum correction enhances the overall extraction efficiency and reduces the optimal reconnection radius. These results suggest that the magnetic-reconnection-driven energy extraction may serve as a probe of effective quantum gravity effects in the rotating black hole spacetime.

title: Additional Observational Signatures of Asymmetric Thin-Shell Wormholes within 4D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we study the optical appearance of a 4D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet asymmetric thin-shell wormhole. Using Visser'scut-and-paste construction, we determine the photon sphere radius and critical impact parameter for different values of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$. We then investigate the effective potential and photon motion inside the wormhole spacetime. It is found that the effective potential, light ray paths, and azimuthal angle are closely tied to the mass ratio of the two spacetimes. Considering an optically thin accretion disk as the only light source, we find that the asymmetric thin-shell wormhole's images exhibit additional photon rings and lensing bands that are absent for a 4D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet blackhole. \textcolor{blue}{Furthermore, the size of these extra rings increases with $\alpha$, whereas the photon ring of a 4D EGB black hole shrinks as $\alpha$ increases. This opposite $\alpha$-dependence is the main distinguishing signature of the wormhole geometry, and the resulting exceptionally bright rings may provide a useful observational criterion for distinguishing and characterizing a thin-shell wormhole spacetime.} We also verify that the mass ratio and throat radius significantly tune the morphology of these extra photon rings.

title: A Pipeline for the AI-Assisted Analysis of Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer Observations of Black Hole X-ray Binaries and Limits on Their Polarization Variability
abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has opened a new window into the high-energy Universe, with the capability to measure the arrival time, arrival direction, energy, and, for the first time with the required sensitivity, the polarization of X-rays from black holes, neutron stars, and other cosmic sources of X-rays. In this paper, we discuss the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents for the analysis of IXPE data. The pipeline combines an immutable code base with evolving knowledge databases. The generation of analysis projects makes use of a literature data base to judge the novelty of the proposed analysis projects. We emphasize that the analysis requires two types of expert knowledge: detailed instructions about how to reduce the X-ray data, and expert knowledge about how to interpret the results. We employ several levels of auditors that scrutinize the analysis plan, the analysis scripts, and the analysis results for data and method adequacy. The pipeline includes a staggered approach to interpret the analysis results. We present exemplary results from the pipeline applied to IXPE observations of Black Hole X-ray Binaries (BHXRBs) including comparisons of results from the analysis pipeline with published results and a systematic search for polarization degree and polarization angle variability in long IXPE observations. We critically discuss the performance of the pipeline and future avenues for improving it.

title: Spectral function approach in NuWro: modeling of multinucleon final states in quasielastic scattering
abstract: Neutrino-oscillation experiments performed in the few-GeV energy region create an urgent demand for a significant improvement in the accuracy of modeling of neutrino interactions with atomic nuclei. Here, we report an updated implementation of the spectral function approach in the \nuwro{} Monte Carlo generator, which consistently treats multinucleon final-states in quasielastic scattering at the inclusive and exclusive level. After validating its accuracy against inclusive electron-scattering data, we compare its predictions to various neutrino cross sections from MicroBooNE. We find that with the multinucleon contribution, these data are reproduced with values of $\chi^2$ per degree of freedom of 0.8--2.5, compared to 2.3--7.3 without it

title: The $R$-Process Alliance: On J0010$-$1735, an Accreted, Chemically Unusual, Metal-poor Star with $R$-process Enhancement
abstract: We present a detailed chemo-dynamical analysis of the chemically peculiar very metal-poor ([Fe/H]$=-2.22\pm 0.11$) Milky Way (MW) halo star, 2MASS J00101758$-$1735387 (hereafter J0010-1735), discovered by the $R$-Process Alliance. We derive abundances for 45 elements, including 28 neutron-capture elements, and confirm that \thestar\ is highly $r$-process-enhanced, with [Eu/Fe]=$+1.30$. The light, $\alpha$, and Fe-peak element abundances ratios relative to Fe are all sub-solar, aside from C, Si, and most extremely, Ca. We investigate three possible formation scenarios based on the star's chemical abundances and orbital kinematics: whether it formed in the \textit{in-situ} MW halo, in a MW dwarf galaxy satellite, or in a satellite of the Magellanic Cloud system. Using the position of \thestar\ in the [Mg/Mn]--[Al/Fe] plane, the abundance pattern of both the light and heavy elements, and the kinematics, we conclude that J0010-1735 most plausibly originated in a now-disrupted ultra-faint dwarf galaxy that was accreted into the MW halo. We examine potential chemical enrichment scenarios of J0010-1735, including one similar to the $r$-process-enhanced UFD Reticulum II, or enrichment via a sub-Chandrasekhar Type Ia SNe, potentially supplemented by a Ca-rich gap transient and by a separate neutron-rich site that facilitated $r$-process enrichment. A nuclear cosmochronometric age of $12.5\pm4.2$ Gyr is derived from the [Th/Eu] ratio, consistent with an ancient origin in one of the earliest star-forming systems in the universe.

title: Seeking a possible approach to understanding the origin of the proton mass using twist-4 contributions in inclusive reactions
abstract: Most of the mass of the visible universe originates from the strong interaction. Quantitatively reproducing the origin of the nucleon mass is one of the important challenges in fundamental science. Since the next-generation Electron-Ion Collider has identified resolving this problem as one of its major goals, further theoretical studies are needed to develop approaches to investigating the origin experimentally. In this paper, we explore the possibility of evaluating the ``gluon condensate term'' which is particularly difficult to determine among the contributions to the nucleon mass, using high-energy scattering experiments. We first express the gluon condensate term in terms of experimentally accessible twist-4 lightcone matrix elements. We then derive, for the first time, analytic formulas for the cross section including all twist-4 contributions from pure quark, quark-gluon, and pure gluon matrix elements in $ep$ collisions, and show how these contributions can be related to the gluon condensate term.

title: Color Lorentz force on a transversely polarized quark in the nucleon
abstract: The $x^2$ moment of the genuine twist-3 component of the unpolarized scalar parton distribution function $e(x)$ is related to the average transverse color Lorentz force experienced by a transversely polarized quark in an unpolarized nucleon. This higher-twist quantity probes quark--gluon correlations and provides unique insight into the nonperturbative dynamics of quantum chromodynamics. For the first time, we study the corresponding off-forward matrix element and derive its Lorentz-covariant decomposition in terms of generalized form factors. We calculate these form factors from light-front wave functions obtained by solving the light-front Hamiltonian eigenvalue problem within the Basis Light-Front Quantization framework. Their Fourier transforms provide a spatial picture of the transverse color forces in impact-parameter space. In particular, $\mathscr{F}_2$, whose forward limit is directly related to the twist-3 matrix element $e_2$, can be interpreted as the impact-parameter-space representation of the Boer--Mulders force, providing an intuitive spatial picture of the final-state interaction mechanism underlying the Boer--Mulders effect.

title: Sequential clusterization of light nuclei and hypernuclei in heavy-ion collisions within a Wigner function coalescence framework
abstract: We investigate the formation of light nuclei and hypernuclei in $\mathrm{Au}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}+\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{Au}$ collisions at $\sqrt{{s}_{NN}}=3$ GeV within a coalescence framework embedded in the microscopic N-body parton-hadron-quantum-molecular dynamics (PHQMD) transport model. The Wigner phase-space distributions employed in the coalescence calculation are constructed from realistic $N$-body wave functions obtained by solving the Schr\"odinger equation in the hyperspherical harmonics formalism, providing a solid and parameter-free description of nuclear clusters and hypernuclei. By comparing calculated rapidity distributions with STAR data, we extract species-dependent coalescence times, revealing a non-universal formation pattern among different clusters. The resulting yields and kinematic distributions of light nuclei and hypernuclei are systematically analyzed and shown to be sensitive to the underlying wave-function structure and formation time. In addition, we explore cluster-nucleon formation channels for $A=4$ systems. These additional channels improve the description of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$ and $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{4}\mathrm{H}$ yields and help address the underestimation of $A=4$ cluster production in theoretical approaches. Finally, we provide predictions for heavier hypernuclei, including $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{5}\mathrm{He}$ and $_{\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}\mathrm{\ensuremath{\Lambda}}}^{5}\mathrm{He}$, which are of interest for future experimental measurements.

title: Erratum: Identification of a new side-band and proposed octupole correlations in very neutron-rich Ce 152 [Phys. Rev. C 86, 067302 (2012)]
abstract: High spin levels of the very neutron-rich 152Ce have been investigated by measuring the prompt γ rays in the spontaneous fission of 252Cf. The yrast band is confirmed and a new side-band has been identified. The side-band is tentatively assigned with negative parity and an octupole band structure with s=+1 in 152Ce has been proposed. Based on the theoretical calculations and systematic comparisons, the characteristics of the octupole correlations have been discussed.

title: Renormalization of the shell-model neutrinoless double- β decay operator starting from effective field theory
abstract: In this work, we approach for the first time the task to perform a shell-model calculation of the matrix element for the neutrinoless double-beta decay, within a fully-consistent framework where the expressions of the nuclear Hamiltonian and of the decay operators have been derived through chiral perturbation theory. More precisely, the effective shell-model Hamiltonian and all transition operators have been constructed by way of the many-body perturbation theory, and then employed to calculate both spectroscopic properties of the nuclei involved in the decays under our consideration - namely 48Ca, 76Ge, and 82Se -, as well as the nuclear matrix elements of the electromagnetic and neutrinoless double-beta decays. We also present a study of the convergence properties of the calculated matrix elements in order to provide the elements for an estimate of the theoretical uncertainty.

title: Astrophysical S factor S 34 ( 0 ) using a Bayesian neural network
abstract: The astrophysical $S$ factor for the radiative capture reaction $^{3}\mathrm{He}(\ensuremath{\alpha},\ensuremath{\gamma})^{7}\mathrm{Be}$ plays a crucial role in big bang nucleosynthesis as well as stellar hydrogen burning. Its precise value is important in the context of primordial elemental abundances and the solar neutrino fluxes. In the present work we carry out a data-driven analysis of the $S$ factor using a Bayesian neural network. Unlike conventional neural networks, the Bayesian formulation produces a posterior distribution of $S$ factor curves consistent with experimental data and their uncertainties. From this distribution we extract the zero-energy astrophysical $S$ factor ${S}_{34}(0)=0.{544}_{\ensuremath{-}0.021}^{+0.022}\phantom{\rule{4pt}{0ex}}\mathrm{keV}\phantom{\rule{0.16em}{0ex}}\mathrm{b}$. The posterior ensemble is further used to obtain reaction rates over the temperature range $T=0.005--4$ GK. The results are in agreement with existing calculations. This work provides an alternative framework for low-energy $S$ factor determination and uncertainty quantification in nuclear astrophysics.

title: Experimental study of the He 6 ( d , t ) He 5 reaction at 52 MeV: Probing the single-neutron wave function of the He 6 ground state
abstract: New experimental data for the He 6 ( d , t ) He 5 one-neutron pickup reaction at 52 MeV were measured in inverse kinematics at the ACCULINNA-2 isotope in-flight separator at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions, Joint Institute for Nuclear Research, Dubna. The data were analyzed using two standard direct reaction models, the distorted wave Born approximation (DWBA) and coupled reaction channels. Single neutron wave functions for the He 6 ground state obtained using three different nuclear structure methods, including the new cluster channel orthogonal function method, were tested and the dependence of the results of the reaction calculations on the properties of these wave functions was observed. The data were well reproduced by a DWBA calculation with the wave function obtained using the ab initio variational Monte Carlo method with no adjustable parameters.

title: Dispersive-optical-model analysis of the asymmetry dependence of neutron skins
abstract: New dispersive optical model analyses of ${}^{54}$Fe and ${}^{90}$Zr together with updated results for ${}^{40}$Ca, ${}^{48}$Ca, and the earlier result for ${}^{208}$Pb shed light on the behavior of neutron skins in nuclei. Starting with a negative skin for ${}^{40}$Ca, a trend increasing somewhat stronger than linear emerges when the neutron skin of these nuclei is considered as a function of asymmetry, $(N-Z)/A$, and linked to the Green's function Monte Carlo results for asymmetric He nuclei. This general trend is consistent with the expectation that nuclei near the neutron drip line are expected to have very large neutron skins. The present analysis therefore motivates the question of which nuclei provide the most relevant link to neutron star physics.

title: Calculation of the electromagnetic radiation emitted from the D–T fusion process in tokamak reactors
abstract: Abstract In the deuterium tritium (D–T) fusion reaction an alpha particle is released with the kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . Since the fusion reaction is governed by the strong interaction, the alpha particle is almost instantaneously accelerated to the final state with its kinetic energy ∼ 3.5 MeV . According to the classical electrodynamics, electromagnetic radiation should be emitted in such an acceleration process. In this work, we calculate the electromagnetic radiation in the D–T fusion process using both the classical electrodynamics and the quantum mechanical models. The radiation is compared with the radiation from the core plasma bremsstrahlung for pure D–T plasmas in large tokamaks. The ratio between the radiation from the D–T fusion reaction and bremsstrahlung depends only on the plasma temperature. The radiation from the D–T fusion reaction is stronger than that from bremsstrahlung if the frequency is higher than a critical value. Although the predicted radiation is much weaker than its high frequency counterpart, it is still possible to be detected in the high fusion gain reactors under some circumstances. Its effect should also be taken into account if one uses the gamma-ray emission spectrum to diagnostic for plasma profiles in tokamaks.

title: Ab initio study of Li 7 with coupled mass partitions
abstract: Background: Lithium is of broad interest in nuclear astrophysics, fusion energy research, and nuclear technology. From a theoretical perspective, the nucleus $^7$Li presents a remarkable challenge, as its bound and resonant states can exhibit contributions from both the $^4$He + $^3$H cluster configuration and configurations involving a neutron or proton coupled to a $^6$Li or $^6$He core, respectively. Purpose: We aim to achieve a unified ab initio description of bound-state and continuum properties of $^7$Li by explicitly including simultaneously the coupled mass/charge partitions $^4$He + $^3$H, $^6$Li + $n$, and $^6$He + $p$. Specifically, we investigate the effect of inter-partition coupling on the spectrum of $^7$Li and calculate cross sections for the $^6$Li($n,p)^6$He, $^6$He($p,n)^6$Li, and $^6$He($p,t)^4$He reactions. Method: We employ the no-core shell model with continuum for the first time in a calculation that couples three mass/charge partitions of the aggregate nucleus $^7$Li, using a chiral nucleon-nucleon interaction as input. Results: The calculated spectrum reproduces all the experimentally observed states of $^7$Li in the correct order and predicts additional resonances. The calculation also reproduces the overall energy dependence of the $^6$Li$(n,p)^6$He cross section. Improved agreement with measured cross sections is obtained after phenomenological adjustment of resonance energies. Conclusions: The present results show that coupling the relevant mass/charge partitions is important for a consistent description of the $^7$Li spectrum and reaction cross sections, and offers a useful framework for interpreting existing data and guiding future measurements.

title: O 17 spectroscopy using C 13 ( α , α ) resonant elastic scattering
abstract: The detailed excitation functions for C 13 ( α , α ) elastic scattering and the additional thick target inverse kinematics measurements were analyzed using the R matrix approach. The analysis covered the excitation region in O 17 from 8.6 up to 11.2 MeV. Information on single particle widths of the levels in the O 17 nucleus and shell model calculations are in good agreement. A comparative analysis of the α -cluster structures of O 16 and O 17 nuclei indicates their common underlying nature. However, the structure in O 17 is more complex. In particular, each α -cluster level with spin J in O 16 corresponds to several levels with spins J = ± 1 / 2 in O 17 . Unexpectedly, the reduced-width-weighted centroids of the higher-spin members of these doublets always lie at lower excitation energies in O 17 .

title: Investigating two-body cluster structures of B 10
abstract: Two-body breakup mechanisms of the weakly bound nucleus B 10 were investigated through an exclusive coincidence measurement in the B 10 + Au 197 system at a beam energy of 57 MeV. Coincident detection of two outgoing charged particles by an array of Si strip detector telescopes shows that the dominant two-body projectile breakup channels are Li 6 + α and Be 9 + p . Projectile excitation energies, reconstructed from the kinetic energies of the fragments, are found to reproduce the energies of specific excited states of B 10 and thereby confirm the coexistence of both Li 6 - α and Be 9 - p two-body cluster configurations for B 10 . Continuum discretized coupled channels (CDCC) calculations, considering each of the above two cluster configurations separately, were able to explain the experimental cross sections for both breakup as well as elastic scattering simultaneously.

title: Comparative study of Langevin and random walk models for nuclear fission in the overdamped regime
abstract: We present a comparative study of Langevin dynamics and a Metropolis random walk model applied to thermal neutron-induced fission of $^{229}$Th, $^{235}$U, $^{239}$Pu, $^{245}$Cm, $^{249}$Cf, and $^{255}$Fm. Both methods are implemented within an identical four-dimensional Fourier-over-Spheroid framework, using potential energy surfaces derived from the macroscopic-microscopic model. We show that the Metropolis walk corresponds to the overdamped limit of the Langevin equations and confirm this correspondence numerically by Langevin calculations performed in the strongly damped regime and with quantum corrections to the random force switched off. Under these conditions, the two approaches produce essentially identical mass distributions for the lighter actinides. Systematic deviations develop for the heavier actinides, where the Langevin dynamics yields a non-negligible symmetric fission component absent in the random walk results. We trace this difference to the kinematic structure of the Metropolis sampling and to the residual inertial dynamics retained in the Langevin framework. A parallel comparison of Langevin calculations with and without the quantum-corrected effective temperature $T^*$ isolates the contribution of zero-point fluctuations and suggests that their standard phenomenological treatment may overestimate their impact in certain cases. Both approaches qualitatively reproduce the asymmetric peak positions and their systematic evolution across the actinide chain, while a common quantitative limitation -- the narrowness of the predicted distributions -- points to the role of higher-dimensional deformation modes not included in the present parametrization.

title: A novel high-performance confinement regime in a tokamak driven by tearing mode locking and rotation shear
abstract: Abstract In magnetically confined fusion plasmas, tearing mode (TM) locking is conventionally regarded as detrimental, often halting rotation and triggering disruptions. Contrary to this expectation, we demonstrate that locked TMs can enhance confinement by inducing an internal transport barrier (ITB). Specifically, the interaction between a locked outer plasma region and neutral beam injection (NBI)-driven core rotation generates a broad and intense toroidal velocity shear layer, which suppresses turbulence and improves core confinement. Beam emission spectroscopy and charge exchange recombination spectroscopy confirm a substantial reduction in turbulent transport and a rise in core ion temperature exceeding T i > 9 keV . This phenomenon—termed the Locking-Induced Flow and Transport (LIFT) mode—transforms a traditionally disruptive mechanism into a confinement enhancement strategy.

title: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
abstract: We present a comparison of the ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics model using a chiral mean field (CMF) equation of state with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies E lab = 0.2 – 2.0 A GeV and varying isospin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of quantum chromodynamics at varying isospin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the isospin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES, and S π RIT data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.

versions.title: Transport simulations with a constrained momentum-dependent chiral mean-field equation of state at various isospin fractions
versions.abstract: We present a comparison of the UrQMD model using a chiral mean field EoS (CMF) with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies $E_{\mathrm{lab}}=0.2-2.0 A$ GeV and varying iso-spin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of QCD at varying iso-spin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the iso-spin dependence of the high-density equation of state. At lower beam energies, comparing to FOPI, HADES and S$\pi$rit data, the sensitivity is higher but the observed deviations and systematic uncertainties of the existing data are larger than the sensitivity to the symmetry energy.

versions.abstract: We present a comparison of the ultrarelativistic quantum molecular dynamics model using a chiral mean field (CMF) equation of state with flow and pion production data in heavy ion collisions at low beam energies E lab = 0.2 – 2.0 A GeV and varying isospin fraction. The CMF model parameters are constrained by known properties of the high density equation of state of quantum chromodynamics at varying isospin fractions. This allows us to calculate the equation of state as well as nuclear interactions for different physical systems like neutron stars and heavy ion collisions in a consistent way. It is found that heavy ion reactions at the upcoming FAIR facility will only have marginal sensitivity on the isospin dependence of the high-density equation of state. title: Implication of multimessenger observations on the relativistic mean-field equation of state of dense nuclear matter and skin thickness of nuclei
abstract: The composition and properties of infinite nuclear matter under extreme conditions of temperature and pressure remain incompletely understood. In this work, we constrain the equation of state (EoS) of nuclear matter$-$constructed within the framework of the Relativistic Mean Field (RMF) model$-$by combining results from chiral effective field theory and multimessenger observations of neutron stars. Using the saturation properties of nuclear matter, we generate a wide ensemble of EoS, which are subsequently constrained within a Bayesian framework. The resulting posterior distributions provide tight bounds on both the saturation parameters and the coupling constants of the RMF model. The radius of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ neutron star is tightly constrained to $12.471_{-0.394}^{+0.427}\,\mathrm{km}$, while the maximum mass reaches $2.156_{-0.120}^{+0.175}\,M_\odot$. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the $\omega$-$\rho$ coupling, which governs the density dependence of the symmetry energy, becomes increasingly significant under successive astrophysical constraints. Finally, the predicted $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ agrees well with the CREX measurement, whereas that of $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ remains in tension with PREX-II. In contrast to earlier studies, we do not observe a clear correlation between the $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{208}$Pb and the symmetry energy slope parameter $L$.

title: Structure and decay of α -condensate candidates from cluster effective field theory interactions
abstract: Dilute gas-like configurations of α particles, often termed α condensates, have been proposed to exist in certain excited states of α -conjugate nuclei. This work investigates the structural and decay properties of α -condensate candidates within a few-body framework using leading-order cluster effective field theory interactions. To isolate dilute N α configurations, a constrained model space strategy is implemented inspired by Yamada and Schuck [Phys. Rev. C 69, 024309 (2004)], which constructs a description specifically for suprathreshold states. By explicitly decoupling the nonuniversal, compact configurations lying below the N α threshold, this framework describes N α condensates as quasibound states localized within the Coulomb barrier. The stochastic variational method is used to perform theoretical calculations for the proposed N α condensates ranging from Be 8 to Ne 20 . The results not only map the formation of these novel cluster states in heavier α -conjugate nuclei but also offer critical insights into the applicability of few-body universality to charged particles.

title: Impact of Decay-Chain Feeding by Long-Lived Heavy Nuclei on Nuclear Cosmochronology
abstract: Abstract Nuclear cosmochronology provides an independent method for determining the ages of astrophysical objects without relying on Galactic chemical evolution models. Long-lived radioactive actinides synthesized via the rapid neutron-capture process (r-process) particularly thorium and uranium serve as ideal chronometric nuclei. However, predicting the initial abundances of these nuclei and their subsequent long-term evolution remains a major source of uncertainty in nuclear cosmochronology. In this work, we investigate the impact of decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei on nuclear cosmochronology and estimate the corresponding age corrections. We develop a self-consistent radioactive decay network that includes all relevant decay pathways and couple it to r-process nucleosynthesis calculations. By tracking the long-term evolution of r-process nucleosynthesis based on neutron star merger trajectories, the dominant long-lived nuclei shaping the evolution of the chronometric elements Th and U are identified as 232Th, 235U, 236U, 238U, and 244Pu. It is found that delayed feeding substantially modifies the long-term evolution of actinides particularly for 232Th, which receives significant late-time contributions from heavier progenitor nuclei such as 244Pu and 236U. As a consequence, the U/Th and Th/X chronometers exhibit significant sensitivity to delayed feeding from the progenitor nuclei 244Pu and 236U, with age corrections reaching ∼5 Gyr. These results suggest that decay-chain feeding from long-lived progenitor nuclei plays a crucial role in nuclear cosmochronology and should be properly accounted for in age determinations based on actinide chronometers.
source: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

title: Orbit correction for a rapid cycling synchrotron using an adjacent-difference-constrained neural network
abstract: In a rapid cycling synchrotron (RCS), closed-orbit correction is an important task for maintaining high beam quality and machine stability. Since the orbits in RCS change during energy ramping, response matrix-based orbit correction is performed in segments, which can result in the corrector current ramp rates exceeding safety limits and accuracy loss in orbits. To address these issues, this paper employs machine learning for orbit correction in RCS. An adjacent-difference-constrained neural network (ADCNN) was built and tested in both simulations and machine experiments at the China Spallation Neutron Source (CSNS). The correction results demonstrate the feasibility of using neural networks for RCS orbit correction. The ADCNN exhibits a correction effect equivalent to that of response matrix-based correction while effectively limiting the current ramp rates of the correctors.

title: Cooling of isolated neutron stars with hyperon-mixed kaon-condensation matter
abstract: We investigate the thermal evolution of isolated neutron stars containing hyperon--mixed kaon--condensed matter, focusing on the role of proton superconductivity. The equation of state utilized for cooling calculation is based upon the minimal relativistic mean--field framework supplemented by chiral SU(3) dynamics for kaon condensation with an additional component on the three-baryon force, which ensures stiffness at high densities enough to meet astrophysical constraints on neutron-star masses and radii. We show that the nucleonic direct Urca processes operate at relatively low stellar masses ($M \gtrsim 1.3\,M_\odot$), erasing any observable signature of strangeness in the absence of superfluidity. However, if the proton $^1{\rm S}_0$ superconductivity works, because of suppression of fast neutrino cooling processes, the cooling scenario could become relevant with the strangeness, depending on the density regions of the pairing gap. In particular, if the proton superconductivity is so strong in high-density regions ($T_{c,p}\sim10^{10}~{\rm K}$), the nucleon and hyperon direct Urca processes shut down, which makes the kaon-induced Urca processes dominant in massive neutron stars. This scenario is in good agreement with several cold isolated neutron stars identified recently recently, such as the Vela Jr., PSR J0205+6449, and PSR B2334+61. Hence, we suggest that strong proton superconductivity can render kaon condensation observationally visible through cold neutron-star observations, providing a potential signature of strangeness in dense matter.

title: Fast-detection of hard x-ray emission and correlation with magnetohydrodynamic instabilities on the High-Beta Tokamak-Extended Pulse (HBT-EP)
abstract: Understanding the spatial and energy dynamics of runaway electrons is essential to preventing damage to next-generation fusion experiments and pilot plants. In the High-Beta Tokamak-Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) device, hard x-rays (HXRs) are produced through thick-target bremsstrahlung radiation when energetic electrons are deconfined and strike limiting surfaces. This paper describes a new HXR detector system composed of ten scintillator detectors and a visible-light fast camera, which is used to detect fast bursts of HXR emission that correlate with magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) perturbations. Hard x-rays cause spatially uncorrelated speckling on the fast camera, and the appearance of speckles is strongly correlated in time with x-ray bursts. We also observe a threshold below which an HXR signal is insufficient to produce a given speckle signal. Using these detectors, HBT-EP can measure the toroidal and temporal characteristics of HXRs, which are used to infer the characteristics of deconfined electrons. We report a strong correlation between the phase of a rotating n = 1 HXR source and an n = 1 MHD mode, suggesting that MHD activity directly enhances the radial transport of energetic electrons.

title: Development of a compact induction oven system for an electron cyclotron resonance ion source
abstract: This paper presents the development of a high-temperature induction oven designed for use in the Dubna electron cyclotron resonance ion source with permanent magnets for superheavy element synthesis experiments at the Flerov Laboratory of Nuclear Reactions. The focus is on ensuring stable evaporation of refractory metals, specifically 50Ti and 54Cr. Multiphysics simulation was carried out in COMSOL Multiphysics, accounting for electromagnetic and thermal processes as well as radiative heat transfer. Experimental studies confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed design and the consistency between simulation results and real operating conditions. The data demonstrate the potential of the developed oven for generating ion beams of refractory metals.

title: Conceptual design of the electron-optics of the magnetic electron recoil gamma-ray spectrometer
abstract: In nuclear fusion reactors, deuterium and tritium are fused together. Most reactions produce a 4He ion and a 14 MeV neutron, while about 2 × 10−5 of them produce a 5He ion and a gamma photon. One of the most important measurements from a fusion reactor is the total fusion power, which can be measured using the 14 MeV neutrons or the gamma-rays. Using both provides two independent measurements, which is valuable for researchers and regulators. Facilities such as JET use scintillators such as LaBr3 to measure gamma-ray emission, but such detectors could struggle with background on high-power reactors such as SPARC and ITER. We propose that a magnetic electron recoil gamma-ray spectrometer (MERGS) can make gamma-ray measurements in these high-background environments. MERGS will consist of a foil that converts photons to electrons via Compton scattering, a magnetic electron-optic system that focuses and disperses the electron beam, and a detector array that counts the electrons and uses their positions to infer their energy. A conceptual design framework of MERGS is presented, along with three numerically optimized electron-optic geometries for three different resolution requirements. Simulations are presented showing that each presented design can meet its requirements. This shows that MERGS can measure the gamma-ray emission spectrum more effectively than scintillators for a variety of price points, enabling improved measurements of fusion power as well as the study of fast ion physics via other nuclear reactions.

title: Diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter using a chiral SU(3) model
abstract: We study the diffusion and shear viscosity coefficients of hot isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter. The effects due to the baryon density, isospin, strangeness, and temperature on the nucleons and hyperons are studied within a chiral SU(3) model. The medium modifications of the baryons arise due to interactions with the mean scalar and vector fields within the model. The thermodynamic and transport properties are studied in the hot strange hadronic matter. The diffusion matrix associated with the multiple charges (baryon number, isospin, and strangeness), as well as the coefficient of shear viscosity, are computed from the Boltzmann equation using first-order Chapman--Enskog expansion within the relaxation time approximation. The diffusion coefficient, $\kappa_{QQ}$ corresponding to the conserved electric charge has also been studied in the present work. There are observed to be significant effects from the isospin asymmetry as well as the strangeness of the medium on the diffusion coefficients. The coefficient of shear viscosity, $\eta$ is observed to have a large enhancement in the presence of finite strangeness in the medium due to additional contributions from the hyperons. The effects due to isospin asymmetry on the shear viscosity coefficient is however observed to be marginal both in nuclear and hyperonic matter. The present study can be relevant for the experimental observables of asymmetric relativistic heavy-ion collisions, e.g., in the compressed baryonic matter (CBM) experiment at the FAIR facility at GSI as well as in the future J-PARC-HI program.

title: Strange quark stars and spontaneous scalarization
abstract: Strange quark matter, as one of the most extreme dense states in astrophysics, can be explored through relativistic compact objects. Hypothetical relativistic stars composed of dense strange quark matter are characterized by the equation of state of that matter. The spontaneous scalarization of strange quark stars is influenced by the equation of state of strange quark matter. Here, we investigate how the equation of state of strange quark matter influences the spontaneous scalarization of these stars. Considering Normal, color-flavor-locked (CFL), and CFLm quark matter in the bag models and applying the scalar-tensor gravity, we calculate the structure of scalarized strange quark stars. We investigate how the effective bag constant, perturbative QCD parameter, CFL pairing gap, and strange quark mass control the mass-radius relation, the central scalar field, the scalarization thresholds, and the scalar charge. Our results demonstrate that strange quark stars in scalar-tensor gravity are viable, testable objects, and they establish a complete framework for constraining both the gravitational theory and the properties of cold quark matter with current and future multimessenger observations.

title: Possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation in triaxial nuclei
abstract: It has been conventionally assumed that triaxial deformation breaks the degeneracy of pseudospin doublets, leading to less discussion of pseudospin partner bands in triaxial nuclei. However, by considering the pairing correlations, the quasiparticle states of pseudospin doublets are found to remain nearly degenerate at appropriate Fermi energies in triaxial systems. In this work, we systematically investigate the pseudospin partner bands based on the $\ensuremath{\pi}({g}_{7/2},{d}_{5/2})$ configuration in triaxial nuclei using the particle rotor model. For the first time, we propose the possible coexistence of pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation. Further analysis of angular momentum geometry and wave function components supports the identification of one structure as a pseudospin partner band and the other as a wobbling band. This study reveals a novel coexistence mode between pseudospin partner bands and wobbling excitation, illustrating the diversity of rotational excitations in atomic nuclei.
