title: Electronic effects on sputtering of fusion materials under light ion impact
abstract: Abstract Understanding material behavior under ion bombardment is a crucial aspect in predicting material surface modification and the lifetime of plasma-facing materials in fusion devices. Atomistic simulations are commonly employed to calculate key ion irradiation outcomes such as sputtering and reflection yields. However, within this simulation framework, the energy dissipation of ions in the electronic system is often neglected or treated using a simple velocity-dependent friction force. Although this approximation can be adequate for slow heavy ions, light ions in the sub-keV range lose a substantial fraction of their energy to electronic excitations, requiring a more realistic energy transfer description. Here, we incorporate trajectory-resolved electronic stopping obtained from ab initio calculations into molecular dynamics simulations of hydrogen and helium irradiation of tungsten and iron. We show that density-dependent electronic stopping leads to systematic variations in sputtering yields, especially for tungsten and lower impact energies, whereas reflection yields are found to be largely insensitive to the model choice. Material-dependent features are identified and mainly attributed to different relative contributions of projectile and recoil electronic energy loss. This work provides a physically motivated approach to improve the accuracy of the sputtering data used in plasma-surface interaction modeling.

title: Disruption halo currents and voltages measured on the HBT-EP tokamak
abstract: Abstract This paper presents measurements of disruption halo currents on the High Beta Tokamak—Extended Pulse (HBT-EP) experiment using 4 high-field side (HFS) tile arrays spaced at equal intervals of toroidal angle. Current flow through the tiles is measured using Rogowski coils external to the tokamak vessel. Tiles can also be operated as floating probes measuring their voltage with respect to the local chamber. Poloidal and toroidal distributions of halo currents are presented, along with a description and explanation of voltage measurements for both axisymmetric and rotating halo currents. Arcing on tiles generates current to components that greatly exceeds ion saturation current limits in the presence of an intact sheath. Furthermore, arcing is observed to occur more frequently as halo current magnitude increases. Measurements of voltages by operating tiles in floating configuration are found to be consistent with the halo voltage generation model presented in Boozer (2013 Phys. Plasmas 20 082510). The dependence of tile polarity on poloidal position as well as halo current peak shape are explained using tile voltage measurements.

title: Extraction of the pion-nucleon coupling constant using the effective-range expansion with the left-hand cut
abstract: We apply the generalized effective-range expansion of Du [], which incorporates the left-hand cut from one-pion exchange to low-energy neutron–proton scattering in the S 0 1 and S 1 3 channels. The amplitude zero for the center-of-mass momentum near 0.35 GeV in the S 0 1 channel is naturally accommodated within this framework. We extract the pole position, scattering length, effective range, shape parameter, and the pseudoscalar pion–nucleon coupling constant g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) at different expansion orders. The low-energy parameters are stable and consistent with established values, while g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) exhibits larger uncertainties. The extraction of g π N 2 / ( 4 π ) is data driven, relying on the analytic constraints from the left-hand cut and phase-shift data within the one-pion-exchange approximation. Despite larger uncertainties compared to high-precision extractions, the consistency with established values demonstrates that this framework can probe the left-hand-cut singularity.

title: Two-color dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser
abstract: We report on the design and performance of a two-color dual-oscillator infrared free-electron laser (FEL). The midinfrared (MIR) FEL at the Fritz Haber Institute has been upgraded to include a second oscillator FEL beamline that permits lasing in the far-infrared (FIR) regime from 4.5 to 175 μ m . In addition, a 500 MHz kicker cavity has been installed downstream of the electron accelerator. It allows deflection of electron bunches of up to 50 MeV energy alternately left and right by an angle of ± 2 ° . It can, thus, split the high-repetition rate (1 GHz) electron bunch train from the accelerator into two bunch trains of 500 MHz repetition rate each; one is steered to the MIR FEL and the other one to the new FIR FEL. In this two-color mode of simultaneous, synchronized operation, the wavelengths in both FELs can be tuned independently over wide ranges of up to a factor of 4 each by undulator gap variation. In addition, two-color operation is also available at reduced repetition rates (e.g., 55.6 MHz of both MIR and FIR pulses), as needed for some applications. This unique two-color mode opens up a wealth of novel user applications, such as MIR-FIR pump-probe experiments.

title: Binary neutron stars in the next-generation era: Multi-messenger detection prospects and constraints on the equation of state, mass distribution, and cosmology
abstract: Abstract Next-generation gravitational-wave (GW) observatories will provide crucial insights into the nature of neutron star (NS) matter and the cosmological expansion history. We estimate the number of multi-messenger detections of binary neutron stars (BNS) with the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) and project the resulting constraints on the equation of state (EOS), BNS mass distribution, and cosmology using joint hierarchical Bayesian inference. Our results rely on specific assumptions for the merger rate, EOS, and mass distribution; we consider two different mass functions, a narrow one centred around 1.4 M⊙ and a wide one ranging from 1.1 to 2 M⊙, and a merger rate with a local value of 107 Gpc−3 yr−1. Under this setup, our mock follow-up algorithm results in between ∼40 and ∼100 short-term electromagnetic counterparts per year for ET, depending on the detector layout and mass distribution. In a joint network with CE, this number ranges from ∼100 to ∼500. Additionally, we project tens to hundreds of late-time afterglow detections from gamma-ray bursts or KNe. Based on the generated multi-messenger events, we perform an injection campaign to hierarchically recover the EOS, mass distribution, and cosmology in a fully Bayesian framework. Focussing on KN events from ET alone, the multi-messenger data from our largest analysed catalogue with 78 events can constrain the canonical NS radius R1.4 to ≲ 0.2 km and the Hubble constant H0 to ≲ 1 km s−1 Mpc−1, at least in absence of systematic modelling offsets. By comparing inference results that are solely based on GW data and those incorporating light-curve information, we find that while the latter has negligible impact on the EOS constraints, it can benefit the inference of cosmological parameters.

Vector meson photoproduction on the nucleus and the extraction of the nuclear suppression factor using asymmetric beams
abstract: Abstract The cross-section for photoproduction of a vector meson on a nucleus is usually determined in nucleus-nucleus collisions, which introduces a twofold ambiguity as to which nucleus emitted the photon. This can be resolved in asymmetric collisions of protons and nuclei, where the ratio of photoproduction cross-sections on the proton and nucleus directly measures the nuclear suppression factor with minimal model dependence. The feasibilty of using existing and future proton-lead collisions at the LHC is evaluated.
journal_abbrev: J. Phys. G: Nucl. Part. Phys.

title: Outflows in a super-Eddington quasar drive clumpy circumgalactic medium and extended Hα nebulae at z ≳ 6
abstract: Abstract The discovery of gargantuan black holes with masses exceeding a billion solar masses at z ≳ 6 suggests rapid black hole growth and significant energy input into their host galaxies in the early Universe. With JWST probing previously unseen phases of the interstellar (ISM) and circumgalactic (CGM) medium around z > 6 quasars, detailed theoretical studies can now be directly confronted with observations. We use zoom-in simulations of a massive protocluster at z ∼ 6, employing both the fiducial fable galaxy formation model and modifications that allow earlier black hole seeding and mildly super-Eddington accretion. The central quasar remains Compton-thick throughout most of its evolution, with the obscuration arising from the ISM of its compact host galaxy. The onset of sufficiently strong quasar feedback drives a ‘blow-out’ episode, clearing out escape channels for ionizing radiation and leaving the central engine unobscured. This leads to a complete transformation of the CGM, whereby powerful, metal-enriched outflows produce a population of cold, fast, neutral clumps, significantly increasing the covering fraction of neutral hydrogen in the host halo. Radiative transfer calculations performed with a new ray-tracing code show that the CGM responds to quasar activity through the formation of Hα nebulae, whose size and luminosity increase with the strength of quasar feedback and decrease with obscuration level. Enhanced early black hole growth thus fundamentally reshapes the ISM and CGM of z ∼ 6 quasars, leaving clear observable signatures in their obscuration, neutral hydrogen distribution, and extended Hα emission.

title: Capability of multimodal large language models to describe gravitational wave images
abstract: Abstract The advent of multi-messenger astronomy has highlighted the necessity for a comprehensive analysis of immense datasets generated by multiple astronomical observation instruments. The field of gravitational wave astronomy has employed deep learning for the efficient processing of data. However, the utilization of this technique has predominantly been confined to a single type of input data, such as images. While image-to-text applications with multimodal large language models (LLMs) are growing in other fields, a notable gap remains in the generation of textual descriptions of astrophysical and astronomical images. This study explores the potential of using multimodal LLMs to describe spectrogram images of anomalies captured by ground-based gravitational wave observatories. Three models, GPT-4, GPT-4o, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, were provided only with an image and a single prompt, without additional context. The generated text responses were then evaluated for length, meaning, and accuracy of the answers. All three models correctly identified each image as a spectrogram representation of gravitational wave data and generated appropriate explanations. However, they exhibited difficulties in detailed signal descriptions and source inference under context-free setting, indicating that further research is needed before practical application to gravitational wave data analysis. This study demonstrates the feasibility of using multimodal LLMs to transform spectrogram images into textual data and provides insight into their potential integration into gravitational wave data analysis workflows.

title: Interpretability as a leakage detector: a case study in machine-learning-based exoplanet detection with TESS
abstract: Abstract The Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) generates photometric time series for hundreds of thousands of stars, far more than can be vetted by hand, motivating machine-learning triage. We present a low-resource, interpretable pipeline that classifies TESS light curves as transit-bearing or not using a random forest trained on engineered summary features, treating feature-importance analysis as a formal auditing step, and apply it to Sector 68. The positive class comprises TESS-confirmed planet hosts; the negative class comprises Sector 68 targets with no catalogued planet or candidate, assembled from a different source. Auditing the model's feature-importance ranking exposes a confound: the two dominant features, the flux energy and its logarithm, are for median-normalized light curves essentially proportional to the number of cadences, that is, to observational baseline. A transit-blind ranking by this feature alone already separates the classes with an AUC of 0.734, and because our train/test split cannot control for the classes' differing provenance, the full model's held-out ROC-AUC of 0.95 (precision 0.94, recall 0.74, F1 0.83) is best read as performance under the current sampling procedure; isolating the confound's precise causal share is left as an open question for a dedicated ablation study. Some evidence of genuine signal survives this caveat: applied to 400 held-out candidates that share the negative class's baseline and so cannot benefit from the confound, the pipeline still flags 61 (15%) as probable planets, with the highest-probability cases showing genuine periodic transit dips. We give concrete recommendations for detecting and avoiding this failure mode: provenance-matched class construction, baseline-invariant features, controlled ablation, and routine interpretability-based leakage audits. The case study is offered as an instance of auditing scientific machine learning with its own tools, and a cautionary lesson for machine-learning-based exoplanet detection.

title: Generation fusion: the human factor in the fusion equation
abstract: Abstract The human factor in fusion energy development is about those who will take fusion from the laboratory to the grid and under what conditions. While this is among the most strategically important dimensions of the field, it is also among the least formally discussed. During the 51st European Physical Society (EPS) Conference on Plasma Physics in Vilnius, Lithuania, Generation Fusion was held as a satellite event on 9th July 2025. It was set-up as a panel discussion and was a direct sequel to the Visions for Fusion event held at the 50th EPS Conference. The panel brought together six researchers and industry representatives from different career stages, working in magnetic confinement fusion, inertial confinement fusion, and related fields. Using live audience polling of approximately 100 participants, panel discussions, and an open Q&A, the event explored topics including motivation and retention of early-career researchers, the role of mentoring and soft skills, public-private partnerships, mobility between institutions and countries, interdisciplinary collaboration, and communication with society and policy-makers. A clear and consistent finding emerged: the field faces not a lack of motivation, the overwhelming majority of attendees expressed a desire to remain in fusion, but rather structural barriers such as employment instability, limiting mentoring frameworks, and insufficient permeability between academia and industry. The panel closed with a strong consensus calling for greater diversity, more equitable career paths, and a shift away from metrics such as the H-index towards broader definitions of scientific impact, including, for example, public communications.

title: Design and integration studies of a DCLL breeding blanket for a stellarator reactor based on the CIEMAT-QI4X configuration
abstract: Abstract The integration of a breeding blanket in a stellarator reactor poses a major challenge due to the intricate geometry and the reduced free space between plasma and coils and between neighbouring coils, which also makes maintenance by remote handling techniques difficult. Conversely, in comparison with tokamaks, the breeding blanket can benefit significantly from the steady-state operation of stellarators. While previous studies have pointed to the feasibility of a Dual Coolant Lithium Lead (DCLL) breeding blanket in stellarators such as HELIAS-5B, each device introduces a different set of geometrical constraints and integration requirements that must be addressed through a dedicated design approach. This work presents a sequential study on several aspects that have clear impact on the functionality and efficiency of a DCLL breeding blanket integrated into a stellarator design based on the CIEMAT-QI4X plasma configuration. The proposal aims to achieve accurate alignment between the magnetic field and the liquid metal flow to avoid electric insulation of the liquid metal circuits as much as possible. Although it has yet to be confirmed through numerical analysis or experimental testing, the specific alignment strategy proves to be highly effective in reducing pressure drop in the liquid metal circuits. Besides, the neutronic results point to an excellent performance in terms of tritium breeding provided there is an optimal use of the available space between the plasma and the coils, although some arrangements must be done to satisfy also the contemplated shielding requirements. Furthermore, the internal design of the blanket segments and the optimization of the cooling system allows achieving a valuable performance in terms of balance of plant, while meeting the structural integrity criteria that have been studied at a very preliminary stage.

title: Projected Sensitivity to Atmospheric Neutrino Oscillations using a 1725 m^3 Liquid Nitrogen Detector at CJPL
abstract: Abstract In atmospheric neutrino analyses, the usable zenith-angle range is generally restricted to upward-going events to suppress the cosmic-ray muon background. Motivated by the exceptionally low underground muon background at the China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), we investigate whether extending the zenith-angle acceptance can improve the sensitivity of atmospheric neutrino oscillation measurements. An existing 1725 m$^{3}$ liquid-nitrogen volume is adopted as the basis of a simplified detector model, in which the accepted zenith-angle range is extended from $\cos\theta_{\mu}\in[-1,0]$ to $\cos\theta_{\mu}\in[-1,0.3]$, and the projected oscillation sensitivity is evaluated for a 10-year exposure. The atmospheric neutrino flux is estimated by interpolating standard flux predictions as a function of geomagnetic latitude. Neutrino interactions in the surrounding rock and the liquid-nitrogen volume are simulated for neutrino energies of $E\ge0.1$ GeV, followed by secondary-particle transport and geometry-based event selection. For the benchmark oscillation parameters $\Delta$m$^{2}_{32}$ = $2.4\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{eV}^{2}$ and $\sin^{2}\theta_{23}=0.5$, the neutrino-induced muon flux from the surrounding rock is estimated to be $(3.65 \pm 1.00)\times10^{-13}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ sr$^{-1}$, corresponding to a muon yield of $(0.13 \pm 0.034)$ day$^{-1}$ in the 1725 m$^{3}$ liquid-nitrogen volume. Three-flavor neutrino oscillations are incorporated into a Poisson-likelihood $\chi^{2}$ analysis to evaluate the sensitivity to the oscillation parameters. Extending the usable zenith-angle range leads to a clear improvement in the projected oscillation sensitivity at the 90\% confidence level over a 10-year exposure. The improvement is most pronounced for $\Delta$m$^{2}_{32}$, while the improvement in the constraint on $\sin^{2}\theta_{23}$ near the best-fit point remains relatively modest. These results demonstrate that the extended zenith-angle coverage enabled by the ultra-low cosmic-ray muon background at CJPL can strengthen the projected constraints on atmospheric neutrino oscillation parameters in a large liquid-nitrogen detector. title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
abstract: Abstract We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.
publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

title: Constrained coupled-cluster computations yield negative-parity rotational bands
abstract: Many deformed nuclei exhibit low-lying rotational bands with negative parity. In mean-field calculations, such bands follow from symmetry restoration when the variational solution spontaneously breaks parity. However, they can also be computed in cases where the breaking of parity is not spontaneous but rather enforced by an octupole constraint. In this paper, we extend these techniques to coupled-cluster computations. We introduce octupole-constrained coupled-cluster theory, which explicitly breaks the parity of the correlated intrinsic state and restores parity and angular momentum as good quantum numbers by projection after variation. We perform coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles (CCSD) computations for $^{20}$Ne using two- and three-nucleon forces from chiral effective field theory. The energies of the positive-parity ground-state rotational band are close to data and depend only weakly on the constrained octupole moment and the Hartree--Fock reference. In contrast, the energies of the negative-parity rotational band are more sensitive to these auxiliary quantities.

title: Octupole correlations in the excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfers in actinide nuclei
abstract: Impacts of octupole correlations on low-energy excited $0^+$ states and two-neutron transfer intensities in Ra and Th isotopes are analyzed within the interacting boson model, using the Hamiltonian parameters that are obtained from microscopic nuclear density functional theory calculations. Incorporating the octupole degree of freedom in the model is shown to give an overall reasonable description of the ground-state-band energy levels and to lower the $0^+_2$ ones significantly. The calculation yields a number of excited $0^+$ states, most of which are formed by the configurations of more than one octupole boson. Octupole correlations make significant contributions to the $0^+_1 \to 0^+_2$ $(p,t)$ and $(t,p)$ transfer intensities in those nuclei in which the octupole collectivity is most enhanced. Behaviors of the predicted transfer intensities with the increasing neutron number along the isotopic chain reflect nuclear structural evolution.

title: Design and initial characterization of a modular tabletop Penning ion-source beamline for low-energy ion irradiation
abstract: Ion beam implantation is an effective technology for material modification, including surface engineering, doping, and irradiation. Its use in laboratories is, however, not very common due to the expensive nature and rigidity of commercial systems. To address this gap, we present the design, simulation, fabrication, and characterization of a new, modular tabletop Penning Ion Gauge source system. This system uniquely integrates high-precision beam optics, including an electrostatic quadrupole triplet for beam focusing and a Wien velocity filter for ion species selection. IBSimu and COMSOL Multiphysics® were used to model the extraction system and downstream beam dynamics, respectively. Experiments demonstrated multi-species operation (H+, He+, N+) over a large operating energy range. A key achievement is the system’s exceptionally broad, tunable beam current, with on-target currents spanning three orders of magnitude (1 nA–3 μA), accessed by adjusting the plasma discharge, gas pressure, and beam-transport conditions, delivered to an aperture-defined, approximately circular 0.5 cm2 on-target spot. The nitrogen transmission scan at 25 keV demonstrates coarse separation between N+ and N2+, with a first-order experimental resolving power of 2.43, as determined from the N+ peak. This system provides a reproducible and accessible platform, offering a useful and accessible resource for researchers in materials science, low-energy nuclear physics, and particle accelerators.

title: Full-event anomaly detection for new physics searches at the Electron-Ion Collider
abstract: The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will offer new opportunities to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study resonant anomaly detection using machine learning and the full particle content of an event. We consider a new neutral gauge boson and a heavy neutral lepton as illustrative signals with different electron-jet topologies. Weakly supervised learning uses this event information to enhance the sensitivity of an invariant-mass search without identifying individual signal events during training. Comparisons with high-level observables show that the electron kinematics account for an important part of the separation, while correlations among the particles provide further sensitivity. We also construct a conditional full-event generator by adapting a model pretrained on LHC jets to produce EIC background events. A scan over signal fractions demonstrates substantial signal enhancement using the learned background reference, providing a proof of concept for this approach at the EIC. Finally, we consider a fully unsupervised graph autoencoder that provides modest signal enhancement but retains sensitivity at signal fractions too small for effective weak supervision. Our results motivate full-event anomaly detection as part of the EIC physics program and identify directions for developing methods suited to its distinct kinematics.

title: Comparison of Silvaco and Synopsys TCAD predictions including the Perugia radiation damage model in silicon pixel detectors for the HL-LHC
abstract: Abstract At the High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), silicon pixel detectors will be exposed to radiation fluences about 5 to 10 times larger than those experienced by the current innermost pixel layers up to today. Due to radiation damage to bulk of pixel detectors, leakage current and depletion voltage will increase significantly over time, posing severe constraints on operating conditions, with important modifications to the electric field profile due to radiation induced deep defects in silicon bulk. It is important to have reliable predictions for all observables — such as leakage current level and breakdown voltage — after irradiation, in order to estimate operational voltage values. In this paper, the predictions of Silvaco and Synopsys TCAD device simulations are compared when the surface and bulk defects and traps of the “New University of Perugia radiation damage model” are included by studying observables like leakage current, depletion and breakdown voltage, along with electric field and trap occupancy profiles. The results are quite promising regarding leakage current, depletion voltage, electric field and trap statistics, at two distinct reference temperatures and fluences.

title: Probing high-momentum components in $^{16}$O via zero-degree $(p,d)$ cross-section ratios
abstract: The $^{16}$O$(p,d)^{15}$O reaction was measured at zero degrees for incident-proton energies of 403, 604, 907 and 1209 MeV. Cross-section ratios for the 6.18-MeV (3/2$^-$) and 5.24-MeV (5/2$^+$) excited-state transitions, normalized to the ground-state transition, were previously reported in Wang et al., Phys. Lett. B 879, 140563 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.physletb.2026.140563, together with their implications for high-momentum neutron components in $^{16}$O. The present work extends that study by providing additional experimental and data-analysis details, and by reporting for the first time the ratio $R_{7.3}$, defined as the cross section populating the 7.28-MeV (7/2$^+$) state relative to that for the ground state. The positive-parity state ratios exhibit a pronounced momentum dependence, consistent with representative variational Monte Carlo trends.
authors: H. J. Ong (State Key Laboratory of Heavy Ion Science
S. Terashima (State Key Laboratory of Heavy Ion Science
I. Tanihata (Research Center for Nuclear Physics
Y. K. Tanaka (RIKEN High Energy Nuclear Physics Laboratory

title: Non-LTE Ionization Modeling for Helium and Strontium in Neutron Star Merger Ejecta
abstract: Abstract The material ejected from a binary neutron star merger produces a “kilonova,” a radioactively powered emission at ultraviolet, optical, and infrared wavelengths. The early-phase spectra of the kilonova AT2017gfo, following the gravitational wave event GW170817, exhibit a strong absorption feature around 1 μ m. Helium (He) and strontium (Sr) have been proposed as the candidate elements contributing to this feature. However, due to the lack of consistent modeling including these two elements simultaneously, the exact contributions of each element to this feature remain unclear. In this study, we develop nonlocal thermodynamic equilibrium ionization models for He and Sr that take into account ionization by high-energy electrons, and estimate the abundances of each element required to reproduce the observed feature in the early-phase spectra of AT2017gfo. Our modeling indicates that about 1% of He or 1%–10% of Sr (in mass fraction) are present in the ejecta moving at v ∼ 0.15 c . This Sr mass fraction nicely agrees with the mass fraction in the solar r -process pattern. Based on comparison with nucleosynthesis calculations, our constraints suggest that r -process nucleosynthesis in GW170817 occurs at relatively low electron fraction ( Y e ≲ 0.35) and low entropy ( s ≲ 30 k B /nucleon) conditions. Generally, for Y e ≲ 0.15, the observed feature can be reproduced by He at the mass fraction expected from the α -decay of trans-Pb nuclei, and may therefore serve as an indirect signature for the production of elements beyond the third r -process peak in binary neutron star mergers.

title: Impact of ab initio E1 strength on neutron capture rates along the nickel isotopic chain
abstract: Nucleosynthesis simulations of the r-process require neutron capture rates for neutron-rich nuclei, many of which lie beyond experimental reach. Predicting these rates relies on theoretical calculations of the low-energy electric dipole (E1) strength near the neutron threshold. We present the first ab initio computation of the E1 strength along the nickel isotopic chain, for $^{58}$Ni and the even-even isotopes $^{68-80}$Ni. The E1 strength is obtained with the Lorentz integral transform coupled-cluster (LIT-CC) method, extended to axially symmetric reference states to reach open-shell nuclei, using two- and three-nucleon interactions from chiral effective field theory. The approach is benchmarked against the measured photoabsorption cross section of $^{58}$Ni and the E1 strength of $^{68}$Ni. Along the chain we find low-lying E1 strength above the neutron threshold that grows with neutron number. Including it in the reaction code TALYS enhances the neutron capture rates forming $^{68-78}$Ni between 3 and 10 GK, with an effect that increases with temperature and neutron number and an uncertainty dominated by the inversion of the integral transform. For $^{80}$Ni, where strong pygmy dipole strength lies just above threshold, the enhancement sets in already around 0.5 GK. Together, these results open the way to ab initio input for neutron capture rates along isotopic chains far from stability.

title: GEANT4-based comparative study of detector response in reduced and fully instrumented silicon-tungsten sampling calorimeter
abstract: Abstract A GEANT4-based simulation study of a silicon-tungsten (Si-W) sampling calorimeter is presented to investigate electromagnetic shower development and detector response in the energy range of 1–120 GeV. Two detector configurations are considered: a reduced sequential-sampling prototype (Configuration-I), where a single silicon detector layer is placed downstream of progressively increasing tungsten absorber depths to sample the longitudinal shower evolution, and a fully instrumented sampling calorimeter (Configuration-II) consisting of twenty silicon layers interleaved with tungsten absorbers. The detector response is studied in terms of longitudinal shower development, shower maximum position, energy deposition, detector linearity, and calorimetric performance. Configuration-II provides simultaneous longitudinal sampling and allows event-by-event reconstruction of the deposited energy, yielding the expected linear response and energy resolution. Configuration-I reproduces the average longitudinal shower profiles and exhibits a strong linear correlation with the integrated shower response of Configuration-II. Although the absence of event-by-event multi-layer sampling prevents a direct determination of calorimetric energy resolution in Configuration-I, the observed correlation between two configurations is used to relate the response of the reduced prototype to that of the fully instrumented calorimeter and to estimate the corresponding calorimetric performance. The results demonstrate that the reduced prototype successfully reproduces the main characteristics of electromagnetic shower development observed in the fully instrumented detector, establishing its usefulness for detector characterization and test-beam studies when the construction of a complete prototype is limited by available resources.

title: Final-state centrality in relativistic heavy-ion simulations from neural networks
abstract: Experiments in relativistic heavy-ion collisions determine centrality from final-state quantities, usually the charged-particle multiplicity. Performing the same in hydrodynamic simulations requires millions of events, which is impractical for state-of-the-art hybrid models, and centrality is therefore commonly approximated by the initial entropy or energy. We show that neural networks trained on a few hundred hybrid events predict the event-by-event multiplicity and mean transverse momentum $[p_T]$ with relative errors of 1--2\%, which makes it possible to generate millions of collisions at a small fraction of the cost of the full simulation. For Pb--Pb collisions at $2.76$~TeV and Au--Au collisions at $200$~GeV, the initial-state and final-state definitions select nearly the same events in 10\%-wide classes, but up to 20\% of the events change class when the classes are 1\% wide. We then compute the fluctuations of $[p_T]$ and its Pearson correlations with a proxy of the elliptic flow, estimated from the initial eccentricity, and with multiplicity. The first correlation is insensitive to how centrality is defined, while the second changes substantially. The approach can be applied at every design point of Bayesian analyses at modest additional cost.

title: First measurement of wind line formation regions in an early O-type star
abstract: Context. Massive stars with their strong ionizing radiation and strong stellar winds are the key feedback agents of the Universe. Stellar winds of massive stars are often measured by fitting resonance lines in the UV using non-local thermal equilibrium (non-LTE) stellar atmosphere models. Aims. We aim to conduct the first measurement of the resonance line formation regions in an early-type eclipsing binary in the Small Magellanic Cloud, namely AzV 75. Methods. We employed photometric data from TESS and ASAS-SN in combination with radial velocity measurements from multi-epoch Hubble Space Telescope UV spectra to derive the ephemeris. We examined the intensity changes in the C IV and N V resonance lines in the UV and combined them with a light-curve analysis to estimate the region in the wind where these lines are formed. Results. We derived that AzV 75 has an orbital period of P orb = 165.925 ± 0.115 d, eccentricity of e = 0.42 ± 0.02, mass ratio of q = 0.72 ± 0.03, and inclination of i = 85.77 ◦ . With this orbital configuration, no secondary eclipse is expected. We report that the optically thick UV resonance lines exhibit flattening and shortening of the absorption trough, and weakening of their emission features, as they approach the phase of the expected secondary eclipse, while the continuum UV flux appears to remain unaffected. We illustrate that this behaviour can be well explained by the primary’s optically thick wind eclipsing the secondary star. The C IV and N V resonance line formation regions in the primary star extend up to 316 R ⊙ . Conclusions. We have measured the line formation regions of resonance lines in a stellar wind of an early O-type star. These are important benchmarks for 1D as well as 3D non-LTE stellar atmosphere models. Even though we have numerous multi-epoch UV spectra at hand, the eclipse is not fully sampled, leaving some freedom in the derived sizes of the line formation regions. A first comparison to 1D stellar atmosphere models indicates that a classical β law with an exponent of β = 0.5 instead of β = 0.8 might be favoured for the primary star’s velocity field.

versions.title: First measurement of wind line formation regions in an early O-type star
versions.abstract: Massive stars with their strong ionizing radiation and strong stellar winds are the key feedback agents of the universe. Stellar winds of massive stars are often measured by fitting resonance lines in the UV using non-LTE stellar atmosphere models. So far, the line formation regions of these lines have not been measured empirically, preventing a comparison to the model's structures. We aim to conduct the first measurement of the resonance line formation regions in an early-type eclipsing binary in the SMC, namely AzV 75. We employ TESS and ASAS-SN photometry in combination with radial velocity measurements from multi-epoch HST UV spectra to derive the ephemeris. We examine the intensity changes in the C IV and N V resonance lines in the UV and combine them with a light-curve analysis to estimate the region in the wind where these lines are formed. AzV 75 has an orbital period P=165.66d, eccentricity e=0.42, mass ratio q=0.72, and inclination i=85.77{\deg}. With this orbital configuration, no secondary eclipse is expected. We report that the optically thick UV resonance lines exhibit flattening and shortening of the absorption trough, and weakening of their emission features, as they approach the phase of the expected secondary eclipse, while the continuum UV flux appears to remain unaffected. We illustrate that this can be explained by the primary's optically thick wind eclipsing the secondary star. The C IV and N V resonance line formation regions in the primary star extend up to 316 Rsol. The measured extend of the formation regions of resonance lines in a stellar wind are important benchmarks for 1D as well as 3D non-LTE stellar atmosphere models. A first comparison to 1D-stellar atmosphere models indicates that a classical beta-law with an exponent of beta=0.5 instead of beta=0.8 might be favoured for the primary star's velocity field.
